peregrination and discovery in the remote north and east part of Asia call Tartary and China the first book chap. i. the journal of friar WILLIAM de RUBRUQVIS a Frenchman of the order of the minorite friar unto the east part of the world dom. 1253. to the most excellent and most christian lord Lewis by God grace the renown king of France friar William rubruk * * master Hak. have publish part of this author but the whole work be find in Benet college library in Cambridg I think fit to communicate it to the world it be never publish as I think in any language I begin with the tartar as be ^^owne to these part before the Chinois yea China or Mang^ become know by they ecclus 39 v 3. or Gasaria the mean of the minorite order wish health and continual triumph in Christ it be write in the book of concern the wiseman he shall travel into foreign country and good and evil shall he try in all thing the very same action my lord and king have I achieve howbeit I wish that I have do it like a wise man and not like a foole. for many there be that perform the same action which a wise man do not wise but more undiscreet of which number I fear myself to be one notwithstanding howsoever I have do it because you command i when I depart from your highness to write all thing unto you which I shall see among the tartar and you wish i also that I shall not fear to write long letter I have do as your majesty enjoin i yet with fear and reverence because I want word and eloquence sufficient to write unto so great a majesty be it know therefore unto your sacred majesty that in the year of our lord 1253. about the Nones of May we enter into the sea of Pontus which the bulgarian call the great Sea it contain in length as I learn of certain merchant one thousand and eight mile and be in a manner divide into two part about the midst thereof be two province one towards the north and another towards the south the south province be call Synopolis and it be the castle and port of the sultan of Turkey but the north province be call of the latin Gasaria of the greek which inhabit upon the sea shore thereof it be call Cassaria that be to say Caesaria and there be certain headland stretch forth into the sea towards Synopolis also there be three hundred mile of distance between Synopolis and Cassaria insomuch that the distance from those point or place to Constantinople in length and breadth be about seven hundred mile and seven hundred mile also from thence to the east namely to the country of which be a province of Georgia at the province of Gasaria or we arrive which province be in a manner three square have a city on the west part thereof call Kersova wherein saint Clement suffer martyrdom and sail before the say city we see a island in which a church be say to be build by the hand of angel but about the midst of the say province towards the south Soldaia as it be upon a sharp angle or point stand a city call Soldaia direct against Synopolis and there do all the Turkey merchant which traffic into the north country in their journey outward arrive and as they return homeward also from Russia and the say northern region into Turkey the foresay merchant transport thither ermine and gray fur with other rich and costly skin other carry clothes make of Cotton or bombast the city of Matriga and silk and diverse kind of spice but upon the east part of the say province stand a city call Matriga where the river Tanais discharge his stream into the sea of Pontus the mouth whereof be twelve mile in breadth for this river before it enter into the sea of Pontus make a little sea which have in breadth and length seven hundred mile and it it be in no place thereof above six pace deep whereupon great vessel can sail over it howbeit the merchant of Constantinople arrive at the foresay city of * * Matriga Materta send their bark unto the river of Tanais to buy dry fish sturgeon thoss barbil and a infinite number of other fish the foresay province of Cassaria be compass in with the sea on three side thereof namely on the westside where Kersova the city of saint Clement be situate on the southside the city of Soldaia whereat we arrive on the east-side Maricandis and there stand the city of Matriga upon the mouth of the river Tanais beyond the say mouth stand which be not in subjection unto the tartar also the people call and towards the east who likewise be not under the tartar dominion moreover towards the south stand the city of Trapesunda which have a governor proper to itself name guydo be of the lineage of the emperor of Constantinople and be subject unto the tartar next unto that be Synopolis the city of the sultan of Turkey who likewise be in subjection unto they next unto these lie the country of Vastacius who son be call astar of his grandfather by the mother side who be not in subjection all the land from the mouth of Tanais westward as far as Danubius be under their jurisdiction yea beyond Danubius also towards Constantinople Valakia which be the land of and Bulgaria minor as far as Solonia do all pay tribute unto they and beside the tribute impose they have also of late year exact of every household a axe and all such corn as they find lie on heap we arrive therefore at Soldaia the twelve of the kalend of june and diverse merchant of Constantinople which be arrive there before we report that certain messenger be come thither from the holy land who be desirous to travel unto Sartach notwithstanding I myself have public give out upon palm Sunday within the church of Sophia that I be not your nor any other man messenger but that I travel unto those infidel according to the rule of our order and be arrive the say merchant admonish i to take diligent heed what I speak because they have report i to be a messenger if I shall say the contrary that I be no messenger I can not have free passage grant unto i then I speak after this manner unto the governor of the city or rather unto their lieutenant because the governor themselves be go to pay tribute unto and be not as yet return we hear of your lord Sartach quoth I in the holy land that he be become a christian and the christian be exceed glad thereof and especial the most Christian king of France who be there now in pilgrimage and fight against the saracen to redeem the holy place out of their hand wherefore I be determine to go unto Sartach and to deliver unto he the letter of my lord the king wherein he admonish he concern the good and commodity of all Christendom and they receive we with gladness and give we entertainment in the cathedral church the bishop of which church be with Sartach who tell i many good thing concern the say Sartach which afterward I find to be nothing so then put they we to our choice whether we will have cart and ox or packe-horse to transport our carriage and the merchant of Constantinople advise i not to take cart of the citizen of Soldaia but to buy cover cart of i own such as the russian carry their skin in and to put all our carriage which I will daily take out into they because if I shall use horse I must be constrain at every bait to take down my carriage and to lift they up again on sundry horse back and beside that I shall ride a more gentle pace by the ox draw the cart wherefore content myself with their evil counsel I be travel unto Sartach two month which I can have do in one if I have go by horse I bring with i from Constantinople be by the merchant advise so to do pleasant fruit muskadel wine and delicate biscuit bread to present unto the governor of Soldaia to the end I may obtain free passage because they look favourable upon no man which come with a empty hand all which thing I bestow in one of my cart not find the governor of the city at home for they tell i if I can carry they to sartach that they will be most acceptable unto he we take our journey therefore about the kalend of june with four cover cart of our own and with two other which we borrow of they wherein we carry our bedding to rest upon in the night and they allow we five horse to ride upon for there be just five person in our company namely friar Bartholomew de Cremona I myself and my associate friar Bartholomew of Cremona and goset the bearer of these present the man of God Turgemannus and Nicolas my servant who I buy at Constantinople with some part of the alm bestow upon i moreover they allow we two man which drive our cart and give attendance unto our ox and horse there be high promontory on the sea shore from Kersova unto the mouth of Tanais also there be forty castle between Kersova and Soldaia every one of which almost have their proper language among who there be many goth who speak the dutch tongue beyond the say mountain towards the north there be a most beautiful wood grow on a plain full of fountain and freshet and beyond the wood there be a mighty plain champion the neck of chersonesan continue five day journey unto the very extremity and border of the say province northward and there it be a narrow isthmus or neck land have sea on the east and west side thereof insomuch that there be a ditch make from one sea unto the other in the same plain before the tartar spring up be the comanian wont to inhabit who compel the foresaid city and castle to pay tribute unto they but when the tartar come upon they the multitude of the comanian enter into the foresaid province and flee all of they even unto the sea shore be in such extreme famine that they which be alive be constrain to eat up those which be dead and as a merchant report unto i who see it with his own eye that the live man devour and tear with their tooth the raw flesh of the dead as dog will gnaw upon carrion towards the border of the say province there be many great lake upon the bank whereof be salt-pit or fountain the water of which so soon as it enter into the lake become hard salt like unto ice and out of those salt-pit baatu and Sartach have great revenue for they repair thither out of all Russia for salt and for each cart load they give two web of Cotton amount to the value of half a Yperpera there come by sea also many ship for salt which pay tribute every one of they according to their burden the three day after we be depart out of the precinct of Soldaia we find the tartar among who be enter i think I be come into a new World the tartar who life and manner I will descrbe unto your highness as well as I can they have in no place any settle city to abide in neither know they of the celestial city to come they have divide all Scythia among themselves chap. 2. of the tartar and of their house which stretch from the river Danubius even unto the rise of the sun and every of their captain according to the great or small number of his people know the bound of his pasture and where he ought to feed his cattle winter and summer spring and autumn for in the winter they descend unto the warm region southward and in the summer they ascend unto the cold region northward in winter when snow lie upon the ground they feed their cattle upon pasture without water because than they use snow in stead of water their house wherein they sleep they ground upon a round foundation of Wickers artificial wrought and compact together the roof whereof consist in like sort of Wickers meet above into one little roundel out of which roundel ascend upward a neck like unto a chimney which they cover with white felt and oftentimes they lay mortar or white earth upon the say felt with the powder of bone that it may shine white and sometime also they cover it with black felt. the say feel on the neck of their house they do garnish over with beautiful variety of picture before the door likewise they hang a feel curious paint over for they spend all their colour felt in paint vine tree bird and beast thereupon the say house they make so large that they contain thirty foot in breadth for measure once the breadth between the wheele-ruts of one of their cart I find it to be twenty foot over and when the house be upon the cart it stretch over the wheel on each side five foot at the least I tell two and twenty ox in one team draw a house upon a cart eleven in one order according to the breadth of the cart and eleven more before they the axletree of the cart be of a huge bigness like unto the mast of a Ship and a fellow stand in the door of the house upon the forestall of the cart drive forth the oxen. moreover they make certain four square basket of small slender Wickers as big as great chest and afterward from one side to another they frame a hollow lid or cover of such like Wickers and make a door in the fore-side thereof and then they cover the say chest or little house with black felt ub over with tallow or sheep milk to keep the rain from soak through which they deck likewise with paint or with feather and in such chest they put their whole householdstuff and treasure also the same chest they do strong bind upon other cart which be draw with camel to the end they may wade through river neither do they at any time take down the say chest from off their cart when they take down their dwell house they turn the door always to the south and next of all they place the cart lade with their chest here and there within half a stone cast of the house insomuch that the house stand between two rank of cart as it be between two wall the matron make for themselves most beautiful cart which I be not able to describe unto your majesty but by picture only the benefit of a painter in strange country for I will right willing have paint all thing for you have my skill be aught in that Art one rich moal or Tartar have two hundred or one hundred such cart with chest duke have sixteen wife every one of which have one great house beside other little house which they place behind the great one be as it be chamber for their maiden to dwell in and unto every of the say house do belong two hundred cart when they take their house from off the cart the principal wife place her court on the west frontier and so all the rest in their order so that the last wife dwell upon the east frontier and one of the say lady court be distant from another about a stone cast whereupon the court of one rich moal or Tartar will appear like unto a great village very few man abide in the same one woman will guide twenty or thirty cart at once for their country be very plain and they bind the cart with camel or ox one behind another and there sit a wench in the fore-most cart drive the ox and all the residue follow on a like pace when they chance to come at any bad passage they let they loose and guide they over one by one for they go a slow pace as fast as a lamb or a ox can walk chap. 3. of their Bed^ puppet image and drink pot have take down their house from off their cart and turn the door southward they place the bed of the master of the house at the north part thereof the woman place be always on the east-side namely on the left hand of the good man of the house sit upon his bed with his face southward but the man place be upon the westside namely at the right hand of their master man when they enter into the house will not in any case hang their quiver on the woman side over the master head there be always a image like a puppet make of Fealt which they call the master brother and another over the head of the good wife or mistress which they call her brother be fasten to the wall and above between both of they there be a little lean one which be as it be the keeper of the whole house the good wife or mistress of the house place aloft at her bed foot on the right hand the skin of a kid stuff with wool or some other matter and near unto that a little image or puppet look towards the maiden and woman next unto the door also on the woman side there be another image with a cow udder for the woman that milk the kine for it be the duty of their woman to milk cow on the other side of the door next unto the man there be another image with the udder of a mare for the man which milk mare and when they come together to drink and make merry they sprinkle part of their drink upon the image which be above the master head idol afterward upon other image in order then go a servant out of the house with a cup full of drink sprinkle it thrice towards the south and bow his knee at every time and this be do for the honour of the fire then perform he the like superstitious idolatry towards the east for the honour of the air and then to the west for the honour of the water and last to the north in the behalf of the dead when the master hold a cup in his hand to drink before he taste thereof he pour his part upon the ground if he drink sit on horseback he pour out part thereof upon the neck or mane of his horse before he himself drink after the servant aforesaid have so discharge his cup to the four quarter of the world he return into the house and two other servant stand ready with two cup and two bason to carry drink unto their master and his wife sit together upon a bed and if he have more wife than one she with who he sleep the night before sit by his side the day follow and all his other wife must that day resort unto the same house to drink and there be the court hold for that day the gift also which be present that day be lay up in the chest of the say wife and upon a bench stand a vessel of milk or of other drink and drink cup in winter time they make excellent drink of rice of mill and of honey be well and high colour like wine chap. 4. of their drink and how they provoke one another to drink also they have wine bring unto they from far country in summer time they care not for any drink but and it stand always within the entrance of his door and next unto it stand a minstrel with his fiddle I see there no such Citernes and vial as we common be but many other musical instrument which be not use among we and when the master of the house begin to drink one of his servant cry out with a loud voice ha and the minstrel play upon his fiddle and when they make any great solemn feast they all of they clap their hand and dance to the noise of music the man before their master and the woman before their mistress and when the master have drink they use the like custom in Florida then cry out his servant as before and the minstrel stay his music then drink they all round both man and woman and sometime they carouse for the victory very filthy and drunken also when they will provoke any man they pull he by the ear to the drink and so lug and draw he strong to stretch out his throat clap their hand and dance before he moreover when some of they will make great feast and rejoice one of the company take a full cup and two other stand one on his right hand and another on his left and so they three come sing to the man who be to have the cup reach unto he still sing and dance before he and when he stretch forth his hand to receive the cup they leap sudden back return again as they do before and so have delude he thrice or four time by draw back the cup until he be merry and have get a good appetite than they give he the cup sing and dance and stamp with their foot until he have do drink concern their food and victual be it know unto your highness that they do chap. 5. of their food and victual without all difference or conception eat all their dead carrion and among so many drove it can be but some cattle must needs die howbeit in summer so long as their that be their mare milk last they care not for any food and if they chance to have a ox or a horse die they dry and flesh thereof for cut it into thin slice dry of flesh in the wind and hang it up against the sun and the wind it be present dry without salt and also without stench or corruption they make better pudding of their horse then of their hog which they eat be new make the rest of the flesh they reserve until winter they make of their ox skin great bladder or bag which they do wonderful dry in the smoke of the hinder part of their horsehide they make very fine sandal and pantofle they give unto fifty of a hundred man the flesh of one ram to eat for they mince it in a bowl with salt and water other sauce they have none and then with the point of a knife or a little fork which they make for the same purpose such as we use to take roast pear and apple out of wine withal they reach unto every one of the company a morsel or twain according to the multitude of guest the master of the house before the ram flesh be distribute first of all himself take thereof what he please also if he give unto any of the company a special part the receiver thereof must eat it alone and must not impart aught thereof unto any other not be able to eat it up all he carry it with he and deliver it unto his boy if he be present to keep it if not he put it up into his saptargat that be to say his four square budget which they use to carry about with they for the save of all such provision and wherein they lie up their bone when they have not time to gnaw they thorough that they may burnish they afterward to the end that no whit of their food may come to nought their drink call which be mare milk be prepare after this manner they fasten a long line unto two post stand firm in the ground chap. 6. how they make their drink call and unto the same line they tie the young foal of those mare which they mean to milk then come the dam to stand by their foal gentle suffer themselves to be milk and if any of they be too unruly than one take her foal and put it under she let it suck a while and present carry it away again there come another man to milk the say mare and have get a good quantity of this milk together be as sweet as cow milk while it be new they pour into a great bladder or bag and they beat the say bag with a piece of wood make for the purpose have a club at the low end like a man head which be hollow within and so soon as they beat upon it it begin to boil like new wine and to be sour and sharp of taste and they beat it in that manner till butter come thereof then taste they thereof and be indifferent sharp they drink it for it bite a man tongue like the wine of Raspes when it be drink after a man have take a draught thereof it leave behind it a taste like the taste of almond-milk and go down very pleasant intoxicate weak brain also it cause urine to be avoid in great measure likewise Caracosmos that be to say black Caracosmos for great lord to drink they make on this manner first they beat the say milk so long till the thick part thereof descend right down to the bottom like the lees of white wine and that which be thin and pure remain above be like unto whey or white must. the say lees and dregs be very white be give to servant and will cause they to sleep exceed that which be thin and clear their master drink and in very deed it be marvelous sweet and wholesome liquor duke have thirty cottage or grange duke within a day journey of his abide place every one of which serve he daily with the Caracosmos of a hundred mare milk store of mare and mare milk and so all of they together every day with the milk of three thousand mare beside white milk which other of his subject bring for even as the husbandman of Syria bestow the three part of their fruit and carry it unto the court of their lord even so do they their mare milk every three day out of their cow milk they first churn butter boil the which butter unto a perfect decoction they put it into ram skin which they reserve for the same purpose neither do they salt their butter and yet by reason of the long seethe it putrefy not and they keep it in store for winter the churnmilke which remain of the butter they let alone till it be as sour as possible it may be than they boil it and in boil it be turn all into curd which curd they dry in the sun make they as hard as the dross of iron and this kind of food also they store up in satchel against winter in the winter season when milk fail they they put the foresay curd which they all gry-ut into a bladder and pour hot water thereinto they beat it lusty till they have resolve it into the say water which be thereby make exceed sour and that they drink in stead of milk they be very scrupulous and take diligent heed that they drink not fair water by itself great lord have cottage or grange towards the south from whence their tenant bring they millet and meal against winter chap. 7. of the beast which they eat of their garment and of their manner of hunt the poor sort provide themselves of such necessary for the exchange of ram and of other beast skin the tartar slave fill their belly with thick water and be therewithal content they will neither eat mouse with long tail nor any kind of mouse with short tail they have also certain little beast call by they Sogur which he in a cave twenty or thirty of they together all the whole winter sleep there for the space of six month and these they take in great abundance there be also a kind of coney have long tail like unto cat and on the outside of their tail grow black and white hair they have many other small beast good to eat which they know and discern right well I see no deer there and but a few hare but a great number of roe I see wild ass in great abundance which be like unto mule also I see another kind of beast call artak our falconer use the left fist another strange custom which I leave to be scan by falconer themselves have in all resemblance the body of a ram and crooked horn which be of such bigness that I can scarce lift up a pair of they with one hand and of these horn they make great drink cup they have falcon girfaulcon and other hawk in great plenty all which they carry upon their right hand and they put always about their falcon neck a string of leather which hang down to the midst of their gorge by the which string when they cast they off the fist at the game with their left hand they bow down the head and breast of the say hawk lest they shall be toss up and down and beat with the wind or lest they shall soar too high wherefore they get a great part of their victual by hunt and hawk concern their garment and attire be it know unto your majesty that out of Cataya and other region of the east out of Persia also and other country of to south there be bring unto they stuff of silk cloth of gold and Cotton cloth which they wear in time of summer but out of Russia Moxell Bulgaria the great and pascatir that be Hungaria the great and out of Kersis all which be northern region and full of wood and also out of many other country of the north which be subject unto they the inhabitant bring they rich and costly skin of diverse sort which I never see in our country wherewithal they be clad in winter and always against winter they make themselves two gown one with the fur inward to their skin and another with the fur outward to defend they from wind and snow which for the most part be make of wolf skin or fox skin or else of papion and when they sit within the house they have a fine gown to wear the poor sort make their upper gown of dog or of goat skin when they go to hunt for wild beast there meet a great company of they together and environ the place round about where they be sure to find some game by little and little they approach on all side till they have get the wild beast into the midst as it be into a circle and then they discharge their arrow at they also they make themselves breeches of skin the rich tartar sometime fur their gown with pelluce or silk shag which be exceed soft light and warm the poor sort do line their clothes with Cotton cloth which be make of the fine wool they can pick out and of the courser part of the say wool they make feel to cover their house and their chist and for their bedding also of the same wool be mix with one three part of horse hair they make all their cordage they make also of the say feel cover for their stool great expense of wool and cap to defend their head from the weather for all which purpose they spend a great quantity of their wool and thus much concern the attire of the man the man shave a plot four square upon the crown of their head and from the two foremost corner they shave chap. 8. of the fashion which the tartar use in cut their hair and of the attire of their woman as it be two seam down to their temple they shave also their temple and the hinder part of their head even unto the nape of the neck likewise they shave the forepart of their scalp down to their forehead and upon their forehead they leave a lock of hair reach down unto their eyebrow upon the two hindermost corner of their head they have two lock also which they twine and braid into knot and so bind and knit they under each ear one moreover their woman garment differ not from their man save that they be somewhat long but on the morrow after one of their woman be marry she shave her scalp from the midst of her head down to her forehead and wear a wide garment like unto the hood of a nun yea large and long in all part then a nun hood be open before and gird unto they under the right side for herein do the tartar differ from the turk because the turk fasten their garment to their body on the left side but the tartar always on the right side they have also a ornament for their head which they call botta be make of the bark of a tree or of some such other light matter as they can find which by reason of the thickness and roundness thereof can be hold but in both hand together and it have a square sharp spire rise from the top thereof be more than a in length and fashion like unto a pinnacle the say botta they cover all over with a piece of rich silk and it be hollow within and upon the midst of the say spire or square top they put a bunch of quill or of slender cane a long and more and the say bunch on the top thereof they beautify with peacock feather and round about all the length thereof with the feather of a malards tail and with precious stone also great lady wear this kind of ornament upon their head bind it strong with a certain hat or coif which have a hole in the crown fit for the spire to come through it and under the foresay ornament they cover the hair of their head which they gather up round together from the hinder part thereof to the crown and so lap they up in a knot or bundle within the say botta which afterward they bind strong under their throat hereupon when a great company of such gentlewoman ride together and be behold a far off they seem to be soldier with helmet on their head carry their lance upright for the say botta appear like a helmet with a lance over it all their woman sit on horseback bestride their horse like man and they bind their hood or gown about their waste with a sky-coloured silk scarf and with another scarf they gird it above their breast and they bind also a piece of white silk like a muffler or mask under their eye reach down unto their breast these gentlewoman be exceed fat and the lesser their nose be the fair they be esteem they daub over their sweet face with grease too shameful and they never lie in bed for their travel of childbirth the duty of woman be to drive cart to lay their house upon cart chap. 9 of the duty enjoin unto the tartarian woman and of their labour and also of their marriage and to take they down again to milk cow to make butter and gry-ut to dress skin and to sew they which they usual sew with thread make of sinew for they divide sinew in slender thread and then twine they into one long thread they make sandal and sock and other garment howbeit they never wash any apparel for they lay that God be then angry and that dreadful thunder will ensue if wash garment be hang forth to dry yea they beat such as wash and take their garment from they they be wonderful afraid of thunder for in the time of thunder they thrust all stranger out of their house and then wrap themselves in black felt they lie hide therein till the thunder be overpass they never wash their dish or bowl yea when their flesh be sodden they wash the platter wherein it must be put with scald hot broth out of the pot and then pour the say broth into the pot again they make feel also and cover their house therewith the duty of the man be to make bow and arrow stirrup bridle and saddle to build house and cart to keep horse to milk mare to churn and mare milk and to make bag wherein to put it they keep camel also and lay burden upon they as for sheep and goat they tend and milk they as well the man as the woman with sheep milk thicked and salt they dress and tan their hide when they will wash their hand or their head they fill their mouth full of water and spout it into their hand by little and little they sprinkle their hair and wash their head therewith as touch marriage your highness be to understand that no man can have a wife among they till he have buy she whereupon sometime their maid be very stale before they be marry for their parent always keep they till they can sell they they keep the first and second degree of consanguinity inviolable as we do but they have no regard of the degree of affinity for they will marry together or by succession two sister their widow marry not at all for this reason because they believe that all who have serve they in this life shall do they service in the life to come also whereupon they be persuade that every widow after death shall return unto she own husband and here-hence arise a abominable and filthy custom among they namely that the son marry sometime all his father wife except his own mother for the court or house of the father or mother fall by inheritance always to the young son whereupon he be to provide for all his father wife because they be part of his inheritance as well as his father possession and then if he will he use they for his own wife for he think it no insurie or disparagement unto himself although they return unto his father after death therefore when any man have bargain with another for a maid the father of the say damsel make he a feast in the mean while she flee unto some of her kinsfolk to hide herself then say her father unto the bridegroom loe my daughter be you take she wheresoever you can find she then he and his friend seek for she till they can find she and have find she he must take she by force and carry she as it be violent unto his own house concern their law or their execution of justice your majesty be to be advertise chap. 10. of their execution of justice and judgement and of their death and burial that when two man fight no three man dare intrude himself to part they yea the father dare not help his own son but he that go by the worst must appeal unto the court of his Lord and whosoever else offer he any violence after appeal be put to death but he must go present without all delay and he that have suffer the injury carry he as it be captive they punish no man with sentence of death unless he be take in the deed do or confess the same but be accuse by the multitude they put he unto extreme torture to make he confess the truth they punish murder with death and carnal copulation also with any other beside his own by his own I mean his wife or his maid servant for he may use his slave as he list himself heinous theft also or felony they punish with death for a light theft as namely for steal of a ram the party not be apprehend in the deed do but otherwise detect be cruel beat and if the executioner lay on a hundred stroke he must have a hundred staff namely for such as be beat upon sentence give in the Court also counterfeit messenger because they feign themselves to be messenger when as indeed they be none at all they punish with death sacrilegious person they use in like manner of which kind of malefactor your majesty shall understand more full hereafter because they esteem such to be witch when any man die they lament and howl most pitiful for he and the say mourner be free from pay any tribute for one whole year after also whosoever be present at the house where any one grow to man estate lie dead he must not enter into the court of mangu-can till one whole year be expire if it be a child decease he must not enter into the say court sepulchre be unknown and always about those place where they inter their noble there be one house of man to keep the sepulcher I can not learn that they use to hide treasure in the grave of their dead sepulcher the comanian build a great tomb over their dead and erect the image of the dead party thereupon with his face towards the east hold a drink cup in his hand before his navel they erect also upon the monument of rich man pyramid that be to say little sharp house or pinnacle and in some place I see mighty tower make of brick in other place pyramid make of stone albeit there be no stone to be find thereabouts I see one new bury in who behalf they hang up sixteen horse-hides unto each quarter of the world four between certain high post and they set beside his grave for he to drink and flesh to eat and yet they say that he be baptize I behold other kind of sepulcher also towards the east namely large floor or pavement make of stone some round and some square and then four long stone pitch upright about the say pavement towards the four region of the world when any man be sick he lie in his bed and cause a sign to be set upon his house to signify that there lie a sick person there to the end that no man may enter into the say house whereupon none at all visit any sick party but his servant only moreover when any one be sick in their great court they appoint watchman to stand round about the say court who will not suffer any person to enter within the precinct thereof for they fear least evil spirit or wind shall come together with the party that enter in they esteem of soothsayer as of their priest chap. 11. of our first entrance among the tartar and of their ingratitude and be come among those barbarous people i think as I say before that I be enter into a new world for they come flock about we on horseback after they have make we a long time to await for they sit in the shadow under their black cart the first question which they demand be whether we have ever be with they heretofore or no and give they answer that we have not they begin impudent to beg our victual from we and we give they some of our biscuit and wine which we have bring with we from the town of Soldaia and have drink off one flagon of our wine they demand another say that a man go not into the house with one foot howbeit we give they no more excuse ourselves that we have but a little then they ask we whence we come and whither we be bind I answer they with the word above mention that we have hear concern duke Sartach that he be become a Christian and that unto he our determination be to travel duke Sartach have your majesty letter to deliver unto he they be very inquisitive to know whether I come of my own accord or whither I be send I answer that no man compel i to come neither have I come unless I myself have be willing and that therefore I be come according to my own will and to the will of my superior I take diligent heed never to say that I be your majesty ambassador then they ask what I have in my cart whether it be gold or silver or rich garment to carry unto Sartach I answer that Sartach shall see what we have bring when we be once come unto he and that they have nothing to do to ask such question but rather ought to conduct i unto their captain and that he if he think good shall cause i to be direct unto Sartach if not that I will return they be satisfy give we horse and ox and two man to conduct we howbeit before they will allow we the foresay necessary for our journey they make we to await a long while beg our bread for their young brat wonder at all thing which they see about our servant as their knife glove purse and point and desire to have they I excuse myself that we have a long way to travel and that we must in no wise so very importunate and shameless and if a man bestow aught upon they it be but cost lose for they be thankless wretch they esteem themselves lord and think that nothing shall be deny they by any man if lade with house and i think that a mighty city come to meet i chap. 12. of the court of Scacatai and how the christian drink no I wonder also at the great multitude of huge drove of ox and horse and funeral astrologer in celebrate the funeral of such as be of esteem the dead body be burn after this manner the kindred send for the astrologer and tell they what year month day and hour he who die be bear who perceive the constellation declare the day when he be to be burn so that when the planet fit not they reserve the dead body sometime seven day and sometime six month prepare a chest for it at home and join the side together with such cunning art that no stink can issue forth they also embalm the body itself with spice and cover the chest fair paint with a costly cloth and every day that the dead corpse be keep at home at the hour of dinner a table be prepare near the chest set wine and meat thereon for the space while one may well eat a meales-meat suppose that the soul of the dead feed of the savour thereof the astrologer sometime forbid to carry it forth at the chief gate pretend some disastrous star thereto and cause they to carry it out another way and sometime break the wall which be opposite to that place which the planet make more lucky for otherwise the spirit depart will be offend and hurt those of the house and if any such evil happen they ascribe it to the dead thus wrong when the body be carry through the city to be burn without wooden cottage be erect in the way with a porch cover with silk in which they set the body and set before it bread wine and flesh and delicate cate suppose the spirit to be refresh therewith which must be present present at the burn of the body and when they come unto the place of burn they write and paint upon paper make of the bark of tree the image of man and woman horse camel money and garment all the instrument of the city meanwhile resound all which be burn together with the dead body for they say that that dead man Rubr. of the original of the dominion of the tartar strong rampire with earth for they want stone near it be a great castle and in it the governor fair palace this be the first place near which in old time the tartar assemble themselves and now we will declare how they begin to reign they dwell in the north part to wit in Ciorza and Bargu where be many and great plain without city and town but goodly pasture river and water they have not a prince of their nation but pay tribute to a certain great king name as I have hear in their language Vmcan which in some man opinion in our tongue signify presbyter or priest John to he the tartar give yearly the ten of all their beast in process of time the tartar so increase in multitude that Vmcan be afraid of they and think to disperse they into several part of the world and therefore when any rebel he send three or four of a hundred of the tartar into those part so diminish their power and the like he do in his other occasion depute some of their principal to that purpose they see their ruin intend and loath to be separate one from another go from the place where they dwell to the desert towards the north where by remoteness they may be safe and deny to vmcan their wont tribute it happen that about an. 1162. the tartar have continue some time in those part choose a king among themselves a wise and valiant man name can. he begin to reign with such justice that he be belove and fear of all as a god rather than a prince insomuch that his fame bring all the tartar in all part to his subjection and he see himself lord of so valiant man will needs leave those desert and command they to provide bow and other weapon begin to subdue city and province in which conquest he place such just governor that the people be not offend the chief of they he carry alongst with he with great provision and gift see therefore that he be advance to so great glory the fruit of a wild government and power he send ambassador politikly to vmcan to entreat that he will bestow his daughter upon he to be his wife which he take in very evil part answer with indignation and reject the ambassador of Cingis say do my servant demand my daughter get you out of my sight and tell your master if he ever make such demand again I will make he die a miserable death but king Cingis levy a great army go forth with a hostile mind Cingis go forrh against Vmcan Tanduc he consult with the magician and encamp in a certain great plain name Tanduc send unto the king and signify unto he that he shall defend himself but he come with a mighty army descend to the plain and pitch his tent within ten mile of the camp of the tartar then Cingis command his astrologer to show he what event and success the battle shall have they cut a reed lengthwise in two part set the piece themselves into the ground and write upon the one Cingis and on the other Vmcan and say unto the king in the mean space while we read the conjuration it shall come to pass by the idol power that these two part of the reed shall fight together and who part shall ascend upon the other that king shall obtain victory in the battle the multitude therefore run together to behold that spectacle the astrologer begin to mumble their prayer and read their enchantment when present the part of the reed be move fight together until at length the part of Cingis ascend upon the part of Vmcan he vanquish the enemy by war which be see the tartar assure of the future victory be encourage to the battle and Vmcan be slay the victory and kingdom and vmcans daughter remain to Cingis Cingis reign six year a^ter this in the which he get many province and last when he endeavour to win a certain castle call thaigin and come somewhat near he die with the shot of a the foresay occasion the marriage of the tartar the tartarean woman be most faithful to their husband adultery be a great shame with they yet it be account lawful and honest that every one may marry as many wife as he be able to maintain although the first be judge to be more principal and honourable than the rest these live together in the same house without one ill word woman concord and industry in admirable concord make their merchandise buy and sell and chaffer all thing necessary to their husband and household the man meddle with nothing but their hunt hawk and thing pertain to arm they have the best falcon in the world and so they have of dog they live only of flesh and milk and what they take in hunt they eat horse camel dog if fat and drink mare milk call chemur so use that it be like white z z wine if the father die the son may have all his wife except his own mother and sister so the brother be dead it be lawful for the brother who remain alive to marry the widow of the brother the husband receive no dowry from the wife but they themselves assign dowry to the wife and their mother through the multitude of wife the tartar have many child nor be the multitude of wife very burdensome unto the tartar see they gain much through their labour beside they be very careful for the government of the family and preparation of food and with no less care execute the other duty of the house but the man apply themselves whole to hunt their substance of cattle fowl and exercise of arm the tartar nourish many herd of ox flock of sheep and other beast and cattle and abide with they in place of pasture in the summer time in the mountain and cold place where they find pasture and wood but in the winter they remove unto the hot country where they find pasture for their cattle cottage and go forthon two or three month together their house be cover with stick and felt ordinary round which they carry with they on cart or wagon of four wheel whither soever they go for they can fold and extend they set they up and take they down and they turn the door of they always to the south they have also neat cart of two wheel cover with felt so well that rain can pierce they draw by ox and camel wherein they carry their wife child and necessary householdstuff with they and defend they from the injury of foul weather and rain the tartar if they be rich be clothe with sable ermine and cloth of gold and all their furniture be costly their arm be bow sword pole-axe and some lance but they can best use their bow whereto they be use from their childhood they be hardy valorous cruel will continue two day and night on horseback arm exceed patient of difficulty and exceed obedient to their lord their cattle also be hardy the tartar religion the law and faith of the tartar be this they say that there be a great God high and heavenly of who with daily incense they desire good understanding and health they have another which they call Natigay which be like a image cover with felt or some other thing which every one have in his house to this god they make a wife and child place the wife image at the left hand and the representation of child before his face this they call the god of earthly thing which keep their child and their beast and corn and give it great reverence before they eat themselves they anoint the mouth of the image with the fat of the sodden flesh and they cast the broth out of door in honour of other spirit say that their god with his family have have their part and after they eat and drink at pleasure if the son of any tartar die who have not yet be marry and also the daughter of another die unmarried the parent of both the decease party meet together paint marriage and make a marriage between the dead and make a draughter in writing of that contract they paint man and woman for servant horse and other creature with clothes of all sort and money in paper and burn they together with the write of contract by the fume whereof they say that all these thing be carry to their child in another world where they be marry and the father and mother think they be join together through such a bond of affinity as if those marriage have be celebrate while the marry couple yet live when the tartar go to war their prince conduct about one hundred thousand horse their war-fare appoint head over ten hundred thousand ten thousand by which orderly subordination command be easy effect every hundred be call a Tuc ten a toman when they set forth they send out man every way as scout that no enemy may assault they unprovided of horse and mare there be for every man about eighteen they carry also their like feel house under the which they shelter themselves in the time of rayn^ when there fall out some important employment they will ride ten day together without victual boil and live of the blood of their horse cut a vein and suck it they have milk dry like paste which they make boil the milk and take the cream which swim on the top put it in another vessel and thereof make good after they set the milk in the sun and dry it and when they go in the army carry ten pound thereof and every morning take half a pound and put it into a little flask or bottle of leather with as much water as he please which while he ride beat together and this be his dinner when they encounter with their enemy they ride here and there shoot and sometime make show of flight shoot as they flee and find the enemy break redintegrate their force and pursue the victory have their horse at command with a sign to turn any way but now the tartar be mix in diverse part and so be their fashion they punish malefacter after this manner if any steal a thing of small value the mulct or penalty of nine fold the mark of the herd of cattle and have not deserve to be deprive of life he be seven time beat with a cudgel or seventeen or seven and twenty or thirty seven or forty and seven give the stroke according to the measure and quality of the offence and that unto a hundred some do often time die through these stroke but if any have steal a horse or another thing for the which he deserve to die he be cut asunder with a sword in the middle but if he will redeem his life he shall restore the theft nine fold such as have horse ox or camel brand they with their mark and send they to the pasture without a keeper leave the city of Carachoran behold this spectacle he take wonderful delight in the midst in a fair wood he have build a royal house on pillar gild and vernish a goodly house of pleasure on every of which be a dragon all gilt which wind his tail about the pillar with his head bear up the loft as also with his wing display on both side the cover also be of reed gild and varnish so that the rain can do it no injury the reed be three handful thick and ten yard long split from knot to knot the house itself also may be sunder and take down like a tent and erect again for it be sustain when it be set up with two hundred silken cord great Chan use to dwell there three month in the year a solemn sacrifice to wit in june july and August on the eight and twenty day of August he depart to make a solemn sacrifice he have a herd of white horse and white mare about ten thousand of the milk whereof none may drink except he be of the progeny of Cingis can except one family mare milk call Boriat privilege hereto by Cingis for their valour and these beast as they go up and down feed be much reverence nor dare any go before they or hinder their way the astrologer or sorcerer tell Chan that on the twenty eight of the moon of August he shall disperse that milk here and there for the honour of all spirit and his idol that they may be careful preserver of all those thing which he possess there be two sort of idolater sorcerer call Thebeth and Chesmir the king magician which in the midst of storm ascend the palace and suffer no rain to fall thereon which they make the people believe come to pass by their sanctity and therefore they go slovenly and regardless of their person never wash nor comb themselves they also have a horrible custom to dress and eat such as be condemn to death but not those which die natural they be call also Bachsi which be the name of their order as friar predicant or minor with we they seem by magic to do what they list when the great can in his hall sit at his table which be eight yard high and in the midst of the hall a good distance from the table be a great cupboard of plate furnish they cause that the piece full of wine or milk or other viand of themselves fill the goblet without any hand touch they and go ten pace in the air into the great can hand and when he have drink return to their place this they do in the presence of any man when their lord command these Bachsi also when they will make feast to their idol go to the can and say sir know that if our idol be not honour with sacrifice they will bring plague to corn and beast and therefore we pray you to give the flesh of so many sheep with black head and so many pound of incense and aloe that we may make they due sacrifice and honour this they speak not to he themselves but by certain lord depute to that office who speak to the can and obtain it on the feast day they sacrifice the say beast and sprinkle the broth before the idol they have great monastery some of the bigness of a city in some of which be about two thousand monk which serve idol sequester from the laity in their shave and garment for they shave their head and beard and be a religious garment shave these in the solemnity of their idol sing with solemn song and light some of they may marry there be some of great abstinence call lead a austere life for they eat nothing but meal mingle with water till all the flower be go and eat the bran without any savour these worship the fire and the man of other rule say that these which be so austere be heretic against their law because they worship not idol as they do austerity and there be great difference betwixt they and these marry not in any case they shave their head and beard they wear black hempen garment and bright yellow they sleep in thick mat and live the severe Naiam^ rebellion of the present can call Cublai can which be in our tongue lord of lord the great prince in people city and treasure that ever be in the world he be descend from the progeny of Chingis the first prince of the tartar be the six emperor of that country begin to reign in the year of our lord 1256. be twenty seven year old and rule the people with great wisdom and gravity he be a valiant man exercise in arm strong of body and of a prompt mind for the performance of matter before he attain to the dignity of the empire which by his wisdom he do against the will of his brethren he often show himself a valiant soldier in the war and carry himself like a wise and bold captain than ever the tartar have but since he sway the kingdom he go but once into the field but send his son and other captain in expedition in the year of our lord 1286. his uncle name Naiam be thirty year of age and have the command of many people and country so that he be able easy to bring together four hundred thousand horse be puff up through youthful vanity will now no long be subject but will needs take away the kingdom from his lord Cubai and send to another great lord name Caydu lord of the part towards great Turkey who be nephew of the emperor Cublai yet hate he who yield consent to rebellion promise to come in proper person with a hundred thousand horse both of they begin to gather force which can not be do so secret but Cublai hear of it and present take order to set guard to the way that no intelligence may pass that way and then assemble all the force within ten day journey of Cambalu with great speed so that in twenty day be gather together three hundred and sixty thousand horse and one hundred thousand foot a great part of they falconier and man of his household with these he make all haste day and night towards naiams country where at the end of twenty five d^yes he arrive altogether unlooked for and rest his man two day then he call his astrologer and cause they before all the army to divine who shall have victory a thing they always use to encourage their man and they promise it to Cublai one morning while Naiam be sleep negligent in his tent have not so much as send out any scout to espy Cublai make show of his army upon a hill to Naiams he himself sit in a certain castle of wood full of archer and crossbow man bear by four elephant on the top whereof be the royal standard with the image of the sun and moon he divide his army into three wing of which he send that on the right hand and the other on the left against naiams army to every ten thousand horse be assign five hundred foot with lance teach to leap up behind the horseman if any occasion of flight happen and sudden on advantage to light and slay the enemy horse with their lance Caidu be not yet come the battle join and make a cruel fight which continue from morning till noon and then be Naiam take and bring before Cublai who command that he shall be sew betwixt two carpet which shall be toss up and down till the breath be out of his body that so the imperial blood may not be expose to the sun and the air the remainder of his people swear obedience to Cublai which be four nation Ciorza Carli Barscol and Sitingui Naiam be secret baptize and by profession a Christian but no follower of the work of faith and sign his principal ensign with the sign of the cross have with he infinite store of christian which be all slay the jew and saracen that be in the army of Cublai begin to upbraid the christian with this disaster of the cross who thereupon complain to Cublai he then sharp reprove the jew and saracen turn to the christian say sure your god and his cross will not give any aid to Naiam but be not you therefore ashamed because God be good and just ought not at all to defend injustice and iniquity Naiam be a traitor to his lord and contrary to all equity raise rebellion and seek the help of your god in his mischievous purpose but he as a good and upright God will not favour his design he return after this with great triumph to Cambalu and stay there till easter on that day he call the christian before he and kiss their gospel and make his baron do the same the like he do in the great feast of saracen jew and that sogomamber can the god of the idol Mahumet Moses or whosoever be great in heaven may help he yet he make best show of like to the christian faith but pretend the ignorance of the professor and the mighty act of the sorcerer to his not profess it now for reward his soldier he have twelve baron or wise counselor which give he notice of each captain merit who raise they command of one hundred to a thousand and from one thousand to ten thousand and so forward give they vessel of plate and tablet the captain of one hundred have a tablet of silver and the captain of one thousand of gold or silver gild the captain of ten thousand have a tablet of gold with a lion head on it the weight of the tablet differ also according to the worth and weight of the dignity on the say tablet be write a command in this manner by the strength and power of the great God and by the grace which he have give to our empire the name of can be bless and let they all die and be destroy which will not obey he all they which have these tablet have privilege in writing of all thing which they be to do or demand and the general when they ride in public they have a cloth bear over their head and when they sit sit on a chair of silver their tablet be of three hundred Saggi fifty ounce of gold with the image of the sun and moon they who tablet have a Gerfalcon may take with they for their guard the whole army of a great commander Cublai^ person describe Cublai be a comeley and fair man of a mean stature of a red and white face black and goodly eye well fashion nose and all the lineament of his body consist of a due proportion he have four wife which he account lawful and the firstborn of they succeed he in the kingdom his wife and concubine and every one of these be call empress and hold a peculiar court and that princely in a proper palace have about three hundred choose handmaid and mayd-seruant and many eunuch servant and at least ten thousand person in their family the king have also many concubine vngut there be a certain nation of fair people tartar call vngut whether every second year he send ambassador to purvey the fair lass for he of great esteem for beauty which bring he four or five hundred more or less as they see cause there be praiser or examiner appoint which take view of all their beauty examine eye nose mouth etc. apart and set price on they at sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen twenty or more carat and they bring those of that rate which their commission appoint these he cause to other the green mountain two lake with a pretty river fill they store with fish and so grate that the fish can get forth the city of Cambalu in the province of Cathai seat on a great river be famous table how dainty and delicate they be and with what magnificence and pomp they be serve in the birth day of Cublai all the tartar observe this custom to celebrate the birth day of their lord most honourable the festival birth day of Cublai be keep the twenty eight of September new moon feast the present of the man of dignity subject unto he the like custom be still use by the mogul as also the new-year day the twelve baron the prayer of diverse religion and this day he account more solemn than any of the whole year except the first of February wherein they begin their year the king therefore in his birth day be clothe with a most precious garment of gold and about two thousand baron and soldier be clothe of the same colour of gold though of silk stuff and a girdle wrought with gold and silver which be give they with a pair of shoe some wear pearl and gem of great price namely the quiecitarie which be next to the can and these garment be not wear but on their thirteen solemn feast according to the thirreene moon of the year all then clothe like king this custom be also observe with the tartar that on the birth day of great cham all the king prince and noble which be subject to his dominion shall send present unto he as to their emperor and they who desire to obtain any place of dignity or office of he offer their request unto twelve baron appoint for this purpose and what they decree be all one as if the emperor himself have answer they all people also of what faith or sect soever whether christian or jew saracen or tartar and other pagan be bind solemn to call upon their god for the life safety and prosperity of great can. newyere day on the day of the kalend of February which be the begin of the tartar year great can and all the tartar wheresoever they be celebrate a very great and solemn feast and all aswell man as woman the white colour account ominous new-year gift desire to be clothe in white garment for they believe that the white garment be a token of good luck therefore that fortune may favour they all the year they wear white in the begin of the year moreover the ruler of city and governor of province mindful of their duty send unto their emperor on this day present of gold and silver pearl and precious stone many white clothes and other white thing and many horse of a white colour the rest of the tartar at the begin of the year bark or paper money it be incredible what multitude of people merchant and merchandise of all sort be see in Cambalu the money of the great can be not make of gold or silver or other metal but they take the middle bark from the mulberry tree and this they make firm and cut it into diverse and round piece great and little and imprint the king mark thereon of this matter therefore Cambalu the mint of money the emperor cause a huge mass of money to be make in the city of Cambalu which suffice for the whole empire and no man under pain of death may lawful coin any other or spend any other money or refuse it in all his kingdom and country nor any come from another kingdom dare spend any other money in the empire of great can. whereby it come to pass that merchant often come from far remote country and region unto the city of Cambalu bring with they gold silver pearl and precious stone and receive the king money for they and because this money be not receive in their country they change it again in the empire of great can for merchandise which they carry away with they he also pay stipend to his officer and army of the mention money and last whatsoever thing he need in his court he buy with this money wherefore there be not a king to be find in the world who exceed he in treasure not expend on the mint as elsewhere the great can have twelve baron as be say before which be his counsel of war and dispose of martial affair and the exalt or disgrace of captain and soldier their office be call Thai that be the high court because they have none above they but the can. other twelve baron be appoint counsellor for the four and thirty province which have a fair palace in Cambalu in which be for every province a judge and many notary these have power to choose governor of the say province and present their name to the can which confirm they these also have the charge of the treasure to exact and dispense the same their office be call singh that be the second court subject to none but the can yet repute less noble than the former that be a martial State @. 5 the can provision for ambassador and for post against dearth for highway for the poor in Cambalu for at their privilege but all the mention post be free from all exaction of tribute and receive a good recompense of their labour from the king rent gatherer beside some also be appoint to examine these to come that year which they sell to those that will buy they and such as speak most truth be most honour if any intend any great work or to go a far journey and will know the event beforehand he make recourse to these astrologer to see it with their eye in the heaven which they do compare the present constellation with that of his birth which they demand of he so foretell he the good or evil tartarian computation of time the tartar reckon the computation of their year by twelve the first signify by a lion the second by a ox the three by a dragon the four by a dog and so through the whole twelve so that if a man be demand when he be bear he will answer such a point of such a hour of such a day in the year lion this their father exact set down in a book and when the twelve be complete they go over the same again their religion of their religion we have say that they be idolater and for their god have a table set aloft in the wall of their chamber on which be write a name represent the high God of heaven and there every day with a censer of incense they adore it in this manner they lift up their hand aloft and strike their tooth thrice pray it to give they a good understanding and health and desire thereof nothing else beside on the ground they have another statue call Natigai the god of earthly thing with his wife and child as before be say who likewise they worship with incense strike * * or gnash the tooth and lift up the hand and desire thereof temperature of the air fruit of the earth child and the like they hold the soul to be immortal and that when a man die it enter into another body better or worse according to the merit in the former life opinion of the soul as of a poor man to become a gentleman and after of a prince or lord and so high till it be assumpt in God or if it have ill deserve to be a poor man after a dog always descend to the low rank of baseness they have a comely speech their custom salute cheerful and honest have a graceful carriage and feed clean they bear great reverence to their parent and if any be undutiful or helpless to their necessity there be a public office design to this particular to punish ungrateful or disobedient child prisoner be release at three year end and mark in the cheek to be know malefactor court reverence the baron and people which go to the grand can observe these rite first within half a mile of the place where the can be all be hush and quiet without noise or cry or any loud speech and every baron carry continual a little fair vessel to spit in after which he cover it none dare to leave the dance they consult with he that be possess for what cause that disease happen unto he and what be to be do for his recovery the devil answer by he because he have do this or that or because he have offend this or that god therefore he fall into this disease then the magician entreat that God to pardon he that offence promise that if the sick party recover he shall offer a sacrifice of his own blood but if the devil think the weak party to be sick of such a disease that he can be free from the same he use to answer this man have so grievous offend that God that he can by any sacrifice be appease but if he think he shall recover he command to offer so many ram have black head and to prepare so many magician with their wife by they to offer sacrifice and that God may then be appease towards he which be hear his kinsman quick cause those thing to be do which the devil command they kill ram and sprinkle their blood in the air and the magician assemble with their witch these thing the idol be appease if he answer no they present prepare themselves to fulfil another command of he but if he answer that he be satisfy they sit down at the table and eat the flesh offer to the idol with great joy and drink the confection and dinner be end and the magician pay every one return to his own home and when the sick have thus escape the disease through the providence of God other trade but this needlework and die of fooles-skinne amu. Amu be a easterly province subject to great can who inhabitant worship idol and have a peculiar language they abound with herd of cattle and have plenty of victual and many horse and those excellent which merchant bring into India they have also many buff and ox because there be delicate pasture there as well man as woman wear bracelet of gold and silver of great value on their arm also the like on their leg but those of the woman be of most value from Amu to Cangigu be five and twenty day journey Tholoman the province Tholoman be eight day journey distant to the east from Amu subject unto great can have a peculiar language and worship idol the man and woman thereof be tall and goodly of a brown colour the country be very well inhabit have many and strong castle and city the man be exercise in arm and accustom to war they burn the body of their dead and enclose the relic of their bone in a chest hide they in the cave of the mountain that they can be touch either of man or beast gold be in great plenty there and in stead of money they use Porcelanes bring from India as also in Cangigu and amu. from the province Tholoman the way lead towards the east on a river by which be many city and castle and at the end of twelve day you come to the great city the country be subject to great can and the inhabitant thereof be addict to idolatry excellent clothes be make in this country of the bark of tree cloth make of bark which be now use in congo great and hardy dog wherewith they be clothe in the summer very many lion be there so that for fear of they none dare sleep without door by night the ship which go up and down the river for fear of the lion be not fasten to the bank there be great dog in the same country so hardy and strong that they fear not to adventure on the lion and it often happen that two dog and one archer kill a lion for the dog set on by the man give the onset and the lion nature be present to seek shelter from some tree that the dog may not come behind he neither yet will his great heart suffer he to run from the dog lest he shall seem afraid but he hold his stately pace the man meanwhile shoot and the dog fasten on his hinder part but with such quickness that when the lion turn on they they be go and then do this magnanimous beast hold on his way again to seek such tree succour that with bite and arrow he sometime come short and with expense of blood die by the way this country abound with silk which by merchant be carry to diverse province by the river they live on merchandise their money be paper Sidinfu Pazanfu they be almesdeed so belove of his subject that thereby and by the strength of the country he seem invincible whereby it come to pass that the king aswell as the people lose the use and exercise of war and his beginning the largeness of the kingdom of cathay land the kingdom of cathay be the great that be to be find in the world and be replenish with people and infinite riches be situate on the shore of the ocean sea in the which there be so many land that their number can no way be know for never be there any man that can say he have see all those land but those of they which have be frequent be find to abound with innumerable wealth and treasure and that which be there most esteem oil of olive and dear sell be oil of olive which the king and commander there cause to be keep with great diligence as a sovereign medicinable thing and moreover in the kingdom of cathay be many marvelous and monstrous thing which I forbear to mention the inhabitant of those part be exceed wise and subtle replenish with all kind of skill and cunning insomuch that they disdain the endeavour of all other nation in all kind of art and science their arrogant presumption effeminate fearfulness say that they only see with two eye the latin but with one eye and that all other nation be blind and albeit they be exceed sharp-sighted in the exercise of all bodily work and labour yet be there not among they any knowledge of spiritual thing the man of that country be not bold or courageous but more fearful of death than befit such as bear arm yet be they very ingenious and have often have victory of their enemy by sea then by land the money use in those part be of square piece of paper sign with the king sign according to which sign or mark the piece be of great or small value and if they begin by age to be waste or wear out he that bring they to the king court shall have new for they of gold and other metal they make vessel and other ornament of this kingdom of cathay it be say that it be in the begin of the world see sir John mandevil travel because the head thereof be in the east and there be not know any other nation to inhabit more easterly thereabouts on the west it confine on the Hoccota can who succeed in the empire be a man of much valour and wisdom which make he very well belove of the tartarian who be always faithful and obedient unto he he therefore bethink himself in good work the kill of man they hold to be no sin but if they happen to leave their bridle in their horse-mouth when he shall feed they think therein they offend God mortal fornication and lechery be hold by they as no sin they marry many wife polygamy and the custom be that the son must marry his stepmother after the death of his father and the brother be marry to his brother wife after his decease in matter of arm they be very good and more obedient to their superior than other nation be and do easy know by certain sign in battle the will of their commander warfare whereby the army of tartarian be easy rule and command their lord bestow not any stipend on they but they live on hunt and such prey as they can get and their lord may take from they when he list whatsoever they have when the tartar ride upon any enterprise they take with they great store of horse drink their milk and feed on their flesh which they reckon very good food eat of horseflesh the tartar be very ready and excellent archer on horseback but on foot they be but slow they be dexterous and ingenious in take of city and castle and be for the most part victorious over their enemy yet will they not forbear to turn their back in the skirmish if it be for their advantage and this advantage they have in the field that they will fight with the enemy when they list themselves and yet they can be compel to fight but at their pleasure their manner of fight be very dangerous so that in one conflict or skirmish of the tartar there be more slay and wound then in any great battle of other nation which happen by reason of their arrow which they shoot strong and sure out of their bow be indeed so skilful in the art of shoot that they common pierce all kind of armour and if they happen to be rout yet they fly in troop and band so well order that it be very dangerous to follow or pursue they because they shoot their arrow backward in their flight wound and kill ofttimes both man and horse that pursue they the army of the tartar make no great show because they go troop close together so that a army of one thousand tartar will scarce seem five hundred their hospitality the tartarian do courteous entertain stranger give they part of their viand and expect the like offer to be make they for otherwise they will take it by violence they be much more skilful in conquer of country then in keep of they when they be weak they be humble and gentle stout and proud when they be grow the strong they can endure lie in other man yet themselves be much give to lie unless it be in two especial thing delight in lie the one be in matter of arm in which none dare affirm that he do any exploit which be not do by he or deny any fair act which he have commit the other be that whosoever have do any offence though it deserve death he confess it present to his lord if he be examine thereon this may suffice at this time concern the manner of the tartar because it be long to rehearse all the
