reins and spring almost always miry he show out of his bosom a picture of the plant bring out of the country which Ramusio in his preface to m. polo have also present with this discourse the description of which be this the leaf he say be ordinary two span long more or less as the plant be in bigness narrow below and broad above downy with as it be small hair in their circumference the stalk or trunk be green four finger high and sometime a span from the ground the green leaf with age grow yellow and spread on the ground in the midst of the trunk grow a thin branch with flower fasten within like the Mamole violet in form but of the colour of milk and azure and great than those violet of a noisome send the root within ground be a span or two long of a tawny colour in the bark some as big as a man thigh or leg the root and juice and prepare out of which grow little root or sprig which spread in the ground and be cut away from the great root which within be yellow with many vein of fair red full of red and yellow juice clean to the finger and make the hand yellow and be cut in piece the viscous juice issue out and the root become light they lay they therefore on board turn they up and down diverse time a day that the juice shall incorporate therein lest it lose the goodness after four or six day hang they to dry in the wind where the sun may not come at they be in two month dry and perfect they ordinary take it out of the ground in the winter a cold climate the virtue be then most unite in the root the spring there beginning at the end of May which at other time be disperse into the leaf and flower that juice also be go and the root light and hollow six Saggi make a ounce they sell one of their cart load of root with leaf for sixteen silver Saggi not much unlike we for they have no coin but make their gold and silver in small thin rod and thence cut piece of a Saggio weight which in silver be twenty Soldi venetian and in gold a ducat and half that all be deceit of the simple laiety which of light matter be move to presume of the people that which be not in they and beside this I find many hindrance for the obtain of my desire and intent king of Camboia a Bramene for first the king be a Bramene and the Bramenes be his principal man and his favourite and most familiar because they be witch for they be much give to be please with witchcraft and they do nothing without consult the witch and Bramenes that be in the kingdom for by this mean they thrive by the devil and so the first thing that the king ask i be if I be a witch Probar the Bramenes do worship among other one God which they call Probar missur which they say make the heaven and the earth Pralocussur and another god which they call Pralocussar this also have obtain power of another which they call Praissur for to give this licence to Probar missur and I show they that not only he have not make the heaven and the earth but that he have be a very wicked man and a great sinner wherefore these priest say that they will worship he no more have worship he thitherto with their God whereupon the hatred of the Bramenes increase towards i and from thence forward I have disfavour of the king which be move for the zeal of his god and the god of his Bramenes there meet about these matter the priest of the idol and all of their troop which go for priest and hold themselves for religious man and in their conversation and life they be separate from all other people which to my think be the three part of the people of the land the king thereof set a hundred thousand man in the field this religious people or that hold itself for such be exceed proud and vain and alive they be worship for god man alive worship in sort that the inferior among they do worship the superior like god pray unto they and prostrate themselves before they and so the common people have a great confidence in they with a great reverence and worship in sort that there be no person that dare contradict they in any thing and their word among they be hold for so sacred that in no wise they will endure to be gainsay insomuch that it happen sometime while I be preach many round about i hear i very well and satisfy themselves of that which I say unto they if there come any of these priest and say this be good but we be better they will all depart and leave i alone further they be very ignorant presume to be very wise and the common people do hold they for such all their knowledge be ignorance and heathenish folly they make seven and twenty heaven some where there be meat and drink and fair woman whether they say all live thing do go even the flea and the louse for they say twenty seven heaven that as they have soul that they must live in the other World and to these they say all do go that be not religious man as they be they place other high whether they say their holy priest do go that live in the wilderness and all the felicity they give they there be to sit refresh themselves with the wind they place other yet high the god of the which they say have round body like bowl those which go to these heaven and the honour they give they be to sin of every one either high or low they have a division of their religious man for some they call massancrache massanchrache nassendeche mitire which be as supreme which sit above the king other they these be the continual war of the chinas and as I have say the chinas have a hundred league other say there be more of a wall between they and the other wall of China where be continual garrison of Cantan describe the public and private building and government the ship and husbandry of China their contempt of the idle and provision for impotent poor be to entreat of the city of Cantan I give first a warning to the reader that among many noble city Cantan be one less noble than many of China and far inferior in build then many other although it be more populous than many this be say by all they that see it and travel within the land where they see many other this advice presuppose it be to be note that Cantan in his compass be of very strong wall very well make and of a good height and to the sight they seem almost new be eighteen hundred year since they be make the wall of Cantan as the chinas do affirm they be very clean without any cleft hole or rift or any thing threaten ruin they be of free stone about a man height and from thence upward of brick make of a clay like unto that of the porcelain dish whence it cause they to be so strong that I build a chapel in malaca one of these which be bring from China can scarce be break with a good pickax joint with this there be in this city and in all the rest a officer of the king which only have care to oversee the wall for the which he have a good stipend and every year when the governor of the border come to visit the province he do visit this as well as the other officer to know if he do well his office and find he in any fault or negligence he be put from his office and punish and if he stand in need of any expense for the mend of the wall the overseer of the rent be bind to give he that which be necessary under pain that if the mend remain undo he shall be well punish for this cause the wall of all the city be continual keep sound and in good reparation these wall be within the city little more than the walk of the same city in their height which be the cause of be much more cool the wall have in compass 12350. pace and it have eighty three bulwark this city and so all the rest have on the one side the river along the which as well this as the rest be build almost in a valley the river and town-ditch and on the other side they have a ditch full of water of a good breadth between the which and the wall remain a good distance where there may run together a good troop of people and the earth that be take out of the ditch be cast between it and the wall whereby the foot of the wall remain a great deal high than the other ground beside the ditch notwithstanding this wall have a great blemish for it have on the contrary side to the river without the wall and the ditch a little hillock that discover all the city within the wall this wall have seven gate the entry of the which be sumptuous and high the gate strong and well make with pinnacle above not square but make like step the other place of the wall have no pinnacle the wall at the enter of the gate be twelve pace thick the gate be all over plate with iron and all of they have their draw-bridge very strong draw-bridge which be always up and be never let down but be ready against they be needful all the gate at the enter have court and the court that be towards the side of the suburb which lie along the river have every one three gate one in the front and two on the side gate-courts which remain for the service of street that lie along the wall the wall of the court be almost of the height of they within the gate which be in the front in the court be like unto that of the wall within it have also a drawbridge the gate which be in the side of the court be small the court that be on the other-side of the field where no suburb be have no more but one gate and this not right against that of the wall but stand on the one side the street of the city be all draw by a line very straight without any manner of make a nook or wind all the cross way be as straight as the street straight street and pave in sort that there be neither street nor traverse that make any turn all the street and traverse be very well pave the pavement go along the house and low in the midst for the course of water the principal street have triumphant arch which do cross they high and very well make which make the street very beautiful and ennoble the city the principal street have along the house close portal in the which and under the arch many thing be sold. the house of they which rule the country be at the enter very sumptuous house of magistrate with high portal great and well wrought of mason work they have in the forefront very great gate like the gate of a city with two giant paint with club in their hand I see four in one pagode which be a temple of idol draw natural from some which they say the king have to keep his weak passage from Tartary they be of great member of about twelve or thirteen span high on the street and other that be as honourable or more than they at the one side of this principal gate be another very great gate but not so big as the principal which be for the service of the house and of the prisoner when the principal gate be shut and when this principal gate be shut they set a glue paper cross over both the leaf on which be write the name or firm of the principal of the house and for to open it again a officer of the house bring the same firm or mark on a playstered board to the porter that he may open it without the which token he may not open it under a great punishment enter by the house when they enter in at the gate they must go present to one side go down to the court which have very great tree for shadow and they go up again by step unto the table abovesaid which be at common people in the outward show be not common very fair but within be much to be admire private house for common they be white as milk that they seem like sleeked paper they be pave with square there be great store of timber and very cheap and much iron and cheap and it be very good there be infinite number of ship and ship store of ship for through the country be infinite grove of fir tree stand in need for to fight and there be no small town along the river that be not plentiful in small and great ship along the city of Cantan more than half a league off the river be so great a multitude of ship that it be a wonderful thing to see they and that which be most to wonder be that that this multitude never decrease nor fail almost all the year for if thirty forty or a hundred go forth one day as many do come in again the next I say the multitude never to diminish nor fail for though sometime there be more some less always there remain a marvelous multitude and that which be more all those that go forth go lade and all that come in come lade carry good and bring good and that which show much the nobleness of the country the plenty and riches thereof be that all these ship bring great store of merchandise of clothes silk provision and other good some do go into the land other come from within the land and nothing come form without China neither go out of it riches of China in itself and that which the portugal do carry and some that they of Syam do carry be so little in comparison of the great traffic of the country that it almost remain as nothing and unperceived see that out of China there go no more but that which the portugal and they of Syam do carry which be as much as though they bring nothing out of China five or six ship come lade with silk and porcelain the great plenty and riches of the country do this that it can sustain itself alone pepper and ivory which be the principal that the portugal do carry a man may well live without it and the traffic of merchandise that be in this country be in all the city within the land which as we have say be almost all build along the river the chinas have a common speech for to show the nobleness of their kingdom proverb that the king of China can make a bridge of ship from China unto malaca which be near five hundred league the which though it seem it can be yet by metaphor it signify the greatness of China and the multitude of ship that of itself it can make the great ship they call junk beside which there be ship for war make like great ship junke for war and for trade ship-fights no ordnance to the which they make great fore-castle and high and likewise abafte to fight from they in such manner that they overmaster their adversary and because they use no ordnance all their use be to come many together and compass the adversary ship they board it and at the first onset they cast a great deal of lime to blind the adversary and as well from the castle as from the top they cast many sharp pike burn at the end which serve for topdart of a very stiff wood they use also great store of stone and the chief they labour for be to break with their ship the dead work of their adversary that they may be master over they have they under they and be destitute of any thing to shelter they and as soon as they can enter they come to the pike or handy-blowe for the which they have long pike and broad-pointed sword hang at their side there be other junke for lade of good they use oar but they be not so high as those of war though there be some very great all these ship as well of war as of burden use two oar a-head they be very great and four or five man do row every one of they lay they along the ship they move they with such a sleight that they make the ship go forward and they help very much for to go out and in at a bar and set upon the enemy for to board they they call these oar lioslio in all manner of their ship they use the lioslio neither do they use any other manner of oar in any kind of ship small ship there be other lesser ship than junke somewhat long call Bancones they bear three oar on a side and row very well and load a great deal of good there be other less call Lanteas which have six or seven oar on a side which do row very swift and bear a good burden also and these two sort of ship viz. Bancones and Lanteas because they be swift the thief do common use the row of these oar be stand two man at every oar every one of his side set one foot forward another backward in the junke go four five or six man at a oar a kind of galley they use also certain ship very long like unto galley without oar or beakhead which do lade great store of good and they make they so long because lade bring a great burden they may sail the better by the river which sometime be not rough they have many other ship of burden which be superfluous to tell of every one there be many small boat of poor people in which be husband and wife and child and they have no other dwell but in their boat in a middle deck for defence of the sun and of the rain as also have the Bancones and Lanteas and other which we say be like galley and these deck be in such sort that under they be very good lodging and chamber in the great ship in these of the poor they be much inferior there they breed their pig their hen and there they have also their poor little garden and there they have all their poor state and harbour dwell in ship the man go to seek work about the city to help to maintain their little house the woman go in the boat and with a long cane that reach well to the bottom of the river at the end of the which be a little basket make of rod wherewith they get shellfish with their industry and pass of people from one side to another they help to sustain their household these poor people notwithstanding do not live so poor and beggarly in their apparel as those which live poor in Portugal there be other great ship wherein be the stock of they both * * the husband merchandise and the wife housewifery which have great lodging where they may bestow a great deal of stuff these have a great stock among the field of rice duck-weeders those which be owner of the ship do receive a fee of they that owe the field for let they feed in they for they do cleanse they eat the grass that grow among they for as the country be well inhabit and people in abundance and the man spender industry cause of plenty and use themselves very delicious in eat and drink and apparel and in the other service of their house especial that they be great eater every one labour to get a live and every one seek way to earn their food and how to maintain their great expense idleness hate a great help to this be the idle people to be much abhor in this country and be very odious unto the rest and that labour not shall not eat for common there be none that do give alm to the poor wherefore if any poor do ask alm of a Portugal and he do give it he the chinas do laugh at they and in mockage say why give thou alm to thi^ which be a knave let he go and earn it alm deride only some jester have some reward go to some knave one day I and certain portugal enter into the house of the overseer of the good about the delivery of certain portugal that be in prison because the matter belong to he for the great profit that come thereof to the king much people come in with we to see we among the which there be a priest assoon as the ruler say set they down all of they run away in great haste the priest run as all the because if any tyranny shall chance to come they may find nothing to take from they from hence it come as I say that they have in India many ground in diverse place unprofitable which be not so in China for every one enjoy the fruit of his labour hence it come that all the ground that in China can yield any kind of fruit receive seed be husband the high place which be not so good for corn thrifty husbandry have very fair grove of pine tree sow also between they some pulse where it may be in the dry land and stiff they sow wheat and pulse in the marsh which be overflow which be many and very long they sow rice and some of these marsh do yield two or three crop a year only the mountain that be high and beat with the weather and be not fit to plant any thing remain unprofitable there be nothing lose in the country be it never so u^le for the bone as well of dog as of other beast they do use make toy nothing lose and with work in stead of ivory they set they in table bed and their back they carry it in tub very clean without and although they go uncover notwithstanding it show the cleanliness of the country and city in some city these tub use to go cover not to annoy they use in all thing more slight than force whereby they plough with one ox make the plough in such fashion that it cut well the earth though the furrow be not so big as among we a ship be it never so big and have it never so great a leak the pomp be make by such a slight pomp which go by the foot that one man alone sit move his foot as one that go up a pair of stair in a very little space he pomp it out these pomp be of many piece as a water wheel lay along the side of the ship between rib and rib every piece have a piece of wood of half a yard little more or less one quarter well wrought in the midst of this piece of wood be a square little board almost of a hand breadth and they join one piece into another in such manner as it may double well the joint which be all very close whereby this manner of pomp do run be within of the breadth of the little board of every one of the piece for they be all equal and this manner of pomp bring so much water as may contain between the two little board puppet play the chinas use also puppet with the which they make representation they bring up nightingale in cage which sing all the year and be use to puppet representation also provision for impotent person see of th^se thing pinto it be a thing worth the note that the blind have a labour appoint they for to get their food which be to serve in a horsemill like horse grind corn and common where be a horsemill there be two because two go together they may recreate themselves in talk one with another as I see they go about with fan in their hand cool themselves and talk very friendly the blind woman be the common woman and they have nurse that do dress they and paint they with vermilion and ceruse and receive the wage of their evil use the lame and the cripple which either have no kindred within a certain degree or if they have they and they do not provide for they that which be necessary or be not able to help they they make their petition to the overseer of the good of the king and his kindred be examine by his officer if among they be any that can maintain they they do bind the near to take they to they their charge and maintain they and if their kindred be not able to maintain they or if they have no kindred in the country the overseer of the good command they be receive into the king hospital for the king have in all the city great hospital which have many lodging the end of February in march and part of April when the great flow be there come great store of fish from the sea to spawn in the mouth of the river along the sea whereby there breed infinite small fish of many sort in the pool of the river of these spawn in these time all the fisher along the sea coast do meet in their boat and there meet so many that they cover the sea and lie near the pool and these fisher do take great quantity of this small fish and cast it in cistern which they have make with stake and a very thick net make of wire where they do feed they to the end of the fish time and at this time there be wont to come a great number of bark from all place of China within the land for I say already that all China be sail by Rivers for it be all cut and water with great river and these bark do bring a great many basket within and without which be all line with oil paper that it may hold water and every one of these bark do buy the fish they have need of then they carry this fish in these basket through all the country inward change every day the water and all man of any possibility within their ground and enclosure have great store of fish in pond for the which they buy the basket they have need they feed this fish in the pond in a very short time with cow dung and buff dung wherewith it grow very fast in all the ditch of the city likewise they breed great store of fish in the same sort of which the ruler be serve in all the city which I say already be build along the river the king have many sea crow in coop in which they breed with the which they make royal fish many time all the bark that be bind to go a fish with these cormorant do meet and set round in the river those that have charge of the bird do tie they about the crop fish with cormorant that the fish they have fish force they to cast it and in this manner they fish the quantity they will till they have to their contentment after they have fish for the bark they untie they and let they go their feast they use very fine silk chief crimson which none in the country may wear but they the poor people wear common coat of white linen because it cost but little on their head they wear a high or ribbon dress very well make their cap remain above it that it may be see they have a superstition in their hair therefore they wear it so long hold that by it they shall be carry to heaven the common priest do keep their hair but be shave for they say they need no help to carry they to heaven yet among they be some priest of the temple of the idol which among the chinas be more reverence than the rest these do wear hair on the top of the head fasten with a stick very curious wrought like a close hand varnish with a very fine varnish which they call Acharan and these priest do wear black coat the other wear a white coat courtesy the chinaes be very courteous man the common courtesy be the left hand close they enclose it within the right hand and they bring they very oft to their breast show they have one another enclose in their heart and to this motion of the hand they join word of courtesy though the word of the common sort be to say one to another Chifan mesan which be to say have you eat or no for all their good in this world be resolve in eat the particular courtesy between man of sort which have not see one another a long while be the arm bow and the finger clasp one within another they stoop and speak with word of great courtesy every one labour to give the hand to the other to make he rise and the more honourable they be the long they stand in these courtesy the honourable and noble people do use also many courtesy at the table the one give drink to the other and every one labour to give the hand to the other in their drink for at the table there be no other service but that of drink if there come any guest new to his friend house or his kinsman if the master of the house be not apparel in holy day clothes when the guest come in he make no account of he nor any mention till he command to bring his festival apparel and after he be so apparel he go to the guest and receive he with many compliment and courtesy for they hold it not convenient that a newcome guest and of reverence be receive with common apparel but clothe in feast-like apparel for in this he show he that his enter into his house be a feast day to he whatsoever person or person come to any man house of quality he have a custom to offer he in a fine basket one porcelain or as many as the person be with a kind of drink which they call drink which be somewhat bitter red and medicinal which they be wont to make of a certain concoction of herb somewhat bitter with this they welcome common all manner of person that they do respect be they stranger or be they not to i they offer it many time the chinaes be great eater and they use many dainty they eat at one table fish and flesh great eater and the base people dress it sometime all together the dainty which be to be eat at one table be set all together on the board that every one may eat where he like best it be a clean and neat people the common people have some gross thing certain noble portugal go to show i on a day in Cantan a banquet which a rich merchant make which be worth the sight the house where it be make be with a loft and very fair with many fair window and casement and all of it be a mirror the table be set in three place of the house for every guest invite a table and a chair very fair and gilt or with silver and every table have before it a cloth of damask down to the ground on the table be neither cloth nor napkin as well because the table be very fine as because they eat so clean that they need none of these thing the fruit be set along the edge of every table all set in order which be roast chestnut and peel and nut crack and shall and sugar cane clean and cut in slice and the fruit we speak of before call Lichias great and small but they be dry all the fruit be set in small heap like turret very well make cross between with certain small stick very neat whereby all the table round about with these little turret be very fair adorn present after the fruit be all the service place in fine Porcelan dish all very well dress and neat carve and every thing set in good order and although the dish be set one over another all be so fine set in such sort that he which sit at the table may eat what he will without any need of stir or remove any of they and present there be two small stick very fine and gilt for to eat with hold they between the finger they use they in stead of a pair of pincer so that they touch nothing of that which be on the board with their hand yea though they eat a dish of rice they do it with those stick without any grain of the rice fall and because they eat so clean not touch with the hand their meat they have no need of cloth or napkin all come carve and well order to the table they have also a very small Porcelan cup gilt which hold a mouth full of wine and only for this there be a waight at the table they drink so little that at every bit they must have the cup and therefore it be so small there be some chinaes that wear very long nail of half a quarter and a quarter long which they keep very clean and these nail do serve they in stead of the stick for to eat withal feast the chinaes do use on their birth day to make great feast continue yet in they the custom of the old gentile in these feast be wont to meet all the kinsman and friend and all do help he to bear the charge of the feast with send he present that when they do celebrate their birth day they may pay they in the same sort birthday and because they have these help they make great expense and solemnity the feast last all night long for all the gentile as they walk in darkness live without the knowledge of God so all their feast through all place of India and in China be make by night night feast in these feast be great abundance of meat and great store of wine all the night they spend in ea^ing and drink and music play on diverse instrument their priest offer their sacrifice to their god apparel very rich they apparel themselves in diverse sort of garment and the priest do sing their song in a very tuneable voice among these sacrifice play and sing the table be always furnish with sundry meat every one take what he like best the priest when they have sing as all the rest do make at their door triumphant arch very well make of paper and scaffold with diverse representation of figure and statue and certain high tree and hang on the break bough very well wrought and paint many light and in every place many lantern very fair and well make all with light in the general feast of all the town and people chief on the first day of the year new year day all the street and door be very rich dress and chief they do endeavour and labour to deck the triumphal arch cover they with many clothes of damask and of other silk with many lantern there be much play of sundry instrument and sing and joint with this great store of meat of sundry kind and great abundance of wine they use many time representation by actor which do represent very well and to the life the actor have very good apparel and well order comedy and fit as be requisite for the person he represent and they that represent a woman part beside the apparel that be requisite for the part he represent they be paint with and ceruse those which understand they not what they represent be sometime weary but they that understand they do delight very much to hear they and one whole night and two and some time three they be continual busy in representation one after another while these representation do last there must be a table set with great store of meat and drink they have in these action two great inconvenience or blemish the one be that if one be to represent two part and be to change his attire he do it before all the beholder the other be that the representer as well as he that speak alone do speak in a very high voice almost sing sometime they go to the ship to play that the portugal may give they money the instrument they use for to play on be certain bandoraes like we though not so well make with their pin to tune they instrument and there be some like gitternes which be small and other like a vial gamba which be less they use also Dulcimeres and rebeck and of a certain kind of hob^yse resemble our use they use a certain manner of instrument that have many wire string they play on they with their nail which for that purpose they wear they have a great sound and make a good harmony they play many instrument together sometime consort in four voice which make a very good consonancy it happen one night by moonshine that I and certain portugal sit at the door of our lodging a few young man pass the time come along the river play on diverse instrument and we be glad to hear the music send for they to come near where we be and that we will invite they they as gallant youth come near with the boat and begin to tune their instrument in such sort that we be glad to see they fit themselves that they may make no discord and beginning to sound they begin not altogether but the one tarry for to enter with the other make many division in the process of the music some stay other play and the most time they play all together in four part the part be two small bandoraes for the tenor a great one for counter-tenor and a instrument call Crano follow the rest and sometime a Rebecke sometime a dulcimere for a treble and they use a good policy that we may remain the more desirous they play but two strain it be not lawful for any man in all the country to carry any manner of weapon arm and quarrel no not a knife therefore when one quarrel with another they go to buffet and pull by the hair only the soldier and minister of the captain of war do wear sword on their hanger when any man die that have house kindred and child after he have give up the ghost they wash the coarse and put on his best apparel and his cap on his head funeral rite and set he on a chair and then come his wife and kneel down before he and with many tear and lamentable word she take her leave of he and after the wife come the child in their order do the like and after the child the rest of the kindred and all the rest of the house and his friend the ceremony end they put he in a coffin make for he of Camfiere wood which be preservative for dead body and smell well they close it and pitch it well that no smell may come out of it they set it upon two little form and cast over it a cloth to cover the coffin down to the ground whereon the picture of the man decease be picture they make a little house before the coffin of white raw cloth with a Portall right against the coarse where a table be set with candle-stick and candle light and set thereon bread and all the fruit of the country and all this they do of superstition for a ceremony and there they keep the coarse eight or fifteen day in the which their priest of their god come continual by night to offer their sacrifice and to pray their heathenish invention there they bring many picture of man and woman and burn they with many ceremony final they hang some picture of man and woman in paper hang on coard and with great pray and move these picture by the coard with great cry and shout they say to send the dead man to heaven all day and all night while they be in these ceremony there be a table set with great store of meat and drink these ceremony end they take the coffin and set it in a field where the dead be and there it consume with time mourn their mourn which they use be the sharp that ever I see for they wear coat after the common sort of very course wool next the flesh and gird with great coard and on their head a cap of the same cloth make like the cap that be use in the country save that these have certain flappe that fall over their eye notwithstanding that as they be near in kindred so they wear the rough mourn weed the rest wear raw cloth and not so course for father or mother they mourn three year and if he be Louthia as soon as he hear the news present he leave the office he serve and go to mourn to his own house for three year which be end he go to the court to demand his office china woman custom and clothes I have many China picture which represent the woman either with their foot wrap up or else very small their eye also and no^es little etc. of the rest as in the map be see the woman common except those of the sea coast and the mountaineer be very white and fine woman some have their nose and eye well proportion from their childhood they wrap their foot in clothes that they may remain small and they do it for the china do hold they for fine woman that have small nose and foot this be use yet among the noble people and not among the base they wear their hair very well comb close and tie to the crown of the head and bind from the root to the top with a long lace very well place and the lace be garnish with jewel and piece of gold round about they use long coat like the Portugal woman which have the waste in the same manner that they have they wear upper-body with long sleeve they spend common more silk in their garment then their husband but in their common apparel they be clothe in white linen-cloth they make courtesy as our woman do but they make three together and very hasty they use paint their face with vermilion and white ceruse very well set they common keep themselves close so that through all the city of Cantan there appear not a woman but some light huswife and base woman and when they go abroad they be not see woman retiredness for they go in close chair whereof we speak before neither when any body come into the house do he see they except for curiosity they chance under the doore-cloath to look on they that come in when they be strange people common the man have one wife which they buy for their money more or less according as they be marriage of their father and mother yet may every one have as many wife as he be able to maintain but one be the principal with who they live and the other he lodge in sundry house and if he have deal in diverse country he have in every one a wife and house with entertainment adultery if the wife commit adultery and the husband accuse she and the adulterer both suffer death and if the husband do suffer the wife to play the adulteress witaldrie he be grievous punish I be in cantan see a merchant of China go from justice to justice very sharp handle for suffer his wife to play the adulteress the common woman be in no wise permit to dwell within the wall harlot and in the suburb without they have their proper street where they dwell out of the which they may not live all the common woman be slave they bring they up for that purpose from their childhood they buy they of their mother and teach they to play on a instrument of music and to sing and those that can best do this because they gain most be worth more and those which can do that be worth less the master either carry they unto the man or sell they to they and when they be to beset in the street of the common woman they be write by a officer of the king in a book and the master be bind to come every year with a certain fee to this officer they be bind to answer their master so much every month when they be old with paint they make they seem young and after they be not for that trade they be altogether free without any obligation either to master or any body and then they feed upon that which they have get I speak so particular of this matter for to come to say that in this country of China be no great captivity than this of these wench and let no man say or affirm any other thing for about the examine of it I labour somewhat in Cantan because some portugal will affirm it otherwise the bondage or slavery of some in China the captivity in this country be in manner follow if any woman by the death of her husband remain a widow and have nothing to maintain herself with neither the child that be leave she be such as be able to get their live neither have she any thing to give her child this woman in this necessity come to a rich man and agree with he for six or seven crown for a son or a daughter and the price receive she deliver it if it be a daughter she serve as abovesaid for a common woman and be bring up for that purpose if it be a son he serve his master some time and when he be of age to marry the master give he a wife and all the child that be bear to he remain free and without any obligation notwithstanding this servant be bind to give his master so much by the year have a house by himself for when he marry they give he a house and he labour either at some trade or by his industry for to earn his live and no man may sell any of these slave to the portugal have great penalty for it the woman as by be common they look for great profit of they in no wise they will sell they beside the run into great penalty also and all those which common be sell to the portugal be steal they carry they deceive and secret to the portugal and so they sell they and if they be perceive or take in these stealth they will be condemn in the utmost punishment the law of China give authority to the woman for to sell their child and not to the man for as the man be bind to get a live for himself and for his child if he want the remedy they hold that he be in the fault of that and that man may the better labour for their live and their child so far be China from have slave that altogether shall be captive that neither those which they take in war be slave only they be bind to the king and be place for soldier in place far from their country where they be take eat of the wage they have of the King these do wear for a device a red cap as I see the tartarian wear in Cantan which have be take in the war @. 4 of their Louthias Mandarines or magistrate their creation privilege maintenance of prison and torture of the king and of ambassador every one that in China have any office command or dignity by the king be call Louthia which be to say with we Senor how this title be give he we will in his place make mention of it sir master or Lord there be in every province of China one thousand Louthias or according to other three thousand beside those that be resident in the court by who be ordain all matter of the kingdom and to who come all the weighty matter of all the realm and because they be to dispatch with the king and converse with he within door and it be not lawful for other to converse with they Louthias of the court eunuch neither do other see they and they have entrance where the wife of the king be which be many they be common eunuch in every province be five which among the rest be most principal which have a very great authority and majesty in their person and be great reverence and honour not only of the common people but also of all the other Lothyas the principal of the five be the governor which in their language be call tutom to this come all matter both great and small of all the province the tutom lieutenant deputy or viceroy and for the authority and majesty of his person he be not resident where the other Lothyas that he may not be frequent of they and so he may be more esteem and fear to these come all the rent of the province except the ordinary expense and by he as well the business as the rent that be gather and all that happen in the province be refer and send to the Court the second dignity of the province be the overseer of the good which in their language be call Ponchassi the ponchassi or treasurer this have the care to send to recover through all the province the rent thereof for the which he have many Lothyas under his jurisdiction which be particular officer for the business and recovery of the good this provide all the ordinary charge of the province and with that which remain he resort to the tutom that he may send it to the court this may intermeddle in grave matter of the other officer inferior and have authority over they likewise all the matter and affair of the province resort unto he to be refer by he to the tutom another chief dignity under this be the chief justice which in their language be call Anchasi the or chief justice and though there be many other officer of justice this be above all and by he be the dispatch distribute to the rest and all matter of justice resort unto he as one that have authority of the other inferior another dignity under this be the chief captain who in their tongue be call Aitao to this Aitao pertain to command to prepare the man of war and all that be necessary of ship and victual the Aitao or chief captain and all other provision against enemy and against thief to this belong also the business of stranger in case which belong not to the good the five and last of the great dignity be of the chief captain which put in execution the matter of war and be resident in the army which the Aitao be a land do ordain when it be necessary beside the put matter in execution and order if the matter require his presence he go in person and so important may the matter be that the Aitao will go his lieutenant the Luthissi each have ten assistant this be call in the country language Inthissi in the house of every one of these except the Luthissi which be the inferior of the five be other ten which be as assistant and be also of great authority five of these do sit at the right hand of the principal in five chair recite before when we speak of the building and five do sit on the left hand these in matter of importance be at the dispatch with the principal of the house and the principal die or by any other mean want one of these according to his antiquity remain in his stead and if it be necessary to go through the province about some matter of importance that appertain to the dignity in who house they assist one of these do go with all the authority of the principal the five that sit on the right hand ensign of dignity girdle and canopy have a great degree and dignity than the five on the left hand and as the dignity consist in their girdle and canopy those of the right hand wear girdle of gold and canopy of yellow and those of the left hand wear girdle of silver and canopy of blue or of changeable colour the girdle be little less than three finger broad and a inch thick and all about of gold or of silver very well wrought make of piece the canopy be very large and fair which a officer do bear upon a staff a fathom long of a Clove tree very fair and they be line with silk beside these assistant and the five principal there be among the inferior one of great dignity the taissu or sheriff which be the chief jailor who they call taissu which have very great house of great receipt where they have great prison but neither this nor any that be under may wear girdle of gold nor silver nor a yellow canopy except he be a officer or captain of man of war that for favour of a gentleman may have a yellow canopy the rest wear girdle of Tartaruga or of other matter make like they of gold or silver and their canopy be of changeable stuff or blue and all these inferior do speak to the superior when they be before they on their knee and do kneel as long as they be with they except the taissu who when he come in kneel and rise up present and be always stand every one of the great one have many inferior officer under his jurisdiction for the matter and business necessary to the office of every one all which as they be the king officer have the title of Lothias and their badge or sign the five principal with their assistant do wear for a badge the king arm on their breast and on their back which be certain serpent weave with gold thread the Chaen or judge of the circuit or visitor every year there be one send to every province as a justice which be call Chaen which come to take account of all the Lothias great and small and examine all the student and choose Louthias and visit the prison and all that be necessary to be see and provide for in all the province he use all mean to spy out their bribery and injustice and have power to displace or prefer when this enter new into this city it be not lawful for any to work they shut their door and no body walk through the street and to preserve his worship and authority they will not bold communicate in sight of the people and many officer with banner display of crimson silk and all the Louthias both great and small be bind to go and meet he the same entertainment be use to every one of the five when he come new to the province where he be to administer his office there be other dignity above all these which be call Quinchais which be to say a plate or seal of gold which be not send but about very serious matter and of great importance the Quinchais commissioner extraordinary for the kingdom or the King every Lothia of what quality soever he be high or low have for a sign or badge beside the abovesaid a high cap and round with certain ear across make of small twig weave with twist all the office be give from three to three year and none be give for long time and all give to man that be not bear in that part of the land because they may not be move by affection in matter of justice that belong to their office and also because they may not become mighty thereby to prevent insurrection the office be distribute by the king with the counsel of the eunuch and because the eunuch be those with who counsel the office be distribute they be many time mighty bribe the Chaens which the king do send every three year common be sound man and bring common more authority than the rest and these beside the yearly Chaen be send the three year when every officer end his office after that the Chaens have take the account of the Lothyas the three year visitor they visit the prison and give audience to the prisoner after this he with the other principal Lothias do visit the scholar and all those that he find to have study well he favour and give they good hope and those which have not study well if he see they have ability for it he command they to be whip and if already they have be whip and have not amend he command they to be put some day in prison beside the whip of they that with these punishment from thence forward they may have a better care if he find that they neither learn nor have ability he thrust they out of the school this do only the Louthias which come every three year after they have dispatch the business of the province he busy himself in make Louthias which he make in form follow he command to come to the principal city of the province all the student that have well study from all the city of the province and from all the great town where the king have schoolmaster of free school maintain at his charge for the student do learn the law of the realm maintain at their father charge and all the principal Louthias of the province assemble with Chaen there examine very well every one of the student demand of he many thing concern their law and if he answer to all well they command he to be put apart and if he be not yet well instruct either they send he to learn more and if it be through his default either they whip he or be whip they send he to prison as the portugal see many in prison for that fault where they be in prison also after the examination end the Chaen rise up and all the Louthias with great ceremony feast music and playing commencement or act. of this see more in the follow relation of the jesuit they give the degree to every one of they they find sufficient which be to give he the title of Louthi^ and after the pass many day in feast and banquet they send they to the court to receive the badge of Louthias which be cap with ear broad girdle and canopy and there they stay the distribution of office so that in this manner they make the Louthias which in the country be to administer justice the Louthias for war be make by chivalry and famous deed which they do in war so that in these country man be much honour by their learning or by their chivalry and yet more for their learning because of the learned do common come the five principal Louthias and the assistant notwithstanding there be many Louthias which be make for simple favour other sort of Louthias either for do some particular service to the king or to the realm or in some town or have some particular favour or quality as they do to a young man of China because the portugal be in prison he serve for a interpreter whereby the Louthias give he the title and badge of Louthia because he can speak Portugal but these and such other do not common serve office of the king but enjoy only the liberty of Louthias as the gentleman portugal have their liberty which some enjoy by favour of the King and these Louthias have great liberty in the country for none can do he any injury without punishment neither can they be imprison but for heinous fault and they may imprison any that do wrong they their privilege and many other liberty and though there be some portugal that report without any certainty that the chinaes do study natural philosophy the truth be that there be no other study nor university in it nor particular but only the school royal of the law of the kingdom the truth be that some be find that have knowledge of the course of heaven whereby they know the eclipse of the sun and of the moon but these if they know it by any write that be find among they they teach it to some person or person in particular but of this there be no school the chinas have no certain letter in their write for all that they write be by character their line be not overthwart as in the write of all other nation but be write up and down when the Louthias be dispatch at the court with office for the province where they go to govern public officer whole maintain of the public they depart carry nothing of their own more than the apparel they be to wear and some few servant to serve he even when they have no office neither need they carry any provision for the journey nor carriage or ship at their own charge for through all the way where he go be provision aswell of ship as of necessary carriage and necessary food for all the king officer which be provide of the royal rent house for officer in all the city and great town the king have many good and noble house for the Louthias both great and small to lodge in and all those which by any mean be the king have sufficient rent for the maintenance of every person that shall dwell in the house according to his degree and that which be to be give to every one for his expense be already limit wherefore he that may lodge there be come the officer of the house come to he and ask he if he will have his ordinary in money or in thing necessary for provision and that which he do demand as far as the money do extend he be to give he very well and clean dress either flesh fish duck or hen or what he will and any Louthia that do lodge there may command the host of the house to be whip if he serve he not to his will and if any Louthia will go to lodge at the house of any acquaintance of he he take the money which the inferior Louthias do also sometime either to spare some money or to be merry at their will more free and in the provision of these house there be no want any way for the ponchasis have the charge to give they sufficient provision that it do not want and at the year end account be take of the officer of the house of the expense he make by the way at every league and at every two league be house which only have bed and chair for the traveller to rest and ease themselves public inn and some of those that have care of these house have provision for to give wine to the guest other give nothing but Chua after the Louthias come to the city where they be to be resident and execute his office they find the house where they be to lodge according to the office they have great or small great or small in these house they find all the servant necessary scrivener porter inferior officer and all other minister necessary for their office for these be continual in the house for to minister at all time all the office of the house where they serve and every officer according to his house and person have his provision necessary for his meat drink and his apparel limit so that it suffice he well which be pay to he without fail every month when the Louthias be old and weary in the charge and office of the kingdom they be lodge in their own country or where they will rest in age with dignity and the king allow they every month so much according to their quality for their maintenance till they die and because the ordinary of the Louthias be common sufficient and with some abundance they may always spare some thing to leave their wife and child before the inferior minister these officer do all thing of their office and matter of justice for they be present at all thing to prevent bribe and partiality while the Louthia be sit in the chair to hear the party and dispatch of matter the porter scrivener sergeant and other minister be at the door and when any person come with any matter one of the porter with a high voice that he may be hear where the Louthias sit for it be far off tell who and wherefore he come and none speak to the Louthias but upon both their knee on the ground and common they speak a pretty space distant from he reverence and from thence with a high voice well understand he propound his case or show he his petition write in paper and lift up the hand desire he to receive it and to show he justice to who a minister run the Louthia make a sign to he and present it unto he after the Louthia read it he either dispatch he of that which he ask write at the foot of the petition with red ink or remit the party to a inferior officer to be dispatch so I see it do to a petition which a woman present to the the promptness and readiness wherewith the Louthias be serve and how fear they be can be write with the pen nor express with the tongue but it must be see with the eye for to know what it be all do their message run and with great speed not only the scrivener and sergeant and other minister but also the inferior Louthias to the superior and if any fail never so little of his diligence and accustom speed or commit the less negligence in the world before the Louthia he have not any remission but immediate they put a little flag in his hand and he must hold it in his hand kneel until the party be dispatch and then the Louthia command to give he the stripe that he think good and the stripe be such as hereafter we will speak of whereby all the minister in the house of the Louthias be plaster or mark with the stripe so that already among themselves they hold it a disgrace not to be mark with the stripe because it be a thing general common among they and when the Louthia wax angry or be move at any thing it be a wonder to see the trouble and fear that be in all the stander by I be in the house of the with certain portugal entreat for the deliverance of certain portugal that be captive and imprison in the jail for the which we carry he eight ounce of Ambar which at that time be much esteem of they and now by carry so much it be not so much esteem we not be willing to give he the Ambar without give we both the portugal he take a occasion for to terrify we to wax angry against the youth servant of a Portugal which be in our company and be our interpreter wherefore he rise out of the chair and become red as blood and his eye be inflame and set one foot forward put his thumb under his girdle look to the stander by with a terrible countenance step forward lift up his foot and stamp on the ground with it and say with a terrible voice Taa taa which be to say whip it be a wonderful thing to see in how little space they take the youth tie his hand behind with a cord and lay he on his belly with his thigh bare and two beadle place themselves on each side one with one foot forward and their whip ready for to give he the stripe that they shall be command to give he certain it be all do in a moment the merchant that come in our favour be trouble and stand aside shake with fear at this time one of the prisoner say sir be not afraid for he can whip that youth and in truth we know it be so for according to their law there be no fault whereby he may command he to be whip and there be a penalty if he do it the Louthia hear the voice of the prisoner command to carry he with speed to the jail again and the Louthia do this for nothing else but to make we afraid that we shall give he the Ambar for one of the prisoner for he can not give we the other because he be already adjudge to die and the sentence confirm by the king which be irrevocable and he be willing to have the Ambar for he hope to have of the king a great reward then to be Ponchasi for the Ambar for he do eat it for to sustain life and many day be past since they have demand it of the portugal but as they know not the name we use for it they never understand one another till that the year after they have for the Aitao of Cantan a little for the delivery of a Portugal whereby he be advance to Ponchasi and this will also have for the same effect the Ambar at our hand for to be advance notwithstanding we see ourselves tie and without a interpreter by who to speak and the youth in disposition of whip we give he the Ambar there come present a chasing-dish for to prove it and the prisoner cast a little in the fire and see the smoke ascend right up he be content and scatter the smoke he set his nose over it and say haoa which be to say it be very good and command present to deliver we the prisoner free it be wonderful to see with what speed it be weigh and the piece tell and put in a paper and note by the scrivener before they all the number of the piece and the weight that be there and after that paper another all glue present and after that another manner of their pomp^ in the street and in the three the Panchasi set his mark with red letter and what be contain within and at the same instant come a little box and be put in it be present stop and upon the cover a paper glue and upon it the mark of the and present come a inferior Louthia captain of the army with his soldier and all afar off kneel down and say at every word quoo which be to say yes incline their head and hand to the ground and receive his message present as he come run so he return run with the box to take ship for to carry the Ambar to the Tutaen to be send from he to the King all this that I have speak be do in a trice before we stir from the place where we be this be also desirous to have the Ambar of we before the Louthia of that seat do come which be look for every day to come a new for this be only a lieutenant when any Louthia that be not of the five neither the Chaen neither very inferior but as they say of the mean sort go abroad into the city he have before he a good space two minister with two mace that seem to be of silver upon long staff make almost after our fashion and the one go on the one side the street the other on the other-side after these a little distant go other two each with a straight cane or pole in his hand after these go other two in the same distance with two cane trail along the pavement which be the instrument of justice wherewith they do whip after these go other two with two table like two target bow and plaster whereon be write the title of the officer that pass the foremost signify in their mace that he which pass be in his office in the king place and the two straight rod the right of justice which he ought to do those which carry the instrument of whip do carry for a sign certain long red lace with two great round tassel at the end and all do carry very gallant plume very well make of the point of a peacock tail and those that go before do now and then say with a loud voice Huuph which be to say give place or beware while these do pass it be not lawful in any wise for any one to cross or go in the middle of the street under pain of be whip without any remission it chance two portugal go through the midst of a street in Cantan walk and behind they come a inferior Louthia which have but four minister which come cry according to their custom they shall give place the portugal either give no heed or make no regard of those that come wherefore a minister come give a great thrust to the one of they and the Portugal answer he with a box on the ear and be bind with his hand behind he be to go to prison it be necessary for the Portugal to come to the Louthia and pacify he with fair word and he make a end of pacify he with fourteen crown that he give he after the minister come the Louthia in a rich chair gild and very fair on four man back these chair be great and sumptuous and the Louthia go compass with all the scrivener and other his minister and all of they while he go by the street go always run and the Louthia wear a long black coat of fine serge with long sleeve which be the common wear he carry the arm a cross like a friar and his eye low without look to any side for even with their eye they will not communicate with the common people for to preserve their authority the more with they that may be more fear when any of the four Louthias go abroad except the Tutan or the yearly Chaen they go accompany with many minister and six officer do carry they on their back and they lead a spare horse with a fair saddle and a cloth of silk over it the chair wherein they go be more sumptuous and rich they carry before four five or six mace and two or three instrument and more minister when the Chaen that come every three year come into the city pomp of the great officer or for form important affair go abroad or some Quinchay they shut up all the door in the street where he pass and none do work nor be any see in the street when he pass the shop be shut up and every thing of sale be out of sight the officer with coard along the street do make three lane where the triumph arch be make in three arch and through the midst pass the Louthia only and the officer on the two side and it be not lawful for any to pass through the middle Chaen and Quinchays splendour they be accompany of many inferior Louthias that go on foot and on the one side of the street and the other be many arm man and other with banner of red silk advance all stand in good order in the court of the house where he be to go in be many kettledrum set upon high stake to be well play upon which be cover down to the ground with clothes of silk quarter after these be many place in order with flag of silk on high after these in the same order be many with trumpet and all be in great silence as soon as the Louthia appear they all sound their instrument in order noise and silence the sound of the instrument end they remain all in so great a silence as if there be no body in the court be a great multitude of people the people as they come in do place themselves on the side the midst between the instrument remain void whereby the Louthia pass before these Louthias go common many inferior Louthias of those that carry mace when they go abroad there be also in this court many man at arm with long gild lance and with very fair armour this be all in the first court. in the second along the gallery whereof we speak above when we treat of the house of the great man that only the Louthias pass through they on the one side and the other be many inferior Louthias with headpiece on their head some gilt some with silver and with sword hang at their belt and with coat and cassock make in fashion of frocke with stud of gold and silver that it seem set upon plate but it be a very fine work make upon very single silk which serve only for bravery and ornament some use on their head white headpiece garnish with gold but be of a very fine leaf and thin that seem a armour be not in this manner also be the Louthias inferior which do environ the superior Louthia the chair where these do go be very rich and of great price and very sumptuous the table whereon be write the title of dignity of these great man be write with letter of silver and when any of these do enter new in any city with these feast and enternaynment all the Louthias great and small receive he at a house where he land very rich and noble and from thence they accompany he unto his lodging and be lodge all do take their leave with many courtesy in these receiving they use no sumptuous apparel the great man when most wear coat of red silk in their own feast in their house and secret one with another and in banquet they use crimson silk and all the bravery in their apparel and in rich attire whensoever by way of inquiry or examination any witness be demand the Louthias do it in public before the officer and minister of his office manner of inquisition and before all the rest that by any mean chance to be there present and this because no falsehood may be use nor any sleight in the manner of inquire and by consequence in writing and first they examine the witness several and if they do agree they join they and examine the one before the other till they bring they to altercation and quarrel by word that by the word the one speak to the other they may come to the knowledge of the truth and if by this mean they do not comprehend the truth they give they many stripe and torture that by one mean or other they may know the truth of the matter they inquire or examine no oath they use no oath for they esteem nothing of their god they have notwithstanding a respect in the witness the person of quality and of who be presume that they will not easy lie when they examine any matter of great weight or a grave person than they write themselves the process of the examination it chance sometime that some of the Louthias for a great bribe or for great friendship let some prisoner loose bribe-tricke and put another in his place for there never want one naughtipacke that will put himself in danger of stripe or death for interest or they bring he in by deceit deceive he with word and make the matter light unto he and give he some interest they name he as the prisoner they will let loose that the fault and punishment of the guilty may fall upon the innocent and when sometime in this sort they can let the guilty person loose they labour to bribe all the officer to give he for dead among those that die in the prison but these invention be not use but where the bribe be great cane-whipping much be here write of prison and execution which I have omit or the adherent very great and mighty and for to eschew the inconvenience which sometime fall out when any be imprison for weighty matter or the prisoner have great adversary they set down all the mark of the prisoner and cause they to be set at the foot of the writing that so they may not use any of the malice abovesaid with how much piety and leisure they kill with so much cruelty and speed they whip for in this case they forgive none the stripe be such that with reason it may be a sufficient punishment for to amend for the cane wherewith they whip be plait below about four finger broad and go straighten upward unto the end where the beadle hold they and they be almost a finger thick for in those part be cane as big as a man leg and because in Portugal be many witness of knowledge of the same I dare simple affirm it and they be of eighty * * huge reed or cane or ninety span long and their whip be make of these cane of the height of a middle stature man to the breast they give the stripe on the ham of the man leg be lay on his breast and his leg lay along and his hand tie behind and the beadle butcher as they be command the Louthias be altogether void of compassion talk one with another eat and drink and pick their tooth the cruelty be such that the court be full of blood and when they have make a end of whip they they carry they not but like butcher with much cruelty they draw they by one leg to the prison miserable evasion of misery and when the beadle be whip they tell with a loud voice the stripe if the miserable prisoner which be in the prson for grievous fault at the time that this correction be to be do can get a piece of a cord wherewith they may hang themselves they go to buffet who shall hang himself first that that the butchery of the stripe be not execute on they and the portugal affirm which be in prison that in one day forty prisoner do hang themselves in the prison where they be to escape the stripe they be rather willing to lose their life and they affirm that the cord be very short that scarce there be so much as to come about the neck to tie it and on a stick which they stick in the wall and because the stick be very low they pull one another till they be choke go to buffet who shall hang himself first when any do kill himself or die in the prison it be the order in China to cast he in the house of office and there to be three day where the rat do eat he up and sometime the chinaes prisoner do eat of they with hunger every city that be the head of the province have thirteen dungeon store of free-people and therefore store of bond by abuse liberty and store and in six of they be the man condemn to death there be in Cantan upward of fifteen thousand prisoner there be in every dungeon only for the condemn to death one hundred and twenty man that serve for watch and have a Louthia over they as their captain or gentleman of the round there be two sort of torture one for the hand another for the foot which be nip by certain stick to the bruise or break of the finger or toe with cruel pain the king have as many wife as he list the king his wife child and servant and within door all the service be almost of woman whereof he have a great multitude and likewise great store of eunuch and there be no other people within the house the first son that be bear unto he of any of his wife succeed in the kingdom the rest he marry and at such time as he marry they they be lodge in some of the city that he best like where they be well provide of all thing necessary for their maintenance as son to the King but they never see the king face any more after they be marry all the ambassador that come to China with embassage from king or princss receive of the king great reward and favour and they give he cap and sign of Lothia whereby he have great privilege in the country they may whip and punish the chinaes themselves ambassador privilege so that they touch not any Louthia small or great for to meddle with these will breed great inconvenience this be the cause that Fernando * * Soarez be send viceroy an. 1515. and send this Perez with a fleet to China and therein Thomas Perez ambassador who be well entertain there but some portugal usurp Tamus a china-iland and exercise all outrage cause t. Perez after 4. month travel from Cantan to the court to be take for a spy and send back to Cantan where he die in prison among malefactor see Maffaeus l. 5 and 6 who seem to disagree or else his people act be ascribe unto he for he have leave 6. ship there when he go to Canton Perez of Adrade go for ambassador to China that the chinaes do rise against he and he escape with his hand on his head lose some ship because have do unaccustomed justice in China and upon the chinaes and they forbear he he will stretch his hand to the Louthias the good of the ambassador and of he be free from custom and to he and to his they give lodging to dwell in and all thing necessary while they be in the country no man no not a Louthia may disturb he in any thing nor any thing of he one Lothia will have whip one of siam for have carry a message to the prison to certain portugal that be in prison one of the officer say unto he that be present that he be of siam of the embassage wherefore be satisfy therewith he let he go in peace desire he he will not do so again with the chinaes be so great as at the beginning we say and declare the king have such mean and industry in the government thereof that every month he know all that pass through all the realm and he know it in this manner all matter of justice and of war and all annuity with all that be worth the know in every one of the province be refer by the Louthias and by other person to the and the Ponchasi make a relation of all by write to the Tutan the Tutan be bind to send a post every month to the court which carry the information in write to the king of all thing that pass in that month they count their month by the moon and they be to be dispatch in such sort that at the begin of every moon the post from all the province be to be at the court that the first day of the moon it may be present to the king as relation of all thing happen in every province and although some province be far distant from the court that the post can come within a month to the court notwithstanding in such manner they agree that every moon the king be to have the relation of every province though the one be of more time than another because of the one province be far and the other near the manner of the post be as among we they carry a horn which they wind when they come near to any town that they may have a horse ready in every town within a certain distance they be bind when they hear the horn to have a horse ready for he which be do with such diligence as all the other service of the officer and where he be to pass a ford as soon as he wind his horn with great speed they carry he a boat as I see once go to the city of Cantan in a town that be in the way call Caaman sometime it happen by the malice of some Louthias when they have any interest in it to keep some thing conceal that the king know not but woe to they if the king come to know it for they be grievous punish as we shall see in a case hereafter follow be in India and also in China I be inform that sometime the king of China do send some man of great confidence disguise through diverse part of China that they may see how his officer do serve they and so the chinaes do now make their merchandise well and now both great and small be glad with the traffic of the portugal and the fame of they run through all china whereby some of the principal of the court come to Cantan only to see they have hear the fame of they before the time aforesaid and after the rise which Fernando Perez of Andrade do cause the business be do with great
