under the name of portugal neither go this name to the court when they agree to pay custom but under the name of fangin which be to say people of another coast. note also that the law in China be that no man of China do sail out of the realm in pain of death only it be lawful for he to sail along the coast of the same china and yet along the coast nor from one place to another in China itself it be lawful to go without a certificate of the Louthias of the country whence they depart in which be set down whither they go and wherefore and the mark of his person and his age law of navigation if he carry not this certificate he be banish to the frontier the merchant that carry good carry a certificate of the good he carry and how he pay duty for they in every customhouse that be in every province he pay certain duty and not pay they he lose the good and be banish to the frontier part notwithstanding the abovesaid law some chinaes do not leave go out of China to traffic covetise lawless but these never return again to China of these some live in Mallaca other in siam other in Patane and so in diverse place of the south some of these that go out without licence be scatter whereby some of these which live already out of China do return again in their ship unto China under the protection of some Portugal and when they be to dispatch the duty of their ship they take some Portugal their friend to who they give some bribe that he may dispatch it in his name and pay the duty some chinaes desire to get their live do go very secret in these ship of the chinaes to traffic abroad and return very secret that it be not know no not to his kindred that it be not spread abroad and they incur the penalty that the like do incur this law be make because the king of China find that the much communication of the stranger may be the cause of some rise and because many chinaes with a excuse of sail abroad become thief and rob the country along the sea coast and yet for all this diligence there be many chinaes robber along the sea coast these chinaes that live out of China and do go thither with the portugal since the offence of Fernando Perez of Andrada do direct the portugal to begin to go to traffic to Liampo China pirate for in those part be no wall city nor village Liampo but many and great town along the coast of poor people which be very glad of the portugal and sell they their provision whereof they make their gain in these town be these merchant of China which come with the portugal and because they be acquaint for their sake the portugal be better entertain and as these chinaes which be among the portugal and the country merchant in their buy and sell they reap a great profit thereby the inferior Louthias of the sea coast receive also great profit of this traffic for they receive great bribe of the one and of the other to give they leave to traffic to carry and recarry their good so that this traffic be among they a long while conceal from the king and from the superior Louthias of the province after these matter have for some space be do secret in Liampoo Chincheo the portugal go by little and little forward and begin to go and which be very far from Cantan without the king be wit or have knowledge of this traffic the matter fall out in such sort that the portugal winter in the land of Liampoo some chinaes that be among the portugal and some portugal with they disorder of outrageous Chinois and insolent portugal come to disorder themselves in such manner that they make great stealth and robbery and kill some of the people these evil increase so much that the clamour of the injure be so great that it come not only to the superior Louthias of the province but also to the King who command present to make a very great armada in the province of fuquen to drive the thief from all the coast especial those that be about Liampoo and all the merchant as well Portugal as chinaes be repute in this number of thief be ready they go forth along the coast of the Sea and because the wind serve they not for to go for Liampoo they go to the coast of Chincheo where find some sh^p^ of portugal they begin to fight with they and in no wise do they permit any ware to come to the portugal who stay many day there fight sometime to see if they can have any remedy for to dispatch their business but see they have no remedy they determine to go without it the captain of the army know this send a message to they very secret by night that if they will that any good shall come to they that they shall send they something the portugal very glad with this message prepare a great and sumptuous present bribery and send it they by night because they be so advise from thenceforward come many good unto they the Louthias make as though they take no heed thereof dissemble with the merchant and so be the business end that year which be the year 1548. the year follow which be 1549. there be a straight watch upon the coast by the captain of the armada and great vigilancy in the port and entrance of China in such sort that neither good nor victual come to the portugal but for all the vigilancy and watch there be as the land along the coast be many for they all run in a rue along the china the army can not have so much vigilancy that some ware be not bring secret to the portugal but they be not so many that they can make as well in the town as out of they temple of idol in all the ship they sail in they make present a place for to worship in where they carry their idol lot in all thing they be to enterprise either journey by sea or by land they use lot and cast they before their god the lot be two stick make like half a nutshell flat on the one side and round on the other and as big again as a half nut and join with a string and when they will cast lot they speak first with their God persuade he with word and promise he some offer if he give he a good lot and in it show he his good voyage or good success of his business and after many word they cast the lot and if both the flat side fall upward or one up another down they hold it for a evil lot and turn they towards their god very melancholy they call they dog with many other reproach after they be weary of rate they they soothe they again with fair mild word and ask pardon say that the melancholy of not give they a good lot cause they to do they injury and speak injurious word unto he but that they will pardon they and give they a good lot and they promise to offer he more such a thing because the promise be the better for they that promise they they make many and great promise and offering and so they cast lot so many time till they fall both on the flat side which they hold for a good lot then remain well content they offer to their god that which they promise cruel man to their foolish god it happen many time when they cast lot about any weighty matter if the lot fall not out good or launch a ship to the sea it go not well and some evil come to it they run to their god and cast they in the water and put they in the flame of the fire sometime and let they scorch a little and spurn they often and tread they under foot and give they rail word till their business be end and then they carry they with play and feast and give they their offering offering they hold for a great offer a hog head boil they offer hen goose duck and rice all dress and a great pot of wine after they present it all to the god they set his portion apart which be to put in a dish the small point of the hog ear the bill and the point of the claw these thing say the base people the better sort say they worship he because he shall do they no hurt when they will launch any new ship to the sea their priest be call by they come into the ship to do all the land great feast they visit one another the chief principal do make great banquet how much these people be curious in the rule and government of the country and in their common traffic so much they be beastly in their gentility in the usage of their god and idolatry traditional fable for beside that which be say they have many gentilicall lie of man that be turn into dog and afterward into man and of snake that be convert into man and many other ignorance I enter one day into a temple and come to a altar where be certain stone set up which they worship and trust in the little estimation they hold their god in and in be man that will be satisfy with reason I throw the stone down to the ground whereat some run very fierce at i and angry ask i wherefore I have do that I go mild to they and smile say to they because they be so inconsiderate that they worship those stone they ask i wherefore shall they not adore they and I show they how they be better than they see they have the use of reason foot hand and eye wherewith they do diverse thing that the stone can not do and that see they be better they shall not abase and esteem so little of themselves as to worship thing so vile they be so noble they answer i that I have reason and go out with i in company leave the stone on the ground so that there be likelihood and show of their become christian and it make also much to this purpose their not make any difference of meat as all the people of India do and see that among all the meat they esteem the pork most it be almost impossible for they to become Turk notwithstanding there be two very great inconvenience to make any christian in this country the one be that in no wise they will permit any novelty in the country as in some sort it may be see in the matter of the moor no novelty so that whatsoever novelty that be in the country the Louthias take order present how to repress it and it go no further whence it happen in Cantan because they see a Portugal measure the entry of the gate they set present watch that none shall come in without licence nor go upon the wall the second be that no strange person may enter into China without leave of the Louthias nor be in Cantan which do give he a certain time to be in Cantan the time of the licence end provision against stay of stranger present they labour to have they depart wherefore because I and those which be with i be one month long in cantan they set up write board that none shall keep nor harbour we in their house under pain of so much till we hold it our best cheap to go to the ship to the abovesaid be join the common people to be great in fear of the Louthias wherefore none of they dare become a christian without their licence or at the least many will not do it therefore as a man can be seel in the country he can continue preach and by consequence he can fructify and preserve the fruit there be notwithstanding one way how to preach free and fruit may be make in the country without any dog bark at the preacher nor any Louthia do he hurt any way which be if he have a licence for it of the king notes and it may be obtain of a solemn embassage be send with a solemn present see they but abbreviated to prevent tediousness chap. 11 the relation of Galeotto PERERA a gentleman of good credit that lie prisoner in China this land of China be part into thirteen * * you shall have a more full description of the country by late author who yet can not so well as this tell their judicial proceed severity prison execution etc. these 13. be to be understand beside the two royal province Pachin pochang or Paquin or Pequim shire which sometime be each one a kingdom by itself but these many year they have be all subject unto one King the king make always his abode in the great city Pachin as much to say in our language as by the name thereof I be advertise the * * Cambalu signify the same and so the mogoll call this city post horse their month excellent wall and a admirable bridge town of the kingdom this kingdom be so large that under five month you be not able to travel from the town by the sea side to the court and back again no not under three month in post at your urgent business the post-horse in this country be little of body but swift of foot many do travel the great part of this journey by water in certain light bark for the multitude of river commodious for passage from one city to another the king notwithstanding the hugeness of his kingdom have such a care thereof that every moon by the moon they reckon their month he be advertise full of whatsoever thing happen therein before that we do come to Cinceo we have to pass through many place and some of great importance for this country be so well inhabit near the sea side that you can go one mile but you shall see some town borough or hostrie the which be so abundant provide of all thing that in the city and town they live civil nevertheless such as dwell abroad be very poor for the multitude of they every where so great that out of a tree you shall see many time swarm a number of child where a man will not have think to have find any one at all from these place in number infinite you shall come unto two city very populous and be compare with Cinceo not possible to be discern which be the great of they these city be as well wall as any city in all the world as you come into either of they stand so great and mighty a bridge that the like thereof I have never see in Portugal nor else where I hear one of my fellow say that he tell in one bridge forty arch the occasion wherefore these bridge be make so great be for that the country be towards the sea very plain and low and overwhelm ever as the sea-water increase the breadth of the bridge although it be well proportion unto the length thereof yet be they equal build no high in the middle than at either end in such wise that you may direct see from the one end to the other the side be wonderful well engrave after the manner of Rome work magnificent stone but that we do most marvel at be therewithal the hugeness of the stone the like whereof as we come into the city we do see many set up in place dishabit by the way to no small charge of they howbeit to little purpose whereas no body see they but such as do come by the arch be not make after our fashion vault with sundry stone set together but pave as it be whole stone reach from one pillar to another in such wise that they lie both for the arch head and gallant serve also for the highway I have be astonish to behold the hugeness of these aforesaid stone some of they be twelve pace long and upward the least eleven good pace long and a half the way each where be gallant pave with foure-square stone except it be where for want of stone they use to lay brick in this voyage we travel over certain hill way pave brick or pitch where the way be pitch and in many place no worse pave than in the plain ground the country be so well inhabit that no one foot of ground be leave untilled Culture and husbandry small store of cattle have we see this way we see only certain ox wherewithal the countryman do plough their ground one ox draw the plough alone not only in this shire but in other place also wherein be great store of cattle these countryman by art do that in tillage which we be constrain to do by force here be sell the voyding of closestool although there want not the dung of beast and the excrement of man be good merchandise throughout all china the dung-fermers seek in every street by exchange to buy their dirty ware for herb and wood the custom be very good for keep the city clean there be great abundance of hen goose duck swine and goat weather have they none the hen be sell by weight and so be all other thing two pound of hen flesh goose or duck be worth two of their money that be three half penny swine flesh be sell at a penny the pound beef bear the same price for the scarcity thereof howbeit northward from Fuquico and further from the sea coast there be beef more plenty and sell better cheap beef only except great abundance of all these viand we have have in all the city we pass through and if this country be like unto India the inhabitant whereof eat neither hen beef nor pork but keep that only for the portugal and moor they will be sell here for nothing but it so fall out that the chinean be the great eater in all the world they do feed upon all thing special upon pork the fat that be unto they the less loathsome the high price of these thing aforesaid I have set down better cheap shall you sometime buy they for the great plenty thereof in this country frog be sell at the same price that be make of hen and be good meat among they as also dog cat rat snake and all other unclean meat building of the city the city be very gallant special near unto the gate the which be marvellous great and cover with iron the gatehouse build on high with tower the low part thereof be make of brick and stone proportional with the wall from the wall upward the building be of timber and many story in it one above the other the strength of their town be in the mighty wall and ditch no artillery large street artillery have they none the street in Cinceo and in all the rest of the city we have see be very fair so large and so straight that it be wonderful to behold their house be build with timber the foundation only except the which be lay with stone in each side of the street be paintese (@) continual porch for the merchant to walk under the breadth of the street be nevertheless such that in they fifteen man may ride commodious side by side as they ride they must needs pass under many high arch of triumph archer that cross over the street make of timber and carve diverse cover with tile of fine clay under these arch the mercer do utter their small ware and such as lift to stand there be defence from rain and the heat of the sun the great gentleman have these arch at their door although some of they be not so mighty build as the rest I shall have occasion to speak of a certain order of gentleman that be call Loutea I will first therefore expound what this word signify Loutea be as much to say in our language as sir and when any of they call his name he answer Sir the manner how gentleman be create Louteas and do come to that honour and title be by give a broad girdle not like to the rest and a cap at the commandment of the King the name Loutea be more general and common unto more than equality of honour thereby signify agree withal such Louteas that do serve their prince in weighty matter for justice be create after trial make of their learning but the other which serve in small affair as captain constable sergeant by land and sea receiver and such like whereof there be in every city as also in this very many be make for favour the chief Louteas be serve kneel the whole province China be divide as I have say into thirteen shire in every shire at the least be one governor chian al. Chaen call there Tutan in some shire there be two chief in office next unto they be certain other name chian that be high commissioner as you will say or visiter with full authority in such wise that they do call unto a account the tutane themselves but their authority last not in any shire long than one year nevertheless in every shire be at the least seven city yea in some of they fifteen or sixteen beside other borough and town not well to be number these visiter where they come be so honour and fear as though they be some great prince at the year end their circuit do they come unto that city which be chief of other in the shire to do justice there final busy themselves in the search out of such as be to receive the order of Louteas whereof more shall be say in another place over and beside these officer in the chief city of each one of these aforesaid thirteen province be resident one Ponchiassi captain thereof and treasurer of all the king revenue this magistrate make his abode in one of the four great house that be in all these head city in the second great house dwell another magistrate al. Tuzi call Anchiassi a great officer also for he have deal in all matter of justice Tuzi another officer so call lie in the three house a magistrate of importance special in thing belong unto warfare for thereof have he charge there be resident in the four house a four officer bear name in this house be the principal prison of all the city each one of these magistrate aforesaid may both lay evil doer in prison prison and sentence offender and deliver they out again except the fact be heinous and of importance in such a case they can do nothing except they do meet altogether and if the deed deserve death all they together can determine thereof without recourse make unto the chian wheresoever he be or to the Tutan and eftsoon it fall out that the case be refer unto high power in all city not only chief in each shire but in the rest also be mean find to make Louteas Louteas commencement or act. many of they do study at the prince his charge wherefore at the year end they resort unto the head city whither the chian do come as it have be erst say as well to give these degree as to sit in judgement over the prisoner the chian go in circuit every year but such as be to be choose to the great office meet not but from three year to three year and that in certain large hall appoint for they to be examine in many thing be ask they whereunto if they do answer according and be find sufficient to take their degree the chian by and by grant it they but the cap and girdle whereby they be know to the Louteas they wear not before that they be confirm by the King their examination do and trial make of they such as have take their degree wont to be give they with all ceremony use to banquet and feast many day together as the chinean fashion be to end all their pleasure with eat and drink and so remain choose to do the king service in matter of learning the other examinate find insufficient to proceed be send back to their study again who ignorance be perceive to come of negligence and default such a one be whip and sometime send to prison where we lie that year when this kind of act be we find many thus punish and demand the cause thereof they say it be for that they know not how to answer unto certain thing ask they it be a world to see how these Louteas be serve and fear in such wise their majesty that in public assembly at one shriek they give all the servitor belong unto justice tremble thereat at their be in these place when they lift to move be it but even to the gate these servitor do take they up and carry they in seat of beat Gold after this sort be they bear when they go in the city either for their own business abroad or to see each other at home for the dignity they have and office they do bear they be all accompany the very mean of they all that go in these seat be usher by two man at the least that cry unto the people to give place howbeit they need it not for that reverence the common people have unto they they have also in their company certain sergeant with their mace either silver or altogether silver some two some four other six other eight convenient for each one his degree the more principal and chief Louteas have go orderly before these sergeant many other with staff and a great many catchpole with rod of indian cane drag to the ground so that the street be pave you may here a far off as well the noise of the rod as the voice of the crier these fellow serve also to apprehend other and the better to be know they wear liverie-red girdle and in their cap peacock feather behind these Louteas come such as do bear certain table hang at staff end wherein be write in silver letter the name degree and office of that Loutea who they follow in like manner they have bear after they hat agreeable unto their title if the Loutea be mean then have be bring after he but one hat and that may not be yellow but if he be of better sort then may he have two three or four the principal and chief Louteas may have all their hat yellow the which among they be account great honour the Loutea for war although he be but mean may notwithstanding have yellow hat the tutane and chian when they go abroad have beside all this before they lead three or four horse with their guard in armour furthermore the Louteas yea and all the people in China be wont to eat their meat sit on stool at high table as we do and that very clean manner of eat although they use neither table-clothe nor napkin whatsoever be set down upon the board be first carve before that it be bring in they feed with two stick refrain from touch their meat with their hand even as we do with fork for the which respect they less do need any table-clothe neither be the nation only civil at meat we that be the italian and spaniard but also in conversation and in courtesy they seem to exceed all other likewise in their deal after their manner they be so ready that they far pass all other gentile and moor the great state be so vain that they line their clothes with the best silk that may be find the Louteas be a idle generation without all manner of exercise and pastime except it be eat and drink sometime they walk abroad in the field to make the soldier shoot at prick with their bow but their eat pass they will stand eat even when the other do draw to shoot the prick be a great blanket spread on certain long pole he that strike it shoot have of the best man there stand a piece of crimson taffeta the which be knit about his head in this sort the winner be honour and the Louteas with their belly full return home again the inhabitant of China be very idolater all general do worship the heaven and as we be wont to say God know it so say they at every word Tien Tautee that be to say idolatry the heaven do know it some do worship the sun and some the moon as they think good for none be bind more to one then to another in their temple the which they do call they have a great altar in the same place as we have true it be that one may go round about it there set they up the image of a certain Loutea of that country who they have in great reverence for certain notable thing he do at the right hand stand the devil much more ugly paint then we do use to set he out whereunto great homage be do by such as come into the temple to ask counsel or to draw lot this opinion they have of he that he be malicious and able to do evil if you ask they what they do think of the soul depart they will answer that they be immortal and that as soon as any one depart out of this life he become a devil if he have live well in this world if otherwise that the same devil change he into a bufle ox or Dog wherefore to this devil do they much honour to he do they sacrifice pray he that he will make they like unto himself and not like other beast they have moreover another sort of temple wherein both upon the altar and also on the wall do stand many idol well proportion but bare head these bear name Omithofon account of they spirit but such as in heaven do neither good nor evil think to be such man and woman as have chaste live in this world in abstinence from fish and flesh devil mos^ respect feed only with rice and Salates of that devil they make some account for these spirit they care little or nothing at all again they hold opinion that if a man do well in this life the heaven will give he many temporal blessing but if he do evil then shall he have infirmity disease trouble and penury and all this without any knowledge of God final this people know no other thing then to live and die yet because they be reasonable creature all seem good unto they we speak in our language though it be not very sufficient our manner of pray so well like they that in prison importunate they beseech we to write for they somewhat as concern heaven the which we do to their contentation with such reason as we know so do the roman augury sodomy frequent new and full moon howbeit not very cunning as they do their idolatry they laugh at themselves the great fault we do find in they be sodomy a vice very common in the mean sort and nothing strange among the best furthermore the Louteas withal the people of China be wont to solemnize the day of the new and full moon in visit one each other and make great banquet for to that end as I have say do tend all their pastime and spend their day in pleasure birthday they be wont also to solemnize each one his birth day whereunto their kindred and friend do resort of custom with present of jewel or money receive again for their reward good cheer they keep in like manner a general feast with great banquet that day their king be bear new year day but their most principal and great feast of all and best cheer be the first day of their new year namely the first day of the new moon of February so that their first month be march and they reckon the time according respect be have unto the reign of their prince as when any deed be write they date it thus make such a day of such a moon and such a year of the reign of such a King justi^e now will I speak of the manner the which the chinean do observe in do justice because the chinish king make his abode continual in the city Pachin his kingdom so great the shire so many as before it have be say in it therefore the governor and ruler much like unto our sheriff be so appoint sudden and speedy discharge again that they have no time to grow nought furthermore to keep the state in more security the Louteas that govern one shire be choose out of some other shire distant far off where they must leave their wife child and good carry nothing with they but themselves true it be that at their come thither they do find in a readiness all thing necessary their house furniture servant and all other thing in such perfection and plenty that they want nothing thus king be well serve without all fear of treason in the principal city of the shire be four chief Louteas before who be bring all matter of the inferior town throughout the whole realm diverse other Louteas have the manage of justice and receive of rent bind to yield a account thereof unto the great officer other do see that there be no evil rule keep in the city each one as it behove he general all these do imprison malefactor cause they to be whip and rack hoist they up and down by the arm with a cord a thing very usual there and account no shame these Louteas do use great diligence in the apprehend of the thief so that it be a wonder to see a thief escape away in any town the italian call it the strappado hard prison beat with cane city or village upon the sea near unto the shore many be take and look even as they be take so be they first whip and afterward lay in prison where short after they all die for hunger and cold at that time when we be in prison there die of they above threescore and ten their whip be certain piece of cane cleave in the middle in such sort that they seem rather plain then sharp he that be to be whip lie grovel on the ground upon his thigh the hangman lay on blow mighty with these cane that the stander by tremble at their cruelty ten stripe draw a great deal of blood twenty or thirty spoil the flesh altogether fifty or threescore will require long time to be heal and if they come to the number of one hundred then be they incurable the Louteas observe moreover this when any man be bring before they to be examine they ask he open in the hear of as many as be present examination be the offence never so great thus do they also behave themselves with we for this cause among they can there be no false witness as daily among we it fall out this good come thereof that many be always about the judge to hear the evidence and bear witness the process can be falsify as it happen sometime with we the moor gentile and jew have all their sundry oath the moor do swear by their Mossafos oath the brahmin by their the rest likewise by the thing they do worship the chinean though they be wont to swear by heaven by the moon by the sun and by all their idol in judgement nevertheless they swear not at all if for some offence a oath be use of any one by and by with the least evidence he be torment so be the witness he bring if they tell not the truth or do in any point disagree except they be man of worship and credit who be believe without any far matter the rest be make to confess the truth by force of torment and whip beside this order observe of they in examination they do fear so much their king and he where he make his abode keep they so low that they dare not once stir again these Louteas as great as they be notwithstanding the multitude of notary they have not trust any other do write all great process and matter of importance themselves patient hear moreover one virtue they have worthy of great praise and that be be man so well regard and account of as though they be prince they be patient above measure in give audience we poor stranger bring before they may say what we will as all to be lie and falace that they do write nor do we stand before they with the usual ceremony of that country yet do they bear with we so patient that they cause we to wonder know special how little any advocate or judge be wont in our country to bear with we for wheresoever in any town of Christendom shall be accuse unknown man as we be I know not what end the very innocent cause will have but we in a heathen country have our great enemy two of the chief man in a whole town want a interpreter ignorant of that country language severe justice do in the end see our great adversary cast into prison for our sake and deprive of their office and honour for not do justice yea not to escape death for as the rumour go they shall be behead somewhat be now to be say of the law that I have be able to know in this country law and first no theft or murder be at any time pardon adulterer be put in prison and the fact once prove condemn to die the woman husband must accuse they this order be keep with man and woman find in that fault but thief and murderer be imprison as I have say where they short die for hunger and cold if any one haply escape by bribe the jailor to give he meat his process go far and come to the court where he be condemn to die sentence be give a pillory board the prisoner be bring in public with a terrible band of man that lay he in iron hand and foot with a board at his neck one handful broad in length reach down to his knee cleave in two part and with a hole one handful downward in the table fit for his neck the which they enclose up therein nail the board fast together one handful of the board stand up behind in the neck the sentence and cause wherefore the felon be condemn to die be write in that part of the table show unto we Seynam in 70. degree that the island be call Seynam which be the latitude of seventy degree and from stanfew thirty league be also under the king of Denmark and that there be no good harbour and on the next day a pilot to bring we to Finmarke unto the wardhouse which be the strong hold in Finmark and most resort to by report but when he will have enter into a harbour the land be very high on every side there come such flaw of wind and terrible whirlwind that we be not able to bear in but by violence be constrain to take the sea again our pinnace be unshipt we sail north and by east the wind increase so sore that we be not able to bear any sail but take they in and lay adrift to the end to let the storm overpass and that night by violence of wind and thickness of mist we be not able to keep together within sight and then about midnight we lose our pinnace the Edward lose or rather the^e two lose and the Edward find and enter the bay of saint Nicolas which be a discomfort unto we as soon as it be day and the fog overpass we look about and at the last we descry one of our ship to lee-ward off we then we spread a hullocke of our foresail and bare room with she which be the confidence but the Edward we can not see then the flaw something abate we and the confidence hoist up our sail the four day sail north-east and by north to the end to fall with the ward-house as we do consult to do before in case we shall part company thus run north-east and by north and north-east fifty league than we found and have one hundred and sixty fathom whereby we think to be far from land and perceive that the land lie not as the globe make mention wherefore we change our course the six day and sail southeast and by south eight and forty league think thereby to find the ward-house the eight day much wind rise at the west northwest we not know how the coast lie strike our sail and lay adrift where sound and find one hundred and sixty fathom as before the nine day the wind bear to the south southeast we sail north-east five and twenty league the ten day we sound and can get no ground neither yet can see any land whereat we wonder then the wind come at the north-east we run southeast about eight and forty league the eleven day the wind be at south we sound and find forty fathom and fair sand the twelve day the wind be at south and by east we lay with our sail east and east and by north thirty league the fourteen day early in the morning we descry land which land we bear withal hoist out our boat to discover what land it may be but the boat can not come to land the water be so shallow where be very much ice also but there be no similitude of habitation willoughby his land in 72. degree and this land lie from Seynam east and by north one hundred and sixty league be in latitude 72. degree then we ply to the northward the fifteen sixteen and seventeen day the eighteen day the wind come at the north-east and the confidence be trouble with bilge water and stock we think it good to seek harbour for her redress then we bare room the eighteen day south southeast about seventy league the one and twenty day we sound and find ten fathom after that we sound again and find but seven fathom so shallow and shallow water and yet can see no land whereat we marvel great to avoid this danger we bare roomer into the sea all that night northwest and by west the next day we sound and have twenty fathom then shape our course and run west south-west until the three and twenty day then we descry low land unto which we bear as nigh as we can and it appear unto we unhabitable then we ply westward along by that land which lie west south-west and east north-east and much wind blow at the west we hale into the sea north and by east thirty league then the wind come about at the north-east we sail west northwest after that the wind bear to the northwest we lay with our sail west south-west about fourteen league and then descry land and bare in with it be the eight and twenty day find shallow water and bare in till we come to three fathom then perceive it to be shallow water and also see dry sand we hale out again north-east along that land until we come to the point thereof that land turn to the westward we run along sixteen league northwest then come into a fair bay we go on land with our boat which place be uninhabited but yet it appear unto we that the people have be there by cross and other sign from thence we go all along the coast westward the four day of September we lose sight of land by reason of contrary wind September and the eight day we descry land again within two day after we lose the sight of it then run west and by south about thirty league we get the sight of land again and bare in with it until night then perceive it to be a lee shore we get we into the sea to the end to have sea room the twelve of September we hale to shoareward again have then indifferent wind and weather then be near unto the shore and the tide almost spend we come to a anchor in thirty fathom water the thirteen day we come along the coast which lie northwest and by west and southeast and by east the fourteen day we come to a anchor within two league off the shore have sixty fathom there we go ashore with our boat and find two or three good harbour the land be rocky and high but as for people can we see none the fifteen day we run still along the coast until the seventeen day then the wind be contrary unto we we think it best to return unto the harbour which we have find before and so we bare roomer with the same howbeit we can not accomplish our desire that day the next day be the eighteen we enter into the haven and there come to a anchor at six fathom this haven run into the main about two league in this haven they die and be in breadth half a league wherein be very many seale-fish and other great fish and upon the main we see bear great deer fox and diverse strange beast as * * or Ellons guloine and such other which be to we unknown and also wonderful thus remain in this haven the space of a week see the year far spend and also very evil weather as frost snow and hail as though it have be the deep of winter we think best to winter there wherefore we send out three man south south-west to search if they can find people who go three day journey but can find none after that we send other three westward four day journey which also return without find any people here end sir Hugh Willoughby his note which be write with his own hand then send we three man southeast three day journey who in like sort return without find of people or any similitude of habitation the river or haven wherein sir Hugh Willoughby with the company of his two ship perish for cold be call Arzina in Lapland near unto Kegor but it appear by a will find in a ship that sir Hugh Willoughby and most of the company be alive in january 1554. a letter of richard chancellor write to his uncle master CHRISTOPHER FROTHINGAM touch his discovery of Moscovia forasmuch as it be meet and necessary for all those that mind to take in hand the travel into strange country to endeavour themselves not only to understand the order commodity and fruitfulness thereof but also to apply they to the set forth of the same whereby it may encourage other to the like travel therefore have I now think good to make a brief rehearsal of the order of this my travel in Russia and Muscovia and other country thereunto adjoin because it be my chance to fall with the north part of Russia before I come towards Moscovia I will partly declare my knowledge therein Russia be very plentiful both of land and people and also wealthy for such commodity as they have they be very great fisher for salmon and small cod they have much oil which we call Trane oil the most whereof be make by a river call D^ina they make it in other place but not so much as there they have also a great trade in seethe of salt water to the north part of that country be the place where they have their fur as sable Marterns bever fox white black and red minx ermine Miniver and heart there be also a fish tooth which fish be call a morsse the taker thereof dwell in a place call Postesora which bring they upon heart to lampas to sell note and from lampas carry they to a place call Colmogro where the high market be hold on saint Nicolas day to the west of Colmogro there be a place call gratanove in our language novogorode where much fine flax and hemp grow and also much wax and honey the dutch merchant have a staple-house there there be also great store of hide and at a place call Plesco and thereabouts be great store of flax hemp wax honey and that town be from colmogro one hundred and twenty mile there be a place call Vologda the commodity whereof be tallow wax and flax but not so great plenty as be in gratanove from Vologda to Colmogro there run a river call Duina and from thence it fall into the Sea Colmogro serve gratanove Vologda and the Moscow with all the country thereabouts with salt and salt Fish jeraslave from Vologda to jereslave be two hundred mile which town be very great the commodity thereof be hide and tallow and corn in great plenty and some wax but not so plentiful as in other place the Moscow be from jeraslave two hundred mile the country betwixt they be very well replenish with small village which be so well fill with people that it be wonder to see they the ground be well store with corn which they carry to the city of Moscow in such abundance that it be wonder to see it you shall meet in a morning seven or eight hundred sled come or go thither that carry corn and some carry fish you shall have some that carry corn to the Moscow and some that fetch corn from thence that at the least dwell a thousand mile off and all their carriage be on sled those which come so far dwell in the north part of the duke dominion where the cold will suffer no corn to grow it be so extreme they bring thither fish fur and beast skin in those part they have but small store of cattle Moscow the Moscow itself be great I take the whole town to be great than London with the suburb but it be very rude and stand without all order their house be all of timber very dangerous for fire there be a fair castle the wall whereof be of brick and very high they say they be eighteen foot thick but I do not believe it it do not so seem notwithstanding I do not certain know it for no stranger may come to view it the one side be ditch and on the other side run a river call Mos^ua which run into Tartary and so into the sea call mare caspium and on the north side there be a base town the which have also a brick wall about it and so it join with the castle wall the castle the emperor lie in the castle wherein be nine fair church and therein be religious man also there be a metropolitan with diverse bishop I will not stand in description of their building nor of the strength thereof because we have better in all point in England they be well furnish with ordnance of all sort the emperor or duke house neither in building nor in the outward show nor yet within the house be so sumptuous as I have see it be very low build in eight square much like the old build of England with small window and so in other point now to declare my come before his majesty after I have remain twelve day the secretary which have the hear of stranger do send for i advertise i that the duke pleasure be to have i to come before his majesty with the king my master letter whereof I be right glad and so I give my attendance he come before the duke and when the duke be in his place appoint the interpreter come for i into the outer chamber where sit one hundred or more gentleman all in cloth of gold very sumptuous and from thence I come into the counsel-chamber where sit the duke himself with his noble which be a fair company they sit round about the chamber on high yet so that he himself sit much high than any of his noble in a chair gilt and in a long garment of beat gold with a imperial crown upon his head and a staff of crystal and gold in his right hand and his other hand half le^ning on his chair the chancellor stand up with the secretary before the duke after my duty do and my letter deliver he bid i welcome and inquire of i the health of the king my master and I answer that he be in good health at my departure from his court and that my trust be that he be now in the same upon the which he bid i to dinner the chancellor present my present unto his grace bareheaded for before they be all cover and when his grace have receive my letter I be require to depart for I have charge not to speak to the duke but when he speak to i so I depart unto the secretary chamber where I remain two hour and then I be send for again unto another palace which be call the golden palace but I see no cause why it shall be so call for I have see many fair than it in all point and so I come into the hall which be small and not great as be the king majesty of England and the table be cover with a tablecloth and the marshal sit at the end of the table with a little white rod in his hand which board be full of vessel of gold and on the other side of the hall do stand a fair cupboard of plate dine with the duke from thence I come into the dine chamber where the duke himself sit at his table without cloth of estate in a gown of silver with a crown imperial upon his head he sit in a chair somewhat high there sit none near he by a great way there be long table set round about the chamber which be full set with such as the duke have at dinner they be all in white also the place where the table stand be high by two step then the rest of the house in the midst of the chamber stand a table or cupboard to set plate on which stand full of cup of gold and among all the rest there stand four marvelous great pot or crudence as they call they of gold and silver I think they be a good yard and a half high by the cupboard stand two gentleman with napkin on their shoulder golden vessel and in their hand each of they have a cup of gold set with pearl and precious stone which be the duke own drink cup when he be dispose he drink they off at a draught and for his service at meat it come in without order yet it be very rich service for all be serve in gold not only be himself but also all the rest of we and it be very massy the cup also be of gold and very massy the number that dine there that day be two hundred person shiver of Bread and all be serve in golden vessel the gentleman that wait be all in cloth of gold and they serve he with their cap on their head before the service come in the duke send to every man a great shiver of bread and the bearer call the party so send to by his name aloud and say John Basilivich emperor of Russia and great duke of Moscovia do reward thou with bread then must all man stand up and do at all time when those word be speak and then last of all he give the marshal bread whereof he eat before the duke grace and so do reverence and depart then come the duke service of the swan all in piece and every one in a several dish the which the duke send as he do the bread and the bearer say the same word as he say before and as I say before the service of his meat be in no order but come in dish by dish and then after that the duke send drink with the like say as before be tell crown change also before dinner he change his crown and in dinner time two crown so that I see three several crown upon his head in one day and thus when his service be all come in he give to every one of his gentleman waiter meat with his own hand and so likewise drink his intent thereby be as I have hear that every man shall know perfect his servant thus when dinner be do he call his noble before he name by name that it be wonder to hear how he can name they have so many as he have thus when dinner be do I depart to my lodging which be a hour within night I will leave this and speak no more of he nor his household but I will somewhat declare of his land and people with their nature and power in the war duke force this duke be lord and emperor of many country and his power be marvelous great for he be able to bring into the field two or three hundred thousand man he never go into the field himself with under two hundred thousand man and when he go himself he furnish his border all with man of war which be no small number he leave on the border of Liefland forty thousand man and upon the border of letto sixty thousand man and towards the nagayan Tartar sixty thousand which be wonder to hear of yet do he never take to his war neither husbandman nor merchant all his man be horseman he use no footman but such as go with the ordnance and labourer which be thirty thousand the horseman be all archer with such bow as the turk have and they ride short as do the turk armour and rich attire their armour be a coat of plate with a skull on their head some of their coat be cover with velvet or cloth of God their desire be to be sumptuous in the field and especial the noble and gentleman as I have hear their trim be very costly and partly I have see it or else I will scarce have believe it but the duke himself be rich attire above all measure his pavilion be cover either with cloth of gold or silver and so set with stone that it be wonderful to see it I have see the king majesty of England and the french king pavilion which be fair yet not like unto he and when they be send into far or strange country or that stranger come to they they be very gorgeous else the duke himself go but mean in apparel and when he go betwixt one place and another he be but reasonable apparel over other time in the while that I be in Moscow the duke send two ambassador to the king of P^leland which have at the leave five hundred horse their sumptuousness be above measure not only in themselves but also in their horse as velvet cloth of gold and cloth of silver set with pearl and not scant what shall I further say I never hear of nor see man so sumptuous but it be no daily guise for when they have not occasion as I say before extreme all their do be but mean and now to the effect of their war vndisciplined soldier they be man without all order in the field for they run hurl on heap and for the most part they never give battle to their enemy but that which they do they do it all by stealth but I believe they be such man for hard live as be not under the sun for no cold will hurt they yea and though they lie in the field two month hardiness at such time as it shall freeze more than a yard thick the common soldier have neither tent nor any thing else over his head the most defence they have against the weather be a feel which be set against the wind and weather and when snow come he do cast it off and make he a fire and lay he down thereby thus do the most of all his man except they be gentleman which have other provision of their own their lie in the field be not so strange as be their hardness for every man must carry and make provision for himself and his horse for a month or two which be very wonderful for he himself shall live upon water and oatmeal mingle together cold and drink water thereto his horse shall eat green wood and such like baggage and shall stand open in the cold field without covert and yet will he labour and serve he right well I pray you among all our boast warrior how many shall we find to endure the field with they but one month I know no such region about we that bear that name for man and beast now what may be make of these man if they be train and break to order and knowledge of civil war if this prince have within his country such man as can make they to understand the thing aforesaid I do believe that two of the best or great prince in Christendom be not well able to match with he consider the greatness of his power and the hardness of his people and straight live both of people and horse and the small charge which his war stand he in for he give no wage except to stranger they have a yearly stipend and not much as for his own countryman every one serve of his own proper cost and charge save that he give to his harquebusier certain allowance for powder and shot or else no man in all his country have one penny wage knight Fee but if any man have do very good service he give he a farm or a piece of land for the which he be bind at all time to be ready with so many man as the duke shall appoint who consider in his mind what that land or farm be well able to find and so many shall he be bind to furnish at all and every such time as war be hold in any of the duke dominion for there be no man of live but he be bind likewise whether the duke call for either soldier or labourer to furnish they with all such necessary as to they belong duke heir general also if any gentleman or man of live do die without issue male immediate after his death the duke enter his land notwithstanding he have never so many daughter and peradventure give it forthwith to another man except a small portion that he spare to marry the daughter withal also if there be a rich man a farmer or man of live which be strike in age or by chance be maim and be not able to do the duke service some other gentleman that be not able to live and more able to do service will come to the duke and complain say your grace have such a one which be unmeet to do service to your highness who have great abundance of wealth and likewise your grace have many gentleman which be poor and lack live and we that lack be well able to do good service your grace may do well to look upon he and make he to help those that want immediate the duke send forth to inquire of his wealth and if it be so prove he shall be call before the duke and it shall be say unto he friend you have too much live and be unserviceable to your prince less will serve you and the rest will serve other man that be more able to serve whereupon immediate his live shall be take away from he save a little to find himself and his wife on and he may not once repine thereat but for answer he will say that he have nothing but it be god and the duke grace and can say as we the common people in England say if we have any thing that it be god and our own man may say that these man be in wonderful great awe and obedience that thus one must give and grant his good which he have be scrape and scratch for all his life to be at his prince pleasure and commandment oh that our sturdy rebel be have in the like subjection to know their duty towards their prince they may not say as some snudge in England say I will find the queen a man to serve in my place or make his friend tarry at home if many have the upper hand no no it be not so in this country for he shall make humble suit to serve the duke and who he send most to the war he think he be most in his favour and yet as I before have say he give no wage no wage if they know their strength no man be able to make match with they for they that dwell near they shall have any rest of they but I think it be not god will for I may compare they to a young horse that know not his strength who a little child rule and guide with a bridle for all his great strength for if he do neither child nor man can rule he their war be hold against the crimme tartarian and the nagayan I will stand no long in the rehearsal of their power and war for it be to tedious to the reader centleman but I will in part declare their law and punishment and the execution of justice and first I will begin with the commons of the country which the gentleman have rule on and that be that every gentleman have rule and justice upon his own tenant and if it so fall out that two gentleman servant or tenant do disagree the two gentleman examine the matter and have the party before they suit and trial and so give the sentence and yet can they make the end betwixt they of the controversy but e^ther of the gentleman must bring his servant or tenant before the high judge or justice of that country and there present they and declare the matter and case the plaintiff say I require the law which be grant then come a officer and arrest the party defendant and use he contrary to the law of England for when they attach any man they heat he about the leg until such time as he find surety to answer the matter and if not his hand and neck be bind together and he be lead about the town and beat about the leg with other extreme punishment till he come to his answer and the justice demand if it be for debt and say owe thou this man any such debt he will perhaps say nay then say the judge be thou able to deny it let we hear how by oath say the defendant then he command to leave beat he till further trial be have no lawyer their order in one point be commendable they have no man of law to plead their cause in any court but every man plead his own cause and give bill and answer in writing contrary to the order in England the complaint be in manner of a supplication and make to the duke grace and deliver he into his own hand require to have justice as in his complaint be allege the duke give sentence himself upon all matter in the Law which be very commendable that such a prince will take pain to see ministration of justice yet notwithstanding it be wonderful abuse and thereby the duke be much deceive but if it fall out that the officer be espy in cloak the truth they have most condign punishment and if the plaintiff can nothing prove than the defendant must take his oath upon the crucifix whether he be in the right or no. then be demand if the plaintiff be any thing able further to make proof if he be not then sometime he will say I be able to prove it by my body and hand combat-triall or by my champion body so require the campe. after the other have his oath it be grant as well to the one as to the other so when they go to the field they swear upon the crucifix that they be both in the right and that the one shall make the other to confess the truth before they depart forth of the field and so they go both to the battle arm with such weapon as they use in that country they fight all on foot and seldom the party themselves do fight except they be gentleman for they stand much upon their reputation for they will not fight but with such as be come of as good a house as themselves so that if either party require the combat it be grant unto they and no champion be to serve in their room wherein be no deceit but otherwise by champion there be for although they take great oath upon they to do the battle true yet be the contrary often see because the common champion have no other live and assoon as the one party have get the victory he demand the debt and the other be carry to prison and there be shameful use till he take order there be also another order in the law that the plaintiff may swear in some cause of debt and if the party defendant be poor he shall be set under the crucifix and the party plaintiff must swear over his head and when he have take his oath the duke take the party defendant home to his house and use he as his bondman and put he to labour bondage or let he for hire to any such as need he until such time as his friend make provision for his redemption or else he remain in bondage all the day of his life again there be many that will sell themselves to gentleman or merchant to be their bond man to have during their life meat drink and cloth punishment for crime and at their come to have a piece of money yea and some will sell their wife and child to be bawd and drudge to the buyer also they have a law for felon and picker contrary to the law of England for by their law they can hang no man for his first offence but may keep he long in prison and oftentimes beat he with whip and other punishment and there he shall remain until his friend be able to bail he if he be a picker or a cutpurse as there be very many the second time he be take he have a piece of his nose cut off and be burn in the forehead and keep in prison till he find surety for his good behaviour and if he be take the three time he be hang and at the first time he be extreme punish and not release except he have very good friend or that some gentleman require to have he to the war and in so do he shall enter into great bond for he by which mean the country be bring into good quietness but they be natural give to great deceit except extreme beat do bridle they beat they be natural give to hard live as well in fare as in lodging I hear a russian say that it be a great deal merry live in prison then forth but for the great beat for they have meat and drink without any labour and get the charity of well dispose people but be at liberty they get nothing the poor be very innumerable miserable poor and live most miserable for I have see they eat the pickle of herring and other stink fish nor the fish can be so stink nor rot but they will eat it and praise it to be more wholesome than other fish or fresh meat in my opinion there be no such people under the sun for their hardness of live well I will leave they in this point and will in part declare their religion they do observe the law of the greek with such excess of superstition superstition as the like have not be hear of they have no grave image in their church but all paint to the intent they will not break the commandment but to their paint image they use such idolatry that the like be never hear of in England image and picture they will neither worship nor honour any image that be make forth of their own country for their own image say they have picture to declare what they be and how they be of God and so be not we they say look how the painter or carver have make they so we do worship they and they worship none before they be christen they say we be but half christian because we observe not part of the old law with the turk therefore they call themselves more holy than we they have none other learning but their mother tongue mother tongue nor will suffer no other in their country among they all their service in church be in their mother tongue they have the old and new testament which be daily read among they and yet their superstition be no less service for when the priest do read they have such trick in their read that no man can understand they nor no man give ear to they for all the while the priest read the people sit down and one talk with another but when the priest be at service no man sit but gaggle and duck like so many goose and as for their prayer they have but little skill but use to say as body as much to say prayer lord have mercy upon i for the ten man within the land can say the and as for the creed no man may be so bold as to meddle therewith but in the church creed for they say it shall not be speak of but in the church speak to they of the commandment and they will say they be give to Moses in the law which Christ have now abrogate by his precious death and passion commandment therefore say they we observe little or none thereof and I do believe they for if they be examine of their law and commandment together they shall agree but in few point they have the sacrament of the lord supper in both kind and more ceremony than we have sacrament they present they in a dish in both kind together and carry they round about the church upon the priest head and so do minister at all such time as any shall require they be great offerer of candle and sometime of money which we call in England soul penny with more ceremony than I be able to declare candle they have four lent in the year whereof our Lent be the great look as we do begin on the Wednesday so they do on the Monday before and the week before that they call the butter-weeke four lent and in that week they eat nothing but butter and milk howbeit I believe there be in no other country the like people for drunkenness the next Lent be call saint Peter lent and begin always the Monday next after Trinity Sunday and end on saint Peter eeven if they shall break that fast their belief be that they shall not come in at heaven gate and when any of they die they have a testimonial with they in the coffin that when the soul come to heaven gate it may deliver the same to saint Peter which declare that the party be a true and holy russian the three Lent begin fifteen day before the late lady day and end on our lady eeven the four Lent begin on saint Martin day and end on Christmas eeven which Lent be fast for saint Philip saint peter saint Nicholas and saint Clement for they four be the principal and great saint in that country chief saint in these lent they eat neither butter egg milk nor cheese but they be very straight keep with fish cabbage and root and out of their lent they observe true the wednesday and friday throughout the year and on the Saturday they do eat flesh furthermore they have a great number of religious man which be black monk and they eat no flesh throughout the year but fish milk and butter by their order they shall eat no fresh-fish and in their lent they eat nothing but colewort cabbage salt cucumber with other root as radish and such like their drink be like our peni^ Al^ and be call quass they have service daily in their church and use to go to service two hour before day and that be end by day light at nine of the clock they go to mass that end to dinner and after that to service again and then to supper you shall understand that at every dinner and supper they have declare the exposition of the gospel that day vice but how they wrest and twine the scripture and that together by report it be wonderful as for wheredome and drunkenness there be none such live and for extortion they be the most abominable under the sun now judge of their holiness they have twice as much land as the duke himself have but yet he be reasonable even with they as thus abbey when they take bribe of any of the poor and simple he have it by a order when the abbot of any of their house die than the duke have all his good movable and unmovable so that the successor buy all at the duke hand and by this mean they be the best farmer the duke have thus with their religion I make a end trust hereafter to know it better some addition for better knowledge of this voyage take by CLEMENT adam schoolmaster to the queen henshman from the mouth of captain chancellor RIchard chancellor with his ship and company be thus leave alone and become very pensive I have this book of Clement adam in latin write in a very elegant hand and eloquent stile to king Philip as I think the very original heavy and sorrowful by this dispersion of the fleet he according to the order before take shape his course for ward-house in Norway there to expect and abide the arrival of the rest of the ship and be come thither and have stay there the space of seven day and look in vain for their come he determine at length to proceed alone in the purpose voyage and as he be prepare himself to depart it happen that he fall in company and speech with certain scottish-man who have understanding of his intention and wish well to his action begin earnest to dissuade he from the further prosecution of the discovery by amplify the danger which he be to fall into and omit no reason that may serve to that purpose but he hold nothing so ignominious and reproachful as inconstancy and levity of mind and persuade himself that a man of valour can not commit a more dishonourable part then for fear of danger to avoid and shun great attempt be nothing at all change or discourage with the speech and word of the scot remain steadfast and immutable in his first resolution determine either to bring that to pass which be intend or else to die the death and as for they which be with master chancellor in his ship although they have great cause of discomfort by the loss of their company who the foresay tempest have separate from they and be not a little trouble with cogitation and perturbation of mind in respect of their doubtful towards they fear leave through any error of he the safety of the company shall be endanger to conclude when they see their desire and hope of the arrival of the rest of the ship to be every day more the length it please God to bring they into a certain great bay which be of one hundred mile or there about over whereinto they enter and somewhat far within it cast anchor and look every way about to avoid and to flee but he still follow they at last overtake they and be come to they they be in great fear as man half dead prostrate themselves before he offer to kiss his foot but he according to his great and singular courtesy look pleasant upon they comfort they by sign and gesture refuse those duty and reverence of they and take they up in all love sort from the ground and it be strange to consider how much favour afterward in that place this humanity of his do purchase to himself for they be dismiss spread by and by a report abroad of the arrival of a strange nation of a singular gentleness and courtesy whereupon the common people come together offer to these newcome guest victual free and not refuse to traffic with they except they have be bind by a certain religious use and custom not to buy any foreign commodity without the knowledge and consent of the King by this time our man have learn that this country be call Russia or muscovie and that juan Vasiliwich which be at that time their king name rule and govern far and wide in those place and the barbarous Russ ask likewise of our man whence they be the discovery of Russia and what they come for whereunto answer be make that they be englishman scent into those coast from the most excellent king Edward the six have from he in commandment certain thing to deliver to their king and seek nothing else but his amity and friendship and traffic with his people whereby they doubt not but that great commodity and profit will grow to the subject of both kingdom the barbarian hear these thing very glad and promise their aid and furtherance to acquaint their king out of hand with so honest and a reasonable a request in the mean time master chancellor entreat victual for his money of the governor of that place who together with other come aboard he and require hostage of they likewise for the more assurance of safety to himself and his company to who the governor answer that they know not in that case the will of their king but yet be willing in such thing as they may lawful do to pleasure he which be as then to afford he the benefit of victual now while these thing be a do they secret send a messenger unto the emperor to certify he of the arrival of a strange nation messenger send to the emperor and withal to know his pleasure concern they which message be very welcome unto he insomuch that voluntary he invite they to come to his Court but if by reason of the tediousness of so long a journey they think it not best so to do than he grant liberty to his subject to bargain and to traffic with they and further promise that if it will please they to come to he he himself will bear the whole charge of post horse in the mean time the governor of the place differ the matter from day to day pretend diverse excuse and say one while that the consent of all the governor and another while that the great and weighty affair of the kingdom compel they to differ their answer and this they do of purpose so long to protract the time until the messenger send before to the king do return with relation of his will and pleasure but master chancellor see himself hold in this suspense with long and vain expectation and think that of intention to delude he they post the matter off so often be very instant with they to perform their promise which if they will not do he tell they that he will depart and proceed in his voyage so that the muscovite although as yet they know not the mind of their king yet fear the departure indeed of our man who have such ware and commodity as they great desire they at last resolve to furnish our people with all thing necessary and to conduct they by land to the presence of their King and so master chancellor begin his journey which be very long and most troublesome wherein he have the use of certain sled which in that country be very common for they be carry themselves upon sled and all their carriage be in the same sort the people almost not know any other manner of carriage the cause whereof be the exceed hardness of the ground congeal in the winter time by the force of the cold which in those place be very extreme and horrible whereof hereafter we will say something but now they have pass the great part of their journey meet at last with the sledman of who I speak before send to the king secret from the justice or governor who by some ill hap have lose his way and have go to the seaside which be near to the country of the tartar think there to have find our ship but have long err and wander out of his way at the last in his direct return he meet as he be come our captain on the way to who he by and by deliver the emperor letter which be write to he with all courtesy and in the most love manner that can be the ^ courteous journey so willing do that they begin to quarrel yea and to fight also in strive and contend which of they shall put their post horse to the sled so that after much ado and great pain take in this long and weary journey for they have travel very near fifteen hundred mile master chancellor come at last to Moscow the chief city of the kingdom and the seat of the King HONDIUS his map of Russia as ambassador from queen Elizabeth to the Muscovite voyage make by master Anthony jenkinson from the city of London towards the land of Russia begin the twelve of May in the year 1557. first by the grace of God the day and year above mention I depart from the say city and the same day at Gravesend embark myself in a good ship name the primrose be appoint although unworthy chief captain of the course north-east and by north until midnight be then clear of Yarmouth sand then we wind north and by west and north northwest until the first of june at noon than it wax calm and continue so until gold with a collar of pearl under his shirt he have linen breech upon his leg a pair of hose without foot and his boot of red or yellow leather on his head he wear a white colepeck with button or
