manner in the town he wear no weapon but only two or three pair of knife have the haft of the tooth of a fish call the Morse in the winter time the people travel with sled in town and country the way be hard and smooth with snow the water and river be all freeze and one horse with a sled will draw a man upon it four hundred mile in three day but in the summer time the way be deep with mire and travel be very ill the ruff if he be a man of any ability never go out of his house in the winter but upon his sled and in summer upon his horse and in his sled he sit upon a carpet or a white bear skin the sled be draw with a horse well deck with many fox and wolf tail at his neck and be conduct by a little boy upon his back his servant stand upon the tail of the sled etc. @. 3 note take out of another man relation of the same voyage touch the russian rite on Christmas day we be all will to dine with the emperor majesty where for bread meat and drink we be serve as at other time before but for goodly and rich plate we never see the like or so much before there dine that day in the emperor presence above five hundred stranger and two hundred Russ and all they be serve in vessel of gold and that as much as can stand one by another upon the table beside this there be four cup-board garnish with goodly plate both of gold and silver among the which there be twelve barrel of silver contain above twelve gallon a piece and at each end of every barrel be six hoop of fine gold this dinner continue about six hour the hallow of the river of Moscow every year upon the twelve day they use to bless or sanctify the river Moscua which run through the city of Moscow after this manner first they make a square hole in the ice about three fathom large every way which be trim about the side and edge with white board then about nine of the clock they come out of the church with procession towards the river in this wise first and foremost there go certain young man with wax taper burn and one carry a great lantern then follow certain banner than the cross than the image of our lady of saint Nicholas and of other saint which image man carry upon their shoulder after the image follow certain priest to the number of one hundred or more after they the metropolitan who be lead between two priest and after the metropolitan come the emperor with his crown upon his head and after his majesty all his noble man orderly thus they follow the procession unto the water and when they come unto the hole that be make the priest set themselves in order round about it and at one side of the same pool there be a scaffold of board make upon which stand a fair chair in which the metropolitan be set but the emperor majesty stand upon the ice after this the priest begin to sing to bless and to sense and do their service and so by that time that they have do the water be holy which be sanctify the metropolitan take a little thereof in his hand and cast it on the emperor likewise upon certain of the duke and then they return again to the church with the priest that sit about the water but that press that there be about the water when the emperor be go be wonderful to behold for there come above five thousand pot to be fill of that water for that Moscovite which have no part of that water think himself unhappy and very many go naked into the water both man and woman and child after the press be a little go the emperor gennet and horse be bring to drink of the same water and likewise many other man bring their horse thither to drink and by that mean they make their horse as holy as themselves all these ceremony be end we go to the emperor to dinner where we be serve in vessel of silver and in all other point as we have be beforetime the Russ begin their lent always eight week before easter the first week they eat egg the Russ Lent milk cheese and butter and make great cheer with pancake and such other thing one friend visit another and from the same Sunday until our Shrove-sunday there be but few Russ sober but they be drink day by day and it be account for no reproach or shame among they the next week be our first week in Lent or our cleanse week begin our Shrove-sunday they make and keep a great fast. it be report and the people do very believe that the metropolitan neither eat nor drink any manner of thing for the space of seven day and they say that there be many religious man which do the like the emperor majesty eat but one morsel of bread and drink but one draught of drink once in the day during that week and all man that be of any reputation come not out of their house during that time so that the street be almost void of company save a few poor folk which wander to and fro the other six week they keep as we do we but not one of they will eat either butter cheese egg or milk on Palme-sunday they have a very solemn procession in this manner follow first Palme-sunday procession they have a tree of a good bigness which be make fast upon two sled as though it be grow there and it be hang with apple raisin fig and date and with many other fruit abundant in the midst of the same tree stand five boy in white vesture which sing in the tree before the procession after this there follow certain young man with wax taper in their hand burn and a great lantern that all the light shall not go out after they follow two with long banner and six with round plate set upon long staff the plate be of copper very full of hole and thin then follow six carry paint image upon their shoulder after the image follow certain priest to the number of one hundred or more with goodly vesture whereof ten or twelve be of white damask set and embroider round about with fair and orient pearl as great as pease and among they certain saphire and other stone after they follow the one half of the emperor nobleman then come the emperor majesty and the metropolitan after this manner first there be a horse cover with white linen cloth down to the ground the emperor lead the metropolitan horse in procession his ear be make long with the same cloth like to a ass ear upon this horse the metropolitan sit side-long like a woman in his lap lie a fair book with a crucifix of goldsmith work upon the cover which he hold fast with his left hand and in his right hand he have a cross of gold with which cross he cease not to bless the people as he ride there be to the number of thirty man which spread abroad their garment before the horse and as soon as the horse be pass over any of they they take they up again and run before and spread they again so that the horse do always go on some of they they which spread the garment be all priest son and for their labour the emperor give unto they new garment one of the emperor nobleman lead the horse by the head but the emperor himself go on foot lead the horse by the end of the reign of his bridle with one of his hand and in the other of his hand he have a branch of a palm tree after this follow the rest of the emperor nobleman and gentleman with a great number of other people in this order they go from one church to another within the castle about the distance of two flight shoot and so return again to the emperor church where they make a end of their service which be do the emperor majesty and certain of his nobleman go to the metropolitan his house to dinner where of delicate fish and good drink there be no lack the rest of this week until easter day they keep very solemn continue in their house for the most part and upon Monday or Thursday the emperor do always use to receive the sacrament and so do most of his noble upon Good-friday they continue all the day in contemplation and prayer and they use every year on Good-friday to let loose a prisoner in the stead of Barrabas the night follow they go to the church where they sleep until the next morning and at easter they have the resurrection and after every of the lent they eat flesh the next week follow Friday Saturday and all they have a order at easter which they always observe and that be this every year against easter to die or colour red with brazell a great number of egg of which every man and woman give one unto the priest of their parish upon Easter day in the morning and moreover the common people use to carry in their hand one of their red egg not only upon easter day but also three or four day after and gentleman and gentlewoman have egg gild which they carry in like manner they use it as they say for a great love and in token of the resurrection whereof they rejoice for when two friend meet during the easter holy day they come and take one another by the hand the one of they say the lord or Christ be rise kiss use in the greek church the other answer it be so of a truth and then they kiss and exchange their egg both man and woman continue in kiss four day together his majesty hear all complaint himself and with his own mouth give sentence and judgement of all matter and that with expedition but religious matter he meddle not withal but refer they whole unto the metropolitan his majesty retain and well reward all stranger that come to serve he and especial man of war he delight not great in hawk hunt or any other pastime nor in hear instrument or music but set all his whole delight upon two thing first to serve God as undoubted he be very devout in his religion and the second how to subdue and conquer his enemy he have abundance of gold and silver in his own hand or treasury but the most part of his know not a crown from a counter nor gold from copper they be so much cumber therewithal and he that be worth two three or four groat be a rich man they have both monk friar and nun with a great number of great and rich monastery monastery and monk they keep great hospitality and do relieve much poor people day by day I have be in one of the monastery call Troietes which be wall about with brick very strong like a castle and much ordnance of brass upon the wall of the same they tell i themselves that there be seven hundred brethren of they which belong unto that house the most part of the land town and village which be within forty mile of it belong unto the same they show i the church image wherein be as many image as can hang about or upon the wall of the church round about and even the roof of the church be paint full of image the chief image be of our lady which be garnish with gold ruby saphire and other rich stone abundant in the midst of the church stand twelve wax taper of two yard long and a fathom about in bigness and there stand a kettle full of wax with about one hundred weight wherein there be always the wick of a candle burn as it be a lamp which go not out day nor night they show i a coffin cover with cloth of gold which stand upon one side within their church miracle in which they tell i lay a holy man who never eat or drink and yet that he live and they tell i suppose that I have believe they that he heal many disease and give the blind their sight with many other miracle but I be hard of belief because I see he work no miracle whilst I be there after this they bring i into their seller and make i taste of diverse kind of drink both wine and beer Meade and Quassie of sundry colour and kind such abundance of drink as they have in their seller drink and vessel I do suppose few prince have more or so much at once their barrel or vessel be of a unmeasurable bigness and size some of they be three yard long and more and two yard and more broad in their head they contain six or seven tun a piece they have none in their seller of their own make that be less than a ton they have nine or ten great vault which be full of those barrel which be seldom remove for they have trunk which come down through the roof of the vault in sundry place through which they pour drink down have the cask right under it to receive the same for it shall be a great trouble to bring it all down the stair the hospitality of their monastery they give bread meat and drink unto all man that come to they not only while they be at their abbey but also when they depart to serve they by the way there be a great number of such monastery in the realm and the emperor majesty ride oftentimes from one to another of they and lie at they three or four day together the same monk be as great merchant as any in the land of Russia and do occupy buy and sell as much as any other man monk merchant and have boat which pass to and fro in the river with merchandise from place to place where any of their country do traffic diet and apparel they eat no flesh during their life as it be report but upon Sunday Monday Tuesday Thursday and Saturday it be lawful for they to eat egg butter cheese and milk and at all time to eat fish and after this sort they lead their life they wear all black garment and so do none other in all the land but at that abbey only they have no preacher no not one in all the land to instruct the people so that there be many want of preacher cause of great ignorance and idolatry and the most part of the poor in the country who if one ask they how many god there be they will say a great many mean that every image which they have be a god for all the country and the emperor majesty himself will bless and bow and knock their head before their image insomuch that they will cry earnest unto their image to help they to the thing which they need all man be bind by their law to have those image in their house and over every gate in all their town and city be image set up unto which the people bow and bend and knock their head against the ground before they as often as they come by any church or cross they do in like manner and when they come to any house they bless themselves three or four time before they will salute any man in the house they reckon and hold it for great sin to touch or handle any of their image within the circle of the board where the paint be but they keep they very dainty and rich man deck they over and about with gold silver and stone sin of superstition and hang they over and about with cloth of Gold the priest be marry as other man be and wear all their garment as other man do except their nightcap which be cloth of some sad colour priest be round and reach unto the ear their crown be shave but the rest of their hair they let grow as long as nature will permit so that it hang beneath their ear upon their shoulder their beard they never shave if his wife happen to die it be not lawful for he to marry again during his life they minister the communion with bread and wine after our order sacrament but he break the bread and put it into the cup unto the wine and common some be partaker with they and they take the bread out again with a spoon together with part of the wine and so take it themselves and give it to other that receive with they after the same manner they will not permit any nation but the greek to be bury in their sacred burial or churchyard all their church be full of image unto the which the people when they assemble do bow and knock their head as I have before say that some will have knob upon their forehead with knock as great as egg all their service be in the russie tongue and they and the common people have no other prayer but this Ghospodi jesus nashe all their service be in their mother tongue that be to say o lord jesus Christ son of God have mercy upon we and this be their prayer so that the most part of the unlearned know neither nor the belief nor ten commandment nor scarce understand the one half of their service which be read in their church when any child be bear it be not baptize until the next Sunday and if it chance that it be not baptize then it must tarry until the second Sunday after the birth and it be lawful for they to take as many godfather and godmother as they will the more the better when they go to the church the midwife go foremost carry the child baptism and the godfather and godmother follow into the midst of the church where there be a small table ready set and on it a earthen pot full of warm water about the which the godfather and godmother with the child settle themselves then the clerk give unto every of they a small wax Candle burn then come the priest and begin to say certain word which the godfather and godmother must answer word for word among which one be that the child shall forsake the devil and as that name be pronounce they must all spit at the word as often as it be repeat then he bless the water which be in the pot and do breathe over it then he take all the candle which the gossip have and hold they all in one hand let part of they drop into the water and then give every one his candle again and when the water be sanctify he take the child and hold it in a small tub and one of the godfather take the pot with warm water and pour it all upon the child head after this he have many more ceremony as anoint ear and eye with hospital and make certain cross with oil upon the back head and breast of the child then take the child in his arm carry it to the image of saint Nicholas and our lady etc. and speak unto the image desire they to take charge of the child that he may live and believe as a christian man or woman ought to do with many other word then come back from the image he take a pair of shear and clip the young and tender hair of the child head in three or four place and then deliver the child whereunto every of the godfather and godmother lay a hand then the priest charge they that the child be bring up in the faith and fear of God or Christ and that it be instruct to clinege and bow to the image and so they make a end than one of the godfather must hang a cross about the neck of the child which he must always wear for that ruff which have not a cross about his neck they esteem as no christian man and thereupon they say that we be no christian because we do not wear cross as they do their matrimony be nothing solemnize but rather in most point abominable and as near as I can learn in this wi^e follow of their matrimony first when there be love between the party the man send unto the woman a small chest or box wherein be a whip needle thread silk linen cloth Sheares and such necessary as she shall occupy when she be a wife and perhaps send therewithal raisin fig or some such thing give she to understand that if she do offend she must be beat with the whip and by the needle thread cloth etc. that she shall apply herself diligent to sew and do such thing as she can best do and by the raisin or fruit he mean if she do well no good thing shall be withdraw from she nor be too dear for she and she send unto he a shirt handkerchief and some such thing of her own make and now to the effect when they be agree and the day of marriage appoint when they shall go towards the church the bride will in no wise consent to go out of the house but resist and strive with they that will have she out and feign herself to weep yet in the end two woman get she out and lead she towards the church her face be cover close because of her dissimulation that it shall not be open perceive for she make a great noise as though she be sob and weep until she come at the church and then her face be uncover the man come after among other of his friend and they carry with they to church a great pot of wine or Meade then the priest couple they together much after our order one promise to love and serve the other during their life together etc. which be do they beginnne to drink and first the woman drink to the man and when he have drink he let the cup fall to the ground haste immediate to tread upon it and so do she and whether of they tread first upon it must have the victory and be master at all time after which common happen to the man for he be ready to set his foot on it because he let it fall himself than they go home again the woman face be uncover the boy in the street cry out and make a noise in the mean time with very dishonest word when they come home the wife be set at the upper end of the table and the husband next unto she they fall then to drink till they be all drink they perchance have a minstrel or two and two naked man which lead she from the church dance naked a long time before all the company when they be weary of drink the bride and the bridegroom get they to bed for it be in the evening always when any of they be marry and when they be go to bed the bridegroom put certain money both gold and silver if he have it into one of his boot and then sit down in the chamber cross his leg than the bride must pluck off one of his boot which she will and if she happen on the boot wherein the money be she have not only the money for her labour but be also at such choice as she need not ever from that day forth to pull off his boot but if she miss the boot wherein the money be she do not only lose the money but be also bind from that day forward to pull off his boot continual then they continue in drink and make good cheer three day follow be accompany with certain of their friend and during the same three day he be call a duke and she a duchess although they be very poor person and this be as much as I have learn of their matrimony but one common rule be among they if the woman be not beat with the whip once a week she will not be good and therefore they look for it orderly and the woman say that if their husband do not beat they they shall not love they they use to marry there very young their son at sixteeene and eighteen year old and the daughter at twelve or thirteen year or young they use to keep their wife very close I mean those that be of any reputation so that a man shall not see one of they but at a chance when she go to church at Christmas or at easter or else go to visit some of her friend the most part of the woman use to ride a-stride in saddle with stirrup as man do and some of they on sled the woman of Russia paint their face which in summer be not commendable the husband be bind to find the wife colour to paint she with all for they use ordinary to paint themselves it be such a common practice among they that it be count for no shame they grease their face with such colour that a man may discern they hang on their face almost a flight shoot off I can so well liken they as to a miller wife for they look as though they be beat about the face with a bag of meal but their eyebrow they colour as black as I eat the best property that the woman have be that they can sue well and embroider with silk and gold excellent of their burial when any man or woman die they stretch he out and put a new pair of shoe on his foot because he have a great journey to go then do they wind he in a sheet as we do but they forget not to put a testimony in his right hand which the priest give he to testify unto saint Nicholas that he die a christian man or woman and they put the corpse always in a coffin of wood although the party be very poor and when they go towards the church the friend and kinsman of the party depart carry in their hand small wax candle and they weep and howl and make much lamentation they that be hang or behead or such like have no testimony with they how they be receive into heaven it be a wonder without their passport there be a great number of poor people among they which die daily for lack of sustenance which be a pitiful case to behold for there have be bury in a small time within these two year above eighty person young and old which have die only for lack of sustenance for if they have have straw and water enough they will make shift to live for a great many be force in the winter to dry straw and stamp it and to make bread thereof or at the least they eat it in stead of bread bread make of straw the unmercifulness of the Russ towards the poor stove or bath usual with the moscovite in the summer they make good shift with grass herb and root bark of tree be good meat with they at all time there be no people in the world as I suppose that live so miserable as do the poverty in those part and the most part of they that have sufficient for themselves and also to relieve other that need be so unmerciful that they care not how many they see die of famine or hunger in the street it be a country full of disease diverse and evil and the best remedy be for any of they as they hold opinion to go often unto the hothouse as in a manner every man have one of his own which he heat common twice every week and all the household sweat and wash themselves therein the first and principal mead be make of the juice or liquor take from a Berrie call in Russia which be of a marvelous sweet taste and of a carmosant colour diverse sort of russian drink report by Thomas Bulley which Berrie I have see in Paris the second mead be call Visnova because it be make of a Berrie so call and be like a black Gooseberrie but it be like in colour and taste to the red wine of France the three mead be call or short of a small Berrie much like to the small raisin and grow in great plenty in Russia the four mead be call Chereunikyna which be make of the wild black cherry the five mead be make of honey and water with other mixture there be also a delicate drink draw from the root of the birch tree call in the ruff tongue berozevite which drink the nobleman and other use in April May and june which be the three month of the springtime for after those month the sap of the tree dry and then they can have it I have by i a letter of master Christopher hoddesdon write the seventeen of November 1555. wherein he write that it seem there be no great punishment for break their region some of they adventure to eat milk with he on a fast day which yet other refuse yarost^sly so he call the town where he write be fair than Volga the river almost a mile broad he be ask seven altines for a sturgeon he have give at dansk nine mark-sprace for Richard johnson and Robert johnson and a tartar tolmach with diverse parcel of ware as by the inventory appear and the eight and twenty day we come to a town call collom distant from the Moscow twenty by this emperor of Russia most of they be christen but lie in the wood and wilderness without town or habitation Swyasko the seven and twenty day we pass by another castle call Swyasko distant from down a river call Cazankareca and enter into the foresay Volga Cazan be a fair town after the ruff or Tartar fashion with a strong castle situate upon a high hill and be wall round about with timber and earth but now the emperor of Russia have give order to pluck down the old wall and to build they again of free stone it have be a city of great wealth and riches and be in the hand of the tartar it be a kingdom of itself and do more vex the Russ in their war than any other nation but nine year past this emperor of Russia conquer it and take the king captive who be but young be now baptize and bring up in his court with two other prince which be also king of the say Cazan and be each of they in time of their reign in danger of their subject through civil discord come and render themselves at several time unto the say emperor so that at this present there be three prince in the court of Russia which have be emperor of the say Cazan who the emperor use with great honour we remain at as well Russ and Cazanites as nagayan and crimme and diverse other nation do resort to keep mart for buy and sell but now it be forsake and stand without any such resort thither or at Cazan or at any Permia into the river of Volga and be from Cazan fifteen league and the country lie betwixt the say Cazan and the say river on the left hand of Volga be call Vachen Vachen and the inhabitant be gentile and live in the wilderness without house or habitation and the country on the other side of Volga over against the say river be call the land of cheremize half gentile half tartar and all the call the country of Mangat or Nagay who inhabitant be of the law of Mahomet and be all destroy in the year 1558. at my be at astracan through civil war among they accompany with famine pestilence and such plague in such sort that in the say year there be consume of the people in one sort and another above one hundred thousand the like plague be never see in those part so that the say country of Nagay be a country of great pasture remain now unreplenish to the great contentation of the Russ who have have cruel war a long time together the nagayan when they flourish live in this manner they be divide into diverse company call horde and every hord have a ruler who they obey as their king and be call a murse town or house they have none but live in the open field every murse or king have his horde or people about he horde with their wife child and cattle who have consume the pasture in one place remove unto another and when they remove they have house like tent set upon wagon or cart which be draw from place to place with camel and therein their wife child and all their riches which be very little be carry about and every man have at the least four or five wife beside concubine use of money they have none but do barter their cattle for apparel and other necessary they delight in no art nor science except the war wherein they be expert but for the most part they be pasture people and have great store of cattle which be all their riches they eat much flesh and especial the horse and they drink mare milk wherewith they be oftentimes drink they be seditious and incline to theft and murder corn they sow not neither do eat any bread mock the christian for the same and disable our strength say we live by eat the top of a weed and drink a drink make of the same allow their great devour of flesh and drink of milk to be the increase of their strength but now to proceed forward to my journey all the country upon our right hand the river Volga from over against the river unto the town of astracan the crimme tartar be the land of crimme who inhabitant be also of the law of Mahomet and live for the most part according to the fashion of the nagaye have continual war with the emperor of Russia and be valiant in the field have countenance and support from the great Turk the sixteen day of june we pass by certain fisherman house call petowse twenty league from the river where be great fish for sturgeon so continue our way until the two and twenty day and pass by another great river call samar which fall out of the aforesaid country and run through Nagay and enter into the say river of Volga the river o^ samar the eight and twenty day we come unto a great hill where be in time past a castle make by the crimme but now it be ruin be the just midway between the say Cazan and Astrachan which be two hundred league or thereabouts in the latitude of one and fifty degree forty seven minute upon all this shore grow abundance of Licoris who root run within the be destroy as I say before but they be but ill entertain or relieve for there die a great number of they for hunger which lie all the island through in heap dead and like to beast unbury very pitiful to behold many of they be also sell by the Russ and the rest be banish from the island at that time it have be a easy thing to have convert that wicked nation to the christian faith if the Russ themselves have be good christian but how shall they show compassion unto other nation when they be not merciful unto their own at my be there I can have buy many goodly tartar child if I will have woman and common they be the child of slave either christian or gentile which the father do keep as concubine and every can or sultan have at the least four or five wife beside young maiden and boy live most vicious and when there be war betwixt these brethren as they be seldom without he that be overcome if he be not slay flee to the field with such company of man as will follow he and there live in the wilderness resort to water place and so rob and spoil as many caravans of merchant and other as they be able to overcome continue in this sort his wicked life until such time as he may get power and aid to invade some of his brethren again from the caspian sea unto the castle of s^llizure aforesaid and all the country about the say sea the people live without town or habitation in the wild field remove from one place to another in great company with their cattle whereof they have great store as camel horse and sheep both tame and wild their sheep be of great stature with great buttock weigh sixty or eighty pound in weight there be many wild horse which the tartar do many time kill with their hawk and that in this order the hawk be lure to seize upon the beast neck or head which with chafe of themselves and sore beat of the hawk be tire then the hunterr follow his game do slay the horse with his arrow or Sword in all this land there grow no grass but a certain brush or heath whereon the cattle feed become very fat the tartar never ride without their bow arrow and sword although it be on hawk or at any other pleasure and they be good archer both on horseback and on foot also these people have not use of gold silver or any other coin but when they lack apparel or other necessary they barter their cattle for the same bread they have none for they neither till nor sow they be great devourer of flesh which they cut in small piece and eat it by handful most greedy and especial the horse flesh their chief drink be mare milk sour as I have say before of the nagayan and they will be drink with the same they have no river nor place of water in this country until you come to the foresay gulf distant from the place of our land twenty day journey except it be in well the water whereof be saltish and yet distant the one from the other two day journey and more they eat their meat upon the ground sit with their leg double under they and so also when they pray art or science they have none but live most idle sit round in great company in the field devise and talk most vain they six and twenty day of November we depart from the town of urgence the river of Ardock with enemy and thief to our great trouble but shall overcome they to which sorcery I and my company give no credit but we find it true for within three hour after that the soldier depart from we which be the fifteen day of December in the morning we escry far off diverse horseman which make towards we and we perceive they to be rover gather ourselves together be forty of we well appoint and able to fight and we make our prayer together every one after his law profess to live and die one with another fight with thief and so prepare ourselves when the thief be nigh unto we we perceive they to be they shoot at we all at once and we at they very hot and so continue our fight from morning until two hour within night diverse man horse and camel be wound and slay on both part and have it not be for four hand-gun hand-gun very profitable which I and my company have and use we have be overcome and destroy for the thief be better arm and be also better archer than we but after we have slay diverse of their man and horse with our gun they dare not approach so nigh which cause they to come to a truce with we until the next morning which we accept and encamp ourselves upon a hill and make the fashion of a castle wall it about with pack of ware and lay our horse and camel within the same to save they from the shot of arrow and the thief also encamp within a arrow shoot of we but they be betwixt we and the water which be to our great discomfort because neither we nor our camel have drink in two day before thus keep good watch when half the night be spend the prince of the thief send a messenger half way unto we require to talk with our captain in their tongue the caravan bassa who answer the messenger I will not depart from my company to go into the half way to talk with thou but if that thy prince with all his company will swear by our law to keep the truce then will I send a man to talk with thou or else not which the prince understanding as well himself as his company swear we we know not but we escape that danger so upon the three and twenty day of December Boghar a city of Bactria in 39 degree 10. minute we arrive at the city of Boghar in the land of Bactria this Boghar be situate in the low part of all the land wall about with a high wall of earth with diverse gate into the same it be divide into three partition whereof two part be the king and the three part be for merchant and market and every science have their dwell and market by themselves the city be very great and the house for the most part of earth but there be also many house temple and monument of stone sumptuous build and gilt and special bath-stove so artificial build that the like thereof be not in the world the manner whereof be too long to rehearse there be a little river run through the midst of the say city but the water thereof be most unwholesome a strange worm in man leg^ for it breed sometime in man that drink thereof and especial in they that be not there bear a worm of a ell long which lie common in the leg betwixt the flesh and the skin and be pluck out about the ankle with great art and cunning the surgeon be much practise therein and if she break in pluck out the party die and every day she come out about a inch which be roll up and so work till she be all out and yet it be there forbid to drink any other thing than water and mare milk and whosoever be find to break that law be whip and beat most cruel through the open market and there be officer appoint for the same who have authority to go into any man house to search if he have either aquavita wine or brag and find the same do break the vessel spoil the drink and punish the master of the house most cruel yea and many time if they perceive but by the breath of a man that he have drink without further examination he shall not escape their hand there be a metropolitan in this boghar who cause this law to be so straight keep and he be more obey than the king and will depose the king and place another at his will and pleasure as he do by this king that reign at our be there and his predecessor by the mean of the say metropolitan for he betray he and in the night slay he in his chamber who be a prince that love all christian well this country of Boghar be sometime subject to the persian these be of the jese^as tartar and do now speak the persian tongue but yet now it be a kingdom of itself and have most cruel war continual with the say persian about their religion although they be all mahometist one occasion of their war be for that the persian will not cut the hair of their upper lip as the bogharians and all other tartar do which they account great sin and call they caphar that be unbeliever as they do the christian the king of Boghar have no great power or riches his revenue be but small and he be most maintain by the city for he take the ten penny of all thing that be there sell as well by the craftsman as by the merchant to the great impoverishment of the people who he keep in great subjection and when he lack money he send his officer to the shop of the say merchant to take their ware to pay his debt and will have credit of force as the like he do to pay i certain money that he owe i for nineteen piece of kersey their money be silver and copper for gold their be none currant they have but one piece of silver the coin of Boghar and that be worth twelvepence english and the copper money be call pool and one hundred and twenty of they go to the value of the say twelvepence and be more common payment than the silver which the king cause to rise and fall to his most advantage every other month and sometime twice a month not care to oppress his people for that he look not to reign above two or three year before he be either slay or drive away to the great destruction of the country and merchant the twenty six day of the month I be command to go before the say king to who I present the emperor of Russia his letter who entertain we most gentle and cause we to eat in his presence and deuers time he send for i and devise with i familiar in his secret chamber as well of the power of the emperor and the great Turk as also of our country law and religion and cause we to shoot in hand-gun before he and do himself practice the use thereof but after all this great entertainment before my departure he show himself a very tartar for he go to the war owe i money and see i not pay before his departure a very tart^r and although indeed he give order for the same yet wa^ I very ill satisfy and force to rebate part and to take ware as payment for the rest contrary to my expectation but of a beggar better payment I can not have and glad I be so to be pay and dispatch but yet I must needs praise and commend this barbarous king who immediate after my arrival at Boghar have understand our trouble with the thief send one hundred man well arm and give they great charge not to return before they have either slay or take the say thief who according to their commission range the wilderness in such sort that they meet with the say company of thief the king justice and slay part and part flee and four they take and bring unto the king and two of they be sore wound in our skirmish with our gun and after the king have send for i to come to see they he cause they all four to be hang at his palace g^te because they be gentleman to the example of other and of such good as be get again I have part restore i and this good justice I find at his hand there be yearly great resort of merchant to this city of Boghar which travel in great caravan from the country thereabouts adjoin as India Persia Balgh Russia with diverse other and in time pass from cathay when there be passage but these merchant be so beggarly and poor and bring so little quantity of ware lie two or three year to sell the same that there be no hope of any good trade there to be have worthy the follow the chief commodity that be bring thither out of these foresay country be these follow the indian do bring fine Whites which the tartar do all roll about their head and all other kind of Whites which serve for apparel make of cotton-wool and Crasca merchandise of India but gold silver precious stone and spice they bring none I inquire and perceive that all such trade pass to the ocean sea and the vein where all such thing be get be in the thence be the great war that have dure three year before my come thither and yet dure betwixt two great country and city of tartar ware that be direct in the way betwixt the say Boghar and the say cathay and certain barbarous field people as well gentile as mahometist border to the say city the city be call Taskent and Caskar and the people that war against Taskent be call cossack of the law of Mahomet and they which war with the say country of Caskar be call king Taskent and Caskar gentile and idolater these two barbarous nation be of great force live in the field without house or town and have almost subdue the foresay city and so stop up the way that it be impossible for any to pass unspoil so that three year before our be there no caravan have go or use trade betwixt the country of cathay and Boghar and when the way be clear it be nine month journey to speak of the say country of cathay and of such news as I have hear thereof I have think it best to reserve it to our meeting I have make my solace at Boghar in the winter time and have learn by much inquisition the trade thereof as also of all the other country thereto adjoin and the time of the year be come for all caravans to depart and also the king be go to the war and news come that he be flee and I advertise by the metropolitan himself that I shall depart because the town be like to be besiege I think it good and meet to take my journey some way and determine to have go from thence into Persia and to have see the trade of that country although I have inform myself sufficient thereof as well at astracan as at Boghar and perceive well the trade not to be much unlike the trade of Tartary but when I shall have take my journey that way it be let by diverse occasion the one be the great war that do new begin betwixt the sophy and the king of Tartary whereby the way be destroy and there be a caravan destroy with rover and thief destroy which come out of India and Persia by safe conduct and about ten day journey from Boghar they be rob and a great part slay also the metropolitan of Boghar who be great than the king take the emperor letter of Russia from i without which I shall have be take slave in every place also all such ware as I have receive in barter for cloth and as I take perforce of the king and other his noble in payment of money due unto i be not vendible in Persia for which cause and diverse other I be constrain to come back again to mare caspium the same way I go so that the eight of march 1559. we depart out of the say city of Boghar he return the eight of march 1559. be a caravan of six hundred camel and if we have not depart when we do I and my company have be in danger to have lose life and good for ten day after our departure the king of samarcand come with a army and besiege the say city of Boghar the king be absent samarcand and go to the war against another prince his kinsman as the like chance in those country once in two or three year for it be marvel if a king reign there above three or four year to the great destruction of the country and merchant the five and twenty of march we come to the foresay town of urgence urgence and escape the danger of four hundred rover which lie in wait for we back again be the most of they of kindred to that company of thief which we meet with go forth as we perceive by four spy which be take there be in my company and commit to my charge two ambassador the one from the king of Boghar the other from the king of balk the king of balk or Balgh and be send unto the emperor of Russia and after have tarry at urgence and the castle of sellysure eight day for the assemble and make ready our Caravan the second of April we depart from thence have four more ambassador in our company send from the king of urgence and other sultan his brethren unto the emperor of Russia with answer of such letter as I bring they and the same ambassador be also commit unto my charge by the say king and prince to who I promise most faithful and swear by our law that they shall be well use in rusland and suffer to depart from thence again in safety according as the emperor have write also in his letter for they somewhat doubt because there have none go out of Tartary into Russia of long time before the three and twenty of April we arrive at the mare caspium again the caspian sea where we find our bark which we come in but neither anchor cable Cock nor sail nevertheless we bring hemp with we and spin a cable ourselves with the rest of our tackle and make we a sail of cloth of cotton-wool and rig our bark as well as we can but boat or anchor we have none in the mean time be devise to make a anchor of wood of a cartwheel there arrive a bark which come from astracan with tartar and Russ wooden anchor which have two anchor with who I agree for the one and thus be in a readiness we set sail and depart I and the two johnsons be master and mariner ourselves have in our bark the say six ambassador and twenty five Russ which have be slave a long time in Tartary nor ever have before my come liberty or mean to get home and these slave serve to row when need be thus sail sometime along the coast and sometime out of sight of land the thirteen day of May have a contrary wind we come to a anchor be three league from the shore and there arise a sore storm which continue forty four hour and our cable be of our own spin brake and lose our anchor and be off a lee shore dangerous tempest and use of the compass and have no boat to help we we hoist our sail and bare roomer with the say shore look for present death but as God provide for we we run into a creek full of oze and so save ourselves with our bark and live in great discomfort for a time for although we shall have escape with our life the danger of the sea yet if our bark have perish we know we shall have be either destroy or take slave by the people of that country who live wild in the field like beast without house or habitation thus when the storm be seize we go out of the creek again and have set the land with our compass and take certain mark of the same during the time of the tempest while we ride at our anchor we go direct to the place where we rid with our bark again and find our anchor which we lose whereat the tartar much marvel how we do it while we be in the creek we make a anchor of wood of cart wheel which we have in our bark which we throw away when we have find our iron anchor again within two day after there arise another great storm at the north-east and we lie a try be drive far into the sea and have much ado to keep our bark from sink the billow be so great but at the last have fair weather we take the sun and know how the land lie from we we fall with the river according to our desire whereof the tartar be very glad fear that we shall have be drive to the coast of Persia who people be unto they great enemy note that during the time of our navigation the english flag in the caspian sea the country much a very storm which cause they to take in all their sail save the fore corse with which they be force to steer before the sea south by west and south south-west and on the eight day about two of those lighter they have get sight of the four land be about eight Verstes south-west from they the wind then at north-east do freeze the sea so as they can not row guide stir or remove the say lighter but as the wind and ice do force they and so they continue drive with the ice southeast into the sea by the space of forty hour and then be the sixteen day the ice stand while they drive with the ice the danger which they incur be great for oftentimes when the ice with force of wind and sea do break piece of it be toss and drive one upon another with great force terrible to behold and the same happen at sometime so near unto the lighter that they expect it will have overwhelm they to their utter destruction but God who have preserve they from many peril before do also save and deliver they then within three or four day after the first stand of the ice when it be firm and strong they take out all their good be forty and eight Bales or pack of raw silk etc. lay it on the ice and cover the same with such provision as they have then for want of victual etc. they agree to leave all the good there upon the ice and to go to the shore and thereupon break up their chest and Corobias travel upon the ice wherewith and with such other thing as they can get they make sleds for every of they to draw upon the ice whereon they lay their clothes to keep they warm and such victual as they have and such other thing as they may convenient carry and so they depart from the say good and pavose very early about one of the clock in the morning and travel on the ice direct their way north as near as they can judge and the same day about two of the clock in the afternoon they have sight of the Babbas four hillock of land so call unto the same they direct themselves Babbas and there remain that the crimme Tartar land or not at length it fortune they meet with a way that have be travel which cross backward towards the sea that way they take and follow the same within two day travel it bring China christian and Christianity tell we she be name inez de Leiria and be the daughter of Thomas Perez which come ambassador to China and by reason of a rebellious Portugal captain he be take as a spy with twelve other so beat that five die the other seven sunder to diverse place where they die in misery only vasco be now leave alive her father she say be banish to this town and there marry with her mother have somewhat to maintain she and by he make a christian. they live together many year like good catholic and converue many to the faith of Christ in that city three hundred assemble bear for to escape with his life do put himself in a ship that remain of the voyage which afterward be name the victory and in she and with a few people that help he with the favour of God he come new world so when all thing be in a readiness for to depart on their voyage the which be do with great brevity they ordain for general of all that fleet one villa Lobos command he to go by the nuova Espania Villa Lobos the villa Lobos arrive at the land of Malucas and at those of terrenate and at other land join unto they the which land be lay to gage by the aforesaid emperor unto the crown of Portugal in these land they have great war by mean of the portugal and see themselves with little help and small resistance for to go forward with their conquest they leave it off and go to the most part of they with the aforesaid portugal unto the India of Portugal from whence afterward they send they as prisoner unto the say king of Portugal as offender that have enter his land without his licence who do not only leave to do they any harm but do entreat they very well and send they unto their own country of Spain and give they all thing necessary for their journey and that in abundance then certain year after don Philip king of Spain be very willing that the discover shall go forward which the emperor his father have so earnest procure send and command don Lewis de Velasco who be his viceroy of the nuova Espania that he will ordain a army and people for to return and discover the say land and to send in the say fleet for governor of all that shall be discover miguel Lopez de legaspi who do accompilsh all that his majesty have command and make the discovery thereof as follow to be declare when the spaniard come unto they they be without lord or head or any other to who they shall show duty but he which have most power and people do most command so that this and that there be so many of equal power be the occasion that civil war continue without any resqect of nature kindred or any other duty but like unto bruit beast kill spoil and captive one another the which be a great help unto the spaniard for to subject that country with so great ease unto the king and call they the land in respect of his name they do use among they to make captive and slave such as they do take in unlawful war and for trifle matter the which God do remedy by the go thither of the spaniard for you shall have a man with forty or fifty friend in his company or servant that upon a sudden will go and set upon a small village of poor people and unprovided and take and bind they all and carry they away for slave without any occasion or reason and make they to serve they all the day of their life or else sell they to other land and if it so chance that one do lend unto another a basket or two of Rice the which may be worth a rial of plate with condition to return it again within ten day if the debtor do not pay it the same day the next day follow he shall pay it double and afterward to double it every day so long as he do keep it which in conclusion will grow to be so great that to pay the same he be force to yield himself for captive and slave but unto all such as be captive in this order or in such like the king of Spain have command to give liberty yet this just commandment be not in every point fulfil and accomplish because such as shall execute the same have interest therein all these land be gentile and idolater but now there be among they many thousand baptise unto who the king have show great mercy in send unto they the remedy for their soul in so good time for if the spaniard have stay any more year they have be all moor at this day for that there be come unto the island of Burneo some of that sect that do teach they and lack little for to worship that false prophet Mahomet who false perverse and corrupt memory be with the gospel of Christ easy root out in all these land they do worship the sun and moon and other second cause figure of man and woman which be call in their language maganito at who feast which they do make very sumptuous with great ceremony and superstition they do call Magaduras but among they all they have in most veneration a idol who they call Batala the which reverence they have for a tradition yet can they not say what shall be the occasion that he shall deserve more than any of the rest to be have in so great estimation in certain land not far off call the they do worship the devil and make unto he many sacrifice the devil be worship in recompense of a great quantity of gold he have give unto they but now by the goodness of God and the great diligence put and do by the father of the order of saint Austin who be the first that pass into those part and live worthy and also by the friar of saint other religious man very well learned and apostolic of the order of saint Dominicke who will do their endeavour to convert they unto Christ as it behoove christian to do they of these land be accustom among they as be the priest among christian these do talk ordinary with the devil and many time in public and do devilish witchcraft both in word and deed into who it be to be believe that that the devil do enter for that straightway they do answer unto all thing that be demand of they although for the most part they will tell a lie or else such word that may be give diverse interpretation of and of diverse understand they do also use to cast lot they be great agorismer or observer of time in so much that if they begin any journey and at the beginning they meet with a cayman or lizard or any other savage worm they know it to be a sign of evil fortune whereupon they will straightway leave off their journey although it do import they very much and return unto their house say that the heaven will not that they shall go forward on that journey but all these lie and falseness have be teach they and they persuade to by the devil be overthrow and take away by the law of the gospel as Islas reyes Lopez de Legaspe general of the spanish armada on Tuesday the one and twenty of November dom. 1565. set forth of the haven of nativity in new Spain and sail betwixt the south and the west and after westward till he come in nine degree in that height seek the land reyes thence to make for the after eight day the ship call saint Luke be miss the captain whereof be Alfonsus de arellano suspect to have malicious withdraw himself the fleet continue their course in nine and ten degree after fifty day have sight of a island of fisherman and many other small land not inhabit which they pass by it be agree that they shall heighten their course to thirteen degree in which way they come on Monday the seventeen of january Islas ladr^nes 1566. to one of the land of thief call goean and sail towards it six mile off fifty or sixty paraos swift sail bark with eight or ten man quite naked meet they and invite they to their habitation where at night they anchor the next morning six hundred of their paraos come about they with victual to sell Rice honey sugarcane fruit of diverse kind and ginger whereof there grow great store natural their principal desire in barter be iron nail give a large sack of rice for a nail their sack deceitful fill with gravel and chaff with rice in the top these people be well proportion and strong they fight with the spaniard which be water and in the time of fight will be truck with the ship as senseless of their danger a mariner which stay behind be slay who death they revenge with many of the savage slay in the night one of they be take and send into new Spain their name fit their thievish disposition the call also the land of the or west Baia de Sibabas eleven day after the fleet renew their voyage and course in thirteen degree eleven day long and then have sight of the have sail from the port of nativity eight thousand mile they anchor in a fair bay call Baia de Sibabas and there ride seven day while two boat go to discover one to the north the other southward a gentleman of one of they be slay by a indian rash leap on shore these indian have iron lance with a head or tongue a handful and half long they have also shield bow and arrow in make peace each man take two or three drop of blood of his arm or breast and mix both in some vessel together which be drink with wine and water many paraos come to the spaniard with a white flag in the prow in token of peace and the admiral erect the like in her poop to signify their leave to enter these indian be clothe but barefoot the spaniard demand provision which the other promise but give only to the captain a suck pig and a egg these people be very timorous perfidious and therefore suspicious the land bear hog goat hen Rice millet potato pomecitrons Frisoles and many sort of fruit they wear bracelet and earring and gold chain and whithersoever the fleet go be show of gold in the land Gold whereof they dig but for necessary use the land be their money bag the fleet depart hence and two day after come to the port of the i will Tandoia Tandoia where a small river enter up which they go in boat and come to a town call Camungo there they be well entertain and have victual set they which while they be eat a indian speak some spanish word and ask for Antony Baptista villalobos and captain Cabeca de vaca for which the lord of the place be angry with he and he appear no more the next day the spaniard return find they arm threaten they if they come on shore they mind not to deal cruel Martin de Goyte be send to discover some convenient harbour who see the city Tandaya and other town of other near land Tandaya and have go sixty mile find the great bay where be Cabalia a town well inhabit thither go the fleet and the inhabitant flee only Camatuan the son of a blind man chief of that place come to they who they detain think thereby to get some provision but in vain he send forth soldier which bring he five and forty hog leave in lieu somewhat for exchange and dismiss Camatuan who have teach the captain the name of the neighbour isle and of their governor he bring they to Mesagua two and thirty mile off Masagua and then be send away apparel and joyful the island Masagua have be frequent but then have but twenty inhabitant which will not see the spaniard they go to another island where the people be flee with their good then go they to Butuan which be subject to the i will Vindena or the land the wind drive they to Bohol Bohol where they anchor the next day they see a junke and send a boat to it which wound some of their man they have arrow and lance and a base and two brass piece they cry to the spaniard abordo the spaniard send out another boat better fit which take eight the rest be slay or flee have fight valiant in the junke they find white sheet paint silk Almayzarez iron tin brass and some Gold the junke be of borneo and so be these moor all be restore their intent be to get friend and the Burneois satisfy the captain send the and rover by who occasion the spaniard send into China the spaniard do enjoy their near habitation of in great quietness and in obedience unto the christian king don Philip and in continual traffic with the Chinois but be in this security and quietness unlooked for they be beset with a mighty and great armada or fleet of ship Limahon a China rover by the rover Limahon of who vocation there be continual on the coast the one by reason that the country be full of people whereas of necessity must be many idle person and the other and principal occasion by reason of the great tyranny that the governor do use unto the subject where Limahon be bear this Limahon come upon they with intent to do they harm as you shall understand this rover be bear in the city of Trucheo in the province of Cuytan which the portugal do call catim he be of mean parentage and bring up in his youth in liberty and vice he be by nature warlike and evil incline he will learn no occupation but be give to rob in the highway and become so expert that many come unto he and follow that trade he make himself captain over they which be more than two thousand and be so strong that they be fear in all that province where as they be this be know unto the king and to his council they do straight way command the viceroy of the province whereas the rover be that with all the haste possible he shall gather together all the garrison of his frontier to apprehend and take he and if it be possible to carry he alive unto the city of Taybin if not his head the viceroy incontinent do gather together people necessary and in great haste to follow he the which be know unto Limahon the rover who see that with the people he have he be not able to make resistance against so great a number as they be and the eminent danger that be therein he call together his company and go from thence unto a port of the sea that be a few league from that place and do it so quick and in such secret that before the people that dwell therein can make any defence for that they be not accustom to any such assault but live in great quietness they be lord of the port and of all such ship as be there into the which they embark themselves straightway weigh anchor and depart to the sea whereas they think to be in more security then on the land as it be true then he see himself lord of all those sea begin to rob and spoil all ship that he can take as well stranger as of the natural people by which mean in a small time he be provide of mariner and other thing which before he lack requisite for that new occupation he sack rob and spoil all the town that be upon the coast and do very much harm so he find himself very strong with forty ship well arm of those he have out of the port and other that he have take at the sea with much people such as be without shame their hand imbrue with robbery and kill of man he imagine with himself to attempt great matter and do put it in execution he assault great town and do a thousand cruelty so he follow this trade and exercise Vintoquian a rover ro^ed by this rover he chance to meet with another rover as himself call Vintoquian like wise natural bear in China who be in a port void of any care or mistrust whereas Limahon find opportunity with great courage do fight with the ship of the other that although they be threescore ship great and small and good soldier therein he do overcome they and take five and fifty of their ship so that Vintoquian escape with five ship then Limahon see himself with a fleet of ninety five ship well arm and with many stout people in they know that if they be take they shall be all execute to death set all fear apart give themselves to attempt new invention of evil not only in rob of great city but also in destroy of they for the which commandment be give straightway unto the viceroy of that province whereas he use to execute his evil that with great expedition he may be take who in few day do set forth to sea one hundred and thirty great ship well appoint with forty thousand man in they and one make general over they all a gentleman call Omoncon one hundred and thirty great ship of war with forty thousand man Omoncon for to go seek and follow this rover with express commandment to apprehend or kill he of all this provision Limahon have by some secret friend who see that his enemy be many and he not able to countervail they neither in ship nor man determine not to abide their come but to retire and depart from that coast so in fly he come unto a island in secret call Tonznacaotican which be forty league from the firm land and be in the right way of navigation to the land from this island they do go forth with some of their ship rob and spoil all such as they meet with merchandise and other thing that they carry from one island to another and from the island unto the firm and come from thence among they all they cause to take two ship of China which come from and be bind to their own country and have they in they have although it be very good yet be it not in order to defend them-nor offend their enemy he determine to go thither with all his fleet and people for to destroy and kill they and to make Omoncon and his company arrive at the port of Tanfuso hard by Tanfuso or Tansuso upon Wednesday in the evening be the five day of july this Tanfuso be a gallant and fresh town of four thousand householder and have continual a thousand soldier in garrison and compass about with a great and strong wall and the gate fortify with plate of iron the foundation of all the house be of lime and stone and the wall of lime and earth and some of brick their house within very fair wrought with great court their street fair and broad all pave before that Omoncon do come unto a anchor they see all the soldier and the people of the town be gather together upon the rock that be join unto the port all arm ready unto the battle among who there be a principal captain and three more of his companion that be send he by the governor of Chincheo who they do call in their language who have understanding of the come of Omoncon when the ship enter into the port Omoncon do salute the town with certain piece of artillery and discharge all his harquebuse six time about and therewithal take in her sail and let anchor fall then straightway the captain who the have send come aboard the ship who have express commission not to leave the company of our people after that they be disembark till such time as they come whereas he be but to bear they company and to provide they of all thing necessary the which he do accomplish ensign to know the all these captain and minister of the king do wear certain ensign for to be know from the common people to wit broad waste or girdle emboss after diverse manner some of gold and silver some of the tortoise shell and of a sweet wood and other some of ivory the high estate have they embroider with pearl and precious stone and their bonnet with two long ear and their buskin make of satin and unshorn velvet board-licence then after so soon as they be come to a anchor in the port the justice do send they a licence in write for to come forth of the ship as a thing necessary for that without it the waiter or guard of the water side will not suffer they to put foot on land this licence be write upon a board white and firm by the justice who charge it be to give the licence then when they come ashore the first land of the friar there be the soldier that be appoint by the in a readiness to bear they company and do direct and lead they unto the king house of the say city the like have every city almost throughout all the kingdom and there they bid lodge they these house be very great and very well wrought and gallant with fair court below and gallery above they have in they stange or pond of water full of fish of sundry sort the people of the city do press very much to see these stranger so that with the press as also with the great heat they be marvellous afflict which be perceive by the justice he give order that they may be ease of that trouble and cause sergeant to keep the door and their yeoman to make resistance against the people when night be come the justice of the city do make a banquet according to the fashion of the country the use of their banquet and it be in the fashion follow they be carry into a hall that be very curious wrought wherein be many torch and wax candle light and in the midst thereof be set for every one of the guest a table by himself as be the use and fashion of that country every table have his cover of damask or satin very well make the table be gallant paint without any table-clothe neither do they use any for they have no need of they for that they do eat all their victual with two little stick make of gold and silver and of a marvelous odoriferous wood and of the length of little fork as they do use in Italy with the which they do feed themselves so clean that although their victual be never so small yet do they let nothing fall neither foul their hand nor face they be set down at these table in very good order and in gallant chair in such sort that although they be every one at his table by himself yet they may see and talk one with another they be serve with diverse sort of cate and very well dress both of flesh and fish as gamon of Bacon capon goose whole hen and before he there he sit down and straightway arise up and stand he do receive the strange guest who do courtesy unto he according unto their fashion which be to join their hand together and to stoop with they and their head down to the ground he gratify they again with bow his head a little and that with great gravity these speech be finish there be bring forth certain piece of black silk of the spanish soldier and unto Omoncon and sinsay and to their interpreter but unto Omoncon and sinsay be give unto either of they a branch or nosegay make of silver which be set upon their head which be accustomable honour that be do unto such as have do some great enterprise or such like after that this ceremony be do they play upon the instrument aforesaid which come with the captain in the mean time of their music there be bring forth great store of conserve marchpane and thing make of sugar and excellent good wine and so be on foot stand he cause they to eat and he himself from the chair whereas he sit do give they to drink every one in order without rise up which be a ceremony and token of great favour and of love this be do he arise from the chair under the cloth of state and go and sit down in that which be bring on man back and with decline of his head a little he depart out of the hall and out of the house and go unto his own house whereas by the counsel of Omoncon and sinsay within a hour after they shall go and visit he the which they do he receive they marvellous well and with great courtesy who marvel at his great majesty and authority for that Omoncon and Sinsay when they do talk with he be upon their kn^es and so do all the rest he give they again in his own house a gallant banquet of diverse sort of conserve and fruit and excellent wine of the palmtree and do talk and reason with they in good sort and be more familiar than at his first visitation after that the father with their companion have remain two day in the port of Tansuso the three day they depart in the morning towards Chincheo at their go forth of the town they be accompany with a great number of soldier both harquebuse and pike and before they a great noise of trumpet drum and hoy-buck till such time as they come unto the river side whereas be a brygandine provide and make ready in all point to carry they up the river all the street alongst whereas they go there follow they so much people that it be innumerable and all to see they all alongst the river whereas they go be seat with village very gallant and fresh both on the one side and on the other at the end of the two league they come unto a great bay where be at a anchor a fleet of more than one hundred and fifty ship man of war who general be this captain who we have speak of at such time as the fleet do discover they they begin to salute they as well with great piece of artillery as with harquebuse and other kind of pastime which common they do use at such time our spaniard do travel up the river more than three league have continual both on the one side and on the other very many and fair town and full of people in the end of the three league they go aland half a league from the town of Tangoa whereas straightway all such thing as they carry with they be take upon man back Tangoa and carry unto the town before they whereas they be tarry their come for to give they great entertainment at their go a foot but Omoncon and the other captain will not consent thereunto the father obey their reason and enter into the chair and be carry with eight man a piece and the other their companion with four man a piece according unto the order give by the governor those that carry the chair (@) it with so good a will that there be strive who shall first lay hand to they this town of Tangoa have three thousand soldier and be call in their language coan at the enter in it have many garden and orchard and a street where through they carry the spaniard unto their lodging they affirm to be half a league long and all the street whereas they go be full of board and stall whereon be lay all kind of merchandise very curious and thing to be eat as fresh fish and salt fish of diverse sort and great abundance of fowl and flesh of all sort fruit and green herb in such quantity that it be sufficient to serve such a city as Seville be they be bring unto the king house which be very great marvelous well wrought with stone and brick and many hall parlour and chamber but none above but all below so soon as they be a foot there be bring from the captain or justice of the town who they do call intelligence of all thing that they have see which do cause great admiration the wall of the town be very broad and wrought with lime and stone full of loophole and watchtower and as they pass through the street there come forth of a house a very honest man China woman as it seem who be very well apparel and stay they for that in the same house there be certain dame principal personage that do see they be bring into a court whereas be set chair for they to sit down and the lady be there a little from they behold they with great honesty and gravity then a little after they set they a banquet
