take their leave house of pleasure they go to see a house of pleasure that be hard by the town-wall wrought upon the water with very fair gallery and open lodge to banquet in make of mason work and therein many table fine paint and round about it cistern of water wherein be store of fish and join unto they table of very fair alabaster all of one stone and the least of they be of eight span long and round about they be brook of run water that give a pleasant sound in the mean time they be banquet and nigh thereunto many garden full of all sort of flower and a little from that place they see a bridge all of mason work stone-bridge and the stone very well wrought and of a mighty bigness they measure some of they that be twenty and two and twenty foot long and five foot broad and seem unto they that it be a thing impossible to be lay there by man hand of this bigness yea and big they do see lay upon many other bridge in the discourse of their voyage go to Chincheo and Aucheo the next day in the morning when they be up and ready they find in the house all thing in a readiness and in very good order for their departure as well their little chair and horse as for man to carry their stuff and apparel which do not a little make they to marvel how that every one of they with a waster upon their shoulder do divide their burden in two part six rove before and six rove behind and do travel with the same with so great ease and swiftness that the horse can not endure with they they go unto the ticoan his house they find he with great majesty but yet give they great and good entertainment he do likewise put upon each of they two piece of silk in the same order as the governor of Tansuso do from this town of Tangoa unto Chincheo be thirteen league and so plain way that it give great content to travel it thrifty tillage in all the way they can not see one span of ground but be till and occupy the like they do say be of all the ground that be in the whole kingdom it be full of people and the town one so near to another that almost you can not judge they to be many town but one for that there be but a quarter of a league distant one town from another and it be tell unto they that in all the province of the kingdom it be people in the same order all their ground they till be water which be the occasion of the fruitfulness thereof so that they do gather fruit all the year long and our spaniard do see in all place whereas they come plough with Buffalos that they be gather of rice some new spring up some with ear and some ripe they do plough and till their ground with cow Bufalos and bull which be very tame and although they be very great yet be their horn but of a span long and turn backward to the tail in such sort that they can do any hurt or harm with they they do govern they with a cord that be make fast to a ring that be in their nose and in like sort do they govern the Bufalos they do feed they common in the field of rice pasturage for that they have no other grasing and all the time that they be feed a boy do ride on every one of they to disturb they that they do no harm therein but to eat the weed and grass that do grow in the rice all the highway be cover with the shadow of very fair orchard which do garnish it very much and they be plant in very good order and among they there be shop whereas be sell all manner of fruit to the comfort of all such as do travel by the way which be a infinite number some on foot some on horseback and other in little chair their water by the highway be very good and light the same day when they have travel half way they see a far off come march towards they in very good order a squadron of soldier which at the first cause they to marvel and to be afraid till such time as they draw nigh it be tell unto they that it be the captain of the guard unto the or governor of Chincheo who come by his order to receive they with four hundred soldier very well arm with pike and harquebuse and well apparel so soon as the captain come unto they he be mount on a bay horse but of small stature as they for the most part be in all that province he alight and come unto the father and his companion who likewise do alight from their little chair and do salute the one the other with great courtesy the captain come very well apparel with a chain of gold about his neck a man of a good audacity and understanding hard unto his stirrup he have a page that go with he and carry a great make of silk that do shadow he all over he have before he great music of trumpet and hoybucke whereon they play in great concord a thing to keep away the sun this captain with his four hundred soldier do continual guard they for pomp not necessity for the people may not wear weapon but the soldier in this highway continual there go and come many packe-horse lade with merchandise and other thing but the most part of they be mule the highway be very broad high way that twenty man may ride together on a rank and one not hinder another and be all pave with great stone upon a Saturday be the eleven of july come our spaniard unto the city of Chincheo four hour before it be night this city be of the common sort in that kingdom Chincheo have seventy thousand household and may have seventy thousand household it be of great traffic and well provide of all thing for that the sea be but two league from it it have a mighty river run alongst by it down into the sea by which be bring by water and carry down all kind of merchandise there be a bridge over the say river which be suppose to be the fair that be in all the world fair bridge it have a draw bridge to serve in time of war or for any other necessity the bridge be eight hundred pace long and all wrought with stone of two and twenty foot long and five foot broad a thing great to be marvel at at the entry thereof there be many arm soldier ready to fight who when they come within harquebusse shoot do salute they in very good order there be nigh unto the say bridge in the river ride at anchor a thousand ship in one river more than a thousand ship of all sort and so great a number of boat and bark that all the river be cover and every one full of people that have enter into they for to see the castillas for so they do call the spaniard in that country for the street in the suburb nor in the city can not hold they the number be so great yet their street be as broad as our ordinary street in any city in all Spain this city be compass with a strong wall make of stone and be seven fathom high and four fathom broad and upon the gate many tower wherein be place their artillery which be all their strength for that they do not use in their kingdom strong castle as they do in Europe they have no use of castle earthquake in this country rich merchandise triumphant arch the house of the city be all build after one sort and fashion but fair and not very high by reason of the earthquake which be ordinary in that country all the street but especial that wherein they pass at their come thither have on the one side and on the other shed under the which be shop full of rich merchandise and of great value and very curious they have in equal distance the one from the other many triumphant arch which do set out the street very much and be use in every principal street throughout all the kingdom in the which they have excellent market-place whereas be to be buy all thing that you will desire to be eat as well of fish as of flesh fruit herb comfit conserve and all thing so good cheap that it be almost buy for nothing the or governor of the city do send that forthwith they shall go unto his house for that he have great desire to see they in the midst of the street the where be no less number of people then in the other whereby they enter into the city they meet with a Loytia that come to entertain they with great majesty and have carry before he many banner mace-bearer and tipstaff and other which carry set or whip which they do trail after they make fast unto long stick which be the executioner the which do go always make of way part the people before the Loytias as you have hear the majesty and company wherewith he come be so great that they very do believe he to be the a assistant but be certify they understand that it be one of his counsellor that come from the governors home to his own house which be in the same street whereas he meet with they serpent knot the king arm this counsellor be carry in a chair of ivory garnish with gold and with curtain of cloth of gold and on they the king arm which be certain serpent knot together as have be tell you but when he come right against the spaniard without any stay he make a sign with his head and command that they shall return back again unto his house which be hard by the captain do straightway obey his commandment and return with they the counsellor enter into his house which be very fair he have in i a fair court and therein a and severe because he do carry they on foot they can not understand whether it be do for a policy or of a truth although the effect wherewith he do chide seem of a truth he straightway command two before they come into a great place whereas be many soldier in good order with their harquebuse pike and other armour in a readiness apparel all in a livery of silk with their ancient display at the his interpretation talk of any matter of importance so when they come thither they be bring whereas he be but with less ceremony he request they to declare unto he the whole circumstance of the come of Limahon the rover unto the land and how the spaniard deal with he that although he have be inform particular in all thing by the captain Omoncon and Sinsay yet he be in a jealousy that they tell he not the truth he be nothing deceive in that he suspect for after that our soldier have make a true relation of the come of the rover unto and of all the rest he find that they differ very much the one from the other vain glory for that they do attribute it whole unto themselves to get honour and benefit but the like a wise man straightway understand their pretence but when that he perceive that Limahon be neither dead nor prisoner but only besiege he offer unto they that if they will return again unto Pagansinan upon he whereas he be he will give unto they five hundred ship of war with people sufficient to serve both by sea and land and more if they will request they answer he that all such cost and labour be but in vain for that the general of the field who have he in siege with the people and ship that he have be sufficient to end that enterprise and to send he hither alive or dead and that long before that their fleet shall come thither and beside this bo^sting their land be poor of victual and can not sustain so great a army many day be satisfy with these reason he give place that the interpreter which they bring shall come in where as they be for he remain at the of small importance for that they be priest and minister of God who he do worship and reverence the with a merry countenance do answer they that unto that time he understand no more of they then in Spaniard feast table-rite in the first chair they cause the friar to sit down every one at a table by himself and each of they other six table place in order compass round like a circle then be the spanish soldier set in the same manner and each of they have five table and next unto they the captain of the guard belong unto the governor and two other captain and every one of they have three table for that it be the custom of that country to make a difference in the quality of the guest by the number of the table all these be place in circle or compass as aforesaid that they may see one another a comedy and other sport in the midst betwixt they there be a round compass whereas be represent a comedy with much pastime and endure all the dinner time and a good while after there be also great store of very good and excellent music accompany with gallant voice also jester with puppet the viand and other thing of great pastime to drive the time away on the first table be set to every down neither to be bare head so after that he have make unto they token of friendship and detain they a while in demand of many thing last he tell they that there be a order come from the viceroy of aforesaid that they do fall out and strive among themselves who shall be the first that shall receive their burden so all thing be in good order they depart have in their company the same captain and soldier that unto that time have be their guard until they come unto the city of Aucheo whereas the viceroy be this day by reason they understand that they shall depart the press and multitude of the people be so great Aucheo that although they have tip-stave before they to beat the people away and to make room yet be it almost night before they can get out of the city so that they be constrain to remain in a town there hard by all that night whereas by the commandment of the governor they be very well lodge and their supper make ready in very good order as it be in seven day together till such time as they come unto Aucheo without take for the same or for any other thing necessary for their sustentaion any price or value there go continual before they a post with a provision from the governor write in a great board wherein be declare who they be and from whence they come and command that there shall be provide for they all thing necessary in abundance upon the king cost which be the occasion that so much people come for to see they that in the highway they be many time disturb with great trouble the three day they come unto a city which be call Megoa Megoa a great city spoil by japanders which be sometime the head government the which be of forty thousand household but a great part thereof be dispeople the occasion thereof they tell we and be that about thirty year past the japone who bring for their guide three Chinois stratagem come upon that city to revenge themselves of a injury that be do unto they the which they put in execution with so great secrecy and policy that they make themselves lord of the city without any danger or hurt unto themselves for that fifty japone man fit for that purpose do apparel themselves in Chinois apparel without be know and come unto a gate of the city whereas the soldier that have the charge thereof be void of all suspicion and within a little while after that follow two thousand that do disimbarke themselves in a secret and unknown place and come in very secret order because they will not be discover and do beset that gate of the city whereas their companion be which they send before who so soon as they see they nigh at hand draw out their weapon the which they carry hide under their apparel and set upon the soldier that be void of fear and unarmed with so great fury and force that they be amaze be easy slay so that see that they can not defend themselves against so many in one night they leave the city and go unto their ship whereas they have leave they in very good order and carry with they the spoil of the this city travel towards Aucheo admirable stone bridge they pass over a mighty great river by a bridge all make of stone the goodly and great that ever they have see who greatness do cause wonderful admiration so that they stay and do measure it from one end to another that it may be put among the wonder of that country which they take a note of they find that it be one thousand and three hundred foot long and that the least stone wherewith it be build be of seventeen foot and many of two and twenty foot long and eight foot broad and seem unto they a thing impossible to be bring thither by man art for that all round about so far as they can see be plain ground without any mountain by which they judge they to be bring from far when they be pass that bridge they travel all the rest of the day till night upon a cawsie that be very broad and plain and on both side many victual house and the field sow with Rice wheat and other seed and so full of people as in the street of a good town or city after they have travel more than half a league in the suburb of the city of Aucheo they meet with a post that come from the viceroy who bring order that they shall remain in a house that be appoint for they in the say suburb suburb of Auc^eo so soon as they be alight there come a gentleman to visit they send from the viceroy to bid they welcome and to know how they do with their journey and also to see that they be well provide for that night of all thing necessary and that in abundance after this gentleman come other captain to visit they and bring with they great store of conserve wine and fruit which be a common custom among they when that they go in the like visitation and it be carry by their servant in little basket very curious wrought or else in barrel make of earth all gilt within two hour after their come thither there come another messenger from the viceroy with many man lade with capon hen goose teal gamon of Bacon and conserve of diverse sort and of great abundance sufficient for one hundred man to sup that night and for their dinner the next day the next day in the morning very early there come much people unto their lodging send by the viceroy and bring with they two rich chair for to carry the father in and the curtain tie up that they may the better be see and for their companion very good horse saddle after the fashion which they do use they forthwith make haste for to depart and although they make great speed yet be they a good hour and a half before they can come unto the gate of the city and seem unto they that they have travel two league in the suburb well people fair house and many shop full of merchandise before they come unto the gate they pass a mighty river three time over bridge that be great and very fair and the river so deep that great ship come up the same but their mast stoop down to pass under the bridge this city be the head city of all the province very rich and fertile and many town belong unto it and but eight league from the Sea they have no leisure to tell the soldier but they see that from the gate until they come unto the viceroy palace on both side which be a good way to be full of they and all rich apparel and of one colour the people that be at the window and in the street betwixt the house and the soldier be so great a number that it seem to be doom day palace open once a day and that all the people in the world be there join together in that street when they come unto the palace which be two hour after day the gentleman that be their guide do cause the spaniard to enter into a room which be hard by till such time as the gate be open for that it be open but once a day and so continue no long time than the audience endure State which be do by the viceroy once every day and that be but a small time but first before he do enter into audience there be shoot off four piece of artillery with a great noise of trumpet drum and Waytes and there be no day that pass without audience as our people do see by experience so long as they be there and be likewise inform of other the hour be come and the ceremony do as aforesaid the gate be open and there be in the court many soldier apparel in the same livery that those be of in the street from the midst among they come forth a gentleman who be as it be tell they the captain of the guard of the viceroy who come with great gravity and authority towards the place whereas our people be and after they have salute the one the other he make sign unto they that they shall go towards the gate of the palace when they be within the first court which be great and wrought with mighty pillar there be a great number of soldier and many sergeant that enter into another great court and mount up a pair of stair that be on the one side whereas all the people be with great silence save the captain of the guard who go with our people till they come to the gate of the hall where be the viceroy at which gate he stay with his head discover and make sign unto we that they shall do the like then straightway come forth of the hall a man apparel in a long robe of good personage ceremony and ask of the spaniard if they will speak with the viceroy and they answer yea then ask he again from who they come and by who they be send they answer that they be send by the governor of who be servant unto the mighty king in all Christendom when he have this answer he return again into the hall and within a little while after he come forth and bid they come in but give they to understand that in enter into the hall whereas the viceroy be that they shall kneel down and talk with he in that order till he command to the contrary if they will use this ceremony that then they shall come in if not that they shall return back again they say that they will observe the order give unto they therewith he go in who seem to be the master of ceremony make a sign that they shall follow after he and do that which he will they to do viceroy state at the enter in at the door they stay a little and then kneel down right over against there whereas the viceroy sit in a chair very high like unto a throne with a table before he and be in so dark a place that almost they can not see his face very well on the one side of he there be some like unto herald of arm with sceptre in their hand and on the other side two man of a gallant comeliness arm with corslet make of scale of gold down to the calf of their leg with bow in their hand of gold and quiver at their back of the same both the one and the other be upon their knee there be upon the table before he paper and all thing necessary to write which be a ordinary use among they at all time when there be any public audience lion the arm of that province perhaps this deceive pinto who mistake they see they common on pillar etc. to be the king arm which be but of some place and on the one side of the board a lion make of black wood which be as after they understand the arm of that province so straightway he make sign unto they to draw near which they do and kneel down a little from the table which be whereas the master of ceremony do will they in this sort they begin to talk with he by their interpreter and tell they the occasion of their come into that city and kingdom and from who and unto who they be send but he make sign unto they that they shall arise the which they do with a very good will and do persevere in their intent but the viceroy do cut they off before they can make a end and ask if they have bring any letter from their king unto the king his lord who they will go to see and talk with but when they answer no he straightway take his leave of they say that they be welcome and that they shall depart unto their lodging and to take their ease for that afterward they shall have occasion to declare their mind unto he and he will give they their answer for that the king be far off and it require along time to come whereas he be but he will write unto he and according unto his commandment he will make they answer and therewith he take the letter and the memorial of the present and command in his presence to put about the neck of the friar in manner of a the say Omoncon and sinsay for their own interest will have carry they to the house of other officer and gentleman of the court. at their come thither they find all their stuff in good order and their be join together little more or less than twenty thousand soldier pike-man and harquebusse shoot who be so expert that at the sound of the drum or trumpet they straightway put themselves in battle use in all the world and if it be so that their stomach and hardiness be equal unto their dexterity and number of people it be a easy thing for they to conquer the dominion of all the world if it so chance that any soldier shall lack in his office and not repair to his place appoint he be straightway punish very cruel soldier be punish which be the occasion that every one of they have a care unto all be ready to so long and dangerous a journey which require many person neither be it perform every year but by they only which know they shall be admit into Catay there be no better merchandise as before be say then a certain shine marble precious marble which we be wont to call jasper for want of a fit word which the king of Catay buy at a great price and what he leave they may sell to other at exceed rate of it they make diverse ornament for vessel garment girdle with leaf and flower artificial engrave the Chinois call it and of it be two kind one more precious which be take out of the river Cotan not far from the city royal in manner as the diverse fish for pearl and be bring out like thick flint the other mean be dig out of hill and be saw into broad stone above two else wide after fit to the voyage this hill be twenty day journey from that city royal and be style Cansangui Cascio that be the stony mountain they be thence take with incredible labour both for the desertnesse of the place and the inexorable hardness of the marble which they say be force with fire make thereon to yield the licence also to take it be dear sell by the king to some one merchant who purchase the monopoly and when they go thither they carry a year provision for the labourer which in that space return not Goez visit the king who name be Mahamethin and present he with a watch a glass and other european commodity which make he very welcome Mahamet C^^ king of Cascar Cialis he will not at first tell he of go to Catay but only speak of the kingdom of Cialis eastward from thence and procure his grant thereto assist by the son of his sister the pilgrim queen before mention six month pass and Demetrius one of his old society which stay at Cabul come thither at that time by the king licence one of the merchant be style emperor as in jest to who the other merchant after the custom give present which Demetrius refuse be in danger to be imprison and beat for so large be his power have not Benedict intercede and by a gift compound the business thief also break into the house and set a sword to the armenian breast terrify he from cry but our brother Demetrius hear cry out and scar they away Benedict be go to the king of quotans mother for payment of his debt his residence be ten day journey thence so that he spend a month therein before his return in this space the saracen raise a report that he be dead slay by their priest for refuse their holy now because he die intestate they seek to seize on his good which be very troublesome to Isaac and Demetrius both for defence of the good and loss of their friend which redouble their joy at his return with plenty of that marble and he in thankfulness give much alm on a day as he be eat with other saracen one come in arm and set his sword to his breast charge he to invoke * * to use as it seem those word la illah illalah mehume resullalah the characteristical note of mahometan profession Mahomet he answer that in his law there be no such name invoke and therefore refuse and by the company that mad fellow be extrude the like zeal oft endanger he on like term of mahometan profession on another day he be call by the king of Cascar in the presence of his cacise the priest and the Mullas or learned man and ask what law he profess whether that of Moses of David or mohammed and which way he turn himself in pray he answer that he profess the law of jesus who they call Isai and turn any way when he pray believe that God be every where about which rise among they great controversy they use to turn to the * * to Mecc^ ward west yet they conclude that our law also may seem good meane-whiles one agiafi of that country be name captain of the future Caravan who invite our brother to his house have hear well of he to a feast wherein they have music after their manner at the end he desire his company to Catay which he much desire but have learn by experience how to deal with the saracen and will be entreat that he may seem to do rather than receive a favour the captain use the king mediation who desire he to accompany the caravan bassa caravan Bassa see before in Chaggi memet the like journey and the same place which he accept upon condition of his letter patent for all that way his Cabul companion be herewith offend as loath to lose his company and much dissuade he but he make show as though he be loath herein to displease the king and for his sake have promise the caravan bassa which now he may not revoke they say that these people be perfidious and will devour he and he nor be their fear causeless for many of the native have tell they that those three armenian so they call all these three christian as soon as they be out of the wall will be slay this terrify Demetrius from go further who also dissuade Goez but in vain say he will not disappoint the hope of so many the archbishop of goa and the viceroy to lose his expense but will adventure his life in the design he provide ten horse for his carriage and for his fellow have another at home the bassa be go to his house five day journey thence to make all ready and thence send to Goez to hasten 1604. about the midst of November they come to a place call jolci voyage to Catay from Hiarchan place in the way where they use to pay custom and their commission be examine hence they go to hancialix alceghet to hagabate to troublesome both with store of stone or rock and with Sands Acsu be a town of the kingdom of Cascar the governor whereof be nephew to the king than twelve year old he will needs see Goez who go and give he childish present sugar and the like and be gentle entertain of he there be then a solemn dance before he he request our brother to dance which to satisfy he he do Goez dance he visit also his send for he in this way one of Goez his horse fall into a swift river and escape to the other side and come again of himself the name of jesus be invoke in this way the desert be pass call Caracathai where they stay a whole month to refresh their beast which by the irksomeness of the way and weight of the marble and want of barley be almost spend here the priest demand of Goez why in their solemn fast Lent he fast not and almost force he in hope of some largesse or fine after they be go hence in five and twenty day they come to the city Cialis which be little but well fortify this country be govern by a base son of the king of Cascar who hear that Goez profess another religion begin to terrify he say it be a bold part for a man of another profession to enter those part for he may lawful take from he his life and good but when he read his letter patent he be pacify and with a present be make also a friend one night dispute about their law with the priest and learned man he send for Benedict into the palace whereupon suspicion arise of some ill intent be at so unseasonable a time he go and be command to dispute with force of argument silence the adversary the viceroy always protect he approve his say and conclude that the christian be the true misermans musulman that be right believer say that his progenitor have profess the same Law after the disputation he make he a banquet and cause he to lie that night in the palace so that Isaac be weep at his return and almost in despair to see he in this city they stay three month for the caravan bassa will not depart without a great company it be so much more gain to he nor suffer any man to go before Goez weary with this tedious stay and chargeable expense with a gift obtain leave of the viceroy the caravan and captain be against it he then intend to proceed from Cialis when the merchant of the former Caravan return from Catay these feign a embassage after their wont have pierce into the royal seat of Catay news of f. m. and the jesuit and have converse in the same palace of stranger with our jesuit report strange and certain news of father Matthew and the company to Goez who wonder that Catay be become China these saracen be the same hereafter report * * in Pantoia and of which live three month with we and tell he that the father have present to the king watch picture and other european present and be much respect in the palace of the great and add some lie say that they have often speak with the King they reasonable well paint their face name change by the jesuit but know not their name by use he kind and ample provide he out of his own house Pucian turphan Aremuth thence they proceed to turphan and stay a whole month in that fortify city thence they pass to Aremuth and after to Camul a and in one day come to socieu a city where they hear much of pequin and other name know so that now he be out of all doubt that Catay and China differ only in name all the way from Cialis to the border of China be infamous with incursion of the tartar and therefore merchant pass these place with great fear borderer thievish search by day from the neighbour hill whether there be any out-rode of tartar and if they judge the way secure they travel by night with silence in the way they find many saracen miserable slay have adventure to go alone although the tartar seldom kill the native say they be their slave and herdsman from who they take away their flock of sheep and herd of bullock they eat no wheat barley nor pulse Tartar custom in the border say it be food for beast not man they feed only on flesh not spare horse mule camel and yet be say to live one hundred year the saracen nation border on these part of China may easy by the Chinois be subdue as be not warlike man if the Chinois care to enlarge their dominion in this way one night Benedict fall from his horse his company go on and not miss he till they come to their lodging and then Isaac go back to seek he and find he by the sound of the name jesus almost despair to see his company any more these wall be build on the west of China as it trend north-ward about the space of two hundred * * this 200. i^ to be Nanquin @. i. of FRANCIS xavier Melchior nuns' VALIGNANUS RUGGERIUS and PASIUS forasmuch as we have sail so late from the to China and back again with our friar and have give you a jesuit land journey we think it worthy our labour also to launch into the deep of their navigation and to honour the jesuit to who in the follow part of this history we be so indebt with observe their observation of japon Ignatius and Francis canonize by greg. 15. march 12. 1622. and the intercourse thereof with China and from it as the great and most glorious eastern Jesuitical conquest to ship ourselves in their barge to China how Francis xavier now saint at Rome together with Ignatius Loiola first founder of that order labour the conversion of gentile and pagan to christianity as in other part of the indies so here in japan I willing acknowledge yea so far be I from envy either he or his order or any other order style religious their trophy of conversion that I can wish the pope seat in Miaco and all the jesuit and friar yea all his jesuited clergy full possess of the bonzian college and temple in japon whence a double good may issue to the some light in stead of a total darkness a disease life be better than death and to Europe to be lighten of their burden where profess themselves light they prove lightning and raise so manifold combustion and most especial can I wish this honour to my countryman the english jesuit and priest popish emissary of whatsoever order that they be there order or which fit their ambition better order that eastern world rather than here disorder and disorder play the lord of misrule in the west the very name of Christ be sweet to i even in japan yea from a jesuit mouth or a jesuit convert and will God they teach they jesus more and less jesuitish fancy of exchange worship of creature howsoever gild with christian name that the japonian may learn to acknowledge jesus and Maria true and not with name and image of they know not what to worship Venus and her son Cupid this happen in capt. Saris his ship see to 1. l. 4. c. 1. p. 367. in stead of the bless virgin and that incarnate blessedness her bless son who be God over all bless for ever one tell Cortes the mexian conqueror then conversion do Francis xavier in the year 1541. sail from Lisbon winter at Mosambique whence he pass into India after that to malaca and to say the former author indigo how little in comparison be Paul from jerusalem to illyricum be first discover and know to the portugal by Mota carry out of his course to China thither by tempest 1542. he die 1552. the five and fifty of his age of his indian peregrination the eleven in the i will sancian on the coast of China this be the indian standrad-bearer to all of that society begin his travel to Lisbon the first year of their confirmation 1540 and now deify or canonize and invoke by doctor chancellor of Collen his orator Ignati and Francisce etc. a letter of his write from japon in November 1549. thus relate letter of xavier we come by God grace in August to japon on the feast day of the assumption of the virgin Marie have set forth from malaca on midsummer day the master of the ship be a chinese which have undertake that office to the captain of malaca and sail prosperous till the master alter his mind as those barbarian be usual inconstant and linger long among the land in the way this trouble we in two respect principal both for the loss of the season which God offer and which be pass devil worship by the Chinois we be compel to winter on the coast of China and again because in the same ship be carry a idol of the devil to which the mariner in sight and spite of we sacrifice after the manner of their country they also by lot demand answer thereof touch their voyage which as they say and believe be sometime good sometime bad a hundred league from malaca hold our course to China we stay at a island where after many ceremony the devil be consult what fortune we shall have who answer very prosperous whereupon with great alacrity we set sail they worship the idol place in the poop with candle burn and incense of sweet wood we trust in God the creator of heaven and earth and in his son our lord jesus Christ desire to carry his religion into those part when we be under sail they demand of the devil whether this ship shall return from japon to malaca the answer be make by the lot-caster that it shall go to japon but not return to malaca which make they alter their mind think it better to winter in China and to defer the voyage to japon till the next year you may well think how it grieve we that the devil must be consult touch our course after this we come to Cauchinchina where two adverse thing happen Emanuel sina our companion by the roll of the ship in the trouble sea fall into the sink almost dead with the bruise and water but in few day recover which before it be end the master daughter with the like roll of the ship fall into the sea and in all our sight be drown and much lamentation follow the barbarian present seek to pacify the devil and without rest all the day and night take pain to kill bird to the idol and to set dish of meat before it and by lot consult to know the cause of that misfortune the answer be that if Emanuel which first fall in have die the girl have not fall into the Sea you see in what danger the devil hereby have cast we if our lord have not restrain his rage etc. the tempest be assuage we come in few day to the port of canton in China and there they purpose to winter Canton notwithstanding all our entreaty and expostulation but I know not how on a sudden they will go to Chincheo on the same coast. and when we be almost there the master be certify by some which sail by in japon Paul have be in India and be baptize that there be store of pirate at Chincheo whereupon the wind be fair for japon and cross for Canton they bring we to Cangoxuma the country of our friend Paul who friend use we unkind there we spend forty day in learning the element of the japonian tongue with great labour and begin to publish the decalogue and other head of christian learning which Paul have accurate convert into his own language and we purpose speedy to print they whereby the knowledge of Christ be further and more easy found etc. the occasion of his journey thither he show in another letter that some portugal be lodge in a house possess by devil sea tempestuous and piratical compass the say house with cross and that there be great hope of good to be do in those part whereupon notwithstanding those sea be very tempestuous and much infest with pirate he resolve to go thither and Trigantius add that the japonian priest allege in defence of their idolatry the Chinois wisdom against he whereupon he return to India to advise with the viceroy to send a ambassage into China without which there be no entrance and obtain that james Pereira be name legate with who he have before confer about the business at sancian where the portugal at that time use to trade with the Chinois Amacao not yet establish but the captain of malaca oppose xavy loathe herein to be cross use the pope bull which constitute he apostolical nuncio and grievous curse all that shall hinder his proceed in promote religion and when Aluarus will not otherwise relent he interdict he and his follower soon after Aluarus be possess with a leprosy and further contemn the viceroy be take and cast in iron and die miserable xavier burn with zeal of his china expedition xavier zeal seek to get some Chinois by favour or reward to convey he by stealth into China and to expose he somewhere on the continent although he know that imprisonment attend such stranger as come into China without licence be admonish to take leave of the captain what say he shall I go to salute a excommunicate person I shall never see he nor he i in this life nor after but when in the vale of josaphat I shall accuse he before the judge Christ and pray for he sancian thirty league from the China shore after with a countenance full of majesty he put off his shoe and shake off the dust according to the evangelical precept thus he come to sancian a desert island where the portugal use to make oath of bough or straw for the time of their trade with the Chinois with who he consult about some way to effect his desire though with loss of liberty or life at last he agree with a China merchant for as much pepper give he of the Portugal merchant in alm as be worth above two hundred ducat to set he and his interpreter on shore secret he undertake it but either secret terrify by other portugal or with his own danger xavier death see and f. pinto and Eman. acosta etc. his interpreter forsake he and after that the merchant also vanish he stay yet wait for he till a fever take he out of the world in December 1552. his corpse be after translate to India the portugal of those time be very desirous of trade with the Chinois who on the other side be very suspicious of they both by Ruggerius Michael Ruggerius a italian of the kingdom of Naples be send and come to Amacao in july 1579. and apply himself to learn the language which the courtier in China use and be common through all china the province have otherwise peculiar language also to learn to read and write their character which be as many as word that language be very hard both in itself and for the want of teacher for those christian Chinois which live at Amacao in habit of european and those which come thither in merchandise be almost as ignorant of the court tongue as of the Portugal and though they understand it yet they can not well pronounce it and for the character they know those which belong to their merchandise and common use with picture his teacher be often force to supply character and whereas the portugal twice a year in the mart season have access to Canton Portugal trade at canton by day and extrusion at night about januarie and june he go with they thither for in time they obtain this liberty that not in a desert island as first nor in the Amacao haven but in the metropolitan city two day up the river they may have trade by day but lie aboard at night with so many eye and watch on they as it be manifest they be not altogether free of their former fear these mart continue two month each of they or long and have be the only mean of admit the jesuit into China rugg first entrance by the industry and piety of other portugal Ruggerius therefore with his merchandise also adventure with they and find a impediment at first another jesuite which before have go thither have convert a youth disciple to a priest and close convey he to Amacao his master make complaint and procure the magistrate to fetch he back by force to the great trouble of we and seem discredit as if by ill art they have seduce child from their parent which be a thing at Canton both usual and capital Ruggerius enterpose himself with great care and discretion and appease the admiral or haitao which have the command of stranger Ruggerius free by the haitao who hereby have a opinion of his virtue and delight to see he studious of the China book he therefore permit he to stand at his side perhaps because the whole way in manner be mountainous way pave and populous I do not remember that ever I see way so frequent not then when merchant resort to public fair for all the merchandise from Nanquin and the place adjoin be bring hither also the merchant which inhabit the remote city in that way on both side have partner for the convey of their ware very fit for our conductor have nothing to do but to deliver one hundred and fifty pack of ware with other provision for the way to his host seat and porter in the highway which all he shall find in his inn in the next town these partner also provide horse for the servant and seat for the master to be carry in by two porter defend from the rain by Sumbreros or shadow which they carry in their hand when he have pass half the way we change our seat and porter and have other to the inn to these nothing be due but some small gratuity the host be pay for all and a seat be at as easy a rate here as a horse in our country with great commodity and frequency of inn in the evening we come to the town faquen and stay there two day faquen such concourse of citizen come to see we that we be almost overwhelm and be glad to get a themselves to the view of passenger seem as big as canton great city thick which make i meditate of the facility of convey the gospel in these part we make all this way with as great tranquillity of body and mind that we may in the ship pray or study and do other thing as commodious as at home on the sixteen of the kalend of january we come to a most frequent city far great than canton where the to say Sciaubin or ciquion like Venice be a type and representation of Venice God have provide we of a good house on one side have the city on the other the river for prospect with convenient room and a garden and a fit place for a chapel on both side of we dwell idolatrous priest which yet use we kind and daily come to hear our doctrine as do other in great multitude that we can yet avoid their frequent concourse to hear and see we to the chief of they we show our altar erect to the immortal God which they behold with great reverence worship the image of our saviour and the great magistrate the city of China and through all their street this be six article or principle which be first obey father and mother second six precept of China reverence betters and elder three make peace among neighbour four teach child and nephew five let every man well discharge his office sixthly commmit no offence that be not to kill steal fornication etc. which in manner comprehend the second table of of honour wear common a outward garment of silk which they use in visitation and other like action and there be many which always go abroad apparel in silk but not in such great number as that book set down whereof I make mention before all man even to the very soldier wear their apparel long down to the instep of the foot with very broad sleeve open before and fasten to the side beneath the arm they be so well content and please with their manner of apparel that they think there be none in the world comparable to they and in very truth they be grave and modest and especial those of the mandarin which differ from all other save the Bonzi which shave their beard and head all the man and woman let their hair grow long and the man truss it up and wind it on a knot on the top of their crown they wear certain net on their head like coyffe make very cunning of horse-hayre and in the summer time many wear cap and hat of the same there be many sort of cap or hat for I know not what their several name be according to the state of every one the base sort which the common people use ordinary be round their shoe be of the same stuff that their garment be of very common of silk make with many fair border and knot it be a discourtesy for a man to be see especial before any man of worship without a cap on his head they great esteem for the most part thing of our country and they be very dear and some piece of silk which the Portugal merchant bring especial velvet of three pile be far more dear than their own all woollen cloth be much esteem and very dear likewise chamblet and fine linnen-cloth which they bring from India be very dear looking-glass and all thing make of glass and many other thing which in our country be very good cheap be here dear and in great estimation be very grave of very good capacity and appear outward very modest and grave there be arificer of all art that be in our country and very many with the selfsame manner form of instrument every man be free to follow what trade he will trade without be bind to follow his father trade as diverse time I have hear it speak when I be in Europe and those which will may study forsake or change that course of life they work very good cheap but in cunning and excellency we most common excel they much though in some thing they be very skilful the service of young man and maid be easy and good cheap because there be great store of people so that a year wage be not above two ducat and meat and drink servant cheap sale of child vile without apparel as there be many poor people that have many son and daughter it be a very ordinary thing to sell they and this the cheap thing in China for a youth of twelve or fifteen year without any natural blemish will cost not pass twelve or fifteen rial of plate and in time of dearth much less and it be a common thing to buy they for service though they use they well and marry they at their time although the abundance and riches of this kingdom be very great as the people also be yet there be no body that be very rich none very rich neither in any state of people may they compare in this point with our country you shall not find in China which be able to spend twenty thousand ducat of rent how near of kin soever he be to the king and very few and those easy to be number that can spend ten thousand ducat and the ordinary be no more which they possess then that which their land and office yield they which be not great yet as rich as we very rich but though it be true that those of our country possess much more silver consider the cheapness of thing in their country all come to one account there be very few of the poor people idle because all of they common take pain few idle and earn their live though the multitude of the nation be so many and the kingdom so great yet the surname of all the kingdom be not above three hundred and all of one syllable surname there be some though very few which may be call knight knight which for service to the king in some necessity have give they office in succession but the common use be not to have any nobility by descent in China neither can any man say nobility only in learning I be of a better house than you but the honour and nobility depend whole upon learning and to obtain degree and office of mandarin and therefore a house which now be in office and his father be one if he have a son a doctor which be make a mandarin he be honourable no lord but the King and the honour continue as long as the learned man and mandarin do live there be no man neither kinsman nor not kinsman of the king which have ever a village of his own that pay he tribute but all man pay it to the king and he give stipend and wage to the mandarin so that they receive nothing of particular man by right though they extort much continual by oppression extortion common the Chinois do marry from fifteen to eighteen and twenty year and all of they do marry one wife that be chief and this be their lawful marriage marriage on the day of their marriage when the bride do pass to the house of her husband she carry open before she through the street all the thing which she bring with she and all her household stuff but beside she they may marry I say they may keep and do keep as many as they be able as many wife as they will which for the most part they buy and afterward when they will polygamy sell they away again they may not only not marry with any kinswoman of their wife but with none of that surname though they have no show of alliance the son of the concubine do likewise inherit and there be little or no difference in their state and honour to be the son of the lawful wife or of the other neither make they any question of it inheritance the thing wherein the Chinois be most observant ceremonious and superstitious be in their burial funeral and mourn funeral and mourn for herein they show their obedience and love to their parent whereof their book be full it be a very ordinary thing to have great respect to their father and mother and the disobedient be grievous punish many grave man and mandarin beg leave of the king to leave their office which they have and to go home to keep their father and mother company yield for a reason that they be old and that they will go to serve they and it be a petition in the sight of all man so just that they grant it very usual three year mourn in white linen when the father or the mother die all the son and daughter from the king to the mean peasant do mourn for three year the mourn colour which among we be black bay among they be white linen whereof they make all their apparel even to the cap. the first month they wear a very rough sackcloth gird with a cord like the barefooted friar and though he be never so great a mandarin without any exception save only the mandarin of the war assoon as he hear news of the death of any of his parent he be to leave his office and dignity and all other employment whatsoever of government and examination of obtain his degree and be to go home for three year to bury his father or mother and to mourn and bewail they the grave man which have a house for this purpose do not straightway bury their dead but keep they two or three year in the house keep the dead at home in a chamber which they keep for this office and it be not the worst in the house and very usual or every day they go thither to make they a thousand ceremony and reverence and to burn incense and other sweet savour and to set over the place where they be lay meat to eat and at several time many of those Bonzi do meet and with great ceremony begin their service and prayer and their son kinsfolk and wife make lamentation the mandarin do not only leave their office other funeral rite and change their weed but also all the thing which they do use many sit not in chair but upon low stool they visit or suffer themselves to be see very seldom they change even the very paper wherein they write wherein they have a piece of another colour in token of mourn when they name themselves in their letter they use not the name which they do at other time but other proper to the party as when he name himself he call himself disobedient signify that by his disobedience to his parent he do not preserve they alive they use no kind of musikce and many change their ordinary diet into courserfood upon the funeral day they provide great company funeral day many kinsfolk and friend meet together all clad in white with many Bonzi according to every man ability which sing with doleful instrument and by their apparel which they wear and their time in sing he that know they not will take they for clerk revest sing plain song for they much resemble they funeral figure they make many beeres with man of paper or of white silk many banner and other ensign the place whither the corpse go be adorn with many figure the corpse be put into a very great coffin this nation hold a great part of their felicity for they and their successor to consist in these thing of their funeral especial in two the coffin or chest wherein the corpse be to be lay and the place of their burial the stuff to make the coffin of coff^n wherein themselves be to be bury and the make of the coffin they leave not to other to do after their death neither then may the body look for much cost to make one of these coffin neither in this as a thing of great importance will they trust no not their own son but they themselves at leisure seek some kind of wood that be least corruptible and plank which be common four six or eight finger thick which because they be so thick and the chist or coffin very close shut they can keep their corpse in their house without any evil smell some spend in make their coffin seventy eighty and a hundred ducat they hold it for a felicity to be able to get one of these that be good on the contrary for a great disgrace not to have a coffin to bury himself in and they be very few which fail in that one point burial place the sepulchre and place thereof be the thing for choose whereof they use great sorcery or cast of lot and do it with great heedfulness and with the help of some that be skilful in this Art for they hold opinion that in make a good choice of the place depend a great part of their own good fortune and of their posterity and oftentimes they be a year in resolve whether it shall look towards the north or to any other part and therefore the great and most contentious suit which be in China be about place of burial these place of burial be always without the wall in the field or mountain wherein they build vault very well make and strong of brick stone or other matter wherein they lie the coffin and then close it up very sure unlucky to bury in the city and afterward now and then they come thither to perform certain ceremony and to bring thing to eat they hold it very unlucky to bury a dead man in the city and if they know it though he be the great man that be in China they will not suf-him to bewail his dead friend much especial those which be woman there be many which believe the pass of the soul from one body into another and therefore after the death of their father and mother transition of soul metempsuchicall superstition they will never kill any live beast yield for a reason why they will not do so lest some of they shall be their mother or father or some other other person and likewise many of they fast because that whereas some of they be poor they desire afterward to be bear again in a rich and honourable family although it be true that the most part of they believe not in idol and it offend they not to speak evil of they yet common all of they at a certain time of the year do they some reverence because it be the custom though in no sort they worship they as god idolatry and those which put most confidence in they burn paper incense and sweet smell unto they and kill beast before they their book of these idol speak of hell and in many place or in a manner in all the city there be set up a portraiture of hell make with bodily shape and many devil as ugly as we paint they it be very well set forth but bad believe for it good or bad fortune whether they shall have that which they desire or no and there be a infinite number of these soothsayer and all of they pratler mumbler and coosener whereby they deceive many and though the Chinois be of good understanding and know that these fellow know nothing and every foot do take they in lie yet for all this there be very few that when any occasion be offer do not consult with they and though they seem to be but few yet some of they be in league with the devil as oftentimes we gather by certain thing many of these grave man of China have common two folly wherein they do err more then in other thing the first be that they persuade themselves that they can much prolong their life and for this purpose they use a thousand invention and take many medicine study to prolong life which indeed rather do shorten their day there be many master and book of this folly which usual be grave and rich man there be many that make themselves very old folk who the people follow like saint to learn some rule of life of they wherein they put all their felicity many do not believe that we be so old as we say we be and that we do dissemble but that in deed we be a hundred year old and that we know this rule to live for ever and that we do not marry because we will live long the other folly be that they persuade themselves that they be able and go about to make silver the skill to be able to write well they print yearly great store of book in China and print every year a great number of book whereof there be no examination nor choice and every man print what he list good or bad and so they make a book of nothing the best which come forth be of no science for as I have say they know none but they be only of moral sentence to the advancement of good custom and government their manner of print be not like we for they join not their letter but for every leaf they make a table which have letter on both side it will seem to be very hard but with the custom which they have get Easie print they do it with great ease speed and cheapness I will send you some book well print that your worship may see it they also print letter in white I say white letter and the ground black and though in the former they come not near we yet in this they go far beyond we they usual print these letter in stone and the letter stand not in the stone upward to touch the paper direct but in the paper and the stone they stand all one way print white and this be the order whereby they do this they wet the paper and lay it upon the top of the stone they gentle beat it with some very gentle thing whereby the paper which lie upon the stone sink into the hollowness of the letter and rest low than the other then with a kind of ink which they have for this purpose they fine lay it over whereby the letter remain white because they be deep and the rest remain black I send you with this letter certain paper thereof that your worship may rejoice in behold the excellency frame that I be not able to understand it to reduce it into order only I will say in general that they have many good thing belong unto government but not the execution final it be a government of gentile government good if well execute law lawless with a thousand fault there be no great store of law but common they decide controversy of their own head and make law in their jurisdiction after their pleasure every one diverse and here your worship may imagine that the government in the practice can be very just since every one that can tell how to make a good theme or exercise be not sufficient to be lawmaker and it be very ordinary among they to direct all thing to their own profit whereby of necessity they commit many absurdity and wrong and take all that they can get bribe
