unless it be at the ordinary hour of feed and then they eat somewhat more when they visit one another unless they be very great friend and familiar a boy go always before which carry a libel or book of visitation which they call paytre which be as much as a paper of visitation and this name never fail for always they use it wherein his name with modest epithet as many perhaps as visitor be write according as the quality be of they that visit and those that be visit so be the manner most different whereafter they write the same to wit with more humility either as our better or as a equal or as a inferior as a scholar or as a master for as the relation be many and particular so the fashion and manner which they use be diverse of these thing and of all that hereafter I shall say touch this point I will send you the example in their own paper of visitation which great mandarin and ordinary man bring unto we set down in our tongue upon every letter the declaration thereof and I doubt not but your worship our most dear father and brethren and as many other as shall see the same will rejoice thereat and when that paper be bring they carry news into the house to he that be visit which prepare himself to receive his guest which come within a while after when they be not people which they see every day they use not ordinary apparel in their visitation but they have garment proper for this purpose of a far different fashion and if by chance one come so apparel and another be not he say that he dare not salute he nor receive he before he have put on his apparel so he get he away in great haste to put on his apparel and then they begin to perform their compliment when the guest depart he always go before and at their go out of the door they use salutation and offer of courtesy according to the quality of the guest take leave and the master of the house so he bring he more or less way or unto the street or if he go so far he stay till he take his chair or his horse and then lift up their arm and sleeve unto their head they take their leaf and depart one from the other when they be depart the visitor and he that be visit each of they send a boy to give one another thanks one for his visitation the other for his good entertainment and friendly usage if he that be visit be not at home they leave the paytre at his house which be a token that he come to visit he he that be visit be bind to requite his visitation present or the next day if he be a man of worship or if they be equal within three or four day which payment be perform after the self same manner and if he find he not at home it suffice to leave the paytre there if he that requite the visitation be a far great person than the first which visit he as if he be some great mandarin he which first visit he return the next day in person with a paper wherein he give he thanks that he come to his house and if they see one another he give he thanks by word of mouth head place of the house when the man which visit be of great worship he send word a good space before with a paytre and the master of the house come forth to receive he and to bring he into the house all their house and lodging have always a head and more honourable place which be the high part where always they place the guest great letter for great person likewise in their writing they use a great difference according to the estate dignity and age and in their letter the great the mandarin be they use the great letter those that be equal or inferior use a very small letter likewise they observe the same order in speak to every one according to his quality when they meet in the street the ordinary courtesy be to put their hand into their sleeve and close they together to hold they up and to use a common speech which they have for this purpose when a couple enter into new acquaintance they do yet more first acquaintance and that be they kneel down and touch the ground with their head so often and with so great ceremony that I dare not speak of they lest I shall never make a end send present when they send present they write down all thing which they send in a paper as they do their speech with word of honour whereof I send likewise example to see of very grave person which send we present and whether the party receive the present or not or only a part he always send back another paper with certain red line as herewith be to be see with a letter which say I thank you much and when he receive the present he always give some money to the youth that bring it and hereby he remain bind to answer he with another present as great at the least and herein they be very precise especial person that be not of the great account a thing which I find very strange and which do put we to much trouble to be drive equal to answer those present which the great mandarin do send we for they always desire some thing of our country and here we be very poor they send we sometime from Macao some clock of sand or hourglass some knife some case of tool for surgeon and other thing for they much esteem all thing that come from our part and with these thing which in our country be little or nothing worth here we procure friend which stand we in exceed great stead to confer with they of our holy faith and of the salvation of our soul beside their present and visitation they have gossip and banquet whereunto very usual they invite one another banquet when these be very solemn they set every guest two table for himself one of flesh and fish etc. another of fruit and sweet meat when they be not so solemn one table for every man or two at every table they provide for these guest great diversity of meat well dress and season which they bring soft and fair one after another that they may be hot when they invite one to a banquet they send six or seven day before a paper inuitation wherein they invite he against such a day if he can come he send another paper wherein he say I excuse myself if he excuse not himself he be resolve to come this paper be send with many word of courtesy and with much honour on the day appoint in the morning he send another to invite he again for the self same day and at the appoint hour he send another to pray he to come and then he go if any of these message shall fail he will not go when he be go to the banquet they use many other ceremony but the most ado be about their place so that it be long before you can place they and allot out the room how they shall sit because they ever seek or at least make show that they seek to give the chief room to other feast to taste and bride it they feed not as man use to do in our country neither seem it that the feast be make to feed but only they taste of some small thing for fashion sake and they drink very sip in small cup of porcelain each of which will contain five or six thimbels-full of wine and herein and in devise they spend five or six hour at a banquet and go home a hunger and thus it happen unto we although we seek to excuse ourselves from they as much as we can because we lose much time unless it be some great mandarin who we fear will take it evil if we shall deny his request when the banquet be end the next day every one of the guest send his boy with a paper wherein he thank his host for his good cheer Chinois complimental and almost all compliment New-yeere here your worship may see wherein the Chinois spend the one half of their life for the great business they have and that waste most of their time be in visitation banquet and send of present and the time wherein they most of all use the same be their new-year which last fifteen day their birth day which all of they keep with great solemnity or when they go forth or come home on a journey and to end the whole year I send you some paper of visitation of all these thing whereof they have send many unto we that your worship may see though you understand not the outward letter the manner and fashion of this people how far different salutation manner and fashion we send you from the plainness of our Europe and especial of our company but for the present we all think it necessary to eat after this fashion and to use their custom to obtain more free access unto they and to win they to Christ there be a Turk here a dweller in this city which above forty year ago bring one or two lion to the father of this king who a Turk disrespect partly because he know no learning nor science and partly because he seek not to apply himself to the habit custom and manner of China there be none that will deal with he nor come near his house and through the grace which God have give we and because they see we apply ourselves to their apparel fashion and courtesy all the grave mandarin come home to our house to visit we and do we the favour to hold we public for their friend which they use not to do to their own countryman of our quality and condition praise be our lord always amen I will not omit to declare the great pleasure wherewith these learned Chinois hear the great consent of the thing and ceremony of our holy faith in Europe and that we have bishop and as we call they here mandarin and superior in spiritual thing and above all they rejoice exceed to hear of our pope the hierarchy applaud by Chinois that be so great a personage they prefer a learned and holy man by way of election and not by succession and likewise the obedience and subjection which other king do yield unto he and that there have be many as we tell they who be choose pope refuse it in good earnest and by no mean will accept the same and that we have all thing which concern the law of God and good manner set down in writing with all other book concern he or his minister and although that which I have speak hitherto of our high priest be a thing very apparent and true and we deliver it for such and they so understand it yet oftentimes they have give we occasion of laughter the first be that when we tell they that some refuse so great a office straightway they ask where you say that they refuse it be it not evident that their excuse will not be accept as who shall say if they will accept of it who be there that will make a excuse and thus they say because they do so themselves ridiculous nicety for when great office be bestow upon they eftsoon they offer up a petition make a thousand excuse to the king not to receive they and they desi^e nothing less neither can any thing happen so grievous unto they as to accept their excuse but usual they be not admit though sometime they be to their great grief of heart as I myself have see but to excuse themselves or to refuse with some danger be the use so common that they will not fail to do so for if they shall not do so it be more certain that they shall go without the Office the second thing that make we more to laugh be that many of they tell we that if we will return into our country without doubt they will make we pope the reason though not open which they yield be that we have a great advantage above other man of our country to wit that we have see and study and understand their book because that they only in their opinion can make a man perfect and general see in all thing such be the high conceit and reputation which they hold of their book @. 7 of their woman of the tartar conquest act and expulsion the greatness of the king and neighbour state of the queen eunuch I will conclude this letter with two point the one concern the woman whereof I have little to say and the last be of the king and of his palace and service palace every man as I say before may keep as many wife as he will and so they do which be the cause of many tumult quarrel polygamy litigious and disorder in their house among their wife and among the son of diverse mother and therefore when we tell they that in our country no man marry but one wife they never be satisfy in praise it in word though nevertheless they do not follow it nor put it in practice and the discontentment which the woman have among themselves and with their husband for this occasion be like to prove a great encouragement unto they to make they desirous to receive our holy faith and to persuade their husband to embrace the same see that it do not permit any more but one lawful wife only of their other conversation custom and other thing we know nothing closeness of woman neither be any thing to be learn for they keep house all their life time and go out of door exceed seldom to visit either their mother or sister or near kinswoman for they go not to any else no not in thought and therefore as they have no conversation but always to keep home I can speak nothing of their behaviour their apparel seem unto i honest and comely for sometime I have see the wife of officer and of the poor people apparel for many of they do go abroad in some part of the country we have meet many woman upon the high way in short garment like to the man of our country without any difference save on their head and their foot for all the rest be all one kind of apparel but these be the common people only one of the great ornament that the woman have be to have very little foot and they be so little that they go very bad and always they seem to go as though they will fall small foot I can not know the cause nor the Chinois themselves know not the original occasion why this be count for a beauty albeit some say it begin not for a comeliness but only with a purpose to cut off all occasion from they of go abroad history of their king the Chinois have be very careful in their history and therefore they have history of their king of above four thousand year and if credit be to be give to that which their book report touch those time and be gather by diverse of their history there be many more year from the flood to our day whereof they also have some knowledge in their book than the most follow and allow calculation among we knowledge of the flood which tr^ate of that matter do allow of for they say it be six thousand year at the least they say that they have continue history but I leave this because I have not well confer the truth and foundation of the chinish history at the least it be certain that they have knowledge of their matter and certain king within a little after the flood whensoever it be they have many ancient king morality make a king and nature make a mandarine contrary to innumerable scripture etc. which be very good man which it may be be save in the law of nature because the heroical work of virtue which they report of they be great and there be no record that they worship idol but some that they worship the lord of heaven and earth there be some that seek not to leave their lawful son to be their heir because they think they not fit for government but choose the wise and best man that they can find and leave the kingdom unto he this kingdom in old time be divide into many small kingdom until by little and little it be unite it be some four hundred year as I say before since a tartar king possess it whole and two hundred since a Bonzo or religious man of China recover it this mahometan tartar king leave some token of himself in thing that he do he leave in Nanquin mathematical instrument certain mathematical instrument of copper the like whereof for goodness peradventure be not in all Europe at least not better the China the chinese Bonzo which expel he out of the kingdom be a very valiant and wise man and there be many history of his wisdom and sententious say and judgement in hard matter and the manner and form of government which he ordain in this kingdom new lord new law which continue inviolable do great declare the same he make new office and give new name to all of they a usual thing when one house begin to reign to change all even the name of the king as also of all office and also of many city I omit the division of the government into so many head and so good distribution that it seem and so the Chinois say it be like to continue thousand of year so that no man of the same kingdom be able nor have any power to make any rebellion of importance for those which in former time revolt be the viceroy of the province and other great mandarin in who power be the government the soldier and the treasure but he divide it in such sort that those which have power over the soldier rebellion prevent by the policy shall have no money at all neither shall the pay of the soldier depend upon they and those which keep the treasure must have no superintendency and dominion over the soldier other which be mighty and rich he impoverish and divide their authority and revenue among many and so there be no man that can call himself great I remember that I have read in a book set out in the spanish tongue of the great power of certain captain and because the king do not trust they he send one of his house to will they to come unto he all which relation with many other thing which he report of the providence of the king how he divide his authority among diverse prince be not so in truth neither in truth neither be there any appearance thereof neither have the captain much authority neither be they very rich for though they have many people yet the government of they be divide into diverse head so that they can hardly assemble to raise any rebellion especial because they remain always in the kingdom and near about the King revenue the revenue of this king without doubt be exceed great and until we have get it out of their book wherein every thing be set down very particular I will not presume to publish the same not as though I know not that it be so since while a man know more of this kingdom he doubt less yet because I fear for all this that it will be hard to make one believe the same which know it not of a certainty make the account not very large his revenue be one year with another a hundred million in silver 100 million other say 150. gold Rice and a infinite number of other thing although the great part be silver and he that consider the greatness of the kingdom and that every man pay tribute to the king of their person land tree and other thing without carry any tribute out of the same that which I speak will not seem excessive expense but as his revenue be very great so his expense be many for those which in this kingdom do live at the king charge be many to wit all the mandarin to who the king give Wages all the soldier all the kinsfolk of the king his eunuch and a infinite number of people whereby his charge be exceed great although always there remain a good deal for he to lay up and there be no doubt but he have it in store in exceed great quantity many small kingdom round about acknowledge the king of China and pay he tribute neighbour kingdom corea or Corai as corea and other who name I know not on this northern part and on the side of malaca and Macao many other and sometime on these northern part they trouble he somewhat in rob and kill of people it may be that your worship or some body else may demand why the king of China be so great subdue not these small kingdom that lie about he to deliver himself of trouble I answer that he want no ability a paradox but I will say one sure thing a paradox to the people of our Europe which be that neither the Chinois nor their king do seek nor dream of dilate their empire more than it be contentedness and this their resolution be such that although they will give they all these kingdom they will not take they and much less if they be far off for they hold it for one of the great misery especial the mandarin and grave sort of people to go out of their kingdom to any other part there be one of the best example hereof that may be give which fall out of late corea join to the continent of China and that be that as by the danger which may grow to his kingdom if the people of japon shall win the kingdom of corea which be join to China by the main land as they begin to do the Chinois aid the corean with many man and the people of japon by the death of their king call do whole abandon it the kingdom remain in the power of the Chinois and so continue two or three year after which they whole give it over without any other great respect then that there be none that be willing to go thither to govern it nor that the king have any need to annex it unto his estate and without doubt it seem that he will do the like with any other although they will put it into his hand and touch those kingdom which pay he tribute there be no great account make whether they come or no and their continual come be more for the profit of those which come then that the king do desire it and therefore the Philippine island which in former time pay tribute to the king of China be make none account of when they cease to pay it this king have one lawful wife as other man have in choice whereof they have regard to nothing else but to her good quality and external beauty for there be no nobility to be seek for beside she he have a great number of concubine choose after the same manner who son if the lawful wife child fail inherit the kingdom which common fall out and such be he which now be king and he which be to succeed he queen closeness when any of these woman be once enter into the king palace to be his wife there be no name which may be compare unto she in be keep close for they may not only not go abroad no nor be see of their father mother or brethren they have little or none authority but such as they obtain of the King also the service of the king of the queen and of his concubine be all by eunuch a service doubtless unworthy of a King eunuch all these eunuch without any exception be of the most base people which be in all the kingdom who father because they can keep they when they be young do make they eunuch in hope that one day they shall get into the court to serve the king the manner be far different from some which be in Europe for these be like those which the turk use the yard and all cut away because their father do this for poverty it follow that they have no excellency for they have no mean to learn it and they be little or nothing learned they elect and choose these eunuch from time to time to supply such as die and this first year that I be here they choose above three thousand for which purpose there assemble above twenty thousaind as they say out of which number they make their choice the elector be a very great mandarin to who as I say before their number and choice the king private business belong and another eunuch of the elder and most private the examination and election consist in two thing which be a good countenance and a good tongue for proof whereof they make they pronounce two word wherein those that have not a ready tongue do stumble when they be choose and go to the court they divide they in diverse office service yet at their first come they be appoint to wait upon the old eunuch as boy which make good trial of their patience and obedience and he that after certain year show himself towardly they begin to employ in great matter of these eunuch the king have his musician and mathematician who to be brief ignorance I say have no sound understanding in th^se thing at all but only for compliment or superficial yet some of they be bind to watch all night and to look whether any comet do appear or any such like thing in the sky to inform the king thereof and to perform other like office they be usual very covetous and as they be base covetousness if they rise to be private with the king some of they be proud and uncourteous they serve the king as slave obey his will which way soever he incline the king chastise they very sharp for every light offence especial the king that now be which be a very wicked man he have cause many to be whip to death for some small matter wherein they have offend he yet there be some of they good and discreet which the king use for dispatch of his business and other matter of weight though the ordinary wage which they have of the king be small yet it serve they well to live of and therefore they go very well apparel in many robe of silk very fine wrought of diverse colour and the manner of their cap and apparel differ from all other people there be of they in number as they say above sixteen thousand of they in the king palace hereby your worship may see what example and education the king of China observe which spend all his time with these and with woman although it be the custom of these king to show themselves from time to time to certain of the great mandarin yet they never suffer the rest of the people to see they nor to speak with they the common people never see nor speak with the King law of nation contemn and when he speak with any body they enter not into the place where he be but the king come forth to a certain place if there be any nation among who the law of nation have no place in many thing it be this for as they have no commerce with other nation so they have not the law which be common to all man and therefore they admit no ambassador in China unless it be by the way of give some present the king not acknowledge any neither do they think that there be any in the world which be able to deal with their king by way of a ambassador emb^assages and if they bring any message as and the entertainment which they give they and honour which they show to all stranger which come unto they be very small but as for the most part they have no great conceit of stranger so their entertainment be like to their conceit whosoever he be that come into their country they shut he up in a very homely house not suffer he to go abroad royal palace the king palace be very great and albeit in the excellency of architecture they be not comparable to those of our Europe yet they much exceed in the hugeness of building they have three wall four square the circuit of the first may be as big as the wall of a good city between the first and the second wall there be a wall which environ the great part of the house and here be many house of the eunuch of the low sort which exercise Chinois person describe the Chinois be white but near the south more brown with thin beard some have none with stare hair and late grow their hair whole black eye narrow of egg form black and stand out the nose very little and scarce stand forth ear mean in some province they be square face many of Canton and Quamsi province on their little toe have two nail woman as they have general in cachinchina their woman be all low and account great beauty in little foot for which cause from their infancy they bind they straight with clothes that one will judge they stump-footed this as be think devise to make they housewife hair the man and woman both alike let their hair grow without cut but boy and girl till they be fifteen year old be cut round leave a lock only on the crown after which they let it grow loose over their shoulder till twenty the most of the priest shave head and beard every eight day when they be man they bind up their hair in a cap or coif make of horse or man hair or in a silken cawl and in winter of woollen on the top it have a hole where the hair come forth and be tie in a neat knot the woman wear not this cap ring but bind up their hair in a knot and make it up with a dress of gold silver stone and flower they wear ring on their ear but not on their finger apparel the man and woman wear long garment the man double they on their breast and fasten they under both the armhole the woman on the midst of the breast they wear wide long sleeve but the woman wide the man straight at the wrist their cap be artificial wrought their shoe be much differ from we the man wear they of silk with diverse work and flower exceed the elegance of our matron shoe of leather none but the mean sort wear and scarce admit they leather sole but of Cloth the cap of their learned be square of other round every one spend half a hour at least in comb and trim his hair they wind also long clout about their foot and leg and therefore wear their breeches loose they wear no shirt but a white coat next the skin and wash often they have a servant to carry a shadow or great Sumbrero over their head against the rain and sun the poor carry one for themselves name-ceremony woman have none father name for name beside the surname of which be speak the father give one to the son for female have no name but the father surname and call as they be bear first second three in order of the sister by this name they be call by the father and elder other call they likewise from that order among the brethren as be say of sister they in their write call themselves by that which their father give they but if other either equal or superior shall so call they it be both uncivil and injurious when a boy go to school his master give he another name school-name which be call his school-name whereby only his master and schoolfellow may style he when he have his man cap put on and marry a wife some more honourable person give he a more honourable name letter-name which they call the letter by this any man may call he but those which be subject to he and when he be now at the full growth gr^^t name he receive of some grave person his most honourable name which they call great whereby any may call he present or absent but his parent and elder still use the letter-name if any profess a new sect his instructor call he by a new name which they call of religion religious name great th^n christian name and when one visit another he will ask what be his honourable name to style he thereby and we be therefore fain to take a great name than that which we receive in baptism for they to call we by they be studious of antiquity much value old trivet of bell metal picture in black and white character and write seal with the author seal for there be many counterfeiter the officer have all a seal proper to their place give by humvu seal of magistrate which they use only seal with red colour and if they lose the seal they lose the office and be beside severe punish and therefore they carry it with they in a seal and lock box and never leave it out of sight at night keep it under their pillow grave man go not on foot through the street but be carry in a seat close except they list to open the forepart whereas magistrate seat be every way open matron seat be altogether close seat in which they be carry on man shoulder boat and ship but easy know from man by the fashion the law forbid coach and litter some city be in the midst of river and lake in which they have very neat boat to pass the street and because they go more by water then we therefore their ship be more convenient and elegant but the magistrate build by public cost be as commodious as house with diverse lodging a hall kitchen cell so neat as seem great man house rather than ship and therefore they make their solemn banquet a shipboard pass along the river and lake for further pleasure all within shine with Ciaram or shine varnish in diverse colour and the carve work gild in place with combine sweet to the eye and nose they honour their master more than with we master respect so that if a man have be another scholar but one day in any art he call he master ever after and never sit in any meeting but at his side and do he all honour diceplay and card be common with they chess also with the grave person not altogether unlike we but their king never remove but to the four next room game chess and the bishop have their queen they have also which they call powder paune which go before the knight and follow the paune they have a grave game in a table of three hundred room with two hundred man white and black in which magistrate spend much time and the cunning skill whereof get much credit to a man although he can do nothing else and some choose such their master with wont rite theft be not punish with death theft punishment the second fault therein be brand with a hot iron and ink in the arm with two character the three time in the with sixteen other man through a Fenniemarsh about the dawn of the day they meet to their seem a great tree lie along the ground the bough be lop off upon which they all begin to sit down and rest themselves but no soon be they sit but that which they take for a tree fierce rouse itself from under they and leave they all to pick straw on the ground for indeed this be one of those serpent their custom be as they say to put themselves in ambush among the bough of a tree and when they espy their prey to draw near be it man or beast they fall upon he with open mouth and devour it wild beast circuit for than they shut they sudden or if they be shut they open they not till the offender be find the king bestow these command on those who be best learned this be a most fair city and well very much from itself by reason of the year difference of Russia in different season so that a man will marvel to see the great alteration and difference betwixt the winter and the summer in Russia the whole country in the winter lie under snow which fall continual and be sometime of a yard or two thick but great towards the north. the river and other water be all freeze up a yard or more thick how swift or broad soever they be and this continue common five month viz. from the begin of November till towards the end of march what time the snow begin to melt so that it will breed a frost in a man to look abroad at that time the cold of Russia and see the winter face of that country the sharpness of the air you may judge of by this for that water drop down or cast up into the air congeal into ice before it come to the ground in the extremity of winter if you hold a pewter dish or pot in your hand m. Cole minister to sir Jerome bow tell i of a liquorish fellow which take a pewter dish of some sweet sauce from his master table in the next room lick it and pay the skin of his tongue for that sweet taste a sour sauce to sweet sauciness the case alter effect of snow or any other metal except in some chamber where their warm stove be your finger will freeze fast unto it and draw of the skin at the part when you pass out of a warm room into a cold you shall sensible feel your breath to wax stark and even stifle with the cold as you draw it in and out diverse not only that travel abroad but in the very market and street of their town be mortal pinch and kill withal so that you shall see many drop down in the street many traveller bring into the town sit dead and stiff in their sled diverse lose their nose the tip of their ear and the ball of their cheek their toe foot etc. many time when the winter be very hard and extreme the bear and wolf issue by troop out of the wood drive by hunger and enter the village tear and raven all they can find so that the inhabitant be fain to flee for safeguard of their life and yet in the summer time you shall see such a new hue and face of a country the wood for the most part which be all of fir and birch so fresh and so sweet the pasture and meadow so green and well grow and that upon the sudden such variety of flower such noise of bird special of nightingale that seem to be more loud and of a more variable note then in other country that a man shall not light travel in a more pleasant country and this fresh and speedy growth of the spring there seem to proceed from the benefit of the snow which all the winter time be spread over the whole country as a white robe and keep it warm from the rigour of the frost in the spring time when the sun wax warm and dissolve it into water do so thorough drench and soak the ground that be somewhat of a sleight and sandy mould and then shine so hot upon it again that it draw the herb and plant forth in great plenty and variety in a very short time as the winter exceed in cold so the summer incline to overmuch heat special in the month of june july and August be much warm than the summer air Trane oil the manner of hunt the seale-fish a other very great and principal commodity be their trane-oyle draw out of the seal-fish where it will not be impertinent to show the manner of their hunt the seal which they make this oil of which be in this sort towards the end of summer before the frost begin they go down with their boat into the bay of saint Nicholas to a cape call cusconesse or foxnose where they leave their boat till the next springtide when the sun wax warm towards the spring and yet the ice not melt within the bay they return thither again then draw their boat over the sea ice they use they for house to rest and lodge in there be common about seventeen or eighteen fleet of they of great large boat which divide themselves into diverse company five or six boat in a consort they that first find the haunt fire a beacon which they carry with they for the nonee which be espy by the other company by such among they as be appoint of purpose they come all together and compass the seal round about in a ring that lie Sunning themselves together upon the ice common four or five thousand in a shoal and so they invade they every man with his club in his hand if they hit they on the nose they be soon kill if on the side or back they bear out the blow and many time so catch and hold down the club with their tooth by main force that the party be force to call for help to his fellow the manner of the seal be when they see themselves beset to gather all close together in a throng or plumb to sway down the ice and to break it if they can which so bend the ice that many time it take the sea-water upon it and make the hunter to wade a foot or more deep after the slaughter when they have kill what they can they fall to share every boat his part in equal portion and so they slay they take from the body the skin and the lard or fat with all that cleave to the skin this they take with they leave the body behind and so go to shore where they dig pit in the ground of a fathom and a half deep or there about and so take the fat or lard off from the skin they throw it into the pit and cast in among it hot burn stone to melt it withal the uppermost and pure be sell and use to oil wool for cloth the grosser that be of a red colour they sell to make Sope. likewise Ickary or cavery a great quantity be make upon the river of Volgha 7. gentleman of novograde and the territory about which only be soldier after the discipline of those country have war with the tartar which be well perform and end by they they return homeward where they understand by the way that their Cholopey or bondslave who they leave at home pleasant history have in their absence possess their town land house wife and all at which news be somewhat amaze and yet disdain the villainy of their servant they make the more speed home and so not far from novograde meet they in warlike manner march against they whereupon advise what be best to be do they agree all to set upon they with no other show of weapon but with their horse whip which as their manner be every man ride withal to put they in remembrance of their servile condition thereby to terrify they and abate their courage like lip like lettuce and so march on and lash altogether with their whip in their hand they give the onset which seem so terrible in the ear of their villain and strike such a sense into they of the smart of the whip which they have feel before that they flee altogether like sheep before the driver in memory of this victory the novogradians ever since have stamp their coin which they call a dingoe Novogrodskoy currant through all Russia with the figure of a horseman shake a whip aloft in his hand these two city exceed the rest in greatness for strength their chief town be Vobsko Cazan and astracan as lie upon the border but for situation jaruslave far exceed the rest for beside the commodity that the soil yield of pasture and corn jaruslave it lie upon the famous the other town have nothing that be great memorable save many ruin within their wall which show the decrease of the ruff people under this government the street of their city and town in stead of pave be plank with fir tree plain and lay ven close the one to the other their house be of wood without any lime or stone the manner of Russee building build very close and warm with fir tree plain and pile one upon another they be fasten together with dent or notch at every corner and so clasp fast together betwixt the tree or timber they thrust in moss whereof they gather plenty in their wood to keep out the air every house have a pair of stair that lead up into the chamber out of the yard or street after the scottish manner this building seem far better for their country then that of stone and brick as be cold and more dampish than their wooden house special of fir that be a dry and warm wood whereof the providence of God have give they such store as that you may build a fair house for twenty or thirty rubbel or little more where wood be most scant the great inconvenience of their wooden building be the aptness for fire which happen very oft and in very fearful sort by reason of the dryness and fatness of the fir that be once fire burn like a torch and be hardly quench till all be burn up the surname of the imperial house of Russia be call Beala^ it take the original as be ruff emperor the solemnity use at the ruff emperor coronation be on this manner in the great church of precheste or our lady within the emperor castle be erect a stage whereon stand a Scrine that bear upon it the imperial cap and robe of very rich stuff when the day of the inauguration be come there resort thither first the patriarch with the metropolitan archbishop bishop abbot and prior all rich clad in their then enter the deacon with the quire of singer who so soon as the emperor set foot into the church begin to sing many year may live noble Theodore juanowich etc. whereunto the patriarch and Metropolite with the rest of the clergy answer with a certain hymn in form of a prayer sing it all together with a great noise the hymn be end the patriarch with the emperor mount up the stage where stand a seat ready for the emperor whereupon the patriarch will he to sit down and then place himself by he upon another seat provide for that purpose bow down his head towards the ground and say this prayer oh lord God king of king lord of lord which by thy prophet Samuel do choose thy servant David and anoint he for king over thy people Israel hear now our prayer and look from thy sanctuary upon this thy servant Theodore who thou have choose and exalt for king over these thy holy nation anoint he with the oil of gladness protect he by thy power but upon his head a crown of gold and precious stone give he length of day place he in the seat of justice strengthen his arm make subject unto he all the barbarous nation let thy fear be in his whole heart turn he from all error and show he the salvation of thy holy and universal church that he may judge thy people with justice and protect the child of the poor and final attain everlasting life this prayer he speak with a low voice and then pronounce a loud all praise and power to God the father the son and the holy ghost the prayer be end he command certain abbot to reach the imperial robe and cap which be do very decent and with great solemnity the patriarch withal pronounce aloud peace be unto all and so he begin another prayer to this effect bow yourselves together with we and pray to he that reign over all preserve he oh lord under thy holy protection keep he that he may do good and holy thing let justice shine forth in his day that we may live quiet without strife and malice this be pronounce somewhat soft by the patriarch whereto he add again aloud thou be the king of the whole world and the saviour of our soul to thou the father son and holy ghost be all praise for ever and ever amen then put on the robe and the cap he bless the emperor with the sign of the cross say withal in the name of the father the son and the holy ghost the like be do by the Metropolites archbishop and bishop who all in their order come to the chair and one after another bless the emperor with their two fore-finger then be say by the patriarch another prayer that begin o most holy virgin mother of God etc. after which a deacon pronounce with a high loud voice many year to noble Theodore good honourable belove of God great duke of volodemer of Mosko emperor and monarch of all Russia etc. whereto the other priest and deacon that stand somewhat far of by the altar or table answer sing many year many year to the noble Theodore the same note be take up by the priest and deacon that be place at the right and left side of the church and then altogether they chant and thunder out sing many year to the noble Theodore good honourable belove of God great duke of Volodemer Mosko emperor of all Russia etc. these solemnity be end first come the patriarch with the Metropolites archishop and bishop than the nobility and the whole company in their order to do homage to the emperor bend down their head and knock they at his foot to the very ground the style wherewith he be invest at his coronation run after this manner Theodore juanowich by the grace of God great lord and emperor of all Russia great duke of Volodemer Mosko and novograd king of Cazan king of astracan lord of Plesko and great duke of Smolensko of Twerria joughoria Permia Vadska Bulghoria and other lord and great duke of Novograd of the low country of Chernigo rezan Polotskoy rostove yaruslaveley Bealozera Leifland Oudoria Obdoria and commander of all siberia and of the north part and lord of many other country etc. this stile contain in it all the emperor province and set forth his greatness and therefore they have a great delight and pride in it force not only there own people but also stranger that have any matter to deliver to the emperor by speech or writing to repeat the whole form from the begin to the end which breed much cavil and sometime quarrel betwixt they and the tartar and Poland ambassador who refuse to call he Czar that be emperor and to repeat the other part of his long style myself when I have audience of the emperor think good to salute he only with thus much viz. emperor of all Russia great duke of Volodemer Mosko and novograd king of Cazan king of astracan the rest I omit of purpose because I know they glory to have their style appear to be of a large volume than the queen of England but this be take in so ill part that the chancellor who then attend the emperor with the rest of the nobility with a loud chase voice call still upon i to say out the rest whereto I answer that the emperor style be very long and can not so well be remember by stranger that I have repeat so much of it as may show that I give honour to the rest etc. but all will not serve till I command my interpreter to say it all out the manner of their government be much after the turkish fashion chap. 7. the state or form of their government the ruff government tyrannical which they seem to imitate as near as the country and reach of their capacity in politic affair will give they leave to do the state and form of their government seem to apply all to the behoof of the prince and that after a most open manner as may appear by the or secret of their government afterward set down aswell for the keep of the nobility and commons in a under proportion and far uneven balance in their several degree as also in their imposition and exaction without any regard of nobility or people far than it give the nobility a kind of liberty to exact upon the commons and base sort of people in all part of the realm wheresoever they come special in the place where their land lie or where they be appoint by the emperor to govern under he also to the commons some small contentment in that they pass over their land by descent of inheritance to whether son they will gavill-kind give-all-kind tenure absolute sovereignty which common they do after our gavill kind and dispose of their good by gift or testament without any controlment concern the principal point and matter of state wherein the sovereignetie consist as the make and annul of public law the make of magistrate power to make war or league with any foreign state to execute or to pardon life with the right of appeal in all matter both civil and criminal they do so whole and absolute pertain to the emperor and his counsel under he as that he may be say to be both the sovereign commander and the executioner of all these for as touch any law or public order of the realm it be ever determine of before any public assembly or parliament be summon where beside his council he have none other to consult with he of such matter as be conclude before hand but only a few bishop abbot and friar to make advantage of the people superstition even against themselves which think all to be holy and just that pass with consent of their bishop and clergy man whatsoever it be for which purpose the emperor be content to make much of the corrupt state of the church as now it be among they and to nourish the same by extraordinary favour and immunity to the bishop sea abbey and friary as know superstition and false religion best to agree with a tyrannical state and to be a special mean to uphold and maintain the same magistracy second as touch the public office and magistracy of the realm there be none hereditary neither any so great nor so little in that country but the bestow of it be do immediate by the emperor himself insomuch that the very diack or clerk in every head town be for the most part assign by himself notwithstanding the emperor that now be the better to intend his devotion refer all such matter pertain to the state whole to the order of his wife brother he succeed he jurisdiction the lord Borris Federewich Godonoe three the like be to be say of the jurisdiction concern matter judicial special such as concern life and death wherein there be none that have any authority or public jurisdiction that go by descent or be hold by charter but all at the appointment and pleasure of the emperor and the same practise by the judge with such awe and restraint as that they dare not determine upon any special matter but must refer the same whole up to the Mosko to the emperor council to show his sovereignty over the life of his subject the late emperor juan Vasilowich in his walk or progress juan Vasilowich cruel if he have mislike the face or person of any man who he meet by the way or that look upon he will command his head to be strike off which be present do and the head cast before he appeal and pardon four for the sovereign appeal and give of pardon in criminal matter to such as be convict it be whole at the pleasure and grace of the emperor wherein also the empress that now be be a woman of great clemency and withal delight to deal in public affair of the realm the rather to supply the defect of her husband do behave herself after a absolute manner give out pardon special on her birth day and other solemn time in her own name by open proclamation without any mention at all of the emperor some there have be of late of the ancient nobility that have hold diverse province by right of inheritance ancient nobility with a absolute authority and jurisdiction over they to order and determine all matter within their own precinct without all appeal or controlment of the emperor but this be all annul and wring clean from they by juan Vasilowich father to this emperor chap. 8. the manner of hold the parliament the state of parliament their high court of public consultation for matter of state be call the zabore that be the public assembly the state and degree of person that be present at their parliament be these in order 1. the emperor himself 2. some of his nobility about the number of twenty be all of his council 3. certain of the clergyman etc. about the same number as for burgher or other to represent the commonalty they have no place there the people be of no better account with they then as servant or bondslave that be to obey not to make law nor to know any thing of public matter before they be conclude the order of the summons or assemble the court of parliament call zabore be hold in this manner the emperor cause to to be summon such of his nobility as himself think meet be as be say all of his council together with the patriarch who call his clergy to wit the two Metropolites the two archbishop with such bishop abbot and friar as be of best account and reputation among they when they be all assemble at the emperor court the day be intimate when the session shall begin which common be upon some Friday for the religion of that day Friday respect when the day be come the clergyman assemble before at the time and place appoint which be call the stollie and when the emperor come attend by his nobility they arise all and meet he in a outroom follow their patriarch who bless the emperor with his two fore-finger lay they on his forehead and the side of his face and then kiss he on the right side of his breast so they pass on into their parliament house where they sit in this order the emperor be enthronize on the one side of the chamber in the next place not far from he at a small square table that give room to twelve person or thereabouts sit the patriarch with the Metropolites and bishop and certain of the principal nobility of the emperor council together with two diack or secretary call Dunmoy dyakey that enact that which pass the rest place themselves on bench round about the room every man in his rank after his degree then be there propound by one of the secretary who represent the speaker the cause of their assembly and the principal matter that they be to consider of for to propound bill what every man think good for the public benefit as the manner be in England the ruff parliament allow no such custom nor liberty to subject the point be open their discourse at parliament the patriarch with his clergyman have the prerogative to be first ask their vote or opinion what they think of the point propound by the secretary whereto they answer in order according to their degree but all in one form without any discourse as have learn their lesson before that serve their turn at all parliament alike whatsoever be propound common it be to this effect that the emperor and his council be of great wisdom and experience touch the policy and public affair of the realm and far better able to judge what be profitable for the commonwealth than they be which attend upon the service of God only and matter of religion and therefore it may please they to proceed that instead of their advice they will aid they with their prayer as their duty and vocation do require etc. to this or like effect have make their answer every man in his course up stand some abbot or friar more bold than the rest yet appoint beforehand as a matter of form and desire the emperor it will please his majesty to command to be deliver unto they what his majesty own judgement and determinate pleasure be as touch those matter propound by his de^ake whereto be reply by the say secretary in the emperor name that his highness with those of his noble council upon good and sound advice have find the matter propose to be very good and necessary for the commonwealth of his realm notwithstanding forasmuch as they be religious man and know what be right his majesty require their godly opinion yea and their censure too for the approve or correct of the say proposition and therefore desire they again to speak their mind free and if they shall like to give their consent that then the matter may pass to a full conclusion hereunto when the clergyman have give their consent which they use to do without any great pause they take their leaf with blessing of the emperor who bring the patriarch on his way so fair as the next room and so return to his seat till all be make ready for his return homeward the act that thus be pass by the zabore or parliament the deiakeis or secretary draw into a form of proclamation which they send abroad into every province and head town of the realm to be publish there by the duke and diakeis or secretary of those place the session of parliament be full end the emperor invite the clergieman to a solemn dinner and so they depart every man to his home the degree of person or estate of Russia beside the sovereign state or emperor himself be these in their order 1. the nobility which be of four sort chap. 9 of the nobility and by what mean it be keep in a under proportion agreeable to that State the Vdelney Knazey chief of the nobility whereof the chief for birth authority and revenue be call the Vdelney Knazey that be the exempt or privilege duke these hold sometime a several jurisdiction and absolute authority within their precinct much like unto the state or noble of Germany but afterward reserve their right upon composition they yield themselves to instrument or private petition which they make to the emperor so that now they hold their authority land life and all at the emperor pleasure as the rest do the mean and practice whereby he wrought this to effect against those and other of the nobility so well as I can note out of the report of his do be these and such like first he cast private emulation among they about prerogative of their title and dignity wherein he use to set on the inferior to prefer or equal themselves to those that be account to be of the noble house where he make his advantage of their malice and contention the one against the other by receive devise matter and accusation of secret practice and conspiracy to be intend against his person and State and so have single out the great of they and cut they off with the good like of the rest he fall at last to open practice by force of the other to yield their right unto he the faction of Oppressini and Zempskey devise by the emperor 2. he divide his subject into two part or faction by a general schism the one part he call the Oppressini or select man these be such of the nobility and gentry as he take to his own part to protect and maintain they as his faithful subject the other he call Zemskey or the commons the Zemskey contain the base and vulgar sort with such nobleman and gentleman as he mean to cut off as suspect to mislike his government and to have a meaning to practice against he wherein he provide that the Oppressini for number and quality of valour money armour etc. far exceed the other of the Zempskey side who he put as it be from under his protection so that if any of they be spoil or kill by those of the Oppressini which he account of his own part there be no amends to be seek for by way of public justice or by complaint to the emperor the whole number of both part be orderly register and keep in a book so that every man know who be a Zempskey man and who of the Oppressini and this liberty of the one part to spoil and kill the other without any help of magistrate or law that continue seven year enrich that side and the emperor treasury and wrought that withal which he intend by this practice viz. to take out of the way such of the nobility as himself mislike whereof be slay within one week to the number of three hundred within the city of Mosko this mischievous practice of make a general schism and public division among the subject of his whole realm proceedeed as shall seem from a extreme doubt and desperate fear which he have conceive of most of his nobility and gentleman of his realm in his war with the polonian and Chrim Tartar what time he grow into a vehement suspicion conceive of the ill success of his affair that they practise treason with the polonian and Chrim whereupon he execute some and devise this way to be rid of the rest pomestnoy tenure 3. have thus pull they and seize all their inheritance land privilege etc. save some very small part which he leave to their name he give they ready dress 3. they make a open show of want when any great tax or imposition be towards as be do by this emperor Theodore juanowich by the advice of some about he at the begin of his reign when be leave very rich as be think by his father he sell most of his plate and stamp some into coin that he may seem to want money whereupon present out come a taxation 4. they suffer their subject to give free to the monastery which for their superstition very many do special in their last will and to lay up their money and substance in they to keep it more safe which all be permit they without any doubt of in the other emperor day to this end juan Vasilowich late emperor use a very strange practice a strange practice to get money that few prince will have do in their great extremity he resign his kingdom to one Simeon the emperor son of Cazan as though he mean to draw himself from all public do to a quiet private life towards the end of the year he cause this new king to call in all charter grant to bishopricke and monastery which they have enjoy many hundred year before which be all cancel this do as in dislike of the fact and of the misgovernment of the new king he resume his sceptre and so be content as in favour to the church and religious man that they shall renew their charter and take they of himself reserve and annex to the crown so much of their land as himself think good by this practice he wring from the bishopricke and monastery beside the land which he annex to the crown a huge mass of money from some forty from some fifty from some a hundred thousand rubbel and this as well for the increase of his treasury as to abate the ill opinion of his hard government by a show of worse in another man wherein his strange spirit be to be note that be hate of his subject as himself know well enough yet shall venture such a practice to set another in his saddle that may have rid away with his horse while himself walk by on foot 5. they send their messenger into the province or shire where the special commodity of their country grow as fur wax honey etc. there to forestall and engross sometime one whole commodity sometime two or more take they at small price what themselves list and sell they again at a excessive rate to their own merchant and to merchant stranger if they refuse to buy they then to force they unto it the like be do when any commodity either native or foreign as cloth of gold broadcloth etc. thus engross by the emperor and receive into his treasury happen to decay or mar by long lie or some other casualty which be force upon the merchant to be buy by they at the emperor price whether they will or no. this last year of 1589. be engross all the wax of the country so that none may deal with that commodity but the emperor only 6. to take up and engross in like sort sometime foreign commodity as silk cloth lead pearl etc. bring into his realm by turkish merchant armenian Bougharians pole english and outstretch and then to force his merchant to buy they of his officer at his own price 7. they make a monopoly for the time of such commodity as be pay he for rent or custom and to enhance the price of they as fur corn wood etc. what time none must sell of the same kind of commodity till the emperor be all sold. by this mean he make of his rent corn and other provision of victual as before be say about 200000. rubbel or mark a year of his rent wood hay etc. 30000. rubbel or thereabouts 8. in every great town of his realm he have a Caback or other drink house where be sell aquavitae which they call concern the manner of their government and the state of the nobility with the order of their province and chief town of the Land and first touch their liberty how it stand with they it may appear by this that they be reckon in no degree at all nor have any suffrage nor place in their zabore or high court of parliament where their law and public order be conclude upon again into what servile condition their liberty be bring not only to the prince but to the noble and gentleman of the country who themselves also be but servile special of late year it may further appear by their own acknowledgement in their supplication and other write to any of the noble or chief officer of the emperor wherein they name and subscribe themselves kolophey that be their villain or bondslave as they of the nobility do unto the emperor this may true be say of they that there be no servant nor bondslave more awe by his master nor keep down in a more servile subjection than the poor people be and that universal not only by the emperor but by his nobility chief officer and soldier so that when a poor mousick meet with any of they upon the high way misery of those time manner and man he must turn himself about as not dare to look he on the face and fa^l down with knock of his head to the very ground as he do unto his idol second concern the land good and other possession of the commons they answer the name and lie common indeed without any fence against the rapine and spoil not only of the high but of his nobility officer and soldier beside the tax custom seazure and other public exaction do upon they by the emperor they be so rack and pull by the noble officer and messenger send abroad by the emperor in his public affair special in the yamme as they call they and through fair town that you shall have many village and town of half a mile and a mile long stand all unhabited the people be flee all into other place by reason of the extreme usage and exaction do upon they so that in the way towards Mosko betwixt Vologda and yaruslaveley which be two ninety after their reckon little more than a hundred mile english there be in sight fifty or village at the least some half a mile some a mile long that stand vacant and desolate without any inhabitant the like be in all other place of the realm as be say by those that have better travel the country than myself have time or occasion to do the great oppression over the poor commons make they to have no courage in follow their trade for the more they have the more danger they be in not only of their good but of their life also and if they have any thing they conceal it all they can sometime convey it into monastery sometime hide it under the ground and in wood as man be wont to do where they be in fear of foreign invasion insomuch that many time you shall see they afraid to be know to any Boiuren or gentleman of such commodity as they have to sell. I have see they sometime when they have lay open their commodity for a like as their principal fur and such like to look still behind they and towards every door as man in some fear that look to be set upon and surprise by some enemy whereof ask the cause I find it to be this that they have doubt lest some nobleman or Sinaboiarskey of the emperor have be in company and so lay a train for they to pray upon their commodity perforce this make the people though otherwise harden to bear any toil to give themselves much to idleness and drink as pass for no more then from hand to mouth and hereof it come that the commodity of Russia as be say before as wax tallow hides flax hemp etc. grow and go abroad in far less plenty than they be wont to do because the people be oppress and spoil of their get be discourage from their labour yet this one thing be much to be note that in all this oppression there be three brethren merchant of late that trade together with one stock in common that be find to be worth 300000. rubbel in money rich russian merchant beside land cattle and other commodity which may partly be impute to their dwelling far off from the eye of the court viz. in Wichida one thousand mile from Mosko and more the same be say by those that know they to have set on work all the year long ten thousand man in make of salt carriage by cart and boat hew of wood and such like beside five thousand bondslave at the least to inhabit and till their Land they have also their physician surgeon apothecary and all manner of artificer of doutches and other belong unto they they be Wichida to perm above one thousand verse and then take it all away from they perforce but this in the end be envy and disdain as a matter not stand with their policy to have any so great special a mousick the emperor begin first to pull from they by piece sometime twenty thousand rubbel at a time sometime more till in the end their son that now be be well ease of their stock and have but small part of their father substance the rest be draw all into the emperor treasury their name be jacone Gregory and Simon the son of O^^ka for the quality of their people otherwise though there seem to be in there some aptness to receive any art as appear by the natural wit in the man and very child yet they excel in no kind of common art much less in any learning or literal kind of knowledge which they be keep from of purpose as they be also from all military practice that they may be fit for the servile condition wherein now they be and have neither reason nor valour to attempt innovation for this purpose also they be keep from travel Russ not permit to travel that they may learn nothing nor see the fashion of other country abroad you shall seldom see a ruff a traveller except he be with some ambassador or that he make a escape out of his country which hardly he can do by reason of the border that be watch so narrow and the punishment for any such attempt which be death if he be take and all his good confiscate only they learn to write and to read and that very few of they neither do they suffer any stranger willing to come into their realm out of any civil country for the same cause far than necessity of utter their commodity and take in of foreign do enforce they to do and therefore this year 1589. they consult about the remove of all merchant stranger to the border town to abide and have their residency there the jealousy of the emperor concern his state and to be more wary in admit other stranger hereafter into the inland part of the realm for the same purpose also they be keep within the bound of their degree by the law of their country so that the son of a mousick artificer or husbandman be ever a mousick artificer etc. and have no mean to aspire any high except have learned to write and read he attain to the preferment of a priest or Dyack their language be all one with the slavonian which be think to have be derive from the ruff tongue rather than the ruff from the slavonian for the people call Sclavonia and the language be know to have have their beginning out of Sarmatia and to have term themselves of their conquest Sclavos that be famous or glorious of the word which in the ruff and slavonian tongue signify as much as glory or fame though afterward be subdue and tread upon by diverse nation the italian their neighbour have turn the word to a contrary signification and term every servant or peasant by the name of sclave as do the roman by the getes and syrian for the same reason the ruff character or letter be no other than the greek somewhat distort concern their trade diet apparel and such like it be to be note in a several chapter of their private behaviour this order that bind every man to keep his rank and several degree quality in nobility or commons as have no further reward nor preferment whereunto they may bend their endeavour and employ themselves to advance their estate but rather procure more danger to civil and criminal matter court of civil justice three the duke and dyack Court the high court of Mosko be of three kind the one be subject unto the other by way of appeal the low court that seem to be appoint for some ease to the subject be the office of the gubnoy staru that signify a alderman and of the Sotskoy staru or bailiff of the soak or hundred whereof I speak before in the order of the province these may end matter among their neighbour within their soak or several hundred where they be appoint under the duke and dyack of the province to who the party may remove their matter if they can be agree by the say gubnoy or Sotskoy staru the second be keep in the head town of every province or shire by the say duke and dyack that be deputy to the four lord of the chetfird as before be say from these court they may appeal and remove their suit to the chief court that be keep at the Mosko where be resident the officer of the four chetfird these be the chief justice or judge every of they in all civil matter that grow within their several chetfird or quarter and may be either commence original before they or prosecute out of the inferior court of the shire by way of appeal their commence and proceed in civil action be on this manner first the plaintiff put up his supplication wherein he declare the effect of his cause their manner of proceed in civil matter or wrong do unto he whereupon be grant unto he a Wepis or warrant which he deliver to the prastave or sergeant to do the arrest upon the party who he mean to implead who upon the arrest be to put in surety to answer the day appoint or else stand at the sergeant devotion to be keep safe by such mean as he think good the sergeant be many and excel for their hard and cruel deal towards their prisoner common they clap iron upon they as many as they can bear to wring out of they some large fee though it be but for six penny you shall see they go with chain on their leg arm and neck when they come before the judge the plaintiff begin to declare his matter after the content of his supplication as for attorney counsellor procurator and advocate to plead their cause for they they have no such order but every man be to tell his own tale and plead for himself as well as he can end of controversy by kiss the crosse. if they have any witness or other evidence they produce it before the judge if they have none or if the truth of the cause can so well be discern by the plea or evidence on both part^ then the judge ask either party which he think good plaintiff or defendant whether he will kiss the cross upon that which he avonch or deny he that take the cross be so offer by the judge be account clear and carry away the matter this ceremony be not do within the court or office but the party be carry to the church by a officer and there the ceremony be do the money in the mean while hang upon a nail or else lie at the idol foot ready to be deliver to the party as soon as he have kiss the cross before the say idol judgement by lot this kiss of the cross call be as their corporal oath and account with they a very holy thing which no man will dare to violate or profane with a false allegation if both party offer to kiss the cross in a contradictory matter than they draw lot the better lot be suppose to have the right and bear away the matter so the party convict be adjudge to pay the debt or penalty whatsoever and withal to pay the emperor fee which be twenty penny upon every mark as before have be note when the matter be thus end the party convict be deliver to the sergeant who have a writ for his warrant out of the office to carry he to the praneush or righter of justice if present he pay not the money or content not the party this praneush or righter be a place near to the office where such as have sentence pass against they and refuse to pay that which be adjudge shi^-beating be beat with great cudgel on the shin and calf of their leg every forenoon from eight to eleven they be set on the praneush and beat in this sort till the money be pay the afternoon and night time they be keep in chain by the sergeant except they put in sufficient surety for their appearance at the praneush at the hour appoint you shall see forty or fifty stand together on the praneush all on a rue and their shin thus becudgel terrible term and beba every morning with a piteous cry if after a year stand on the praneush the party will not or lack wherewithal to satisfy his creditor it be lawful for he to sell his wife and child either outright or for a certain term of year and if the price of they do not amount to the full payment the creditor may take they to be his bondslave for year or for ever according as the value of the debt require such kind of suit as lack direct evidence or stand upon conjecture and circumstance to be weigh by the judge draw of great length and yield great advantage to the judge and officer if the suit be upon a bond or bill they have for the most part chetfird to the duke and diack to be put in execution the prisoner be carry to the place of execution with his hand bind and a wax candle burn hold betwixt his finger their capital punishment be hang head knock on the head drown put under the ice set on a stake and such like but for the most part execution the prisoner that be condemn in summer be keep for the winter to be knock in the head and put under the ice this be to be understand of common person for theft and murder if they be commit upon a poor mousick by one of nobility be not light punish nor yet be he call to any account for it their reason be because they be account their kolophey or bondslave if by some Sinaboiarskey or gentleman soldier a murder or theft be commit peradventure he shall be imprison at the emperor pleasure if the manner of the fact be very notorious he be whip perchance and this be common all the punishment that be inflict upon they if a man kill his own servant little or nothing be say unto he for the
