send forth their summons in the emperor name to all the duke and dyack of the province to be proclaim in the head town of every shire that all the Sinaboiarskey or son of gentleman make their repair to such a border where the service be to be do at such a place and by such a day and there present themselves to such and such captain when they come to the place assign they in the summons or proclamation their name be take by certain officer that have commission for that purpose from the roserade or high constable as clerk of the band if any make default and fail at the day he be mulct and punish very severe as for the general and other chief captain they be send thither from the emperor own hand with such commission and charge as he think behooveful for the present service when the soldier be assemble they be reduce into their band and company under their several captain of ten fifty hundred thousand etc. and these band into four polikeis or legion but of far great number than the roman legion be under their four great leader which also have the authority of marshal of the field as be say before concern their armour they be but slight appoint the horseman furniture the common horseman have nothing else but his bow in his case under his right arm and his quiver and sword hang on the left side except some few that bear a case of dag or a javelin or short staff along their horse side the under captain will have common some piece of armour beside as a shirt of male or such like the general with the other chief captain and man of nobility will have their horse very rich furnish their saddle of cloth of gold their bridle fair boss and tassel with gold and silk fringe bestud with pearl and precious stone themselves in very fair armour which they call bullatnoy make of fair shine steel yet cover common with cloth of gold and edge round about with Armine fur his steel helmet on his head of a very great price his sword bow and arrow at his side his spear in his hand with another helmet and his or horseman sceptre carry before he their sword Bowes and arrow be of the turkish fashion they practise like the tartar to shoot forward and backward as they fly and retire shoot forward and backward the footman furniture provision of victual the Strelsey or Footman have nothing but his piece in his hand his strike hatchet at his back and his sword by his side the stock of his piece be not make caleever wise but with a plain and strait stock somewhat like a fowling-peece the barrel be rude and unartificial make very heavy yet shoot but a very small bullet as for their provision of victual the emperor allow none either for captain or soldier neither provide any for they except peradventure some corn for their money every man be to bring sufficient for himself to serve his turn for four month provision and if need require to give order for more to be bring unto he to the camp from his tenant that till his land or some other place one great help they have that for lodging and diet every ruff be prepare to be a soldier beforehand though the chief captain and other of account carry tent with they after the fashion of we with some better provision of victual then the rest they bring with they common into the camp for victual a kind of dry bread which they call Sucharie with some store of meal which they temper with water and so make it into a ball or small lump of dough call Tollockno and this they eat raw in stead of Bread their meat be Bacon or some other flesh or fish dry after the dutch manner if the ruff soldier be as hardy to execute a enterprise as he be hard to bear out toil and travel or be otherwise as apt and well train for the war as he be indifferent for his lodging and diet he will far exceed the soldier of our part whereas now he be far mean of courage and execution in any warlike service which come partly of his servile condition that will not suffer any great courage or valour to grow in he partly for lack of due honour and reward which he have no great hope of whatsoever service or execution he do the ruff trust rather to his number then to the valour of his soldier chap. 17. of their march charge and other martial discipline george-ensigne horseman drum or good order of his force their march or lead be without all order save that the fore Polskey or legion whereinto their army be divide keep themselves several under their ensign and so thrust all on together in a hurry as they be direct by their general their ensign be the image of saint George the bulsha Dworaney or chief horseman have every man a small drum of brass at his saddlebow which he strike when he give the charge or onset they have drum beside of a huge bigness which they carry with they upon a board lay on four horse the horsemans manner of charge that be spar together with chain every drum have eight striker or drummer beside trumpet and shawm which they sound after a wild manner much different from we when they give any charge or make any invasion they make a great hallow or shout altogether as loud as they can which with the sound of their trumpet shawm and drum make a confuse and horrible noise so they set on first discharge their arrow then deal with their sword which they use in a bravery to shake and brandish over their head before they come to stroke the footman charge their footman because otherise they want order in lead be common place in some ambush or place of advantage where they may most annoy the enemy with least hurt to themselves if it be a set battle or if any great invasion be make upon the ruff border by the tartar the walk castle they be set with in the run or move castle call Beza or Gulay gorod which be carry about with they by the Voiavoda gulavoy or the walk general who I speak of before this walk or move castle be so frame that it may be set up in length as occasion do require the space of one two three four five six or seven mile for so long it will reach it be nothing else but a double wall of wood to defend they on both side behind and before with a space of three yard or thereabouts betwixt the two side so that they may stand within it and have room enough to charge and discharge their piece and to use their other weapon it be close at both end and make with loophole on either side to lay out the nose of their piece or to push forth any other weapon it be carry with the army wheresoever it go be take into piece and so lay on cart spar together and draw by horse that be not see by reason that they be cover with their carriage as with a shelf or penthouse when it be bring to the place where it be to be use which be devise and choose out before by the the walk voiavod it be plant so much as the present use require sometime a mile long sometime two sometime three or more which be soon do without the help of any carpenter or instrument because the timber be so frame to clasp together one piece within a other as be easy understand by those that know the manner of the ruff building in this castle stand their shot well fence for advantage special against the tartar that bring no ordnance nor other weapon into the field with he save his sword and bow and arrow they have also within it diverse field piece which they use as occasion do require of piece for the field they carry no great store when they war against the tartar but when they deal with the polonian of who force they make more account they go better furnish with all kind of munition and other necessary provision it be think that no prince of Christendom have better store of munition store of munition than the ruff emperor and it may partly appear by the artillery house at Mosko where be of all sort of great ordnance all brass piece very fair to a exceed great number the ruff soldier be think to be better at his defence within some castle or town than he be abroad at a set pitch field which be ever note in the practice of his war and namely at the siege of Vobsko about eight year since where he repulse the polonian king Stepan Batore with his whole army of 100000. man and force he in the end to give over his siege with the loss of many of his best captain and soldier but in a set field the ruff be note to have ever the worse of the polonian and Sweden if any behave himself more valiant than the rest or do any special piece of service the emperor send he a piece of gold stamp with the image of saint George on horseback which they hang on their sleeve reward for valour and set in their cap and this be account the great honour they can receive for any service they do chap. 18. of their colony a maintain of their conquest or purchase by force the Russee emperor of late year have very much enlarge their dominion and territory their first conquest after the dukedom of Mosko for before that time they be but duke of Volodomer as before be say be the city and dukedom of Novograd on the west and northwest side which be no small enlargement of their dominion and strengthen to they for the win of the rest this be do by juan great grandfather to Theodore now emperor about the year 1480. the same begin likewise to encroach upon the country of Lituania and livonia but the conquest only intend and attempt by he upon some part of those country be pursue and perform by his son basileus who first win the city and dukedom of Plesko afterward the city and dukedom of Smolensko and many other fair town with a large territory belong unto they about the year 1514. these victory against the lettoe or lituanian in the time of Alexander their duke he achieve rather by advantage of civil dissension and treason among themselves then by any great policy or force of his own but all this be lose again by his son juan Vasilowich about eight or nine year past upon composition with the polonian king Stepan Batore whereunto he be force by the advantage which the pole have then of he by reason of the foil he have give he before and the disquietness of his own state at home only the ruff emperor at this time have leave he on that side his country the city of Smolensko Cheringo and Beala gorod in Lituonia in livonia not a town not one foot of ground when basileus first conquer those country he suffer the native to keep their possession and to inhabit all their town only pay he a tribute under the government of his ruff or sell to the tartar that serve he in those war and in stead of they place there his Russ so many as may over-match the rest with certain garrison of strength beside wherein notwithstanding this oversight be commit for that take away with he the upland or country people that shall have till the ground and may easy have be keep in order without any danger by other good policy he be drive afterward many year together to victual the country especial the great town out of his own country of Russia the soil lie there in the meanwhile waste and untilled the like fall out at the port of narve in Liefland narve where his son juan Vasilowich devise to build a town and a castle on the other side the river call juangorod to keep the town and country in subjection the castle he cause to like again but have leave the native all within their own country without abate their number or strength the town and castle not long after be betray and surrender again to the king of Sweden on the southeast side they have get the kingdom of Cazan and astracan these be win from the tartar by the late emperor juan Vasilowich father to the emperor that now be the one about thirty five the other be bold to write himself now the great commander of siberia the country likewise of Permia and Pechora Permia and Pechora be a diverse people and language from the ruff overcome not long since and that rather by threaten and shake of the sword then by any actual force as be a weak and naked people without mean to resist their neighbour with who they have great deal and intercourse chap. 19 of the tartar and other borderer to the country of Russia with who they have most to do in war and peace th^ polonian call laches by the ruff the chrim Tartar the fire of Mosko by the chrim tartar in the year 1575. both in peace and war be first the tartar second the polonian who the ruff call laches note the first author or founder of the nation who be call laches or leches whereunto be add Po which signify people and so be make polache that be the people or posterity of laches which the latin after their manner of writing call the three be the sweden the polonian and sweden be better know to these part of Europe then be the tartar that be far off from we as be of Asia and divide into many tribe different both in name and government one from another the great and mighty of they be the chrim tartar who some call the great cham that lie south and south-east-ward from Russia and do most annoy the country by often invasion common once every year sometime enter very far within the inland part in the year 1571. he come as far as the city of Mosko with a army of 200000. man without any battle or resistance at all for that the ruff emperor than juan Vasilowich lead forth his army to encounter with he march a wrong way but as it be think of very purpose as not dare to adventure the field by reason that he doubt his nobility and chief captain of a meaning to betray he to the Tartar the city he take not but fire the suburb which by reason of the building which be all of wood without any stone brick or lime save certain out room kindle so quick and go on with such rage as that it consume the great part of the city almost within the space of four hour be of thirty mile or more of compass then may you have see a lamentable spectacle beside the huge and mighty flame of the city all on light fire the people burn in their house and street but most of all of such as labour to pass out of the gate far from the enemy where meet together in a mighty throng and so press every man to prevent another wedge themselves so fast within the gate and street near unto it as that three rank walk one upon the other head the uppermost tread down those that be low so that there perish at that time as be say by the fire and the press the number of 80000. people or more the chrim thus have fire the city and feed his eye with the sight of it all of a light flame return with his army and send to the ruff emperor a knife as be say to stick himself withal obrayd this loss and his desperate case as not dare either to meet his enemy in the field nor to trust his friend or subject at home the principal cause of this continual quarrel betwixt the ruff and the chrim be for the right of certain border part claim by the tartar but possess by the ruff the tartar allege that beside astracan and Cazan that be the ancient possession of the east Tartar the whole country from his bound north and westward so far as the city of Mosko and Mosko itself pertain to his right which seem to have be true by the report of the Russ themselves homage do by the ruff to the chrim tartar see the first book of Bathay and of the tartar conquest that tell of a certain homage that be do by the ruff emperor every year to the great chrim or cham the ruff emperor stand on foot and feed the Chrims horse himself sit on his back with oat out of his own cap in stead of a boll or manger and that within the castle of Mosko and this homage they say be do till the time of basileus grandfather to this man who surprise the chrim emperor by a stratagem do by one of his nobility call juan Demetrowich Belschey be content with this ransom viz. with the change of this homage into a tribute of fur which afterward also be deny to be pay by this emperor father hereupon they continue the quarrel the ruff defend his country and that which he have win the chrim tartar invade he once or twice every year sometime about Whitsuntide but often in harvest what time if the great cham or chrim come in his own person he bring with he a great army of 100000. or 200000. man otherwise they make short and sudden road into the country with lesser number run about the list of the border as wild goose fly invade and retire where they see advantage their common practice be very populous be to make diverse army and so draw the ruff to one the manner of the tartar fight and armour or two place of the frontier to invade at some other place that be leave without defence their manner of fight or order of their force be much after the ruff manner speak of before save that they be all horseman and carry nothing else but a bow a sheaf of arrow and a falcon sword after the turkish fashion they be very expert horseman and use to shoot as ready backward as forward some will have a horseman staff like to a bear spear beside their other weapon the common soldier have no other armour then his ordinary apparel apparel viz. a black sheep skin with the wooll-side outward in the day time and inward in the night time with a cap of the same but their morsey or nobleman imitate the Turk Mirzohs or morseis both in apparel and armour when they be to pass over a river with their army they tie three or four horse together and take long pole or piece of wood bind they fast to the tail of their horse so sit on the pole they drive their horse over at handy stroke when they come to join battle they be account far better man than the ruff people fierce by nature but more hardy and bloody by continual practice of war as man know no art of peace nor any civil practice the subtlety of the Tartar yet their subtlety be more than may seem to agree with their barbarous condition by reason they be practise to invade continual and to rob their neighbour that border about they they be very pregnant and ready witted to devise stratagem upon the sudden for their better advantage as in their war against Beala the four king of Hungary who they invade with five hundred thousand man and obtain against he a great u^ctorie where among other have slay his chancellor call Nicholas Schinick they find about he the king privy seal whereupon they devise present to counterfeit letter in the king name to the city and town next about the place where the field be fight with charge that in no case they shall convey themselves and their good out of their dwelling where they may abide safe without all fear of danger and not leave the country desolate to the possession of so vile and barbarous a enemy as be the tartar nation term themselves in all reproachful manner for notwithstanding he have lose his carriage with some few straggler that have march disorderly yet he doubt not but to recover that loss with the access of a notable victory if the savage tartar dare abide he in the field to this purpose have write their letter in the polish character by certain young man who they take in the field and sign they with the king seal they dispatch they forth to all the quarter of Hungary that lie near about the place whereupon the vngarians that be now fly away with their good wife and child upon the rumour of the king overthrow take comfort of these counterfeit letter stay at home and so be make a prey be surprise on the sudden by this huge number of these tartar that have compass they about before they be aware when they besiege a town or fort they offer much parley and send many flatter message to persuade a surrendry promise all thing that the inhabitant will require but be once possess of the place they use all manner of hostility and cruelty this they do upon a rule they have viz. that justice be to be practise but towards their own they encounter not light but they have some ambush whereunto have once show themselves and make some short conflict they retire as repulse for fear and so draw the enemy into it if they can but the Russee be well acquaint with their practice be more wary of they when they come a rove with some small number they set on horseback counterfeit shape of man that their number may seem great when they make any onset their manner be to make a great shout cry all out together God help we God help we they contemn death so much as that they choose rather to die then to yield to their enemy and be see when they be slay to bite the very weapon Tartar resolution when they be pass strike or help of themselves wherein appear how different the tartar be in his desperate courage from the ruff and Turk for the Russee soldier if he begin once to retire put all his safety in his speedy flight and if once he be take by his enemy he neither defend himself nor intreat for his life as reckon straight to die the Turk common when he be past hope of escape fall to entreaty and cast away his weapon offer both his hand and hold they up as it be to be tie hope to save his life by offer himself bondslave the chief booty the tartar seek for in all their war be to get store of captive captive special young boy and girl who they sell to the turk or other their neighbour to this purpose they take with they great basket make like baker pannier to carry they tender and if any of they happen to tire or to be sick on the way they dash he against the ground or some tree and so leave he dead the soldier be not trouble with keep the captive and other booty for hinder the execution of their war but they have certain band that intend nothing else appoint of purpose to receive and keep the captive and the other prey the ruff border be use to their invasion light every year in the summer keep few other cattle on the border part save swine only which the tartar will not touch the tartar religion nor drive away with he for that he be of the turkish religion and will eat no swines-flesh of Christ our saviour they confess as much as do the Turk in his Koran viz. that he come of the angel Gabriel and the virgin Marie that he be a great prophet and shall be the judge of the world at the last day in other matter likewise they be much order after the manner and direction of the Turk have feel the turkish force when he win from they and Caffa with some other town about the euxine or black sea that be before tributary to the chrim Tartar so that now the emperor of the Chrims for the most part be choose some one of the nobility who the Turk do commend whereby it be bring now to that pass that the chrim tartar give to the Turk the ten part of the spoil which he get in his war against the christian herein they differ from the turkish religion for that they have certain idol puppet make of silk or like stuff of the fashion of a man idol which they fasten to the door of their walk house to be as januss or keeper of their house and these idol be make not by all but by certain religious woman which they have among they for that and like use they have beside the image of their king or great cham of a huge bigness which they erect at every stage when the army march and this every one must bend or bow unto as he pass by it be he tartar or stranger they be much give to witchcraft and ominous conjecture upon every accident which they hear or see sorcery in make of marriage they have no regard of alliance or consanguinity marriage only with his mother sister and daughter a man may not marry and though he take the woman into his house and accompany with she yet he account she not for his wife till he have a child by she then he begin to take a dowry of her friend of horse sheep cow etc. if she be barren after a certain time he turn she home again under the emperor they have certain duke who they call morseis or dynoymorseis that rule over a certain number of 10000 20000. or 40000. a piece which they call hoard the tartar nobility when the emperor have any use of they to serve in his war they be bind to come and to bring with they their soldier to a certain number every man with his two horse at the least the one to ride on the other to kill when it come to his turn to have his horse eat for their chief victual be horseflesh which they eat without bread the tartar diet or any other thing with it so that if a tartar be take by a ruff he shall be sure light to find a horse-legge or some other part of he at his saddle bow this last year when I be at the Mosko come in one Kiriach morsey nephew to the emperor of the Chrims that now be who father be emperor before accompany with three hundred tartar and his two wife whereof one be his brother widow where be entertain in very good sort after the ruff manner he have send unto his lodging for his welcome to be make ready for his supper and his company two very large and fat horse ready flay in a sled they prefer it before other flesh because the meat be strong as they say than beef mutton and such like and yet which be marvel though they serve all as horseman in the war and eat all of horseflesh there be bring yearly to the Mosko to be exchange for other commodity thirty or forty thousand tartar horse which they call Cones they keep also great herd of cow and flock of black sheep rather for the skin and milk which they carry with they in great bottle then for the use of the flesh though sometime they eat of it some use they have of rice fig and other fruit they drink milk or warm blood and for the most part card they both together they use sometime as they travel by the way to let their horse blood in a vein and to drink it warm as it come from his body town they plant none nor other stand building the tartar dwell but have walk house which the latin call build upon wheel like a shepherd cottage these they draw with they whithersoever they go drive their cattle with they and when they come to their stage or stand place they plant their cart-house very orderly in a rank and so make the form of street movable city and Court and of a large town and this be the manner of the emperor himself who have no other seat of his empire but a agora or town of wood that move with he whithersoever he go as for the fix and stand building use in other country they say they be unwholesome and unpleasant they begin to move their house and cattle in the spring time from the south part of their country towards the north part and so drive on till they have grae all up to the further part northward they return back again towards their south country where they continue all the winter by ten or twelve mile a stage in the mean while the grass be spring up again to serve for their cattle as they return from the border of the Shalcan towards the caspian sea to the ruff frontier they have a goodly country special on the south and southeast part but lose for lack of tillage of money they have no use at all and therefore prefer brass and steel before other metal special bullate which they use for sword knife and other necessary as for gold and silver they neglect it of very purpose as they do all tillage of their ground to be more free for their wander kind of life and to keep their country less subject to invasion which give they great advantage against all their neighbour ever invade and never be invade Tartar person describe for person and complexion they have broad and flat visage of a tan colour yellow and black fierce and cruel look thin haired upon the upper lip and a pit on the chin light and nimble body with short leg as if they be make natural for horseman whereto they practise themselves from their childhood seldom go a soot about any business their speech be very sudden and loud speak as it be out of a deep hollow throat when they sing you will think a cow low speech song shoot or some great bandog howl their great exercise be shoot wherein they train up their child from their very infancy not suffer they to eat till they have shoot near the mark within a certain scantling diverse kind of tartar there be diverse other tartar that border upon Russia as the nagay the cheremissen the mordwite the chircass and the shalcans which all differ in name more than in regiment or other condition from the chrim tartar except the chircass that border south-west towards Lituania the nagay Tartar the cruel the Chircasce the civil tartar the Cheremissen Tartar and be far more civil than the rest of the tartar of a comely person and of a stately behaviour as apply themselves to the fashion of the polonian some of they have subject themselves to the king of Poland and profess Christianity the nagay lie eastward and be reckon for the best man of war among all the tartar but very savage and cruel above all the rest the cheremisin Tartar that lie betwixt the ruff and the nagay be of two sort the Lugavoy that be of the valley and the Nagornay or of the hilly country these have much trouble the emperor of Russia and therefore they be content now to buy peace of they under pretence of give a yearly pension of Russee commodity to their morseis or dyvoymorseis that be chief of their tribe for which also they be bind to serve they in their war under certain condition they be say to be just and true in their deal and for that cause they hate the Russee people who they account to be double and false in all their deal and therefore the common sort be very unwilling to keep agreement with they but that they be keep in by their morseis or duke for their pension sake the most rude and barbarous be count the morduite Tartar that have many self fashion and strange kind of behaviour the mordwit Tartar the most barbarous of the rest differ from the rest for his religion though he acknowledge one God yet his manner be to worship for God that live thing that he first meet in the morning and to swear by it all that whole day whether it be horse dog cat or whatsoever else it be when his friend die he kill his best horse and have flay off the skin he carry it on high upon a long pole before the corpse to the place of burial this he do as the ruff say that his friend may have a good horse to carry he to heaven but it be likely to declare his love towards his dead friend in that he will have to die with he the best thing that he have next to the kingdom of astracan that be the further part south-eastward of the ruff dominion lie the Shalcan and the country of Media whither the ruff merchant trade for raw silk Shalcan Syndon Saphyon skin and other commodity the chief town of Media where the ruff trade be derbent build by Alexander the great as the inhabitant say and zamachie where the staple be keep for raw silk their manner be in the spring time to revive the silkworm that lie dead all the winter by lay they in the warm sun and to hasten their quicken that they may soon go to work to put they into bag and so to hang they under their child arm as for the worm call Chrinisin as we call it crimson that make colour silk it be breed not in Media but in Assyria this trade to derbent and samachie for raw silk and other commodity of that country as also in Persia and Bougharia down the river Volgha and through the caspian sea be permit as well to the english as to the ruff merchant by the emperor last grant at my be there which he account for a very special favour and may prove indeed very beneficial to our english merchant if the trade be well and orderly use the whole nation of the tartar be utter void of all learning and without write Law yet certain rule they have which they hold by tradition common to all the hoard for the practice of their life which be of this sort first to obey their emperor and other magistrate whatsoever they command about the public service second except for the public behoof Tartar general rule every man to be free and out of controlment three no private man to possess any land but the whole country to be as a common four to neglect all daintiness and variety of meat and to content themselves with that which come next to ^and for more hardness and readiness in the execute of their affair five to wear any base attire and to patch their clothes whether there be any need or not that when there be use it be no shame to wear a patch coat six to take or steal from any stranger whatsoever they can get as be enemy to all man save to such (@) will subject themselves to they seven towards their own Hoord and nation to be true in word and deed eight to suffer no stranger to come within the realm if any do the same to be bond-sla^e to he that first take he except such merchant and other a^ have the tartar bull or passport about they the permian and samoit that lie from Russia north and north-east be think likewise to have take their beginning from the tartar kind chap. 20. of the permian samoit and lap the permian and it may partly be guess by the fashion of their countenance as have all broad and flatface as the tartar have except the chircass the permian be account for a very ancient people they be now subject to the ruff they live by hunt and trade with their fur as do also the samoyt that dwell more towards the north Sea the samoyt have his name as the ruff say of eat him-himselfe as if in time past they live as the cannibal eat one another the samoit which they make more probable because at this time they eat all kind of raw flesh whatsoever it be even the very carrion that lie in the ditch but as the samoit themselves will say they be call samoie that be of themselves as though they be or people breed upon that very soil that never change their seat from one place to another as most nation have do they be subject at this time to the emperor of Russia I talk with certain of they and find that they acknowledge one god the samoit religion Baba or the golden hag. but represent he by such thing as they have most use and good by and therefore they worship the sun the olen the Losh and such like as for the story of Slata Baba or the golden hag which I have read in some map and description of these country to be a idol after the form of a old woman that be demand by the priest give they certain oracle concern the success and event of thing I find it to be but a very fable only in the province of Obdoria upon the sea side near to the mouth of the great river Obba there be a rock which natural be somewhat help by imagination may seem to bear the shape of a ragged woman with a child in her arm as the rock by the north cape the shape of a friar where the obdorian samoit use much to resort by reason of the commodity of the place for fish and there sometime as their manner be conceive and practise their sorcery and ominous conjecture about the good or bad speed of their journey fish hunt and such like they be clad in seale-skinne with the hairy side outward down as low as the knee with their breeches and nether-stock of the same both man and woman the samoit habit and behaviour they be all black haired natural beardless and therefore the man be hardly discern from the woman by their look save that the woman wear a lock of hair down along both their ear they live in a manner a wild and a savage life rove still from one place of the country to another without any property of house or land more to one then to another their leader or direct in every company be their Papa or Priest on the north side of Russia next to Corelia lie the country of Lappia the lap which reach in length from the further point northward towards the north cape to the further part southeast which the ruff call sweetness or holy nose the the hill side the lake lie between their diet be very bare and simple bread they have none but feed only upon fish and fowl they be subject to the emperor of Russia and the two king of Sweden and witch though for the enchant of ship that sail along their coast as I have hear it report and their give of wind good to their friend and contrary to other who they mean to hurt by tie of certain knot upon a rope somewhat like to the tale of Aeolus his windbag be a very fable devise as may seem by themselves to terrify sailor for come near their coast. their weapon be the longbow and hand-gunne wherein they excel as well for quickness to charge and discharge as for nearness at the mark by reason of their continual practice whereto they be force of shoot at wildfowl their manner be in summer time to come down in great company to the seaside wardhuyse to wardhuyse Cola Kegor and the bay of Vedagoba and there to fish for cod Salmon and but-fish which they sell to the Russ dane and norwegian and now of late to the englishman that trade thither with cloth which they exchange with the lap and corelians for their fish oil and fur whereof also they have some store cola. they hold their mart at Cola on saint Peter day what time the captain of wardhuyse that be resiant there for the king of Denmark must be present or at least send his deputy to set price upon their stockfish trane-oyle fur and other commodity as also the ruff emperor customer or tribute taker to receive his custom which be ever pay before any thing can be buy or sold. when their fish be do their manner be to draw their carbass or boat on shore and there to leave they with the keel turn upward sled draw with deer till the next springtide their travel too and fro be upon sled draw by the olen deer which they use to turn a graze all the summer time in a island call Kilden of a very good soil compare with other part of that country and towards the winter time when the snow begin to fall they fetch they home again together the whole service time in the body of the church and some in the church porch for piew or seat they have none within their church the manner of the ruff baptism the sacrament of baptism they administer after this manner the child be bring unto the church and this be do within eight day after it be bear if it be the child of some nobleman it be bring with great pomp in a rich sled or wagon with chair and cushion of cloth of gold and such like sumptuous show of their best furniture when they be come to the church the priest stand ready to receive the child within the church porch with his tub of water by he and then begin to declare unto they that they have bring a little infidel to be make a christian etc. this end he teach the witness that be two or three in a certain set form out of his book what their duty be in bring up the child after he be baptize uz. that he must be teach to know God and Christ the saviour and because God be of great majesty and we must not presume to come unto he without mediator as the manner be when we make any suit to a emperor or great prince therefore they must teach he what saint be the best and chief mediator etc. this do he command the devil in the name of God after a conjure manner to come out of the water and so after certain prayer he plunge the child thrice over head and ear for this they hold to be a point necessary that no part of the child be undip in the water the word that bear with they the form of baptism utter by the priest when he dip in the child be the very same that be prescribe in the gospel and use by we uz. in the name of the father and of the son and of the holy ghost for that they shall alter the form of the word and say by the holy ghost as I have hear that they do follow certain heretic of the greek church I round to be untrue as well by report of they that have be often at their baptism as by their book of liturgy itself wherein the order of baptism be precise set down when the child be baptize oil and Salt the priest lay oil and salt temper together upon the forehead and both side of his face and then upon his mouth draw it along with his finger over the child lip as do the popish priest say withal certain prayer to this effect that God will make he a good christian etc. all this be do in the church porch then be the child as be now make a christian and meet to be receive within the church door carry into the church the priest go before present and there he be present to the chief idol of the church be lay on a cushion before the foot of the image by it as by the mediator to be commend unto God if the child be sick or weak special in the winter they use to make the water warm cut off hair after baptism the manner be to cut off the hair from the child head and have wrap it within a piece of wax to lay it up as a relic or monument in a secret place of the church this be the manner of their baptism which they account to be the best and perfect form as they do all other part of their religion receive as they say by tradition from the best church mean the greek and therefore they will take great pain to make a proselyte proselyte-paine or convert either of a infidel or of a foreign christian by rebaptise he after the ruff manner when they take any tartar prisoner common they will offer he life with condition to be baptize and yet they persuade very few of they to redeem their life so because of the natural hatred the tartar bear to the ruff and the opinion he have of his fashood and injustice the year after Mosko be fire by the chrim tartar there be take a divoymorsey one of the chief in that exploit with three hundred tartar more tartar choose to die rather than turn christian who have all their life offer they if they will be baptize after the ruff manner which they refuse all to do with many reproach against those that persuade they and so be carry to the river Mosko that run through the city they be all baptise after a violent manner be thrust down with a knock on the head into the water through a hole make in the ice for that purpose of lieflander that be captive rebaptise there be many that take on they this second ruff baptism to get more liberty and somewhat beside towards their live which the emperor ordinary use to give they of englishman since they frequent the country there be never any find that so much forget God his faith and country as that he will be content to be baptize Russee for any respect of fear preferment or other mean whatsoever save only Richard Relph that follow before a ungodly trade by keep a Caback against the order of the country and be put off from that trade and spoil by the emperor officer of that which he have enter himself this last year into the ruff profession and so be rebaptise live now asmuch a idolater as before he be a rioter and unthrifty person such as thus receive the ruff baptism be first carry into some monastery to be instruct there in the doctrine and ceremony of the church where they use these ceremony first they put he into a new and fresh suit of apparel make after the ruff fashion and set a coronet or in summer a garland upon his head then they anoint his head with oil and put a wax candle light into his hand and so pray over he four time a day the space of seven day all this while he be to abstain from flesh and white meat the seven day be end he be purify and wash in a bathstove and so the eight day he be bring into the church where he be teach by the friar how to behave himself in presence of their idol by duck down knock of the head cross himself and such like gesture which be the great part of the ruff religion the sacrament of the lord supper they receive but once a year in their great lend time a little before easter the administer of the lord supper confession three at the most be admit at one time and never above the manner of their communicate be thus first they confess themselves of all their sin to the priest who they call their ghostly father then they come to the church and be call up to the communion table that stand like a altar a little remove from the upper end of the church after the dutch manner here first they be ask of the priest whether they be clean or no that be whether they have never a sin behind that they leave unconfess if they answer no they be take to the table where the priest begin with certain usual prayer the communicant stand in the mean while with their arm fold one within another like penitentiary or mourner when these prayer be end the priest take a spoon and fill it full of claret wine then he put into it a small piece of bread and temper they both together communion in both kind and so deliver they in the spoon to the communicant that stand in order speak the usual word of the sacrament eat this etc. drink this etc. both at one time without any pause after that he deliver they again bread by itself and then wine card together with a little warm water to represent blood more right as they think and the water withal that flow out of the side of Christ while this be in do the communicant unfold their arm and then fold they again follow the priest thrice round about the communion table and so return to their place again where have say certain other prayer he dismiss the communicant with charge to be merry and to cheer up themselves for the seven day next follow which be end he enjoin they to fast for it as long time after which they use to observe with very great devotion eat nothing else but bread and salt except a little cabbage and some other herb or root with water or quasse Mead for their drink this be their manner of administer the sacrament wherein what they differ from the institution of Christ and what ceremony they have add of their own or rather borrow of the greek may easy be note their chief error in matter of faith I find to be these first concern the word of God itself they will not read public certain book of the canonical scripture chap. 23. of the doctrine of the ruff church and what error it hold as the book of Moses special the four last and Deuteronomie which they say be all make disauthentique and put out of use by the come of Christ as not able to discern the difference betwixt the moral and the ceremonial Law the book of the prophet they allow of but read they not public in their church for the same reason because they be but director unto Christ 1. their disallow of certain part of the canonical scripture and proper as they say to the nation of the jew only the book of psalm they have in great estimation and sing and say they daily in their church of the new testament they allow and read all except the revelation which therefore they read not though they allow it because they understand it not neither have the like occasion to know the fulfil of the prophecy contain within it concern especial the apostasy of the antichristian church as have the western church notwithstanding they have have their antichrist of the greek church and may find their own fall off and the punishment for it by the turkish invasion in the prophecy of the book 2. tradition equal to the holy scripture second which be the fountain of the rest of all their corruption both in doctrine and ceremony they hold with the papist that their church tradition be of equal authority with the write word of God wherein they prefer themselves before other church affirm that they have the true and right tradition deliver by the apostle to the greek church and so unto they 3. the church to have sovereign authority in interpret the scripture three that the church mean the greek and special the patriarch and his synod as the head of the rest have a sovereign authority to interpret the scripture and that all be bind to hold that interpretation as sound and authentic four concern the divine nature and the three person in the one substance of God that the holy ghost proceed from the father only and not from the son 4. the holy ghost to proceed from the father only five about the office of Christ they hold many foul error and the same almost as do the popish church namely that he be the sole mediator of redemption but not of intercession their chief reason if they be talk withal for defence of this error be that unapt and foolish comparison 5. Christ not sole mediator of intercession saint Nicolas his 300. angel betwixt God and a monarch or prince of this world that must be sue unto by mediator about he wherein they give special preferment to some above other as to the bless virgin who they call procheste or undefiled and saint Nicolas who they call Scora pomosnick or the speedy helper and say that he have three hundred angel of the chief appoint by God to attend upon he this have bring they to a horrible excess of idolatry after the gross and profane manner image give unto their image all religious worship of prayer thanksgiving offering and adoration with prostrate and knock their head to the ground before they as to God himself which because they do to the picture not to the portraiture of the saint they say they worship not a idol but the saint in his image and so offend not God forget the commandment of God that forbid to make the image or likeness of any thing for any religious worship or use whatsoever their church wall be very full of they rich hang and set forth with pearl and stone upon the smooth table though some also they have emboss that stick from the board almost a inch outward they call they chudovodite or their miracle worker and when they provide they to set up in their church in no case they may say that they have buy the image but exchange money for it six for the mean of justification they agree with the papist 6. justification by work that it be not by faith only apprehend Christ but by their work also and that or the work for the work sake must needs please God and therefore they be all in their number of prayer fast vow and offering to saint alm deed cross and such like and carry their number bead about with they continual as well the emperor and his nobility as the common people not only in the church but in all other public place special at any set or solemn meeting as in their fast law court common consultation entertainment of ambassador and such like seven they say with the papist that no man can be assure of his salvation 7. salvation uncertain till the sentence be pass at the day of judgement eight they use auricular confession 8. auricular confession and think they be purge by the very action from so many sin as they confess by name and in particular to the Priest nine they hold three sacrament of baptism the lord supper and the last anoil or unction yet concern their sacrament of extreme unction 9 three sacrament they hold it not so necessary to salvation as they do baptism but think it a great curse and punishment of God if any die without it ten they think there be a necessity of baptism 10. all damn that die without baptism and that all be condemn that die without it eleven 11. anabaptism they rebaptise as many christian not be of the greek church as they convert to their ruff profession because they be divide from the true church which be the greek as they say twelve they make a difference of meat and drink 12. difference of meat account the use of one to be more holy then of another and therefore in their set fast they forbear to eat flesh and white meat as we call they after the manner of the popish superstition which they observe so strict and with such blind devotion as that they will rather die then eat one bit of flesh egg or such like for the health of their body in their extreme sickness thirteen they hold marriage to be unlawful for all the clergy man 13. marriage for some person unlawful except the priest only and for they also after the first wife as be say before neither do they well allow of it in layman after the second marriage which be a pretence now use against the emperor only brother a child of six year old who therefore be not pray for in their church as their manner be otherwise for the prince blood because he be bear of the six marriage and so not legitimate this charge be give to the priest by the emperor himself by procurement of the godone who make he believe that it be a good policy to turn away the like of the people from the next successor many other false opinion they have in matter of religion but these be the chief which they hold partly by mean of only or book of common service whereof there be great number which notwithstanding it be not to be doubt but that have the word of God in some sort though without the ordinary mean to attain to a true sense and understanding of it God have also his number among they as may partly appear by that which a ruff at Mosko say in secret to one of my servant speak against their image and other superstition that God have give unto England light to day and may give it to morrow if he please to they as for any inquisition or proceed against man for matter of religion inquisition I can hear of none save a few year since against one man and his wife who be keep in a close prison the space of eight and twenty year till they be overgrow into a deform fashion for their hair nail colour of countenance and such like and in the end be burn at Mosko in a small house set on fire the cause be keep secret but like it be for some part of truth in matter of religion though the people be make to believe by the priest and friar that they hold some great and damnable heresy the manner of make and solemnize their marriage chap. 24. of the manner of solemnize their marriage be different from the manner of other country the man though he never see the woman before be not permit to have any sight of she all the time of his woo which he do not by himself but by his mother or some other ancient woman of his kin or acquaintance when the like be take as well by the parent as by the party themselves for without the knowledge and consent of the parent the contract be not lawful the father on both side or such as be to they in stead of father with their other chief friend have a meeting and conference about the dowry which be common very large after the ability of the parent so that you shall have a market man as they call they give a thousand rubbel or more with his daughter as for the man it be never require of he nor stand with their custom to make any jointure in recompense of the dowry the manner of endowment for wife but in case he have a child by his wife she enjoy a three deal after his decease if he have two child by she or more she be to have a courtesy more at the discretion of the husband if the husband depart without issue by his wife she be return home to her friend without any thing at all save only her dowry if the husband leave so much behind he in good when the agreement be make concern the dowry they sign bond one to the other as well for the payment of the dowry as the perform of the marriage by a certain day if the woman be never marry before her father and friend be bind beside to assure she a maiden which breed many brabble and quarrel at law if the man take any conceit concern the behaviour and honesty of his wife thus the contract be make the party begin to send token the one to the other the woman first than afterward the man but yet see not one another till the marriage be solemnize on the Eve before the marriage day the bride be carry in a or coach or in a sled if it be winter to the bridegroom house with her marriage apparel and bedstead with she which they be to lie in for this be ever provide by the bride and be common very fair with much cost bestow upon it here she be accompany all that night by her mother and other woman but not welcome nor once see by the bridegroom himself when the time be come to have the marriage solemnize the bride have put upon she a kind of hood ceremony in marriage make of fine knit-worke or lawn that cover her head and all her body down to the middle and so accompany with her friend and the bridegroom with he they go to church all on horseback though the church be near hand and themselves but of very mean degree the word of contract and other ceremony in solemnize the marriage be much after the order ring and with the same word that be use with we with a ring also give to the bride which be put on and the word of contract pronounce the bride hand be deliver into the hand of the bridegroom which stand all this while on the one side of the altar or table and the bride on the other so the marriage knot be knit by the priest the bride come to the bridegroom stand at the end of the altar or table and fall down at his foot knock her head upon his shoe in token of her subjection and obedience and the bridegroom again cast the lap of his gown or upper garment over the bride in token of his duty to protect and cherish she then the bridegroom and bride stand both together at the table end come first the father and the other friend of the bride and how themselves down low to the bridegroom and so likewise his friend bow themselves to the bride in token of affinity and love ever after betwixt the two kindred loaf and withal the father of the bridegroom offer to the priest a loaf of bread who deliver it straight again to the father and other friend of the bride with attestation before God and their idol that he deliver the dowry whole and true at the day appoint and hold love ever after one kindred with another whereupon they break the loaf into piece and eat of it to testify their true and sincere meaning for perform of that charge and thenceforth to become as grain of one loaf or man of one table these ceremony be end the bridegroom take the bride by the hand and so they go on together with their friend after they towards the church porch Mead. where meet they certain with pot and cup in their hand with mead and Russee wine whereof the bridegroom take first a charke or little cup full in his hand and drink to the bride who open her hood or vale below and put the cup to her mouth underneath it for be see of the bridegroom pledge he again thus return all together from the church the bridegroom go not home to his own but to his father house and she likewise to she where either entertain their friend apart corne. at the enter into the house they use to fling corn out of the window upon the bridegroom and bride in token of plenty and fruitfulness to be with they ever after when the evening be come the bride be bring to the bridegroom father house and there lodge that night silence with she veil or cover still over her head all that night she may not speak one word for that charge she receive by tradition from her mother and other matron her friend that the bridegroom must neither hear nor see she till the day after the marriage neither three day after may she be hear to speak save certain few word at the table in a set form with great manner and reverence to the bridegroom if she behave herself otherwise it be a great prejudice to her credit and life ever after and will high be dislike of the bridegroom himself after the three day they depart to their own and make a feast to both their friend together the marriage day and the whole time of their festival the bridegroom have the honour to be call moloday Knez or young duke and the bride moloday knezay or young duchess in live with their wife they show themselves to be but of a barbarous condition use they as servant rather than wife except the noble-woman which be or seem to be of more estimation with their husband than the rest of mean sort they have this foul abuse contrary to good order and the word of God itself that upon dislike of his wife or other cause whatsoever the man may go into a monastery and shire himself a friar by pretence of devotion and so leave his wife to shift for herself so well as she can the other ceremony of their church be many in number especial chap. 25. of the other ceremony o^ the ruff church the sign of the cross how it cross out other devotion the abuse about the sign of the cross which they set up in their high way in the top of their church and in every door of their house sign themselves continual with it on their forehead and breast with great devotion as they will seem by their outward gesture which be less offence if they give not withal that religious reverence and worship unto it which be due to God only and use the dumb show and sign of it instead of thanksgiving and of all other duty which they owe unto God when they rise in the morning they go common in the sight of some steeple that have a cross on the top and so bow themselves towards the cross sign themselves withal on their forehead and breast and this be their thanksgiving to God for their night rest without any word speak except peradventure they say aspody or lord have mercy upon we when they sit down to meat and rise again from it the thanksgiving to God be the cross of their forehead and breast except it be some few that add peradventure a word or two of some ordinary prayer impertinent to that purpose when they be to give a oath for the decide of any controversy at law they do it by swear by the cross and kiss the foot of it make it as God who name only be to be use in such trial of justice when they enter into any house where ever there be a idol hang on the wall they sign themselves with the cross and bow themselves to it when they begin any work be it little or much they arm themselves first with the sign of the crosse. and this common be all their prayer to God for good speed of their business and thus they serve God with cross after a cross and vain manner notwithstanding what the cross of Christ be nor the power of it and yet they think all stranger christian to be no better than Turk in comparison of themselves and so they will say because they bow not themselves when they meet with the cross nor sign themselves with it as the ruff manner be they have Holywater in like use and estimation as the popish church have Holywater but herein they exceed they in that they do not only hollow their holy-water stock and tub full of water but all the river of the country once every year hallow of Rivers at Mosko it be do with great pomp and solemnity the emperor himself be present at it with all his nobility march through the street towards the river of Moskua in manner of procession in this order as follow first go two deacon with banner in their hand the one of precheste or our lady the other of saint Michael fight with his dragon then follow after the rest of the deacon and the priest of Mosko two and two in a rank with coap on their back and their idol at their breast carry with girdle or sling make fast about their neck next the priest come their bishop in their then the friar monk and abbot and after the patriarch in very rich attire with a ball or sphere on the top of his mitre to signify his universality over that church last come the emperor with all his nobility the whole train be of a mile long or more when they be come to the river a great hole be make in the ice where the market be keep of a road and a half broad with a stage round about it to keep off the press then begin the patriarch to say certain prayer and coniur the devil to come out of the water and so cast in salt and cense it with frankincense make the whole river to become Holywater the morning before all the people of Mosko use to make cross of chalk over every door and window of their house lest the devil be conjure out of the water shall fly into their house when the ceremony be end you shall see the black guard of the emperor house and then the rest of the town with their pail and bucket to take off the hallow water for drink and other use you shall also see the woman dip in their child over head and ear and many man and woman leap into it some naked some with their clothes on when some man will think his finger will freeze off if he shall but dip it into the water when the man have do they bring their horse to the river to drink of the sanctify water and so make they as holy as a horse their set day for the solemn action of hallow their river be that we call twelfthday the like be do by other bishop in all part of the realm their manner be also to give it to their sick in their great extremity think that it will either recover they or sanctify they to God whereby they kill many through their unreasonable superstition as do the lord Borris his only son at my be at the Mosko drink of Holywater who he kill as be say by the physician by pour into he cold Holywater and present he naked into the church cruel blindness of superstition to their saint Basileo in the cold of winter in a extremity of sickness they have a image of Christ which they call Neruchi which signify as much as make without hand for so their priest and superstition withal persuade they it be this in their procession they carry about with they on high upon a pole enclose within a pyx make like a lantern and do reverence to it as to a great mystery brew with Holywater at every brew their manner be likewise to bring a dish of their wort to the priest within the church which be hollow by he be pour into the brew and so give it such a virtue as when they drink of it they be seldom sober the like they do with the first fruit of their corn in harvest Palm-sunday they have another ceremony on Palm-sunday of ancient tradition what time the patriarch ride through the Mosko the emperor himself hold his horse bridle and the people cry hosanna and spread their upper garment under his horse foot the emperor have of the patriarch for his good service of that day two hundred rubbel of stand pension another pageant they have much like to this the week before the nativity of Christ when every bishop in his cathedral church set forth a show of the three child in the oven where the angel be make to come fly from the roof of the church with great admiration of the looker on and many terrible flash of fire be make with rosin and gunpowder by the chaldean as they call they that run about the town all the twelve day disguise in their player coat and make much good sport for the honour of the bishop pageant at the Mosko the emperor himself and the empress never fail to be at it though it be but the same matter play every year without any new invention at all fast beside their fast on wednesday and friday throughout the whole year the one because they say Christ be sell on the Wednesday the other because he suffer on the Friday they have four great fast or lent every year the first which they call their great Lent be at the same time with we the second about midsummer the three in harvest time the four about hallontide which they keep not of policy but of mere superstition in their great Lent for the first week they eat nothing but bread and salt and drink nothing but water neither meddle with any matter of their vocation but intend their shrive and fast only they have also three vigil or wake in their great Lent which they call Stoiania and the last Friday their great vigil vigil as they call it what time the whole parish must be present in the church and watch from nine a clock in the evening till six in the morning all the while stand save when they fall down and knock their head to their idol which must be a hundred and seventy time just through the whole night burial about their burial also they have many superstitious and profane ceremony as put within the finger of the corpse a letter to saint Nicolas who they make their chief mediator and as it be the porter of heaven gate as the papist do their Peter in winter time when all be cover with snow and the ground so hard freeze as that no spade nor pickax can enter their manner be not to bury their dead but to keep the body so many as die all the winter time in a house in the suburb or outpart of the town which they call bohsedom that be God house where the dead body be pyle up together like billet on a woodstacke as hard with the frost as a very stone till the springtide come and resolve the frost what time every man take his dead friend and commit he to the ground months mind they have beside their year and month mind for their friend depart what time they have prayer say over the grave by the priest who have a penny ordinary for his pain when any die they have ordinary woman mourner that come to lament for the dead party and stand howl over the body after a profane and heathenish manner sometime in the house sometime bring the body into the backside ask he what he want and what he mean to die they bury their dead as the party use to go with coat hose boot hat and the rest of his apparel many other vain and superstitious ceremony they have which be long and tedious to report by these it may appear how far they be fall from the true knowledge and practice of christian religion have exchange the word of God for their vain tradition and bring all to external and ridiculous ceremony without any regard of spirit and truth which God require in his true worship chap. 26. of the emperor domestic or private behaviour the emperor private behaviour so much as may be or be meet to be know be after this manner he rise common about four a clock in the morning after his apparel and wash in come his ghostly father or priest of his chamber which be name in their tongue Otetz Duhouna with his cross in his hand where with he bless he lay it first on his forehead then upon his cheek or side of his face and then offer he the end of it to kiss this do the clerk of the cross call Chresby Deyack Profery bring into his chamber a paint image represent the saint for that day for every day with they have his several saint as it be the patron for that day this he place among the rest of his image god wherewithal his chamber be deck his private prayer as thick almost as the wall can bear with lamp and waxe-candle burn before they they be very costly and gorgeous deck with pearl and precious stone this image be place before he the emperor begin to cross himself after the ruff manner first on the forehead then on both side of his breast with aspody hospody gresnick Syhodestua which be as much to say as help i o lord my god lord comfort i defend and keep i a sinner from do evil etc. this he direct towards the image or saint for that day who he name in his prayer together with our lady who they call precheste saint Nicholas or some other to who he bear most devotion bow himself prostrate unto they with knock his head to the very ground thus he continue the space of a quarter of a hour or thereabouts then come again the ghostly father or chamber priest with a silver bowl full of Holywater which they call in Russee Sweta Voda and a sprinkle of Basill as they call it in his hand and so all to besprinkle first the image god and then the emperor this holy-water be bring fresh every day from the monastery far and near send to the emperor from the abbot or prior in the name of the saint that be patron of that monastery as a special token of good will from he these devotion be end he send into the empress to ask whether she have rest in health etc. and after a little pause go himself to salute she in a middle room betwixt both their chamber the empress lie apart from he and keep not one chamber nor table with the emperor ordinary save upon the eve of their lent or common fast what time she be his ordinary guest at bed and board after their meeting in the morning they go together to their private church or chapel where be say or sing a morning service call Zautrana of a hour long or thereabouts from the church he return home the emperor give presence every morning and sit he down in a great chamber to be see and salute by his nobility such as be in favour about the court. if he have to say to any of they or they to he then be the time and this be ordinary except his health or some other occasion alter the custom about nine in the morning he go to another church within his castle where be sing by priest and choristers the high service call Obead^a or Complin which common last two hour the emperor in the meantime talk common with some of his council nobility or captain which have to say to he or he to they and the council likewise confer together among themselves as if they be in their council-house this end he return home and recreate himself until it be dinner time he be serve at his table on this manner first every dish as it be deliver at the dresser be taste by the cook in the presence of the high steward or his deputy the emperor service at his table and so be receive by the gentlemen-wayter call Shilshey and by they carry up to the emperor table the high steward or his deputy go before there it be receive by the sewer call erastnoy who give a taste of every dish to the taster and so place it before the emperor the number of his dish for his ordinary service be about seventy dress somewhat gross with much garlic and salt much after the dutch manner when he exceed upon some occasion of the day or entertainment of some ambassador he have many more dish the service be send up by two dish at a time or three at the most that he may eat it warm first the bake than the roast meat and last the broth in his dine chamber be another table where sit the chief of his nobility that be about his court and his ghostly father or chaplain on the one side of the chamber stand a cubboord or table of plate very fair and rich with a great cistern of copper by it full of ice and snow wherein stand the pot that serve for that meal the taster hold the cup that he drink in all dinner time and deliver it unto he with a say when he call for it the manner be to make many dish out of the service after it be set on the table and to send they to such nobleman and officer as the emperor like best and this be count a great favour and honour after dinner he lay he down to rest where common he take three hour sleep except he employ one of the hour to bathe or box and this custom for sleep after dinner be a ordinary matter with he as withal the Russ after his sleep he go to evensong call Vechurna and thence return for the most part recreate himself with the empress till supper time with jester and dwarf man and woman that tumble before he and sing many song after the ruff manner this be his common recreation betwixt meal that he most delight in one other special recreation be the fight with wild bear bear bait which be catch in pit or net and be keep in bar cage for that purpose against the emperor be dispose to see the pastime the fight with the bear be on this sort the man be turn into a circle wall round about where he be to quit himself so well as he can for there be no way to fly out when the bear be turn loose he come upon he with open mouth if at the first push he miss his aim so that the bear come within he he be in great danger but the wild bear be very scarce have this quality that give advantage to the hunter his manner be when he assail a man to rise up right on his two hinder-leg and so to come roar with open-mouth upon he and if the hunter then can push right into the very breast of he betwixt his foreleg as common he will not miss rest the other end of their boar-spear at the side of his foot and so keep the pike still towards the face of the bear he speed he common at one blow but many time these hunter come short and be either slay or miserable tear with the tooth and talent of the fierce beast if the party quite himself well in this fight with the bear he be carry to drink at the emperor seller door where he drink himself drink for the honour of Hospodare and this be his reward for adventure his life for the emperor pleasure to maintain this pastime the emperor have certain huntsman that be appoint for that purpose to take the wild bear this be his recreation common on the holy day sometime he spend his time in look upon his goldsmith and jeweller tailor embroiderer painter and such like and so go to his supper when it draw towards bedtime his priest say certain prayer and then the emperor bless and cross himself as in the morning for a quarter of a hour or thereabouts and so go to his Bed emperor Theodore describe the emperor that now be call Theodore juanowich be for his person of a mean stature somewhat low and gross of a sallow complexion and incline to the dropsy hawke-nosed unsteady in his pace by reason of some weakness of his limb heavy and unactive yet common smile almost to a laughter for quality otherwise simple and slow witted but very gentle and of a easy nature quiet merciful of no martial disposition nor great apt for matter of policy very superstitious and infinite that way beside his private devotion at home he go every week common on pilgrimage to some monastery or other that be near hand pilgrimage he be of thirty four year old or thereabouts and have reign almost the space of
