history of law ceremony and account of their affair there be officer appoint to keep these Quippos the which at this day they call Quipocamayos the which be bind to give a account of every thing as the four and twenty letter apply they in diverse sort so do they draw innumerable word from their knot and diversity of colour which thing they do in such a manner that if at this day in Peru any another kind of Quippos which they make of grain of may for to cast up a hard account wherein a good arithmetician will be trouble with his pen to make a division to see how much every one must they do apply themselves of the order the indian hold in their write ch. 9 it shall be good to add hereunto what we have observe touch the indian write for their manner be not to write with a continue line but from the top to the bottom or in circlewise the latin and greek do write from the left hand unto the right which be the vulgar and common manner we do use the hebrew contrariwise begin at the right to the left and therefore their book begin where we do end the Chinois write neither like the greek nor like the hebrew but from the top to the bottom for as they be no letter but whole word diverse manner of writing and that every figure and character signify a thing they have no need to assemble the part one with another and therefore they may well write from the top to the bottom those of Mexico for the same cause do not write in line from one side to another but contrary to the Chinois begin below they mount upward they use this manner of writing in the account of their day and other thing which they observe yet when they do write in their wheel or sign they begin from the midst where the sun be figure and so mount by their year unto the round and circumference of the wheel by word picture and these memorial the king be often advertise of that which pass for this cause there be man of great agility which serve as currier to go and come who they do nourish in this bridge which seem fabulous yet be it very true for as we have say before they do bind together certain bundle of reed and weed which do grow in the lake that they call Torora and be a light matter diversity of head-tire although the indian be simple in their manner and habit yet do we see great diversity among the province especial in the attire of their head for in some place they carry a long and govern themselves have some chief man who the vulgar do respect and sometime though not often some of they assemble together about matter of importance to consult what they shall think necessary the three kind of government be altogether barbarous compose of indian without law without king and without any certain place of abode but go in troop like savage beast as far as I can conceive the first inhabitant of the indies be of this kind as at this day a great part of the bresillians Chiraguanas Chunchos Yscycingas and the great part of the floridians and all the in new Spain of this kind the other sort of government by commonalty be frame by the industry and wisdom of some among they in which there be some more order hold a more stay place as at this day those of Auracano and of teucapell in Chille and in the new kingdom of grenado the Moscas and the ottomitte in new Spain and in all these there be less fierceness and incivility and much more quiet than in the rest of this kind by the valour and knowledge of some excellent man grow the other government more mighty and potent which do institute a kingdom and monarchy it appear by their register continuance of their monarchy that their government have continue above three hundred year but not full four although their signiory for a long time be not above five or six league compass about the city of cusco their original and beginning be in the valley of cusco where by little and little they conquer the land which we call Peru pass beyond quitto unto the river of Pasto towards the north stretch even unto abundance of water marsh lake and river which run in those part these pass all other nation of America in policy and government strife betwixt and canary and much more in valour and arm although the canary which be their mortal enemy and favour the spaniard will never confess it nor yield they this advantage so as even at this day if they fall into any discourse or comparison and that they be a commonweal and government yet will I speak brief what I shall think fit in general to be most observe whereof I w^ll discourse more ample in the history the first point whereby we may judge the mexican government to be very politic be the order they have and keep inviolable in the election of their king for since their first call Acamapach unto their last which be Motecuma the second of that name there come none to the crown by right of succession but by a lawful nomination and election this election in the beginning be by the voice of the commons although the chief man manage it since in the time of iscoalt the four king by the advice and order of a wise and valiant man call Tlacael there be four certain elector appoint which with two lord or king subject to the mexican the one of Tescuco and the other of Tucuba have power to make this election they do common choose young man for their king because they go always to the war and this be in a manner the chief cause why they desire they so they have a special regard that they shall be fit for the war and take delight and glory therein after the election they make two kind of feast the one in take possession of the royal estate for the which they go to the temple make great ceremony and sacrifice upon the hearth call divine where there be a continual fire before the altar of the idol and after some rhetorician practise therein make many oration and speech the other feast and the most solemn be at his coronation for the which he must first overcome in battle and bring a certain number of captive which they must sacrifice to their god he enter in triumph with great pomp make he a solemn reception aswell they of the temple who go all in procession sound on sundry sort of instrument give incense and sing like secular man as also the courtier who come forth with their device to receive the u^ctorious King royal diadem see the picture story the crown or royal ensign be before like a mitre and behind it be cut so as it be not round for the forepart be high and do rise like a point the king of Tescuco have the privilege to crown the king of Mexico in the beginning when the mexican be but poor and weak the king be very moderate in their expense and in their court but as they increase in power they increase likewise in pomp and state until they come to the greatness of Motecuma house of live creature who if he have have no other thing but his house of beast and bird it have be a proud thing the like whereof have not be see for there be in this house all sort of fish bird of Xacamamas and beast as in a other Noah ark for sea fish there be pool of salt-water and for river fish lake of freshwater bird that do prey be feed and likewise wild beast in great abundance there be very many indian employ for the keep of these beast and when he find a impossibility to nourish any sort of fish foul or wild beast he cause the image or likeness to be make rich cut in precious stone silver or gold in marble or in stone and for all sort of entertainment he have his several house and palace some of pleasure other of sorrow and mourn and other to treat of the affair of the realm there be in this palace many chamber his palace according to the quality of the noble man that serve he with a strange order and distinction the mexican have be very curious to divide the degree and dignity among the their Law priest and teacher of the Law hereupon one day a Christian priest make his complaint that the indian be no good christian and do not profit in the law of God a old indian answer he very well to the purpose in these term let the priest say he employ as much care and diligence to make the indian christian as the minister of idol do to teach they their ceremony for with half that care they will make we the best christian in the world for that the law of jesus Christ be much better but the indian learn it not for want of man to instruct they wherein he speak the very truth to our great shame and confusion the mexican give the first place of honour to the profession of arm how the mexican make war and of the order of knighthood chap. 26. and therefore the nobleman be their chief soldier and other that be not noble by their valour and reputation get in war come to dignity and honour so as they be hold for nobleman they give goodly recompense to such as have do valiant who enjoy privilege that none else may have the which do much encourage they their arm be of razor of sharp cut flint which they set on either side of a staff which be so furious a weapon as they affirm that with one blow they will cut off the neck of a horse their arm they have strange and heavy club lance fashion like pike and other manner of dart to cast wherein they be very expert but the great part of their combat be perform with stone for defensive arm they have little rondache or target and some kind of morion or headpiece environ with feather they be clad in the skin of tiger lion and other savage beast they come present to hand with the enemy and be great practise to run and wrestle for their chief manner of combat be not so much to kill as to take captive the which they use in their sacrifice as have be say Motecuma set knighthood in his high splendour ordain certain military order as commander with certain mark and ensign the most honourable among the knight be those that carry the crown of their hair tie with a little red ribbon have a rich plume of feather from the which eagle-order do hang branch of feather upon their shoulder and roll of the same they carry so many of these roll as they have do worthy deed in war the king himself be of this order as may be see in chapultepec where Motecuma and his son be attire with those kind of feather cut in the rock the which be worthy the sight there be another order of knighthood which they call the lion and the tiger the which be common the most valiant and most note in war they go always with their mark and armoury there be other knight order of lion and tiger grey knight as the grey knight the which be not so much respect as the rest they have their hair cut round about the ear they go to the war with mark like to the other knight yet they be not arm but to the girdle and the most honourable be arm all over all knight may carry gold and silver and wear rich Cotton use paint and gild vessel and carry shoe after their manner but the common people may use none but earthen vessel knight pri^^lidges neither may they carry shoe nor attire themselves but in nequen the which be a gross stuff every memory of the great order and diligence the mexican use to instruct their youth chap. 27. than the order and care the mexican have to nourish their youth for they know well that all the good hope of a commonweal consist in the nurture and institution of youth whereof Plato treat ample in his book and for this reason they labour and take pain to sequester their child from delight and liberty which be the two plague of this age employ they in honest and profitable exercise for this cause there be in their temple see the picture story college a private house for child as school or college which be separate from that of the young man and maid of the temple whereof we have discourse as large there be in these school a great number of child who their father do willing bring thither and which have teacher and master to instruct they in all commendable exercise to be of good behaviour to respect their superior to serve and obey they give they to this end certain precept and instruction and to the end they may be please to nobleman they teach they to sing and dance and do practice they in the exercise of war some to shoot a arrow to cast a dart or a staff burnr at the end and to handle well a target and a Sword they suffer they not to sleep much to the end they may accustom themselves to labour in their youth and not be man give to delight beside the ordinary number of these child there be in the same college other child of lord and nobleman the which be instruct more private they bring they their meat and ordinary from their house their employment and trial and be recommend to ancient and old man to have care over they who continual do advise they to be virtuous and to live chaste to be sober in their diet to fast and to march grave and with measure they be accustom to exercise they to travel and in laborious exercise and when they see they instruct in all these thing they do careful look into their inclination if they find any one addict unto war be of sufficient year they seek all occasion to make trial of they send they to the war under colour to carry victual and munition to the soldier to the end they may there see what pass and the labour they suffer and that they may abandon all fear they be lade with heavy burden that show their courage therein they may more easy be admit into the company of soldier by this mean it happen that many go lade to the army and return captain with mark of honour some of they be so desirous to be note as they be either take or slay and they hold it less honourable to remain a prisoner and therefore they seek rather to be cut in piece then to fall captive into their enemy hand see how nobleman child that be incline to the war be employ the other that have their inclination to matter of the temple and to speak Christianity shall flourish much among the indian some godly person have begin and the king with his counsel have favour it but for that it be a matter of no profit they advance little and proceed cold we have not discover any nation at the indian that live in commonalty which have not their recreation play and dance military game in play dance and exercise of pleasure at Peru I have see play in manner of combat where the man of both side be sometime so chafe that often their Paella which be the name of this exercise fall out dangerous I have also see diverse sort of dance wherein they do counterfeit and represent certain trade and office as shepherd labourer fisher and hunter and common they make all those dance with a very grave sound and pale there be other dance and mask which they call Guacones who action be pure representation of the devil there be also man that dance on the shoulder one of another idol game Exo. 32. a thing usual to heathen as their comedy etc. manife music as they do in Portugal the which they call Paellas the great of these dance be superstition and kind of idolatry for that they honour their idol and guaca in that manner for this reason the prelate have labour to take from they these dance all they can but yet they suffer they for that part of they be but sport of recreation for always they dance after their manner in these dance they use sundry sort of instrument whereof some be like flute or little canon other like drum and other like cornet but common they sing all with the voice and first one or two sing the song than all the rest answer they some of these song be very witty compose contain history and other be full of superstition and some be mere folly our man that have converse among they have labour to reduce matter of our holy faith to their tune the which have profit well for that they employ whole day to rehearse and sing they for the great pleasure and content they take in their tune they have likewise put our composition of music into their language as octave song and rondel the which they have very apt turn and in truth it be a goodly and very necessary mean to instruct the people in Peru they common call dance Tagui in other province Areittos and in Mexico Mittottes there have not be in any other place any such curiosity of play and dance as in new Spain where at this day we see indian so excellent dancer as it be admirable some dance upon a cord some upon a long and straight stake in a thousand sundry sort other with the sole of their foot and their ham do handle curious dancer cast up and receive again a very heavy block which seem incredible but in see it they do make many other show of their great agility in leap vault and tumble sometime bear a great and heavy burden sometime endure blow able to break a bar of iron but the most usual exercise of recreation among the mexican be the solemn mittotte great agility and that be a kind of dance they hold so brave and so honourable that the king himself dance but not ordinary as the king don Pedro of Arragon with the barber of valencia this dance or Mittotte be common make in the court of the temple and in those of the king house which be more spacious they do place in the midst of the court two instrument one like to a drum and the other like a barrel make of one piece and hollow within which they set upon the form of a man a beast or upon a pillar these two instrument be so well accord together that they make a good harmony and with these instrument they make many kind of air and song they do all sing and dance to the sound and measure of these instrument with so goodly a order and accord both of their foot and voice as it be a pleasant thing to behold in these dance they make two circle or wheel the one be in the midst near to the instrument wherein the ancient and nobleman do sing and dance with a soft and slow motion and the other be of the rest of the people round about they but a good distance from the first wherein they dance two and two more light make diverse kind of pace with certain leap to the measure all which together make a very great circle they attire themselves for these dance with their most precious apparel and jewel every one according to his ability hold it for a very honourable thing for this cause they learn these dance from their infancy and although the great part of they be do in honour of their idol yet be it not so institute as have be say but only as a recreation and pastime for the people therefore it be not convenient to take they quite from the indian but they must take good heed they mingle not their superstition among they I have see this mittotte in the court of the church of Topetzotlan a village seven league from Mexico and in my opinion it be a good thing to busy the indian upon festival day see they have need of some recreation and because it be public and without the prejudice of any other there be less inconvenience then in other which may be do city of Mexico found and inhabit by the mexican who at that time be call Meciti who original beginning of be lord and their act and life be declare brief in this history according as it be signify and set out successive by the picture and paint follow in the year 1324. after the come of our lord and saviour jesus Christ the mexican people first arrive at the place of the city of Mexico and because they like well the greatness and the situation of that place after that they have travail in their journey and wander many year from country to country and in some of they have make their abode for some year be come from far country in follow their journey and not be content with the other place where they have make their abode they come and settle themselves in the place of Mexico the which place at that time be all drown with water and be cover with great bog and bank of moorish sheg and bulrush which they call and it have Carrizales and great plait of dry ground cover with shrub bush and brier like wood and through all the space of that place there go a spring and stream of fair clear water which be free from all sedge and bush which water stream go through it crosswise in manner of saint Andrew cross as it be show in the picture and about the middle of that place of that water-streame the Meciti find a great rock of stone and grow thereon a great tree or bush call tunal wherein a great eagle candal have she haunt and abode for her food so as all about that place be scatter full of bone and feather of diverse bird and fowl of diverse colour and they have go throughout all that place and country thereabouts and find it very fruitful and full of wild beast wild fowl bird and fish and thing of the water wherewith to sustain themselves and to profit themselves in their business in deal with the town thereabouts and find the watercourse of that place so commodious and that their neighbour can not trouble nor hurt they and for other thing and cause to their good like they determine to pass no further on their journey in travel but to settle themselves and dwell still and according to their determination they do settle themselves there effectual and make themselves a strong city of defence with bank and wall about the water and on the plait of ground among the ^egges and bush of Tulis and Carrizales and for a beginning of that their seat and habitation it be determine by they to give name and title to that place call it Tenultitlan by reason and cause of the tunal grow out of the rock for Tenuchtitlan interpret in our castilian Spanish tongue be tunal grow upon a rock the army of the mexican people have with they for chief governor ten person name Ocelopan Quapan Acacitli Ahuexolt te^uch t^cincuh (@) xocoyol Xuihcaqui Atototl as it be show in the exercise lordship and they appoint the other chief governor that they shall be agent and captain governor under he and after some year be pass of their dwell in that place and the people multiply the city likewise be name Mexico so name and derive of the mexican call it the place of settle of the mexican people and when the people be some what multiply like bold and warlike people they take beginning of courageous mind in prevail over their neighbour and so show themselves in force of arm whereby they subdue and make tributary to they two town next adjoin to Mexico name colhuacan and signify one year and they be the number of year it be to be understand that every several space or partition signify the one several year and so they account and number every year several proceed by the number of rundle or prick therein contain begin at one and proceed to thirteen rundle and from thence they begin again at the begin in their account from one point or rundle and so according they do proceed in number again till they come to thirteen and although that in the partition or space several there be diverse several figure yet the principal account of number be that account of the picture or rundle therein contain and although the name of the year that they give to every partition from the number of the first point till the thirteen be to some purpose yet for to advertise the reader thereof here be make by itself a declaration of the name with their interpretation in the order and rule of the partition which be number for year that partition where there be a branch with a foot like a flower it do signify a bitter and unfortunate year which the mexican have and do fear say that their predecessor time out of mind do give they warning that such year which befall every two and fifty year be dangerous and unfortunate and bitter year because that in such year there be flood general and likewise darkness of the eclipse of the sun and universal earthquake and likewise in such year they make great sacrifice and ceremony to their god and give themselves to repentance and do abstain from all vice against the very day and hour of such a year in the which day general they put out all their light and fire till that day be pass and be pass they kindle new light be have out of a mountain by a Priest this be a week of year after the mexican computation all colour blue the Motezuma Motezuma Mexico be now grow into great majesty renown and authority and he by his gravity and severity enlarge exceed the state and dominion of Mexico yea a great deal more than his predecessor Motexzeuma be the son of Axayacaci which have be lord of Mexico and before he come to the say lordship he have the desert of a worthy captain and a valiant man in war whereby he have the title of Tlacatecatl and so he succeed in the lordship of Mexico as be before rehearse and be in the say lordship he do great increase the mexican empire bear the rule over all the town in this new Spain his weal and greatness insomuch that they give and pay he great tribute of much riches and val^e he be fear very much of all his servant and likewise of his captain and principal insomuch that not one when they have any business with he for the great reverence they have he i^ majesty dare for fear look he in the face but that they hold down their eye and their head low and incline to the ground and many other extraordinary respect and ceremony they do unto he for the majesty he represent unto they not mention here for avoid of tediousness after M^t^zuma have succeed in the say lordship he conquer four and forty town hereafter name conquest and he subdue they under his lordship and empire and in their acknowledge of servitude all the continuance of his life they pay he many and great tribute as hereafter by their picture and declaration be make manifest wisdom and learning Motecuma be by nature wise and a ginger and a philosopher subtle and skill general in all art aswell of war as all other matter temporal and for his gravity and estate he have of his lordship the beginning of a empire according as his servant do reverence he with great honour and power that in comparison of he not one of his predecessor come to half so much estate and majesty law the statute and law of his predecessor since the time of Gueguemotecuma until his time he command to be keep and whole fulfil with great zeal and because he be a man so wise by his good nature he ordain and make other statute and law which he think defective for the execution of the former not abrogate any all which be for the welfare and good government of his commonwealth and subject he be incline to keep many house and woman many woman some wife some concubine which be daughter of the lord his subject and confederate and by they he have many child and to have so many wife be for to set forth his majesty the more for they hold it for a point of great estate among which the daughter of the lord of you again such as you hear be the receive of Hernando Cortes by Mutezuma a most mighty king into his great and famous city of Mexico the eight day of November 1519. the house where the spaniard be lodge be great and large the oration of Mutezuma to the spaniard with many fair chamber sufficient for they all it be neat clean mat and hang with cloth of Cotton and feather of many colour pleasant to behold when Mutezuma be depart from Cortes he begin to set his house in order and place the ordnance at his door and have all his thing in good sort he go to a sumptuous dinner that be prepare for he assoon as Mutezuma have make a end of his dinner hear that the stranger be rise from the table and repose a while then come he to Cortes salute he and sit down by he he give unto he diverse jewel of gold plate feather and many garment of Cotton both rich well weave and wrought of strange colour a thing comely that do manifest his greatness and also confirm their imagination this gift be deliver honourable and then begin his talk as follow lord and gentleman I do much rejoice to have in my house such valiant man as you be for to use you with courtesy and entreat you with honour according to your desert and my estate and where heretofore I desire that you shall not come hither the only cause be my people have a great fear to see you for your gesture and grim beard do terrify they yea they report that you have such beast as swallow man and that your come be from heaven bring with you lightning thunder and thunderbolt wherewith you make the earth to tremble and to shake and that you slay therewith who you please but now I do see and know that you be mortal man and that you be quiet and hurt no man also I have see your horse which be but your servant and your gun like unto shoot trunk I do now hold all for fable and lie which have be report of you and I do also accept you for my mere kinsman my father tell i that he have hear his forefather say of who I do descend that they hold opinion how they be not natural of this land but come hither by chance in company of a mighty lord who after a while that he have abide here they return to their natural soil after many year expire they cam^ again for those who they have leave here behind they a strange opinion but they will not go with they because they have here inhabit and have wife and child and great government in the Land now these mighty lord see that they be so stubborn and will not return with they depart from they sore displease say that he will send his child that shall both rule and govern they in justice peace and ancient religion and for this consideration we have always suspect and believe that such a people shall come to rule and govern we and consider from whence you come I do think that you be they who we look for and the notice which the great emperor Charles have for we who have now send you hither therefore lord and captain be well assure that we will obey you if there be no feign or deceitful matter in your deal and will also divide with you and you all that we have and although this which I have say be not only for your virtue fame and deed of valiant gentleman I will yet do it for your worthiness in the battle of Tavasco Teocazinco and chollolla be so few to overcome so many now again if you imagine that I be a God and the wall and roof of my house and all my vessel of service to be of pure gold as the man of Zempoallan Tlaxcallan and Huexozinco have inform you it be not so and I judge you to be so wise that you give no credit to such fable you shall also note that through your come hither many of my subject have rebel and be become my mortal enemy but yet I purpose to break their wing come feel you my body I be of flesh and bone a mortal man as other be and no god although as a king I do esteem myself of great dignity and pre-eminence than other my house you do also see which be of timber and earth and the princpal of mason work therefore now you do both know and see what odious liar those tale-bearer be but troth it be that gold plate feather armour jewel and other riches I have in the treasury of my forefather a long time preserve as the use of king be all the which you and you shall enjoy at all time and now it may please you to take your rest for I know that you be weary of your journey Cortes with joyful countenance humble himself see some tear fall from Mutezuma his eye say unto he upon the trust I have have in your clemency I insist to come both to see and talk with your highness and now I know that all be lie which have be tell i the like your highness have hear report of we assure yourself that the emperor king of Spain be your natural lord who you have expect he be the only heir from whence your lineage do proceed and as touch the offer of your highness treasure I do most hearty thank you after all this communication Mutezuma demand whether the beard man which come with he be either his vassal or his slave because he will entertain each one according to his estate a love answer Cortes answer that they be all his brethren friend and fellow except some that be his servant then he depart and go home to his palace and mariner and other servitor by a page of his household Mutezuma be a man of a small stature and lean his colour tawny as all the indian be Mutezuma describe he have long hair on his head six little hair upon he as though they have be put in with a bodkin his thin beard be black he be a man of a fair condition and a doer of justice well speak grave and wise belove and fear among his subject Mutezuma do signify sadness cin. to the proper name of king and lord they do add this syllable Cin which be for courtesy and dignity as we use Lord the Turk use zultan the Moor or barbarian call his lord muley title cin. and so the indian say Mutezumazin his people have he in such reverence that he permit none to sit in his sight nor yet in his presence to wear shoe nor look he in the face except very few prince he be glad of the conversation of the spaniard and will not suffer they to stand on foot for the great estimation he have of they and if he like any of the spaniard garment he will exchange his apparel for they he change his own apparel four time every day and he never clothe himself again with the garment which he have once wear change of apparel but all such be keep in his guardrobe for to give in present to his servant and ambassador and unto valiant soldier which have take any enemy prisoner and that be esteem a great reward and a title of privilege the costly mantle whereof have be diverse send to Cortes be of the same guardrobe his wardrobe his diet^rites Mutezuma go always very neat and fine in his attire he bathe he in his hothouse four time every day he go seldom out of his chamber but when he go to his meat he eat always alone but solemn and with great abundance his table be a pillow or else a couple of colour skin his chair be a fourfooted stool make of one piece and hollow in the midst well wrought and paint his table-clothe napkin and towel be make of cotton-wool very white and new for he be never serve but once with that naperie four hundred page bring in his meat all son of great lord and place it upon a table in his great Hall magnificent attendance the meat be bring in than come Mutezuma to behold the dish and appoint those dish that like he best and chafing-dish be prepare to keep that meat warm and seldom will he eat of any other dish except the lord steward or controller shall high commend any other dish before he sit down come twenty of his wife of the fair and best esteem or else those that serve weekly by turn his wife bring in the basin and ewer with great humbleness this do he sit he down and then come the lord steward and draw a wooden net before he because none shall come nigh his table and this noble man alone place the dish and also take they away for the page who bring in the meat come not near the table nor yet speak any word nor no man else while the lord Mutezuma be at his meat except some jester they all serve he barefooted barefoot service there assist always somewhat a far off six ancient and nobleman unto who he use to give of the dish that best like he who receive the same at his hand with great reverence and eat it incontinent without look in his face which be the great humility that they can use before he music he have music of fiddle flute and of a snaile-shell and a cauldron cover with a skin and such other strange instrument they have very evil voice to sing always at dinner time he have dwarf crooke-backe and other deform counterfeit all for majesty and to laugh at who have their meat in the hall among the jester and idiot jester which be feed with part of the meat that come from Mutezuma his table all the rest of the meat be give to three thousand of the guard who attend ordinary in the yard or court and therefore they say that there be bring for his table three thousand dish and as many pot of wine such as they use and that continual the buttery and Pantrey stand open which be a wonder to see what be in they the platter dish and cup be all of earth whereof the king be serve but once and so from meal to meal new he have likewise his service of gold and plate very rich but he use not to be serve with it they say because he will not be serve twice therewith the which he think a base thing plate some affirm that young child be slay and dress in diverse kind of dish for Mutezuma his table but it be not so only of man flesh sacrifice he feed now and then man flesh the table be take up then come again the gentlewoman to bring water for his hand with the like reverence as they use at the first and then go they to dinner with the other wife so that then the gentleman and page wait as their course fall when his table be take up and his servitor go to meat Mutezuma sit still then come in the suitor that have any affair to deal with he barefooted for all the person do use that reverence except some prince his kinsman as the lord of Tescuco and Tlacopan and a few other and be cold weather state ceremony they use to wear old ragged clothes upon their rich garment all suitor use to make three or four courtesy not look towards his face and speak unto he their head dowwards and in that order retire back again Mutezuma answer his suitor very grave with low voice and in few word and not to all suitor for other his secretary or counsellor that stand by answer for he and have their answer they return backward not turn their tail to the prince after these business do he use some recreation hear jester or song wherein he delight much jester and player or else to look upon the player who play with their foot as we do with our hand these have a cudgel like unto a pastler roller which they toss high and low as it be a ball in the air strange to behold they use other play to pass the time in such a order game that it seem marvelous to the looker on Cortes bring into Spain some of these player also they use matachines in such sort they do play that there stand each upon other shoulder and he that stand high show many feat sometime Mutezuma do behold the player who play at a game call Pacoliztli which be much like our table and they play with bean square like dice which they call Patolli and throw they out of both their hand upon a mat or else upon the ground where be make certain strike upon which they set down the chance that be throw and at this game they play all that they have and many time they value their own body and play that into captivity and to remain a slave I mean such as be common gamester of small estate sometime Mutezuma go to the tennis Court their ball be cell Villamaliztli and be make of the gum which come from a tree call Vlli. the tennis play in Mexico this tree grow in a hot country the gum be knead together and so make round be as black as pitch and somewhat heavy and very hard for the hand but yet good and light to rebound and better than our wind-bal they play not at chase but at Bandy or at check that be if the ball touch the wall it lose they may strike the ball with any part of their body but there be always a penalty if they only strike not with the buttock or side which be the fine play whereof they use a skin upon each buttock they play so many to so many for a pack of mantle or according to the ability of the player also they play for gold and feather and sometime for their own body as they use at Patolli which be there permit and lawful the tennis court be call Tlachco and be a hall long and narrow but wide upward then downward and high on the side then at the end which be a industry for their play the house be always white and smooth in the side wall they have certain stone like unto millstone with a little hole in the midst that pass through the stone the hole be so small that scarce the ball may pass through but he that chance to strike the ball into the hole which seldome happen win the game and by a ancient law and custom among tennis player he ought to have the cloak of all those that stand and behold the play on that side that the ball go in and in some tennis court the half of the garment of they that stand look on the winner be then bind to make certain sacrifice to the god of the tennis play and to the stone where the ball enter the beholder of the play will say that such a winner shall be a thief and a adulterer or else that he shall die quick they use in the temple of the tennis play two image of the god of the ball God of the ball. which stand upon the two low wall the sacrifice be celebrate at midnight with many ceremony and witchcraft and song for that purpose then come a priest from the cathedral church with other religious person to bless the sacrifice say certain devilish prayer and throw the ball four time in the tennis Court in this order be the tennis play consecrate and after this consecration it be lawful to play or else not for this diligence be first to be do when any tennis court or play be new build the owner of the tennis court also will never suffer any to play until he have first offer something to the idol their superstition be so great his palace Mutezuma have many house as well in Mexico as without for his recreation and pleasure as also for his ordinary dwell to their out-comming into the common street it have three court and in the one stand a fair fountain many hals and a hundred chamber of twenty three and thirty foot long a hundred bath and hothouse and for Mutezuma have another house with very good lodging and fair gallery build upon pillar of jaspe which extend towards a goodly garden in the which there be ten pond or more some of salt-water for sea-fowle and other some of fresh water for river-fowle and lake-fowle which pond be devise with sluice to empty and to fill at their pleasure for the cleanness of the feather there be such a number of fowl that scarce the pond may hold they and of such diverse kind both in feather and make as sure it be a admiration for the spaniard to behold for the most of they they know not nor yet have at any time see the like and to every kind of fowl they give such bait as they be wont to feed of in the field or Rivers there do belong to that house three hundred person of service some be to cleanse the pond other some do fish for bait other some serve they with meat other do loose they and trim their feather other have care to look to their egg other to set they abrood other cure they when they be sick and the princpal office be to pluck the feather for of they be make rich mantle tapissary target tuffe of feather and many other thing wrought with gold and silver a most perfect work their feather a house of foul for hawk and other strange thing there be another house with large quarter and lodging which be call a house for fowl not because there be more than in the other but because they be big and to hawk with all and be foul of rapine wherefore they be esteem as more noble than all the other there be in this house many high hals in the which be keep man woman and child in some of they be keep such as be bear white of colour white man which do very seldom happen in other some be dwarf crooked-backe burstenman counterfeits and monstrous person in great number they say that they use to deform they when they be child to set forth the king greatness every of these person be in several Halles by themselves wild beast in the low Halles be great cage make of timber in some of stone or a piece of a fish bone call Libisa and that be venomous for if any be hurt therewith and the head remain in the wound it so fester that it be almost incurable their sword be of wood and the for security of rebellion and for this cause they have general house in the city such and so great be the court of Mutezuma tribute and subjection of the indian to their King there be not in all the dominion of Mutezuma any subject that pay not tribute unto he the nobleman pay their tribute in personal service the husbandman call macevaltin with body and good in this sort they be either tenant or else heir to their possession those which be heir do pay one three part of all their fruit and commodity that they do reap or bring up as dog hen foul coney gold silver stone salt wax honey mantle feather Cotten and a certain fruit call Cacao that serve for money and also to eat also all kind of grain and garden herb and fruit whereof they do maintain themselves the tenant do pay monthly or yearly as they can agree and because their tribute be great they be call slave for when they may have licence to eat egg they think it a great favour it be report that they be tax what they shall eat and all the residue be take from they poverty of the tenant they go very poor clothe yea and the most of their treasure be a earthen pot wherein they boil their herb a couple of millstone to grind their corn and a Mat to lie upon they do not only pay this rent and tribute but also serve with their body at all time when the great king shall command they be in such great subjection to their prince that they dare not speak one word although their daughter shall be take from they to be use at pleasure all the aforesaid rent they bring to Mexico upon their back and in boat I mean so much as be necessary for the provision of the house and court of Mutezuma all the rest be spend among soldier and barter for gold plate precious stone and other rich jewel esteem of prince all the which be bring to the treasury in Mexico be large and great barn and house to receive and keep the corn for provision of the city see our picture book with officer and underofficer who do receive the same and keep account thereof in book of paint figure and in every town be a receiver who bear in his hand a rod or a bush of feather and those give up their account in Mexico receiver if any such have be take with deceit and falsehood death be his reward yea and his kindred punish with penalty as of a lineage of a traitor to his prince the husbandman if they pay not well their tribute be apprehend for the same and if they be find to be poor through sickness and infirmity than they be bear withal but if they be find to be lazy and slothful they shall be use according but in conclusion if they pay it not at a day appoint than they shall be sell for slave to pay their debt or else be sacrifice there be many other province which pay a certain portion and reknowledge service but this tribute be more of honour than profit in this sort Mutezuma have more than suffitient to provide his house and war and to heap up great store in his treasury moreover he spend nothing in the build of his house for of long time he have certain town that pay no other tribute tribute of man labour but only to work and repair continual his house at their own proper cost and pay all kind of workman carry upon their back or draw in sled stone lime timber water and all other necessary for the work likewise they be bind to provide all the firewood that shall be spend in the court which be a great thing and do amount to two hundred and thirty weight a day which be five hundred man burden and some day in the winter much more and for the king chimney they bring the bark of oak tree which be best esteem for the light thereof for they be great sorcerer Mutezuma have one hundred city with their province of who he receive rent tribute and vassalage where he maintain garrison of soldier and have treasurer in each of they his dominion do extend from the north sea to the south sea and six hundred mile in longitude within the main land although in very deed there be some town as tlaxcallon mechuacan Panuco and Teocantepec which be his enemy and pay he neither tribute nor service but yet the ransom be much when any of they be take also there be o^her king and nobleman as of Texcuto and Tlacopan which be not in subjection unto he but only in homage and obedience for they be of his own lineage unto who Mutezuma marry his daughter description of Mexico as it flourish in those time MExico at the time when Cortes enter be a city of sixty thousand house the king house and o^her nobleman house be great large and beautiful the other be small and mean without either door or window and although they be small yet there dwell in some of they two three yea and ten person by reason whereof the city be wonderful replenish with people this city be build upon the water even in the same order as Venice be all the body of the city stand in a great large lake of water three sort of street there be three sort of street very broad and fair the one sort be only water with many bridge another sort of only earth and the three of earth and water that be to say the one half earth to walk upon and the other half for boat to bring provision of all sort these street be keep always clean and the most part of the house have two door the one towards the causeway and the other towards the water at the which they take boat to go where they list and although this city be found upon water yet the same water be not good to drink whereof there be bring by conduit water from a place call Capultepec three mile distant from the city which spring out of a little hill at the foot whereof stand two statue or cover image wrought in stone with their target and lance the one be of Mutezuma and the other of Axaiaca his father the water be bring from thence in two pipe or canal in great quantity and when the one be foul than all the water be convey into the other till the first be make clean from this fountain all the whole city be provide so that they go sell the same water from street to street in little boat and do pay a certain tribute for the same this city be divide into two street the one be call Tlatelulco that be to say a little island and the other Mexico where Mutezuma his dwell and court be and be to be interpret a spring this street be the fair and most principal and because of the king palace there the city be name Mexico although the old and first name of the city be Tenuchtitlan which do signify fruit out of stone for the name be compound of Tetl which be stone and Nuchtl^ which be a fruit in Cuba and hispaniola call the tree or to speak proper the thistle that bear this fruit be name Nopal it grow also in bermuda and be nothing almost but leaf of a footebroad and round and three inch thick some more and some less according to the growth full of thorn which be venomous the leaf be green and the thorn or prick russet after that be plant it increase grow leaf unto leaf and the foot thereof come to be as the body of a tree and one leaf do only produce another at the point but at the side of the same leave proceed other leaf in some province where water be scant they use to drink the juice of these leaf the fruit thereof call Nuchtli be like unto fig and even so have his little kernel or grain within but they be somewhat large and crown like unto a meddler there be of they of sundry colour some be green without and carnationlike within which have a good taste other be yellow and other white and some speckled the best sort be the white it be a fruit that will last long some of they have the taste of pear and othersome of grape it be a cold and a fresh fruit and best esteem in the heat of summer the spaniard do more esteem they then the indian the more the ground be labour where they grow the fruit be so much the better there be yet another kind of this fruit red and that be nothing esteem although his taste be not evil but because it do colour and die the eater mouth lip and apparel yea and make his urine look like pure blood many spaniard at their first come into India and eat this fruit be in a maze and at their wit end think that all the blood in their body come out in urine yea and many physician at their first come be of the same belief for it have happen when they have be send for unto such as have eat this fruit they not know the cause and behold the urine by and by they minister medicine to staunch the blood a thing ridiculous to see the physician so deceive of this fruit Nuchtli and Tetl which be a stone be compound tenuchtlitan when this city be begin to be found it be place near unto a great stone that stand in the midst of the lake at the foot whereof grow one of these nopal tree and therefore Mexico give for arm and devise the foot of a nopal tree spring from a stone according to the city name Mexico be as much to say as a spring or fountain according to the property of the vowel and speech other do affirm that Mexico have his name of a more ancient time the name of Mexico who first founder be call Mexiti for unto this day the indian dweller in one street of this city be call of Mexico the mexiti take name of their princpal idol call Mexitli who be in as great veneration as Vitzilopuchtli god of the war Mexico be environ with sweet water and have three way to come unto it by cawsie the one be from the west and that cawsie be a mile and a half long another from the north and contain three mile in length eastward the city have no entry but southward the causeway be six mile long which be the way that Cortes enter into the city two lake one s^lt the other fresh the lake that Mexico be plant in although it seemteh one yet it be two for the one be of water saltish bitter and pestiferous and no kind of fish live in it and the other water be wholesome good and sweet and bring forth small fish the salt water ebb and flow eb and flow by the wind some as hence move derive the cause of the sea flow from the saltness cause of the saltness according to the wind that blow the sweet water stand high so that the good water fall into the evil and revert not backward as some hold opinion the salt lake contain fifteen mile in breadth and fifteen in length and more than five and forty in circuit and the lake of sweet water contain even as much in such sort that the whole lake contain more than thirty league and have about fifty town situate round about it many of which town do contain five thousand household and some ten thousand yea and one town call Tezcuco be as big as Mexico all this lake of water spring out of a mountain that stand within sight of Mexico the cause that the one part of the lake be brackish or saltish be that the bottom or ground be all salt and of that water great quantity of salt be daily make in this great lake be above two hundred thousand little boat which the indian call acalle 200000. canoas and the spaniard call they canoas according to the speech of Cuba and santo Domingo wrought like a knead trough some be big than other some according to the greatness of the body of the tree whereof they be make and where I number two hundred thousand of these boat I speak of the least for Mexico alone have above fifty thousand ordinary to carry and bring unto the city victual provision and passenger so that on the market day all the street of water be full of they the market place of Mexico the market be call in the indian tongue Tlanquiztli every parish have his market place to buy and sell in but Mexico and Tlatelulco only which be the chief city have great fair and place fit for the same and especial Mexico have one place where most day in the year be buy and sell but every four day be the great market ordinary and the like custom be use throughout the dominion of Mutezuma this place be wide and large compass round about with door and be so great that a hundred thousand person come thither to chop and change as a city most principal in all that region wherefore the resort be from far part unto that place every occupation and kind of merchandise have his proper place appoint which no other may by any mean occupy or disturb order of seller likewise pesterous ware have their place according that be to say stone timber lime brick and all kind of stuff unwrought be necessary to build withal also mat both fine and course of sundry workmanship also coal the diverse ware wood and all sort of earthen vessel glaze and paint very curious dear skin both raw and tan in hair and without hair of many colour for shoemaker buckler target jerkin and line of wooden corselet also skin of other beast and foul in feather ready dress of all sort the colour and strangeness thereof be a thing to behold the rich merchandise be salt and mantle of cotton wool of diverse colour both great and small some for bed other for garment and clothing outstretch for tapissarie to hang house other cotton cloth for line breech shirt table clothes towel napkin and such like thing there be also mantle make of the leaf of the tree call Metl and of palm tree and coney hair which be well esteem be very warm but the coverlet make of feather be the best they sell thread make of cony hair piece of linen cloth make of cotton wool also skein of thread of all colour also it be strange to see the great store of foul some wild some tame some water foul and other some of rapine all the bravery of the market be the place where gold and feather joint wrought be sell for any thing that be in request be there lively wrought in gold and feather indian workmanship and gallant colour the indian be so expert and perfect in this science that they will work or make a butterfly any wild beast tree rose flower herb root or any other thing so lively that it be a thing marvelous to behold it happen many time that one of these workman in a whole day will eat nothing only to place one feather in his due perfection turn and toss the feather to the light of the sun into the shade or dark place to see where be his most natural perfection and till his work be finish he will neither eat nor drink there be few nation of so much patience the art or science of goldsmith among they be the most curious and very good workmanship engrave with tool make of flint goldsmith or in mould they will cast a platter in mould with eight corner and every corner of several metal that be to say the one of gold and the other of silver without any kind of solder they will also find or cast a little caldron with loose handle hang thereat as we use to cast a bell they will also cast in mould a fish of metal with one scale of silver on his back and another of gold they will make a parrot or popinjay of metal that his tongue shall shake and his head move and his wing flutter they will cast a ape in mould that both hand and foot shall stir and hold a spindle in his hand seem to spin yea and a apple in his hand as though he will eat it our spaniard be not a little amaze at the sight of these thing for our goldsmith be not to be compare unto they they have skill also of Amell work and to set any precious stone but now as touch the market there be to sell gold silver copper lead latton and tin although there be but little of the three last metal mention there be pearl precious stone diverse and sundry sort of shell and bone sponge and other pedlar ware which certain be many and strange sort yea and a thing to laugh at their haberdash toy and trifle there be also many kind of herb root and seed as well to be eat as for medicine for both man woman and child have great knowledge in herb for through poverty and necessity they seek they for their sustenance and help of their infirmity and disease they spend little among physician although there be some of that art and many apothecary who do bring into the market ointment syrup water and other drug fit for sick person they cure all disease almost with herb yea as much as for to kill louse they have a proper herb for the purpose the several kind of meat to be sell be without number as snake without head and tail little dog geld moll rat long worm louse yea and a kind of earth victual of diverse sort for at one season in the year they have net of mail with the which they rake up a certain dust that be breed upon the water of the lake of Mexico and that be knead together like unto Oas of the sea they gather much of this victual and keep it in heap and make thereof cake like unto brickbat they sell not only this ware in the market but also send it abroad to other fair and market afar off they eat this meat with as good stomach as we eat cheese yea and they hold opinion that this scum or fatness of the water be the cause that such great number of fowl come to the lake which in the winter season be infinite all the seller pay a certain sum for their shop or stand to the king as a custom and they to be preserve and defend from thief and for that cause there go certain sergeant or officer up and down the market to espy out malefactor in the midst of the market stand a house which may be see throughout the fair and there sit twelve ancient man for judge to dispatch law matter their buy and sell be to change one ware for another as thus barter one give a hen for a bundle of Maiz other give mantle for salt or money which be Cacao and this be their order to chop and change they have measure and strike for all kind of corn and other earthen measure for honey and wine and if any measure be falsify they punish the offender and break their measure the temple be call Teucalli that be to say God house Teutl signify God the great temple of Mexico and Calianax be a house a name very fit if that house have be of the true God the spaniard that understand not the language do pronounce and call those temple cue and the god Vitzilopuchtli Vchilobos there be in Mexico many church with tower for their parish and street wherein be chapel and altar where the image and idol do stand and those chapel do serve for burial place of their founder for other be bury in the ground about they or churchyard all their temple be of one fashion therefore it shall be now sufficient to speak of the principal church this temple be square and do contain every way as much ground as a crossbow can reach level it be make of stone with four door that abut upon the three cawsey and upon another part of the city that have no causeway but a fair street in the midst of this quaderne stand a mount of earth and stone square likewise chief temple describe and fifty fathom long every way build upward like unto a pyramid of Egypt save the top be not sharp but plain and flat and ten fathom square upon the west side be step up to the top in number a hundred and fourteen which be so many high and make of good stone do seem a beautiful thing it be a strange sight to behold the priest some go up and some down with ceremony or with man to be sacrifice two altar upon the top of this temple be two great altar a good space distant the one from the other and so nigh the edge or brim of the wall that scarce a man may go behind they at pleasure the one altar stand on the right hand and the other on the left they be but of five foot high each of they have the back part make of stone paint with monstrous and foul figure the chapel be fair and well wrought of mason work and timber every chapel have three loft one above another sustain upon pillar and with the height thereof it show like unto a fair tower and beautify the city afar off from thence a man may see all the city and town round about the lake which be undoubted a goodly prospect and because Cortes and his their service without disturbance of any their general prayer be make towards the rise of the sun upon each altar stand a great idol beside this tower that stand upon the pyramid forty tower there be forty tower great and small belong to other little temple which stand in the same circuit the which although they be of the same make yet their prospect be not westward but other way because there shall be a difference betwixt the great temple and they some of these temple be big than other and every one of a several God several temple to several god among the which there be one round temple dedicate to the god of the air call Quecalcovatl for even as the air go round about the heaven even for that consideration they make his temple round the entrance of that temple have a door a strange door make like unto the mouth of a serpent and be paint with foul and devilish gesture with great tooth and gum wrought which be a thing to fear those that shall enter in thereat and especial the christian unto who it represent very hell with that ugly face and monstrous tooth there be other teucalle in the city that have the ascend up by step in three place all these temple have house by themselves with all service and priest and particular god at every door of the great temple stand a large hall and goodly lodging both high and low round about temple-hall which house be common armoury for the city for the force and strength of every town be the temple and therefore they have there place their store-house of munition they have other dark house full of idol idoll-hole great and small wrought of sundry metal they be all bathe and wash with blood and do show very black through their daily sprinkle and anoint they with the same when any man be sacrifice yea and the wall be a inch thick with blood bloody wall and the ground be a foot thick of blood so that there be a devilish stinch the priest or minister go daily into those oratory devilish priest and suffer none other but great personage to enter in yea and when any such go in they be bind to offer some man to be sacrifice that those bloody hangman and minister of the devil may wash their hand in blood of those so sacrifice and to sprinkle their house therewith for their service in the kitchen they have a pond of water that be fill once a year which be bring by conduit from the principal fountain all the residue of the foresay circuit serve for place to breed foul with garden of herb and sweet tree with rose and flower for the altar such so great and strange be this temple of Mexico for the service of the devil who have deceive those simple indian there do reside in the same temple continual five thousand person 5000. resident and all they be lodge and have their live there for that temple be marvelous rich and have diverse town only for their maintenance and reparation and be bind to sustain the same always on foot they do sow corn and maintain all those five thousand person with bread fruit flesh fish and firewood as much as they need for they spend more firewood than be spend in the king court these person do live at their heart ease as servant and vassal unto the god the idol of
