that all the four week make two and fifty year which be a perfect number in their reckon and be call the year of grace for from fifty two year to fifty two year they use to make solemn feast with strange ceremony as hereafter shall be declare and when fifty two year be end than they begin again by the same order before declare until they come to as many more begin at Tochtli and so forward but always they begin at the coney figure so that in the form of reckon they keep and have in memory thing of eight hundred and fifty year and by this chronicle they know in what year every thing happen and how long every king reign how many child they have and all thing else that import to the estate of the government of the Land the indian of Culhua do believe that the god have make the world but they know not how yet they believe that since the creation of the world four sun be pass the indian believe that five age be pass which they call sun and that the five and last be the sun that now give light to the World they hold opinion that the first sun perish by water and at the same time all live creature perish likewise the second sun say they fall from the heaven with who fall all live creature be slay and then say they be many giant in that country and certain monstrous bone which our man find in open of grave by proportion whereof some shall seem to be man of twenty span high the three sun be consume by fire which burn day and night so that then all live creature be burn the four sun finish by tempest of air or wind which blow down house tree yea and the mountain and rock be blow a sunder but the lineage of mankind perish not save that they be convert into ape and touch the five sun which now reign they know not how it shall consume but they say that when the four sun perish all the world fall into darkness and so remain for the space of five and twenty year continual and at the fifteen year of that fearful darkness the god do form one man and woman who bring forth child and at the end of the other ten year appear the sun which be new bear upon the figure of the coney day and therefore they begin their account of year at that day and reckon from the year of our lord 1552. their age or sun be 858. so that it appear that they have use many year their writing in figure and they have not only this use from Cetochli which be the begin of their year month and day of their five sun but also they have the same order and use in the other four sun which be pass but they let many thing slip out of memory say that with the new sun all other thing shall be likewise new they hold also opinion that three day after this last sun appear all the god do die and that in process of time the god which now they have and worship be bear although one brother be heir to another among the mexican and after their decease do inherit the son of the elder brother the coronation of the king of Mexico yet they take no possession of the state or name of king until they be anoint and crown open as soon as any king of Mexico decease and his funeral end then be call to parliament the lord of Tezcuco and the lord of Tlacopan who be the chief estate and then in order all other nobleman who owe any service to the mexican empire and be come together if any doubt of the inheritance of the crown happen than the matter be decide with all haste then the new king be know he be strip stark naked except a cloth to cover his privy part and in this sort be carry among they to the great temple of Vitzilopuchtli with great silence and without any joy or pleasure two gentleman of the city who office it be lead he up the stair of the temple by the arm and before he go the prince of Tezcuco and Tlacopan who that day do wear their robe of coronation whereupon be paint their arm and title very few of the laity go up into the chapel but only those that be appoint to attire the new king and to serve in other ceremony for all the residue stand upon the step and below to behold the coronation these magistrate be above in the chapel come with great humility and reverence kneel down upon their knee before the idol of Vitzilopuchtli and touch the earth with one finger and then kiss the same then come the high priest clothe in his pontifical vestment with many other in his company who do wear surplice and without speak any word they paint or colour the king person with ink make for the purpose as black as any coal after this ceremony do they bless the anoint king the ointment and sprinkle he four time with a certain holy water that be make at the time of consecration of the god make of dough or paste with a sprinkle make of bow of cane leave cedar and willow leave then they put upon his head cloth paint with the bone and soul of dead man and next they clothe he with a black garment and upon that another blue and both be paint with the figure of dead man skull and bone then they put about his neck certain lace whereat do hang the arm of the crown and behind his back they do hang certain little bottle full of powder by virtue whereof he be deliver from pestilence and disease according to their opinion yea and thereby witch nor witchcraft can not hurt he nor yet evil man deceive he in fine with those relic he be sure from all peril and danger upon his left arm they bind a little bag of incense and then bring unto he a chaffingdish of embers make of the bark of a oak tree then the king arise and with his own hand throw of the same incense into the chaffingdish and with great reverence bring the same to the god Vitzilopuchtli and after he have smoke he therewith he sit he down then come the high priest and take his oath to maintain the religion of the god to keep also all the law and custom of his predecessor to maintain justice and not to aggravate any of his vassal or subject and that he shall be valiant in the war that he shall cause the sun to give his light the cloud to yield rain the river to run and the earth to bring forth all kind of grain fruit and other needful herb and tree these and many other impossible thing the new king do swear to perform and then he give thanks to the high priest and commend himself to the god and to the looker on and they who bring he up in the same order carry he down again then all the people cry the god preserve the new king and that he may reign many year in health with all his people but then some begin to dance other to play on their instrument show outward their inward joy of heart and before the king come to the foot of the step all the nobleman come to yield their obedience and in token of love and faithful subject they present unto he feather string of snaile-shel collar and other jewel of gold and silver also mantle paint with death and bear he company unto a great hall within the compass of the temple and there leave he the king sit down under his cloth of estate call Tlacatecco and in four day depart not out of the circuit of the temple the which he spend in prayer sacrifice and penance he eat then but once a day and every day he bathe himself and again in the night in a great pond of water and then let himself blood in his ear and sense therewith the god of water call Tlaloc he likewise sense the other idol unto who he offer bread flower paper and little cane die in the blood of his own tongue nose hand and other part of his body after the four day expire then come all the nobleman to bear he company to his palace with great triumph and pleasure of all the city but after his consecration few or none dare look he in the face and now with the declaration of the act and ceremony that the mexican king be crown I shall not need to rehearse of other king for general they all do use the same order save that other prince go not up to the top of the temple but abide at the foot of the step to be crown and after their coronation they come to Mexico for their confirmation and then at their return to their country they make many drunken feast and banquet the mexican do believe that the soul be immortal the opinion of the mexican concern the soul and that they receive either joy or pain according to their desert and live in this world unto which opinion all their religion do attain and chief appear at their burial they hold for a assure faith that there be nine place appoint for soul and the chief place of glory to be near unto the sun nine place for soul where the soul of those which be good man slay in the war and those which be sacrifice be place and that all other sort of evil person their soul abode on the earth and be divide after this sort child that be dead bear go to one place those which die of age or other disease go to another those which die of sudden death to another those which die of wound or contagious disease go to another place those which be drown go to another those which be put to death for offence by order of justice as for robbery and adultery to another those which slay their father mother wife or child to another place by themselves also those who slay their master or any religious person go to another place the common sort of people be bury but lord and rich man have their body burn and their ash bury in their shroud they have a great difference for many dead body be bury better apparel then when they be on live woman be shroud after another sort and he that suffer death for adultery be shroud like unto the god of lechery call Tlazoulteutl he that be drown like unto the god of water name Tlacoc and he that die with drunkenness be shroud like unto the god of wine call Ometochtli but the soldier have a honourable shroud like unto the attire of Vitzilopuchtli and the like order in all other sort of death when any king of Mexico happen to fall sick they use forthwith to put a visor upon the face of Tezcatlipaca the burial of king in Mexico or Vitzilopuchtli or some other idol which visor be not take away until they see whether the king do amend or else die but if he chance to die than word be send throughout all his dominion to bewail his death and also other post be send be call the nobleman that be his nigh kinsman and to warn they within four day to come unto his burial the dead body be lay upon a fair Mat and be watch four night with great lamentation and mourn then the body be wash and a lock of hair cut from the crown of his head which be preserve as a great relic say that therein remain the remembrance of his soul this do a fine emerald be put in his mouth and his body shroud in seventeen rich mantle of colour both rich and costly wrought upon the upper mantle be set the device or arm of Vitzilopuchtli or Tezcalipuca or some other idol in who the king have great confidence in his life time and in his temple shall the body be bury upon his face they put a visor paint with foul and devilish gesture beset with many jewel precious stone and pearl then they kill his slave who office be to light the lamp and make fire unto the god of his palace these thing do they carry the dead body unto the temple some follow he with doleful tune other sing the death of the king by note for so be the custom the nobleman and gentleman of his household carry target arrow mases and ensign to throw into the fire where the body shall be bury in the temple the high priest and all the clergy receive he at the temple gate with a sorrowful song and after he have say certain word the body be throne into a great fire make for the purpose with all the jewel that he have about he and all the other thing which be bring to honour the burial also a dog new strangle with a arrow which be to guide he his way in the mean while that the king and dog be burn the priest sacrifice two hundred person howbeit in his ceremony there be no ordinary tax for sometime they sacrifice many more they be open with a razor of flint in the breast and their heart take out and throw into the fire where the king body be these miserable person be sacrifice and their body throw into a hole they believe assure that those shall serve for his slave in another world some of they be dwarf monstrous and deform person with some woman they place about the dead body of the king before his burial rose flower and sundry dish of meat and drink and no creature dare touch the same but only the priest for it seem to be a offering the next day follow all the ash be gather together and the tooth with the emerald that be in his mouth the which thing be put into a chest paint on the inside with horrible figure of devil and the lock of hair which be cut from his crown and another lock of hair which be preserve from the time of his birth then the chest be lock and a image of wood make and clothe like unto the king person which be set on the top of the chest. the obsequy endure four day in the which the wife and daughter of the king offer great offering at the place where his body be bury and before the chest and his image on the four day after the burial fifteen slave be sacrifice for his soul and on the twenty day other five person be also sacrifice likewise on the sixty three and fourscore which be like unto the year mind the kingdom of michuacan be almost as great as the empire of Mexico and when any king of that country happen to be visit with sickness the order of burial of the king of michuacan and bring to such extremity that hope of life be pass according to the opinion of physician than will he name and appoint which of his son shall inherit the estate and be know the new king or heir incontinent send for all the governor captain and valiant soldier who have any office or charge to come unto the burial of his father and he that come not from thenceforth be hold for a traitor and so punish when the death of the old king be certain than come all degree of estate and bring present to the new king for the approbation of his kingdom but if the king be not thorough dead but at the point of death than the gate be shut in and none permit to enter and when his life be depart then begin a general cry and mourn and they be permit to come where their dead king lay and to touch he with their hand this be do the carcase be wash with sweet water and then a fine shirt put upon he and a pair of shoe make of a dear skin put on his foot and about his ankle be tie certain bell of gold about his wrist of his hand be put Manyllias of turkey and other bracelet of gold likewise about his neck they hang other collar of precious stone and gold and ring in his ear with a great turquois in his neither lip then his body be lay upon a large beer whereon be place a good bed under he on his one side lay a bow with a quiver of arrow and on his other side lay a image make of fine mantle of his own stature or highness with a great tough of fine feather shoe upon his foot with bracelet and a collar of gold while his work be a do other be busy in wash the man and woman which shall be slay for to accompany he into hell these wretched folk that shall be slay be banquet and fill with drink because they shall receive their death with less pain the new king do appoint those who shall die for to serve the king his father but yet many of they have rather have be without his service notwithstanding some simple soul esteem that odious death for a thing of immortal glory first seven gentlewoman of noble parentage be appoint to die the one to have the office of keeper of his jewel which he be wont to wear another for the office of cupbearer another to give he water with a basin and Ewer another to give he always the urinal another to be his cook and another to serve for laundress they slay also many woman-slave and free maiden for to attend upon the gentlewoman and moreover one of every occupation within the city when all these that be appoint to die be wash and their belly full with meat and drink than they paint their face yellow and put garland of sweet flower upon each of their head then they go in order of procession before the beer whereon the dead king be carry some go play on instrument make of snail shell other play upon bone and shell of sea-turtils other go whistle and the most part weep the son of the dead king and other nobleman carry upon their shoulder the beer where the course lie and proceed with a easy pace towards the temple of the god his kinsman go round about the beer sing a sorrowful song the officer and household servant of the court with other magistrate and ruler of justice bear the standard and diverse other arm about midnight they depart in the order aforesaid out of the king palace with great light of fire brand and with a heavy noise of trumpet and drum the citizen which dwell where the corpse pass attend to make clean the street and when they be come to the temple they go four time round about a great fire make of the wood of pine tree which be prepare to burn the dead body then the beer be lay upon the fire and in the mean while that the body be burn they maul with a club those which have the garland and afterward bury they by four and four as they be apparel behind the temple the next day in the morning the ash bone and jewel be gather and lay upon a rich mantle the which be carry to the temple gate where the priest attend to bless those devilish relic whereof they make a dough or paste and thereof a image which be apparel like a man with a visor on his face and all other sort of jewel that the dea^ king be wont to wear so that it seem a gallant I doll at the foot of the temple stair they open a grave ready make which be square large and two fathom deep it be also hang with new mat round about and a far bed therein in the which a religious man place the idol make of a^hes with his eye towards the east part and hang round about the wall target of gold and silver with bow and arrow and many gallant tuffe of feather with earthen vessel as pot dish and platter so that the grave be fill up with household stuff chest cover with leather apparel jewel meat drink and armour this do the grave be shut up and make sure with beam board and flore with earth on the top all those gentleman which have serve or touch any thing in the burial wash themselves and go to dinner in the court or yard of the king house without any table and have dine they wipe their hand upon certain lock of Cotten will hang down their head and not speak any word except it be to ask for drink this ceremony endure five day and in all that time no fire be permit to be kindle in the city except in the king house and temple nor yet any corn be ground or market keep nor none dare go out of their house show all the sorrow that may be possible for the death of their King in Mexico be twelve judge who be all nobleman grave judge and well learn in the mexican law these man live only by the rent that proper appertain to the maintenance of justice and in any cause judge by they it be lawful for the party to appeal unto other twelve judge who be of the prince blood and always abide in the court and be maintain at the king own cost and charge the inferior judge come ordinary once every month to consult with the high and in every fourscore day come the judge of every province within the mexican empire to consult with the judge of Mexico but all doubtful cause be reserve to the king only to pass by his order and determination the painter serve for notary painter to paint all the case which be to be resolve but no suit pass above fourscore day without final end and determination there be in that city twelve sergeant who office be to arrest and to call party before the judge their garment be paint mantle whereby they be know a far off the prison be under ground sergeant prison moist and dark the cause whereof be to put the people in fear to offend if any witness be call to take a oath the order be that he shall touch the ground with one of his finger witness and oath and then to touch his tongue with the same which signify that he have swear and promise to speak the troth with his tongue take witness thereof of the earth which do maintain he but some do interpret the oath that if the pa^tie swear not true that then he may come to such extremity as to eat earth sometime they name and call upon the god of the crime who cause the matter touch the judge that take bribe or gift be forthwith put out of his office which
